question:
Fill in the blanks:

The composition "Guru Bin Kaise Gun Gaaye" is set to the rhythmic cycle known as ____
solution:
The correct answer is __**Teentaal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Teentaal** is one of the most widely used taals (rhythmic cycles) in Hindustani classical music.
 
• It consists of **16 beats**, divided into four equal sections (vibhags) of four beats each, making it highly versatile.
 
• The structure of Teentaal follows a systematic pattern of claps (taali) and a wave (khali), with claps on beats 1, 5, and 13, and a wave on beat 9.
 
• Teentaal is extensively used in instrumental, vocal, and dance performances due to its symmetry and adaptability.
 
• The composition "Guru Bin Kaise Gun Gaaye" is set to Teentaal, showcasing its balanced and rhythmic framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jhaptaal**

 
 
• Jhaptaal is a rhythmic cycle of **10 beats**, divided into four sections (2+3+2+3).
 
• It is commonly used in semi-classical and classical music forms like khayal and instrumental compositions.
 
• Jhaptaal's unique structure offers a dynamic and intricate rhythmic framework for performances.
 
 
 
• **Keharwa**
 
 
• Keharwa is a **8-beat taal**, divided into two sections (4+4).
 
• It is widely used in light classical, folk, and popular music across various Indian music traditions.
 
• Keharwa is known for its simplicity and is frequently used in bhajans, ghazals, and Bollywood songs.
 
 
 
• **Roopak**
 
 
• Roopak taal is composed of **7 beats**, divided into three sections (3+2+2).
 
• It is often employed in semi-classical and classical music, providing a unique rhythmic feel.
 
• Roopak taal's distinctive structure makes it suitable for compositions requiring a lighter rhythmic touch.

question: Which of the following is NOT a type of raga-based performance?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sonata**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Raga-based performances** are integral to Indian classical music, where compositions are structured around specific melodic frameworks called **ragas**. 
• **Thumri**: A semi-classical vocal form in Indian music, known for its romantic or devotional themes and expressive melodic improvisation. *It is a type of raga-based performance.* 
• **Dhrupad**: The oldest form of Indian classical vocal music, characterized by its meditative and austere style. *It is also a type of raga-based performance.* 
• **Prabandha**: An ancient form of Indian classical composition that predates Dhrupad and involves fixed lyrics and melodies. *It is raga-based as well.* 
• **Sonata**: A Western classical music composition, usually written for solo instruments or small ensembles, structured in movements and not based on ragas. **Hence, it is NOT a type of raga-based performance.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Thumri:** 
• Originated in the courts of North India during the 18th century. 
• Emphasizes **emotion (bhava)** and features a romantic or devotional theme. 
• Instruments like the tabla, harmonium, and sarangi often accompany Thumri performances. 
• It is closely associated with dance forms like **Kathak**. 
• **Dhrupad:** 
• Dates back to the medieval period and is considered the **oldest surviving form** of Indian classical music. 
• Performed in a slow and meditative style, focusing on purity of raga. 
• Often accompanied by the **pakhawaj** and tanpura. 
• It is traditionally sung in praise of deities or royal patrons. 
• **Prabandha:** 
• An ancient compositional form that predates Dhrupad. 
• Involves a fixed structure of lyrics and melody. 
• It was a precursor to later forms like Dhrupad and Khayal. 
• **Sonata:** 
• A form of **Western classical music** composition. 
• Typically consists of three or four movements with contrasting tempos and moods. 
• Developed in Europe during the **Classical period** (18th century). 
• Prominent composers of sonatas include **Beethoven, Mozart, and Haydn**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Raga:** 
• A raga is a melodic framework in Indian classical music used to express specific emotions. 
• Each raga is associated with a particular time of day, season, or mood (rasa). 
• It serves as the foundation for composition and improvisation in both Hindustani and Carnatic music traditions. 
• **Comparison with Western Classical Music:** 
• Western music relies on harmonic structures and fixed compositions, while Indian music emphasizes melody and improvisation. 
• Forms like the sonata, symphony, and concerto dominate Western classical music. 
• Indian music uses instruments such as sitar, tabla, and veena, whereas Western music uses piano, violin, and flute. </ul

The correct answer is **Kathak**.

• **Kathak dancer** and choreographer** Aditi Mangaldas **was born in 1960.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Kathak:**

 
• The well-known ancient Indian classical dance known as Kathak is said to have originated with the **nomadic storytellers from North India known as Kathakars**.
 
• These Kathakars traveled and told tales using songs, dances, and music that were reminiscent of classical Greek theatre.
 
• The foundations of Kathak are rooted in Natya Shastra, an ancient Sanskrit text written by Bharata Muni.
 
• **The three chief sections of a Kathak dance are:**
 
 
• **Invocation**: The act of an artist offering a prayer or salutation to God and their guru is known as an invocation.
 
 
• Hindu performers employ mudras, or hand gestures, to convey the same message.
 
• On Muslim holidays, the artist presents a "salami."
 
 
 
• **Nritta**: The artist's portrayal of pure dancing.
 
 
• He or she begins by moving the neck, wrists, and eyebrows slowly and elegantly.
 
• The quick sequences according to "bols" come next. A bol is a brief rhythmic pattern sequence. Here, the artist also demonstrates lively footwork.
 
 
 
• **Nritya**: In this piece, the performer uses facial expressions, slow body motions, and vocal and instrumental music to tell a tale or explore a theme.

• **Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT)**
 
 
• CCRT is an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.

• CCRT conducts training programs, workshops, and provides resources for teachers and students to promote cultural education.

question: Fill in the Blank: Kalbelia dance represents the movement of _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Snakes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalbelia Dance** is a traditional folk dance performed by the Kalbelia community of **Rajasthan, India**, primarily known for their expertise in snake charming.
 
• The movements of the dancers in Kalbelia mimic the graceful and fluid movements of a **snake**. This is in line with the community’s traditional association with snake charming.
 
• It is performed by women wearing traditional black swirling skirts that are embroidered with silver ribbons, representing the **color and movement of snakes**.
 
• The **music** accompanying the dance is provided by male members of the community using traditional instruments like the **pungi** (a wind instrument traditionally used by snake charmers), the dholak (a type of drum), and the khanjari (a tambourine-like instrument).
 
• In **2010**, Kalbelia dance was included in the **UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**, recognizing its cultural significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kalbelia Community:**

 
 
• The Kalbelias are a semi-nomadic community traditionally involved in snake charming and trading snake venom.
 
• Their livelihood has historically revolved around their deep connection with snakes, which is reflected in their art forms like dance and music.
 
• In modern times, the Kalbelia community has shifted from snake charming due to legal restrictions and has focused more on preserving their cultural heritage through dance and music.
 
 
 
• **Costumes:**
 
 
• The dancers wear black skirts that are embroidered with silver or white patterns resembling snake skin.
 
• Their jewelry is elaborate, often including headpieces, necklaces, and bangles, complementing the vibrant and dynamic dance movements.
 
 
 
• **Musical Instruments:**
 
 
• The **pungi** is the primary instrument, traditionally used by snake charmers to control snakes.
 
• Other instruments like the **dholak** and **khanjari** add rhythm and vibrancy to the performance, creating a lively and captivating atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Performance Style:**
 
 
• The dance is characterized by intricate footwork, swirling movements, and graceful gestures, all mimicking the sinuous and undulating motion of a snake.
 
• The performers often incorporate storytelling elements into their dance, narrating tales of their heritage and connection to nature.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:**
 
 
• Kalbelia dance was recognized by UNESCO in **2010** as part of the **Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**.
 
• This recognition has helped in preserving and promoting the dance on global platforms, highlighting its cultural significance and artistic value.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kalbelia Dance and Indian Culture:**

 
 
• The Kalbelia dance is a significant representation of India’s diverse cultural heritage, showcasing the unique traditions of a marginalized community.
 
• Its inclusion in UNESCO’s list has brought attention to the need for preserving endangered cultural practices and supporting the communities that sustain them.
 
 
 
• **Connection with Wildlife:**
 
 
• The dance reflects the Kalbelia community’s historical relationship with wildlife, particularly snakes, and their environment.
 
• Their cultural practices highlight the importance of coexistence with nature and respecting biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Tourism and Cultural Preservation:**
 
 
• Kalbelia dance has become a popular attraction in Rajasthan’s cultural festivals and tourism events, contributing to the local economy and cultural preservation.
 
• Efforts are being made by the government and NGOs to promote and support the Kalbelia community in preserving their cultural identity.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Perini Shivatandavam** is a warrior dance that was traditionally performed before soldiers set off for war.
 
• The dance form has its origins in the **Kakatiya dynasty**, which ruled parts of present-day Telangana and Andhra Pradesh during the 12th and 13th centuries.
 
• It was revived in modern times by the renowned dance guru **Nataraja Ramakrishna**.
 
• The dance is dedicated to Lord Shiva, and its performance is characterized by vigorous movements symbolizing strength and valor.
 
• The second statement, which associates the dance form with the Chola kings of Tamil Nadu, is incorrect as Perini Shivatandavam is specific to the Kakatiya dynasty of Telangana.

• The Kakatiya dynasty ruled the Deccan region, particularly Telangana and parts of Andhra Pradesh, during the 12th and 13th centuries.
 
• They were known for their patronage of art and architecture, including temples like the Ramappa Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Chola Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Chola dynasty ruled over Tamil Nadu and parts of South India, Sri Lanka, and the Maldives during the medieval period.
 
• They were known for their contributions to art, literature, and architecture, including the construction of the Brihadeeswarar Temple.

question: Which Indian martial art involves the use of a flexible sword called "Urumi"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalaripayattu**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Kalaripayattu** is one of the oldest martial arts in the world and is native to **Kerala, India**. 
• It involves the use of various weapons, including a unique flexible sword called the **"Urumi"**, which is considered one of the deadliest weapons in this martial art. 
• The **Urumi** is a long, flexible whip-like sword made of metal that requires exceptional skill and mastery to wield effectively. 
• Kalaripayattu combines physical training, self-defense techniques, and medicinal practices, making it a holistic martial art form. 
• It is deeply rooted in the cultural and historical traditions of Kerala, with connections to ancient Indian martial practices and spiritual philosophies. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Silambam:** 
• Silambam is a weapon-based martial art originating from **Tamil Nadu, India**. 
• It primarily uses a **staff (stick)** as the main weapon, along with other tools such as knives and swords. 
• It focuses on speed, agility, and precision, and is traditionally practiced for self-defense and combat training. 
• **Gatka:** 
• Gatka is a traditional Sikh martial art that originated in **Punjab, India**. 
• It involves the use of various weapons, including swords, sticks, and shields, and emphasizes spiritual and physical discipline. 
• Gatka is often performed during Sikh festivals and events as a demonstration of martial skills and cultural heritage. 
• **Thang-Ta:** 
• Thang-Ta is a martial art form from **Manipur, India**, focusing on the use of swords and spears. 
• It integrates physical combat techniques with dance movements and spiritual practices. 
• Thang-Ta is deeply connected to the cultural and religious traditions of Manipur. 
• **Urumi:** 
• The **Urumi** is unique to Kalaripayattu and requires advanced expertise to handle due to its flexible nature. 
• It is used both offensively and defensively, allowing the wielder to attack multiple opponents simultaneously. 
• The weapon symbolizes precision, agility, and mastery in Kalaripayattu. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Historical Significance:** 
• Kalaripayattu is believed to have influenced other martial arts, including **Kung Fu**, through the teachings of Indian monks such as **Bodhidharma**. 
• Its origins date back to ancient India and are mentioned in texts such as the **Mahabharata**. 
• **Training and Philosophy:** 
• Kalaripayattu training includes mastery of weapons, hand-to-hand combat, acrobatics, and medicinal knowledge. 
• It emphasizes physical fitness, mental discipline, and spiritual growth. 
• **Modern Revival:** 
• Efforts are being made to preserve and promote Kalaripayattu as a cultural and martial art heritage. 
• It is gaining recognition globally and is often showcased in movies, performances, and exhibitions. </ul

question: Which of the following is NOT a percussion instrument?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Sarod.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sarod** is not a percussion instrument whereas Mridangam, Tabla, and Ghatam are **percussion instruments**.
 
• In percussion, the sound is produced by striking the animal skin which has been stretched across an earthen or metal pot or a wooden barrel or frame.
 
• The main categories are-
 
 
• Oordhwaka,
 
• Ankya,
 
• Alingya, and
 
• the waisted or the Damaru family of drums
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tabla** pair is a set of two vertical Oordhwaka drums.
 
• **Ankya drums** are held horizontally before the musician and usually, both sides are covered with animal hide.
 
• **Oordhwaka drums** are placed vertically before the musician and sound is produced by striking them with sticks or fingers.
 
• **Alingya drums** have the animal hide fixed to a wooden round frame and are embraced or held close to the body with one hand while the other hand is used for playing the instrument.
 
• **Damru family** is also known as the hourglass variety of drums as their shape resembles an hourglass.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea9dab231bacb90443f7815bbd6e9af2762117c9714ed485d416439aba22297e.png]

question: Tansen, who was included in the Navaratnas of Akbar, was an expert in playing which of the following musical instruments?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabab**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tansen, one of the Navaratnas of Akbar's court, was a notable figure in Hindustani classical music.
 
• He was an exceptional vocalist and is also known for his expertise in playing the Rudra Veena or "Rabab" an ancient Indian string instrument.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**Akbar's Navaratnas, or Nine Jewels, were a group of nine talented individuals at the court of the Mughal Emperor Akbar. Each of them was well known for their respective skills and contributions. They were:

 
• **Abul Fazl (also known as Allami)**: The full name of** Abul Fazl is Abu'l-Fazl ibn Mubarak**. He was one of the most important historians during the reign of Akbar. His most known writings are the **Akbarnama and the Ain-i-Akbari**. Akbarnama is a historical account of Akbar's reign, and Ain-i-Akbari is a detailed document recording the administration of the empire.
 
• **Faizi (or Shaikh Faiz)**: His real name was Shaikh Faizi Sirhindi. He was a brilliant poet and scholar. He is known for his poetry collection called **"Taskeen-e-ruh-o-dil"** and also his interpretation of ancient texts.
 
• **Raja Birbal (originally named Mahesh Das)**: He was a poet and musician, admired for his quick wit, intelligence and his keen sense of humor. Among his notable contributions are the Birbal stories, popular folklore that's been passed down generations.
 
• **Raja Todar Mal (Todar Mall)**: He was a finance minister **(Diwan-i-Ashraff)** who undertook innovative measures like standardizing land measurements to improve the revenue system. He doesn't have any known books or musical contributions.
 
• **Tansen (originally named Ramtanu Pandey)**: He was associated with the Dhrupad style and a pioneer of Indian classical music. He composed many ragas which are still in use today.
 
• **Raja Man Singh (Man Singh I)**: He led many successful military campaigns for Emperor Akbar. He was influential in the administration and politics.
 
• **Abdul Rahim Khan-I-Khana (Rahim)**: He is known for his 'dohas' or couplings in Hindi. He is also known for translating Babar's memoirs, Baburnama from Chagatai language to Persian.
 
• **Fakir Aziao-Din**: He was one of the chief advisors to Akbar and was highly respected for his wisdom and spirituality. 
 
• **Mullah Do Piaza**: His contributions are mainly in the form of folklore, with stories about his wisdom and wit being highlighted in Mughal anecdotes.

question: Ustad Zia Mohiuddin Dagar was a ________ player of profound depth, favouring sparse and slow realisations of ragas.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudra veena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ustad Zia Mohiuddin Dagar was a renowned player of the Rudra veena, an ancient Indian string instrument.
 
• He was known for his profound depth in playing, often favoring sparse and slow realizations of ragas, which is a distinctive feature of Rudra veena performances.
 
• The Rudra veena, also known as Been, is one of the oldest classical instruments in India, used primarily in the Dhrupad genre of Indian classical music.
 
• Ustad Zia Mohiuddin Dagar's contributions to the music world include reviving and popularizing the Rudra veena, which was at risk of becoming obsolete.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rudra veena**

 
 
• The Rudra veena is a large plucked string instrument used in Hindustani classical music, particularly in the Dhrupad genre.
 
• It consists of a long tubular body with two large resonating gourds attached at both ends. The strings are plucked using a plectrum.
 
• The instrument is known for its deep, rich tones and is considered one of the most difficult to master due to its size and playing technique.
 
• The Rudra veena is associated with the ancient music traditions of India and is believed to have divine origins, often linked to the god Shiva.
 
 
 
• **Dhrupad**
 
 
• Dhrupad is the oldest form of Hindustani classical music still in practice today. It is a vocal genre, but also performed on instruments like the Rudra veena.
 
• This genre emphasizes a strict adherence to the raga (melodic structure) and tala (rhythmic cycle) and is known for its meditative and spiritual qualities.
 
• Dhrupad performances are characterized by their slow and deliberate pace, with a focus on precise intonation and deep emotional expression.
 
• It was traditionally performed in temples and courts, and today it continues to be a revered form of classical music in India.
 
 
 
• **Raga**
 
 
• A raga is a framework for improvisation akin to a melodic mode in Indian classical music. It provides a set of rules for building a melody.
 
• Each raga is associated with specific moods, times of the day, and seasons, and it is believed to evoke certain emotions in the listener.
 
• Ragas are composed of specific sequences of notes and characteristic musical phrases that define their unique identities.
 
• Musicians use these frameworks to improvise and create music that is both structured and expressive.

• It has a trapezoid shape and is usually made of walnut or maple wood, with a total of 72 strings arranged in sets of three, producing a bright, shimmering sound.
 
• The instrument is placed on the lap and played while sitting cross-legged, and it is used in both classical and folk music.
 
 
 
• **Tabla**
 
 
• The Tabla is a pair of twin hand drums used in Indian classical, popular, and devotional music.
 
• Consisting of a smaller drum called 'dayan' (right) and a larger drum called 'bayan' (left), the Tabla is known for its complex rhythms and tonal versatility.
 
• It is played with the fingers and palms, allowing for a wide range of dynamic and expressive sounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Annapurna Devi was an Indian surbahar (bass sitar) player of the Maihar gharana.
 
• She was the daughter and disciple of Allauddin Khan, who was a prominent figure in Hindustani classical music.
 
• Annapurna Devi was considered one of the foremost exponents of the surbahar, a rare and difficult instrument to master.
 
• She was also the spouse of the renowned sitar player Ravi Shankar and significantly contributed to the popularity of Indian classical music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Surbahar:**

 
 
• The surbahar, also known as the bass sitar, is a plucked string instrument used in the Hindustani classical music of North India.
 
• It is often referred to as the "bass sitar" because it is larger than the sitar and has a lower pitch.
 
• The surbahar is designed for the elaborate, slow-tempo alap section of a raga performance, with its deep, resonant tones.
 
• The instrument has a wide range and can produce a variety of tonal colors, making it suitable for both solo and accompanying performances.
 
 
 
• **Maihar Gharana:**
 
 
• The Maihar gharana is a school of Hindustani classical music named after the town of Maihar in Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• It was founded by the legendary musician Allauddin Khan, who was a master of multiple instruments including the sarod, surbahar, and sitar.
 
• The gharana is known for its emphasis on the dhrupad style of alap, intricate raga improvisations, and the use of both vocal and instrumental techniques.
 
• Some of the prominent disciples of Allauddin Khan from the Maihar gharana include Ravi Shankar, Ali Akbar Khan, and Annapurna Devi.
 
 
 
• **Hindustani Classical Music:**
 
 
• Hindustani classical music is a tradition of Indian classical music that developed in North India around the 13th and 14th centuries.
 
• It is characterized by a variety of ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic cycles) used in compositions and improvisations.
 
• Instruments commonly used in Hindustani classical music include the sitar, tabla, sarod, surbahar, and bansuri, among others.
 
• This genre of music is known for its intricate ornamentation, improvisational freedom, and deep emotional expression.

question: Tarun Bhattacharya, who was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018, is known for playing which musical instrument?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Santoor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tarun Bhattacharya is a renowned Indian Santoor player known for his significant contributions to Indian classical music.
 
• He was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018, which is one of the highest recognitions in the field of performing arts in India.
 
• Tarun Bhattacharya has been instrumental in popularizing the Santoor globally and has performed in various prestigious venues worldwide.
 
• He is a disciple of Pandit Ravi Shankar and has played a crucial role in innovating and evolving the playing technique of the Santoor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Santoor**

 
 
• The Santoor is a hammered dulcimer, a stringed musical instrument originating from the valleys of Kashmir in India.
 
• It consists of a wooden trapezoid-shaped body with numerous strings stretched across it, played by striking the strings with a pair of curved mallets.
 
• The Santoor is commonly used in Indian classical music and is known for its distinct, melodious sound.
 
• The instrument has a significant presence in Sufi music and has been incorporated into various musical genres over time.
 
 
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award**
 
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is a national honor bestowed by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy of Music, Dance & Drama.
 
• It was established in 1952 to recognize and reward outstanding achievements in the performing arts.
 
• Recipients of the award are given a citation, a cash prize, and a shawl as a mark of honor.
 
• This prestigious award is a testament to an artist's dedication and excellence in their respective field.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Music**
 
 
• Indian classical music is a rich tradition that dates back thousands of years and is categorized into two major traditions: Hindustani (North Indian) and Carnatic (South Indian).
 
• It is characterized by intricate ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic cycles) that form the basis of compositions and improvisations.
 
• Instruments like the sitar, tabla, veena, and santoor play pivotal roles in Indian classical music performances.
 
• The music is deeply spiritual, often associated with various deities and used in religious and ceremonial contexts.

question: Alla Rakha is famous for playing which of the following musical instruments?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tabla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ustad Alla Rakha, born as Allah Rakha Qureshi, was an Indian tabla player known for his virtuosity and innovation on the instrument.
 
• He is most famous for his collaboration with sitar maestro Ravi Shankar, with whom he performed at many prestigious venues worldwide.
 
• Alla Rakha played a crucial role in popularizing the tabla and Indian classical music in the West during the 20th century.
 
• He is also the father of renowned tabla player Zakir Hussain, who continues his legacy in Indian classical music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tabla**

 
 
• The tabla is a pair of twin hand drums from the Indian subcontinent, used in traditional, classical, popular, and folk music.
 
• The instrument consists of a small right-hand drum called "Dayan" and a larger metal drum called "Bayan".
 
• It is used in a variety of genres and is a significant instrument in Hindustani classical music.
 
• The technique of playing tabla involves extensive use of fingers and palms in various configurations to create a wide range of sounds and rhythms.
 
 
 
• **Damaru**
 
 
• The damaru is a small two-headed drum, which is played by twisting it back and forth, causing the strikers to beat against the drumheads.
 
• It is often associated with the Hindu deity Shiva and is used in various religious and spiritual contexts.
 
 
 
• **Bansuri**
 
 
• The bansuri is a traditional Indian flute made from bamboo.
 
• It is used in Hindustani classical music and is known for its soothing sound.
 
• The instrument has six to eight holes and is played by blowing air into a hole near one end.
 
 
 
• **Shehnai**
 
 
• The shehnai is a double-reed instrument, similar to the oboe, and is used in North Indian classical music.
 
• It is often played during weddings and other auspicious occasions in India.

question: Arvind Parikh, a Padma Bhushan awardee, plays which of the following musical instruments?

The correct answer is __**Sitar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Arvind Parikh is a renowned sitar player from India.
 
• He is a disciple of Ustad Vilayat Khan, one of the most influential sitar maestros.
 
• Parikh has performed extensively in India and abroad, contributing significantly to the global recognition of Indian classical music.
 
• He has been honored with the Padma Bhushan award, one of India's highest civilian awards, for his contributions to the field of music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sitar**

 
 
• The sitar is a plucked stringed instrument used in Hindustani classical music.
 
• It has a long neck and a gourd-shaped body, with 18-20 strings including both playing and sympathetic strings.
 
• Renowned sitar players include Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan, and Anoushka Shankar.
 
• The sitar is known for its deep, resonant sound and is often used to play ragas, which are melodic frameworks for improvisation in Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Bansuri**
 
 
• The bansuri is an Indian flute made from a single hollow shaft of bamboo with six or seven finger holes.
 
• It is traditionally used in Indian classical music and folk music.
 
• Notable bansuri players include Hariprasad Chaurasia and Pannalal Ghosh.
 
 
 
• **Tabla**
 
 
• The tabla is a pair of twin hand drums from the Indian subcontinent, used in traditional, classical, popular, and religious music.
 
• It consists of a small right-hand drum called the dayan and a larger left-hand drum called the bayan.
 
• Famous tabla players include Zakir Hussain and Alla Rakha.
 
 
 
• **Sarangi**
 
 
• The sarangi is a bowed, short-necked string instrument from India, Nepal, and Pakistan.
 
• It is used in Hindustani classical music and is known for its rich, resonant sound.
 
• Prominent sarangi players include Ram Narayan and Sabri Khan.

question: Umayalpuram K Sivaraman is an eminent musician associated with which of the following musical instruments?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mridangam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Umayalpuram K Sivaraman is a renowned Indian percussionist, known for his contributions to Carnatic music.
 
• He is specifically famous for his mastery over the **Mridangam**, a traditional South Indian drum.
 
• He has received numerous awards and honors, including the Padma Vibhushan, the second-highest civilian award in India, for his contributions to the field of music.
 
• He has performed in various prestigious music festivals and has collaborated with many other eminent musicians both within India and internationally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mridangam**

 
 
• The Mridangam is a traditional double-headed drum used in South Indian classical music, known as Carnatic music.
 
• It is made from a hollow piece of jackfruit wood, and its two drumheads are made from goat or cow skin.
 
• The right head produces a high-pitched sound, while the left head produces a low-pitched sound, and the drum is played using both hands.
 
• The Mridangam plays a crucial role in the rhythm section of Carnatic music ensembles, providing intricate rhythmic patterns and beats to accompany vocal and instrumental performances.
 
 
 
• **Sitar**
 
 
• The Sitar is a plucked string instrument used in Hindustani classical music, primarily in North India.
 
• It has a long, hollow neck and a gourd body, with a varying number of strings, typically ranging from 18 to 20.
 
• The Sitar is known for its distinctive sound, produced by plucking the strings with a metallic plectrum called a mizrab.
 
 
 
• **Guitar**
 
 
• The Guitar is a versatile string instrument used in various musical genres worldwide, including Western classical, rock, jazz, and folk music.
 
• It usually has six strings, although there are variations with different numbers of strings.
 
• The Guitar can be played by strumming or plucking the strings, and it is often used for both rhythm and lead parts in music.
 
 
 
• **Dhol**
 
 
• The Dhol is a traditional double-headed drum from the Indian subcontinent, commonly used in Punjabi folk music and Bhangra dance.
 
• It is played with two wooden sticks, with one head producing a high-pitched sound and the other a low-pitched sound.
 
• The Dhol is known for its powerful and lively beats, making it a popular choice for festive and celebratory occasions.

question: Pandit Ram Narayan was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarangi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pandit Ram Narayan is a renowned musician who is credited with popularizing the **Sarangi** as a solo concert instrument in Hindustani classical music.
 
• He was born on December 25, 1927, in Udaipur, Rajasthan, India.
 
• Ram Narayan started his career as an accompanist for vocalists but later became a solo performer, showcasing the versatility and expressive capacity of the Sarangi.
 
• He has received numerous awards and honors for his contribution to Indian classical music, including the Padma Vibhushan in 2005, one of India's highest civilian honors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sarangi**

 
 
• The Sarangi is a bowed, short-necked string instrument from the Indian subcontinent, used primarily in Hindustani classical music.
 
• It is said to most resemble the sound of the human voice, able to imitate vocal ornaments such as gamaks (shakes) and meends (sliding movements).
 
• The Sarangi is typically played while sitting cross-legged, with the instrument held vertically in front of the player.
 
• The instrument is played with a bow, and the main strings are stopped with the cuticles or nails of the left hand, while the other fingers are used to modulate the pitch and resonance.
 
 
 
• **Rudra Veena**
 
 
• The Rudra Veena is a large plucked string instrument used in Hindustani classical music.
 
• It is considered one of the most ancient and revered instruments in Indian music.
 
• The instrument consists of a long tubular body with two large resonating gourds at either end.
 
 
 
• **Sarod**
 
 
• The Sarod is another prominent string instrument used in Hindustani classical music.
 
• It is known for its deep, weighty, introspective sound and is used both for solo performances and as an accompaniment.
 
• The Sarod is played with a plectrum, and the strings are stopped with the nails of the left hand.
 
 
 
• **Mohan Veena**
 
 
• The Mohan Veena is a modified slide guitar used in Indian classical music.
 
• It was popularized by Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt, who won a Grammy Award for his performance with Ry Cooder in "A Meeting by the River".
 
• The instrument is played with a slide, and it combines techniques and sounds from both Indian and Western musical traditions.

question: Which of the following statements best defines Ghana Vadya in the context of Indian traditional music?

options.text: Tuned melodic instruments played with strings and bow
Percussion instruments requiring precise tuning before use
Solid, non-tunable instruments primarily used for rhythm in folk music
Wind instruments made of bamboo or reed used in classical traditions

solution:
The correct answer is __**Solid, non-tunable instruments primarily used for rhythm in folk music**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ghana Vadya** refers to solid, non-tunable instruments used to produce rhythm and percussion in Indian traditional and folk music.
 
• These instruments are primarily made of solid materials like wood, metal, or clay and are struck or shaken to create sound.
 
• Unlike other musical instruments, Ghana Vadya do not require tuning as their sound is determined by the material and shape.
 
• Some prominent examples of Ghana Vadya include **kartal, manjira, ghunghroo, jal tarang, and chimta**, which are widely used in folk and devotional music.
 
• Ghana Vadya instruments are among the oldest types of musical instruments in India and are considered precursors to more complex percussion instruments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The classification of musical instruments in Indian tradition is based on the Natyashastra by Bharat Muni, which categorizes them into four types:
 
 
• Ghana Vadya (solid instruments), Avanaddha Vadya (membrane-covered instruments), Tat Vadya (string instruments), and Sushir Vadya (wind instruments).
 
 
 
• Each category plays a significant role in Indian classical, folk, and devotional music, contributing to the rich and diverse musical heritage of India.

question: Which of the following best describes traditional Rajasthani music?

options.text: Uses electric sounds as the base
Tied to nature, life, and stories

solution:
The correct answer is __**Tied to nature, life, and stories**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Traditional Rajasthani music is deeply connected to the region's nature, daily life, and folklore, reflecting its cultural richness and heritage.
 
• It revolves around the themes of love, valor, devotion, and the natural beauty of Rajasthan, often inspired by the desert landscape.
 
• The music is primarily folk in nature, featuring instruments like the dholak, sarangi, and khartal, which produce earthy, melodious sounds.
 
• Rajasthani music often incorporates storytelling, where singers narrate tales of local heroes, legends, and deities through soulful melodies.
 
• The traditional music has been preserved and passed down orally through generations, primarily by communities like the Manganiyars and Langas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Focuses only on temple rituals**

 
 
• While temple music is an important aspect of Indian traditional music, Rajasthani music extends far beyond temple rituals.
 
• Devotional music like bhajans and chants are a part of the cultural fabric but do not encompass the entirety of Rajasthani music.
 
• The region's music includes a wide variety of forms such as folk songs, dance music, and storytelling traditions.
 
 
 
• **Uses electric sounds as the base**

• Instruments like the ektara, algoza, and morchang are commonly used to produce authentic folk sounds.
 
• Modern adaptations or fusion versions might include electric elements, but these are not part of the traditional music.
 
 
 
• **Known only for classical ragas**

• Classical ragas are performed in royal courts or by highly trained musicians, whereas folk music is more community-oriented and widely practiced.
 
• Both classical and folk traditions coexist, but Rajasthani music is best characterized by its folk roots tied to daily life and oral storytelling.

question: Lavani is a rhythmic and sensual folk dance form from Maharashtra. What is the traditional percussion instrument used to accompany it?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dholki**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 

• **Lavani** is a traditional folk dance and music form that originated in the state of **Maharashtra**, India, and is known for its rhythmic and sensual performances. 

• The primary instrument used to accompany Lavani is the **Dholki**, a double-headed hand drum that provides a vibrant and rhythmic beat to the performance. 

• The **Dholki** is crucial in setting the tempo for Lavani performances and is played with both hands, producing a mix of bass and treble sounds. 

• Lavani performances are characterized by their energetic beats, fast-paced rhythms, and expressive lyrics, which the **Dholki** enhances effectively. 

• Other instruments like the **Manjeera** (cymbals) and **harmonium** may also be used during Lavani performances, but the **Dholki** remains the central percussion instrument. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **Dholki:** 
 

• The **Dholki** is a smaller version of the **Dholak** and is often used in various Indian folk music traditions, including Lavani. 

• It is made of wood and features two drum heads, one for producing bass sounds and the other for treble sounds. 

• The drum is played with both hands, and its portability makes it ideal for folk performances. 
 
 

• **Lavani:** 
 

• **Lavani** combines traditional dance with music and is performed by women wearing **Nauvari sarees** (nine-yard sarees). 

• The themes of Lavani songs often focus on social issues, romance, and political satire, making it both entertaining and thought-provoking. 

• It gained popularity during the **Peshwa era** in the 18th century and continues to be a vital part of Maharashtra's cultural heritage. 
 
 

• **Other Instruments in Lavani:** 
 

• **Manjeera:** Small cymbals used to add rhythm and accentuate beats. 

• **Harmonium:** A keyboard instrument used to provide melodic accompaniment. 

• **Lezim:** A traditional percussion instrument often used in Maharashtrian folk dances. 
 
 

• **Significance of Lavani:** 
 

• Lavani has played a significant role in preserving Maharashtra's folk traditions and continues to be a popular form of entertainment in rural and urban areas. 

• It is performed during festivals and cultural events and is an integral part of Maharashtra's identity. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Regional Impact:** Lavani is not only popular in Maharashtra but also in parts of **Madhya Pradesh** and **Karnataka**. 

• **Performance Style:** The dance is known for its **expressive gestures**, quick footwork, and synchronized movements with the beats of the Dholki. 

• **Modern Adaptations:** Lavani has been adapted into **Bollywood films** and contemporary stage performances, increasing its global recognition.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1:** A gold reliquary with figures in an arcade was found at Bimaran—This is correct. The Bimaran casket, discovered in Afghanistan, is a gold reliquary attributed to the Gandhara art style. It features intricate depictions of Buddha and other figures, showcasing Gandhara's fusion of Hellenistic and Buddhist art.
 
• **Statement 2:** Intricately carved ivory plaques were discovered at Begram—This is also correct. The Begram ivories, excavated from the ancient city of Begram in Afghanistan, are well-known examples of Gandhara art. These carvings reflect a blend of local and foreign artistic traditions, including Indian, Greco-Roman, and Central Asian influences.
 
• The Gandhara art style is renowned for its fusion of Indo-Greek, Roman, and Indian artistic elements, which is evident not only in stone sculptures but also in artifacts such as reliquaries, ivories, and coins.
 
• Both statements collectively highlight the diversity of Gandhara art beyond stone sculptures, emphasizing its influence on various forms of artistic expression.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gandhara Art:**

 
 
• Gandhara art flourished during the Kushan Empire (1st–5th century CE) in the northwestern region of the Indian subcontinent, encompassing parts of modern-day Pakistan and Afghanistan.
 
• It is known for its depiction of Buddhist themes, particularly the life of the Buddha, using techniques and styles influenced by Greco-Roman art.
 
• The use of schist stone, stucco, and metal for sculptures was common, and the art often depicted intricate drapery, realistic facial expressions, and curly hair reminiscent of Hellenistic influences.
 
 
 
• **Artifacts Found at Bimaran:**
 
 
• The Bimaran casket, a notable gold reliquary, is a key example of Gandhara art. It is believed to have contained relics of the Buddha and features exquisite depictions of Buddhist figures in an arcade setting.
 
• This artifact demonstrates the influence of Hellenistic art on Buddhist iconography in the region.
 
 
 
• **Artifacts Found at Begram:**
 
 
• Begram, an ancient city on the Silk Road, yielded a treasure trove of artifacts, including intricately carved ivory plaques, glassware, and coins.
 
• The Begram ivories, in particular, showcase exceptional craftsmanship and provide insights into the cultural exchanges between India, Central Asia, and the Mediterranean during ancient times.

• The Nalanda School drew significant inspiration from the **Sarnath School of Art**, known for its simplicity, elegance, and spiritual themes.

subject: GK
question: Which of the following sculptures does not originate from the Mathura region's Kushana-period artistic production?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bala Buddha of Sultanganj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Bala Buddha of Sultanganj** is a sculpture that does not originate from the **Mathura region's Kushana-period artistic production**.

• It is a famous bronze sculpture from the **Gupta period** (5th–6th century CE) and was discovered in **Sultanganj, Bihar**, not Mathura.

• The other sculptures mentioned in the options, such as the **Katra Keshav Dev fragment**, **Govind Nagar Yaksha**, and the **Standing Buddha from Govindnagar**, are directly linked to the **Mathura school of art** during the Kushana period.

• The Mathura school of art during the Kushana period (1st–3rd century CE) was known for its production of red sandstone sculptures and its unique style of depicting Buddha and other deities.

• The **Bala Buddha of Sultanganj**, being a Gupta-period artifact, showcases a different artistic style and geographical origin, which differentiates it from the Mathura Kushana-period sculptures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Mathura School of Art:**

• It flourished during the **Kushana period (1st–3rd century CE)** and was centered in Mathura, Uttar Pradesh.

• Known for its production of **sculptures in red sandstone**, it depicted Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu deities.

• Key features include the **depiction of Buddha** with a distinctive smile, **spiritual calmness**, and **ornamentation**.

• Examples include the **Standing Buddha from Govindnagar** and the **Govind Nagar Yaksha**.

• **Bala Buddha of Sultanganj:**

• A famous bronze statue from the **Gupta period (5th–6th century CE)**, discovered in Sultanganj, Bihar.

• It is about **2.3 meters tall** and is one of the largest surviving bronze sculptures from ancient India.

• The statue is currently housed in the **Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery** in the United Kingdom.

• It represents the Gupta style of art, which is known for its **refined and graceful depictions of religious figures**.

• **Kushana Art Characteristics:**

• The Kushana period saw the emergence of two major schools of art: the **Mathura school** and the **Gandhara school**.

• The Mathura school focused on **native Indian art traditions**, while the Gandhara school incorporated **Greco-Roman influences**.

• Sculptures from this period are known for their **iconographic innovations** and the introduction of the anthropomorphic form of Buddha.

• **Comparison of Styles:**

• The **Mathura school** is characterized by **red sandstone sculptures** with an emphasis on spirituality and indigenous elements.

• The **Gupta period art**, including the Bala Buddha of Sultanganj, is known for its **refinement, grace, and emphasis on idealized human forms**.

• The Gupta art style marked the culmination of artistic development in ancient India, often referred to as the **Golden Age of Indian Art**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Katra Keshav Dev Fragment:** Belongs to the Mathura school of art and represents the indigenous style of the Kushana period.

• **Govind Nagar Yaksha:** A prominent example of Mathura art that reflects early Kushana-period artistry.

• **Standing Buddha from Govindnagar:** A red sandstone sculpture that embodies the Mathura style's anthropomorphic depiction of Buddha.

• **Bala Buddha of Sultanganj:** A Gupta-period bronze sculpture discovered in Bihar, showcasing advanced metallurgical and artistic techniques.

question: Which of the following statements most accurately describes a key difference between the Mathura and Gandhara schools of art, as broadly understood in Indian architectural history?

options.text: Mathura art primarily used green phyllite, while Gandhara art used spotted red sandstone.
Gandhara art developed on purely indigenous lines, whereas Mathura art showed foreign influences
Mathura art predominantly focused on Buddhist themes, while Gandhara focused on Hindu deities
Mathura art depicted Buddha in an indigenous Yaksha-like style, whereas Gandhara art reflected Hellenistic (Greco-Roman) features.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Mathura art depicted Buddha in an indigenous Yaksha-like style, whereas Gandhara art reflected Hellenistic (Greco-Roman) features.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• **Mathura School of Art** developed during the **Kushan Period** (1st to 3rd century CE) in and around Mathura, Uttar Pradesh. It is characterized by its **indigenous style** of sculpting, which evolved from earlier Yaksha and Yakshi imagery.

• The **Buddha images in Mathura art** have a more **iconic Indian appearance**, depicting him with a smiling face, wide eyes, and a robust physique resembling Yaksha figures. The drapery is closely clinging and transparent.

• **Gandhara School of Art** flourished in the northwestern region of the Indian subcontinent (modern-day Pakistan and Afghanistan), particularly during the **Kushan and Indo-Greek periods**. It is heavily influenced by **Hellenistic (Greco-Roman) artistic traditions.**

• The Buddha images in Gandhara art are marked by **Greco-Roman features**

question: Which of the following best characterizes the Mathura school of Buddhist art and architecture?

options.text: Use of sandstone and floral arches

solution:
The correct answer is __**Indigenous features with Yaksha influence**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Mathura School of Buddhist Art**, which thrived during the Kushan period (1st century CE to 3rd century CE), is characterized by **indigenous artistic traditions** with strong influences of **Yaksha and Yakshi iconography**. 
• Unlike the Gandhara School, which exhibited **Hellenistic features**, the Mathura School evolved from local traditions and prominently displayed **Indian motifs, techniques, and cultural themes**. 
• The Yaksha influence is evident in the **robust and cheerful figures** of Buddha and Bodhisattvas, which were depicted as wearing **simple drapery and adorned with ornaments**. 
• Mathura sculptures were primarily made of **red sandstone**, which was locally available and had a smooth finish. This material contributed to the unique aesthetic of the Mathura art style. 
• Mathura artists developed the concept of **anthropomorphic representations** of Buddha, marking a significant departure from earlier symbolic depictions like stupas or footprints. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Comparison with Gandhara School:** 
• The **Gandhara School**, which developed in present-day Pakistan and Afghanistan, is known for its **Greco-Roman influence**. It used **grey schist stone** and displayed features like curly hair, realistic anatomy, and flowing drapery. 
• In contrast, the Mathura School focused on **Indian traditions** and emphasized cheerful expressions and indigenous themes. 
• **Yaksha Influence in Indian Art:** 
• Yakshas and Yakshis are ancient nature spirits associated with fertility, abundance, and protection. Their statues often depicted **rounded, corpulent figures** with lively expressions. 
• The Mathura School adopted these stylistic features to create Buddha and Bodhisattva figures that emphasized **spiritual vitality**. 
• **Significance of Red Sandstone:** 
• Red sandstone was widely used by Mathura artists due to its **local availability**. The smooth and durable nature of the stone allowed intricate carvings and polished finishes. 
• This material distinguished Mathura sculptures from those of the Gandhara School, which predominantly used grey schist stone. 
• **Evolution of Anthropomorphic Buddha:** 
• The Mathura School played a crucial role in transitioning from symbolic representations of Buddha (like stupas, wheels, or footprints) to **anthropomorphic depictions**. 
• Buddha statues from Mathura often depicted him in a seated or standing posture, with a serene expression and a **halo behind his head**. 
• **Cultural Impact:** 
• The Mathura School influenced later Indian art forms, including the Gupta period, which is considered the **Golden Age** of Indian art and architecture. 
• Its emphasis on indigenous themes and techniques contributed to the **uniquely Indian identity** of Buddhist art. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Historical Context:** 
• The Mathura School flourished under **Kushan rulers**, who were patrons of art and architecture. Their support facilitated the development of Buddhist art in Mathura. 
• Mathura was an important center for religious and cultural activities during this period, contributing to its prominence in artistic innovations. 
• **Examples of Mathura Art:** 
• Iconic Buddha sculptures with distinct features like a **halo, urna (mark on the forehead), and elongated ears**. 
• Yaksha statues and images of Hindu deities, which showcased the versatility of Mathura artists. 
• **Legacy:** 
• The artistic traditions of the Mathura School influenced subsequent developments in Indian art, especially during the **Gupta period**. 
• Its emphasis on indigenous elements established a foundation for the evolution of Indian artistic identity. </ul

question: The story of Maynamati and Gopichandra is a part of which of the following literary works?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nath literature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The story of Maynamati and Gopichandra is a part of Nath literature**__.
 
• Maynamati-Gopichandrer Gan is the story of Queen Maynamati and her husband, Manik Chandra, that propagates yoga guidelines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **Nath Literature**

 
 
• It is a **branch of medieval Bangla literature.**
 
• It is based on the Nath cult or yoga-sadhana.
 
• The main god of the Naths is shiva, who is also called Adinath.
 
• The five Nath siddhas (or enlightened)- Minanath, Goraksanath, Hadipa, Kanupa and Chauranginath, are described as having been born from different parts of the body of Adinath.
 
• Nath literature was of two types, didactic and narrative.
 
• Didactic literature was in the form of doha, prahelika or chara, where secrecy was observed with the abundant use of code words and sentences.
 
• Narrative Nath literature was based on legends and stories about the siddhas. The aim of the stories was to attract people to the cult.

question: Three Poets Pampa, Ponna and Ranna are called as the 'Three Jewels' of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kannada Literature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pampa, Ponna, and Ranna are renowned as the ‘Three Jewels’ (Ratnatraya) of **Kannada literature**.
 
• These poets made significant contributions during the period of Kannada classical literature which is also known as the Old Kannada period.
 
• Pampa is celebrated for his epic works like ‘Adi Purana’ and ‘Vikramarjuna Vijaya’.
 
• Ranna is known for his famous work ‘Sahasa Bhima Vijaya’ or ‘Gadayuddha’.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pampa**

 
 
• Pampa, also known as Adikavi, is one of the earliest poets of Kannada literature.
 
• His significant works include ‘Adi Purana’, which narrates the story of the first Jain Tirthankara Rishabhadeva, and ‘Vikramarjuna Vijaya’, which is a Jain version of the Mahabharata.
 
 
 
• **Ponna**
 
 
• Ponna was another celebrated Kannada poet and a contemporary of Pampa.
 
• He is known for his work ‘Shanti Purana’ which is a Jain epic that narrates the life of Shantinatha, the 16th Tirthankara.
 
 
 
• **Ranna**
 
 
• Ranna is considered one of the greatest Kannada poets.
 
• His notable work ‘Gadayuddha’ (The Battle of Clubs) is a retelling of the Mahabharata focusing on the duel between Bhima and Duryodhana.
 
 
 
• **Kannada Literature**
 
 
• Kannada literature has a rich heritage dating back over a thousand years.
 
• It includes a wide range of texts in poetry, prose, and drama, and is known for its classical and medieval works.
 
• The period of the ‘Three Jewels’ is particularly significant in the history of Kannada literature, often regarded as its golden age.

question: Which of the following is a folk song genre popular in parts of West Bengal, Assam and Bangladesh?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhawaiya.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhawaiya** is a major genre of** folk song **popular throughout the **entire sub-Himalayan belt of northern West Bengal, western Assam and parts of Bangladesh.**
 
• Its origin is drawn from various theatrical and matriarchal ritual folk music traditions.
 
• Bhawaiya has developed into a socially conscious yet lyrical song tradition that is a **mainstay of the culture of the Rajbanshi, Koch and other communities of North Bengal.**
 
• Mostly** written from the perspective of the woman.**
 
• **Songs speak of love not socially mandated but arising unbidden** between men and women thrown together by the vagaries of a marginalized socio-economic existence.
 
• The** woman in a bhawaiya song **is **often a loner, a young widow or a woman in the full bloom of youth** who is yet to find a loving husband.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rekham Pada**

 
 
• ​Rekham Pada is a** folk dance popular in Arunachal Pradesh.**
 
• It is one of the** main dance forms of the Nishi Tribe.**
 
• Both men and women participate in this dance.
 
• Rekham Pada is accompanied by a song, which is sung normally in chorus.
 
• The tribe members dance Rekham Pada during important rituals, during festivals, and also for recreation occasionally.
 
 
 
• **Chalo**
 
 
• **​The Chalo dance is part of Arunachal Pradesh's most awaited festival, called Chalo Loku.**
 
• This festival is a grand celebration in the state and takes place** every year in October and November.**
 
• It is a celebration of the **Nocte tribe.**
 
• The name “Chalo Loku” translates to** paddy cultivation season **in English.
 
 
 
• **Roppi**
 
 
• **​Roppi is one of the popular folk dances of Arunachal Pradesh.**
 
• It is mainly performed by the tribal group of the state.

question: In which of the following dances do dancers balance pots containing lit lamps on their heads?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chari dance.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chari dance is one of the popular folk dances in Rajasthan India.**
 
• In chari dance,** women hold chari or pots on their heads, and a lighted lamp is then placed in the pot.**
 
• The famous** Chari dance belongs to Gujjar community of Kishangarh** and **only women perform in this dance.**
 
• These **ladies carry brass pots on their heads** balancing them to perfection.
 
• These **pots are kept ignited with the cotton seeds dipped in oil.**
 
• These** lit pots display beautiful effects in the dark night.**
 
• This **dance does not have any particular movements **except balancing the pots on their heads.
 
• This dance is also** known as a welcome dance and is a sign of goodness.**
 
• It can also be** considered the traditional fire dance of Rajasthan.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **​​__Dhangari Gaja dance****​**

 
 
• It is a **folk dance of Maharashtra.**
 
• **Dhangari Gaja dance is performed in traditional Marathi dresses - dhoti, angarakha, and pheta with colorful handkerchiefs.** 
 
• The **Dhangars of the Sholapur district of Maharashtra herd in green pastures** for grazing their cattle. 
 
• They become acquainted with nature.
 
• They honor God Biruba once every year when they return home.
 
• They spend their time with their families and beloved ones.
 
• And this is the time when the** Dhangari Gaja dance is performed to please their God for His blessings.**
 
 
 
• **Koli dance​**
 
 
• ​Koli is the** dance form of the Koli fisher folk of Maharashtra.**
 
• The **community has its own distinct identity** and lively dances.
 
• The dance** incorporates elements that this community is most familiar with - sea and fishing.**
 
• The **dance is performed by both men and women** divided into two groups
 
• Fishermen stand in two rows holding oars in their hands.
 
• The dancers move in unison, **portraying the movement of the rowing of a boat.**
 
 
 
• **Tamasha dance​**
 
 
• **Kolhati and Mahar communities are associated with Tamasha.**
 
• Tamasha is** generally started with a devotional song **and is** followed by the dramatic sequence known as 'Gaulan'.**
 
• **Love songs like lavanis are the spirit of Tamasha** and are very much popular.
 
• Musical instruments like:
 
 
• dholki drum, tuntuni (a single string instrument), manjeera cymbals, daf are used to increase the aestheticism of the dance.

__
 
• **Padma Shri awardee, Gulabo Sapera** is a **Kalbelia dancer** of Rajasthan.
 
• The** Kalbelia** are the** tribe of snake charmers** located at the **Thar Desert in Rajasthan**. 
 
• Both **men and women can perform **the Kalbelia dance, which is an essential component of their culture.
 
• The Kalbelia dance is also known as **"Sapera Dance"** and **"Snake Charmer Dance"**.
 
• Beginning in** 2010**, Rajasthan's Kalbelia dance and songs were added to **UNESCO's representative list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**.
 
• At the Kalbelia dance, **men play a variety of traditional instruments as women dance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A prominent form of** folk dance** in the northern Indian state of Rajasthan is **Bhavai**.
 
• During the Bhavai performance, the **male or female performers balance several earthen pots or brass/metal pitchers** while dancing dexterously, **pirouetting and then swaying with the soles of their feet perched on the top of glass bottles**, on the edge of a sword, on the rim of a brass/metal thali or plate and on the broken glass.
 
• The** Kamar tribes** perform the **Tertali or Terah Taali **traditional dance. **Two or three ladies typically perform it while seated** on the ground.
 
• The** Bhil tribe** performs the** Ghoomar or Ghumar**, a traditional Rajasthani folk dance. The dance is **mostly done by veiled ladies wearing the ghaghara**, which are long, flowing dresses.

question: Dekhni is a folk dance associated with which Indian state?
solution:
The correct answer is __Goa.__​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dekhni dance represents an attractive mixture of folk culture and Western music, danced mostly by Christian girls in fully Indian dress.
 
• The gestures in the dance appear to have been borrowed from the Kathak and Bharata Natyam.
 
• Dekhni in Konkani language means bewitching beauty.
 
• Dekhni dance is one of the oldest dance forms of Goa.
 
• Dekhni dance can be associated with those people who converted into Christianity from Hinduism during Portuguese rule.
 
• Dekhni Dance is performed by a group of girls caring earthen oil lamps in their hands.
 
• These girls are represented as the servants of God in this dance form. It represents the life of a devadasi.
 
• Ghumat Drum is the main instrument used in this dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hanv Saiba Poltodi Vetam is one of the most famous songs of Dekni dance.
 
• It was written by Carlos Eugenio Ferreira.
 
• This song was first published in 1895 in Paris and then in Goa in 1926.
 
• This song talks about a dancer who wanted to cross the river but the boatman refused to take her because the river was very rough that day.

• There's no school or written lessons for this dance. The knowledge is shared by talking and showing to the next generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhavai**:-

 
 
• **Bhavai is a traditional, popular folk theatre form of the Indian state of Gujarat. **
 
• It is used as a medium to convey social messages and entertain audiences in villages and towns.
 
• Bhavai performances involve numerous acts, known as "veshas", depicting popular tales from Indian mythology, history, and contemporary social and political scenarios.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paika:- **

 
 
• The term "Paika" comes from the Odia word 'Paika', which means 'fighter' or 'warrior'.
 
• The Paikas were the traditional landed militia of Odisha, found in particular in the districts of Khurdha, Puri, and Cuttack.
 
• They served as warriors for the local kings or regional rulers, and in times of peace, they worked primarily as farmers.
 
 
 
• **Ghumra:-**
 
 
• **It **is a folk dance form native to the Indian state of Odisha, particularly prevalent in the Kalahandi district.
 
• Known for its rhythmic, energetic movements and beats, Ghumura dance draws its name from the Ghumura instrument, which is an earthen terracotta pot with both ends open, played by strapping it to the chest and beaten with two sticks.
 
 
 
• **Dhap:-**
 
 
• It is a folk dance form indigenous to the Mayurbhanj district of Odisha, India.
 
• This dance form was traditionally performed by the Kshatriya community (the warrior class in the traditional Indian caste structure), symbolizing the spirit of martial traditions and chivalry.

• It is primarily performed in the central part of Kerala, especially in the Pathanamthitta district.
 
• The dance is performed to please Goddess Bhadrakali, a fierce form of the Goddess Kali.
 
• Padayani is known for its elaborate and colorful costumes, masks, and energetic performances.

• **Padayani**

 
 
• Padayani, also spelled Padeni, is a ceremonial dance performed in Bhadrakali temples in Kerala.
 
• It is a combination of music, dance, theatre, satire, facial masks, and paintings.
 
• The term Padayani literally means "rows of warriors" and represents the martial traditions of the region.
 
• Padayani is performed during the festival season, particularly in the Malayalam months of Kumbham and Meenam (February to April).
 
• The performers wear huge masks known as "Kolams" which are traditionally made of areca nut tree sheaths, and they depict various characters including gods, goddesses, and spirits.
 
• The dance is accompanied by the rhythmic beats of the "Chenda" (drum) and "Ilathalam" (cymbals).
 
 
 
• **Goddess Bhadrakali**
 
 
• Bhadrakali is a Hindu goddess popular in Southern India, particularly in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
 
• She is considered a fierce and powerful form of the goddess Kali, associated with the destruction of evil and protection of the good.
 
• Bhadrakali is worshipped for her protective and benevolent qualities, and is often depicted with multiple arms, holding various weapons, and riding a lion.
 
• Various rituals and ceremonies, including Padayani, are performed to honor and seek blessings from Goddess Bhadrakali.

solution:

__
 
• **Paika Nritya** is a traditional war dance originating from the state of Odisha, India. It is performed by the Paika community, who were historically warriors.
 
• The performance comprises four segments, showcasing the warrior spirit and martial skills through a structured sequence of movements and actions.
 
• The sequence starts with **Blowing the war conch (shankha)**, symbolizing the announcement of war or the beginning of the performance.
 
• Next, the performers engage in **Shield-sword sparring drills**, demonstrating their martial prowess and ability to handle weapons.
 
• The third segment involves **Acrobatic somersaults**, highlighting the agility and physical strength of the performers.
 
• Finally, the performance concludes with a **Group victory shout of "Jai Jagannath"**, signifying triumph and devotion to Lord Jagannath.
 
• The segments are performed in the precise sequence of **1-2-3-4**, maintaining the traditional structure and flow of the dance. This format is widely recognized and followed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Paika Nritya** has its roots in Odisha’s cultural history, with the Paika warriors playing a significant role in resisting colonial forces during pre-independence India.
 
• The dance was traditionally performed to celebrate military victories and instill courage among soldiers.
 
 
 
• **Symbolism:**
 
 
• The **war conch** symbolizes the call to battle and spiritual awakening, as conches are considered auspicious in Hindu culture.
 
• **Shield-sword sparring drills** reflect historical battle practices, showcasing the combat readiness of the warriors.
 
• **Acrobatic somersaults** highlight the physical fitness and agility required in warfare.
 
• The **victory shout**, "Jai Jagannath," demonstrates devotion to Lord Jagannath, the presiding deity of Odisha, and celebrates the triumph of good over evil.
 
 
 
• **Performance Style:**
 
 
• The dance is performed in a vibrant and energetic style, with traditional costumes, including turbans, dhotis, and decorative shields and swords.
 
• Musical instruments like the conch, drums, and cymbals accompany the dance, creating a rhythmic backdrop.
 
 
 
• **Significance in Odisha:**
 
 
• **Paika Nritya** is an integral part of Odisha’s cultural heritage and is performed during festivals and cultural events.
 
• It serves as a reminder of the bravery and sacrifices of the Paika warriors in Odisha’s history.

• **Thoda** is a traditional martial art form originating from the state of **Himachal Pradesh**, India. It is believed to have roots in ancient warfare techniques practiced in the region.

• The practice of Thoda involves **precision, agility, and coordination**. Fighters aim to showcase their skills by hitting specific targets on their opponent's body while avoiding being hit themselves.

• The state is rich in **mineral resources** and is one of the leading producers of steel and electricity in India. 
• **Pandwani Style:** 
• The **Vedamati style** of Pandwani is more focused on narration, with the performer singing and reciting verses while playing a tambura. 
• The **Kapalika style** involves dramatic performances, with the narrator enacting scenes from the Mahabharata, making it more engaging and theatrical.

• Pandwani emphasizes **oral tradition**, preserving the stories of the Mahabharata for generations.

• **Musical Instruments:** Traditional instruments like the **tambura** (a string instrument) and **manjira** (small cymbals) are essential to Pandwani performances.

• The performance is primarily based on **mythological stories** and **epics** such as the **Ramayana** and **Mahabharata**.

question: A Hindu festival celebrated by the Tamil community that falls in the Tamil Solar Month is called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Thaipusam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thaipusam** is an important festival celebrated by the Hindus of southern India during the Tamil month of Thai (January - February). Outside of India, it is observed mainly by the Tamil-speaking community settled in Malaysia, Singapore, South Africa, Sri Lanka and elsewhere around the world.
 
• Thaipusam is devoted to the Hindu god **Murugan**, the son of Shiva and Parvati.
 
• **Murugan **is also known as **Karttikeya**, **Subrahmanya**, Shadanana, Skanda and Guha.
 
• It is believed that on this day, Goddess Parvati offered a lance to Lord Murugan to defeat the demon army of Tarakasura and combat their evil deeds. Therefore, Thaipusam is a celebration of the victory of good over evil.
 
• In **Singapore**, the festival is celebrated with a chariot procession that begins at the **Sri Srinivasa Perumal Temple **at 397 Serangoon Road in the Little India district.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Karaga**

 
 
• The Karaga festival is held at the **Dharmaraya Swamy Temple** in **Bangalore**.
 
• During Mahabharata, Draupadi, wife of five Pandavas made several Veera Kumaras (brave sons) to form a mini army and conquer the demon Timirasura. At the time of her death, these Veera Kumaras begged Draupadi not to leave them. Draupadi instead promised to return each year during the full moon day of Chaitra masa (month). Karaga festival is celebrated each year to mark the return of Draupadi in the form of Adishakti.
 
 
 
• **Bihu**
 
 
• It is the soul of **Assam **and is celebrated across the state with enormous zeal and enthusiasm.
 
• There are **three Bihu** festivals namely ‘**Bohag Bihu**’ celebrated in the month of ‘Bohag’ (Baisakh, the middle of **April**), ‘**Magh Bihu**’ observed in the month of ‘Magh’ (the middle of **January**), and **‘Kati Bihu**’ celebrated in the month of ‘Kati’ (Kartik, the middle of **October**).
 
 
 
• **Onam**
 
 
• The festival of Onam is celebrated all over the state of Kerala. Kerala during Onam is marked by happiness, excitement and enjoyment among all sections of people.
 
• Onam is marked as an outcome of reasons that have to do with mythology as well as old agrarian practices.

• Fasting during the month of** Ramadan** is one of the most significant Islamic practices, and it is one of the most important festivals observed by Muslims worldwide.
 
• One of the** five pillars of Islam** is the Ramadan fast.
