question: Which of the following is a festival of merriment and heralds the Assamese New Year and the onset of spring?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bohag Bihu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Bohag Bihu, also known as the** Rongali Bihu**, is a joyous festival that marks the start of spring and the** Assamese New Yea**r.
 
• Assam celebrates **Bihu, Baishagu, Ali-Ai-Ligang, Baikho, Rongker, and Rajini Gabra as its important holidays. Bohaggiyo Bishu, Jonbill Mela, Ambubashi Mela, and others include Harni Gabra.**
 
• The most well-known** Bihu**, Bohag Bihu (mid-April; also known as Rongali Bihu), marks the beginning of the Assamese New Year (**about 14–15 April**) and the arrival of spring.
 
• On April 14th of every year, the Indian state of Assam observes a regional public holiday known as Bohag Bihu.
 
• Depending on the day of the week it falls on, a number of days of public holidays may be announced, and occasionally it is also a public holiday in the neighbouring state of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• This national holiday, also known as Rongali Bihu, is celebrated in Assam, one of India's most picturesque states noted for its tea gardens, verdant forests, and the Brahmaputra River.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "Garu Bihu" is the name given to the** first day** of the **Bihu**.
 
• On this day, folks bathe and pray for the health and safety of their home cattle while they take them to the river for a bath.
 
• People take a turmeric-based bath on **"Manuh Bihu," the second day **of Bihu.
 
• Families eat a variety of larus or laddus and pithas, or rice cakes.
 
• People visit neighbours and family members during Bihu celebrations to say hello to one another and show their respect for the **family's elders** by giving them a fresh "**Gamosa**" (a traditional Assamese hand-woven cotton towel with red designs with a white background).
 
• **Ali-ai-ligang:**
 
 
• **​**The** Mising or Mishing tribal people of Assam **and other** Northeast Indian states** celebrate Ali-Aye-Ligang or Ali-Ai-Ligang, a spring festival related with agriculture, on the occasion of the start of the **Ahu paddy cultivation.**
 
• The celebration signifies the beginning of seeding.
 
• Three words make up the festival's name: **"Ali" (legumes), "Aye" (seed), and "Ligang" (sow)**.
 
• On the first Wednesday of Phalguna, the **12th month of the Hindu calendar**, the festival gets underway.
 
 
 
• **Me-Dum-Me-Phi: **
 
 
• **​**Mae Dam Mae Phi is a significant event that the **Tai-Ahom** have celebrated since** very early times**.
 
• "Me" is an offering word. Both **"Dam" and "Phi" refer to the gods**.
 
• Hence, "Mae Dam Mae Phi" refers to** sacrifices** made to the **spirits of the ancestors**.
 
 
 
• **Kati Bihu:**
 
 
• **​**On the first day of the Assamese calendar's "**Kati" month**, which often falls in the middle of October, Kati Bihu is observed. It falls on October 18 this year.
 
• The celebration heralds the shifting of the **rice crop** and the start of the season of new harvest.
 
• An observation of service, penance, and the** desire for a better future**, Kati Bihu.
 
• Despite the fact that each **Assamese tribe** has its own customs and celebrations of the day, the event is observed throughout the entire state of Assam.
 
• Outside the houses, **lamps** are lit, and a **bamboo path** is built as a trail for the ancestors.

• Hundred Drum Festival also known as the 'Wangala Festival, the Wangala Festival is a traditional festival in the northeastern Indian state of Meghalaya.
 
• A group of 30 dancers with 10 drums would form a group and 10 such groups will be there. 
 
• Thus, a total of 100 drummers and 300 dancers make up what is now known as the “100 Drums Wangala Festival”.
 
• Every year the festival is celebrated for 3 days during the month of November.
 
• Ordinary Garo people pay gratitude and reverence to Missi Saljong or 'Pattigipa Ra'Rongipa' (Great Giver) for blessing humans with a prosperous harvest for the season.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• It is also celebrated in honour of the Sun God that marks the end of the long harvest season.
 
• Wangala is celebrated with different forms of dance.
 
• These dances are performed on the tunes of folk songs that are played on drums and primitive flute.
 
• Additionally, these flutes are made of buffalo horns.
 
• On the first day of the festival, people celebrate it with a ceremony called Ragula.
 
• This ceremony is performed in the house of the village’s chief.
 
• Then on the second day of celebration, which is called Kakkat, people begin the ceremony by dancing to the rhythms of long oval-shaped drums
 
• In this celebration, young and old join together while men play the drums and women perform traditional dance forms. The dance form is known as Dama Dagota.​

question: Guru Purnima, a festival celebrated by Hindus, Jains and Buddhists in India falls in which month of Hindu calendar?
solution:
the correct answer is __**Ashadha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Guru Purnima

 
 
• Guru Purnima is a significant Hindu festival celebrated in honor of the spiritual gurus, mentors, and teachers in one's life. 
 
• The festival falls on the full moon day or Purnima of the Hindu month of Ashadha (June-July in the Gregorian calendar). 
 
• The word 'Guru' is derived from the Sanskrit language and means 'teacher' or 'guide,' while 'Purnima' means 'full moon day'. 
 
• It is believed that Guru Purnima is the day when the great sage Vyasa, who is considered the Adi Guru or the first Guru in Hinduism, was born.
 
• Therefore, the day is also known as Vyasa Purnima. 
 
• The festival is celebrated across India, Nepal, and Bhutan with great enthusiasm and devotion.
 
• Devotees offer puja (worship) to their gurus, seek their blessings, and express their gratitude by presenting them with gifts, sweets, and flowers. 
 
• Guru Purnima also holds great significance in the Buddhist and Jain traditions.
 
• In Buddhism, the day is celebrated as the day when the Lord Buddha gave his first sermon to his disciples at Sarnath. 
 
• In the Jain tradition, the day is celebrated as the day when Lord Mahavira, the last Tirthankara, made Indrabhuti Gautam his first disciple. 
 
• Overall, Guru Purnima is a day to express gratitude and reverence towards one's spiritual and academic gurus, and seek their blessings for a fulfilling and meaningful life spiritual growth.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Hindu calendar, also known as the **Vikram Samvat calendar**, is a lunisolar calendar used in Hinduism, with many variations regionally.
 
• It is based on the movement of the Moon and the Sun, and its months are based on the lunar cycles. 
 
• The calendar begins in the month of Chaitra, which usually falls in March or April in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• Here are the months of the **Hindu calendar **with their corresponding **Gregorian calendar months**:
 
• Chaitra - **March/April**
 
• Vaisakha -** April/May**
 
• Jyaistha - **May/June**
 
• Asadha - **June/July**
 
• Sravana - **July/August**
 
• Bhadra - **August/September**
 
• Asvina - **September/October**
 
• Kartika - **October/November**
 
• Agrahayana - **November/December**
 
• Pausa - **December/January**
 
• Magha - **January/February**
 
• Phalguna - **February/March**
 
• **Note:**
 
 
• **Please note that the dates of the Hindu calendar vary from year to year as they are based on the positions of the Moon and the Sun**.

• It is a common bird among the folklores and tribes of Nagaland.
 
 

 
• Ambubachi Mela:

 
 
• It is celebrated at Kamakhya Temple in the month of June.
 
• It is one of the biggest congregations in eastern India.
 
• It is the belief that Kamakhya embodies the mother cult, the Shakti.
 
• The meaning of Ambubachi is* spoken with water.*

• Known as the '100 Drum Festival', the Wangala Festival is a traditional festival in the northeastern Indian state of Meghalaya.
 
• The festival kicked off on November 12th, 2021.
 
• The festival lasts from two days to a week. 
 
• It is one of the most important festivals of the Garo Tribe.
 
• The tribesmen make sacrifices to please their god Saljong.

question: Nag Panchami is celebrated in which month of Hindu Calendar?

__
 
• **Nag Panchami **is a **Hindu festival** dedicated to the **worship of snakes**, which is celebrated on the** fifth day of the bright half **of the** lunar month of Shravan.**
 
• The festival is celebrated in various parts of India, especially in states like **Maharashtra, Karnataka, West Bengal, and Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• It is believed that **worshipping snakes** on this day will bring** good luck and prosperity** to the family.
 
• People offer** milk, flowers, and sweets** to the idols of snakes and also visit** temples** dedicated to **Nagas (the serpent deities).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• In some regions, people also observe a** fast on Nag Panchami **and break it after **offering prayers** to the snakes.
 
• In **West Bengal,** the festival is celebrated as** Manasa Puja**, dedicated to the goddess of **snakes, Manasa Devi.**
 
• In **Maharashtra,** people decorate their homes with **rangoli **and offer a special dish called '**kanda bhaji'** to the snakes.
 
• **Kartik** is the** eighth month **of the Hindu calendar, which usually falls in **October-November.**
 
 
• It is known for several festivals like **Diwali, Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj.**
 
 
 
• **Sharad** is the season of **autumn**, which falls between **September and November**.
 
 
• It is known for festivals like **Navratri, Durga Puja, and Vijayadashami.**
 
 
 
• **Asadh** is the 4th month of the Hindu calendar, which usually falls in **June-July**.
 
 
• It is known for the beginning of the** monsoon season** and several **agricultural festivals.**

subject: GK
question: This event is celebrated to mark the resurrection of Christ. Identify the event.
solution:
The correct answer is Easter.

 
 

 Event
 Explanation
 
 
 
 

 Easter
 - Easter is a major Christian holiday celebrating the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead, as described in the New Testament of the Bible.

 - It symbolizes the triumph of life over death and holds central importance in Christian theology.

 - Observed on the first Sunday after the first full moon following the vernal equinox, usually falling between March 22 and April 25.

 - Easter Sunday marks the culmination of the season of Lent, a period of fasting, prayer, and reflection.
 
 

 Christmas
 - Christmas commemorates the birth of Jesus Christ, the central figure of Christianity.

 - Celebrated on December 25th (in most Christian traditions), it holds both religious and cultural significance.

 - The holiday includes traditions such as decorating trees, exchanging gifts, and festive gatherings.

 - It marks the incarnation of Jesus, emphasizing the belief that God became human to save humanity.
 
 

 Holy Thursday
 - Also known as Maundy Thursday, it falls on the Thursday before Easter Sunday.

 - Commemorates the Last Supper of Jesus Christ with his disciples, where he instituted the Eucharist (Holy Communion).

 - "Maundy" originates from the Latin word "mandatum," referring to Jesus' commandment to love one another.

 - Some Christian denominations practice foot washing ceremonies to symbolize humility and service, as Jesus washed his disciples' feet.
 
 

 Good Friday
 - Good Friday is observed on the Friday before Easter Sunday, commemorating the crucifixion and death of Jesus Christ.

 - It's a solemn day of reflection, fasting, and church services focusing on Jesus' sacrifice for humanity.

 - In many Christian traditions, no Mass or Communion is celebrated on Good Friday.

 - It's a day of mourning, emphasizing the somber aspect of the Easter story before the joyous celebration of the resurrection.

question: During which festival is Garba performed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Navratri.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Navratri **typically involves the **worship of the goddess Durga**, commemorated in nine different forms over the course of the festival.
 
• **Garba** is a popular folk dance native to** Gujarat**, a state in western India.
 
• Its performance is central to** Navratri celebrations in Gujarat **and is now popular all over India and among Indian communities worldwide.
 
• **Beyond Navratri,** Garba is also performed during **other special occasions **in Gujarat, indicating its cultural importance.
 
• The tradition of Garba, along with another dance form called **Raas,** is also being promoted to wider audiences, demonstrating the cultural heritage of Gujarat and fostering community ties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pongal:**

 
 
• Pongal is a major** harvest festival **celebrated in **Tamil Nadu**, a southern state in India. It typically falls in **mid-January**.
 
• The festival is named after the Tamil word **"pongal,"** which means **"to boil over,"** symbolizing **prosperity and abundance.**
 
• It is traditionally marked by cooking a special dish called 'Pongal' - made from **newly-harvested rice boiled in milk with jaggery**.
 
 
 
• **Diwali:**
 
 
• Diwali, also known as **Deepavali,** is a major Hindu festival celebrated by millions worldwide.
 
• Known as the **"festival of lights," **it symbolizes the triumph of light over darkness and good over evil.
 
• The festival involves** lighting lamps and fireworks, decorating homes, feasting on sweets, and exchanging gifts.**
 
 
 
• **Bihu:**
 
 
• Bihu is a set of three important cultural festivals celebrated in **Assam,** a northeastern state in India.
 
• These festivals, celebrated throughout the year, mark the changing seasons and are **significant for agriculture.**
 
• The most recognized Bihu, Rongali Bihu, celebrates the onset of the **Assamese New Year **and the spring season.
 
• Bihu dance and music are integral parts of the celebrations, and these have become emblematic of Assamese culture.

question: Which of the following states recognise the Dahi Handi as a sports event?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dahi Handi is recognised as an adventure sport in the state of Maharashtra, India.
 
• This decision was taken by the Maharashtra government to ensure the safety regulations are adhered to during the event, as it involves forming a human pyramid which often leads to the possibility of injuries.
 
• The sport is traditionally played during the celebration of Janmashtami, the birthday of Lord Krishna, reflecting his childhood mischief of stealing curd and butter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Event Name
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Dahi Handi
 Associated with Krishna Janmashtami, this event involves forming a pyramid of people to break a pot hung high in the air, mirroring the antics of Lord Krishna in his youth. This event is particularly popular in Maharashtra.
 
 

 Jallikattu
 Conducted during Pongal celebrations in Tamil Nadu, Jallikattu is a bull-taming event. It's a part of the centuries-old Tamil cultural heritage.
 
 

 Rath Yatra Chariot Race
 This event occurs during the Ratha Yatra, a public procession with chariots of deities, primarily held in Odisha, dedicated to Lord Jagannath (Lord Krishna), his sister Subhadra, and his elder brother Balabhadra (Balarama).
 
 

 Sikh Games or Gatka
 Gatka is a traditional martial art associated with Sikhism, often performed during religious processions. It is also competitively performed in an arena in tournaments and events known as Sikh games.
 
 

 Onam Boat Races
 These races are a part of Onam celebrations in Kerala. Snake boats (Chundan Vallam) and other types of traditional boats participate in these exhilarating races. The most famous among them is the Nehru Trophy Boat Race.
 
 

 Rural Olympics in Kila Raipur
 This sports festival is held annually in Kila Raipur (near Ludhiana) in Punjab, featuring rural sports like cart-racing, tug-of-war, and feats of strength and agility. Though not directly religious, it is deeply interconnected with Punjabi and Sikh culture.

question: Lathmar Holi is primarily celebrated in the state of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Lathmar Holi** is a unique and traditional form of Holi celebration primarily observed in the towns of **Barsana and Nandgaon** in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• This festival is celebrated a few days before the main Holi festival and involves women playfully beating men with sticks, hence the name 'Lathmar' which translates to 'beating with sticks'.
 
• The celebration is rooted in the legend of **Radha and Krishna**, where Krishna visited Radha's village and teased her and her friends, leading to the women chasing him away with sticks.
 
• The festival attracts numerous tourists and devotees who come to witness and participate in the vibrant and joyful celebrations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Holi Festival**

 
 
• Holi, also known as the 'Festival of Colors', is an ancient Hindu festival celebrated predominantly in India and Nepal.
 
• The festival signifies the victory of good over evil, the arrival of spring, and the end of winter. It also serves as a thanksgiving for a good harvest.
 
• The celebrations begin with a Holika bonfire on the night before Holi, where people gather, sing, dance, and perform rituals.
 
• The following day is celebrated with vibrant colors, water balloons, and traditional sweets. It is a day of festivity and joy, bringing people together to forgive and forget past grievances.
 
 
 
• **Radha and Krishna**
 
 
• Radha and Krishna are central figures in Hindu mythology and are considered the epitome of divine love.
 
• Krishna, an incarnation of Lord Vishnu, is known for his playful and mischievous nature, while Radha symbolizes the ultimate devotee and beloved of Krishna.
 
• Their love story is celebrated in various cultural and religious contexts, including dance, music, and festivals like Holi.
 
• The stories of their divine love have inspired countless artistic and literary works in Indian culture.
 
 
 
• **Braj Region**
 
 
• Braj, also known as Brij or Braj Bhoomi, is a region in Uttar Pradesh associated with the childhood and youthful pastimes of Lord Krishna.
 
• It includes important pilgrimage sites like Mathura, Vrindavan, Govardhan, Gokul, and Barsana.
 
• The region is known for its rich cultural heritage, including traditional music, dance, and festivals dedicated to Krishna.
 
• Braj attracts millions of devotees and tourists annually, making it a significant religious and cultural destination in India.

question: Which of the following celebrations is dedicated to Sun God and his wife Usha to thank them for sustaining life on earth and for granting wishes?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Chhath Puja__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chhath is predominantly a Hindu festival dedicated to the Sun god and his wife Usha with the motive of thanking them for providing the bounties of life on the Earth.
 
• The literal meaning of the word chhath is sixth and hence, this festival is celebrated on the sixth day of the Kartika month of the Hindu calendar "Vikram Samvat".
 
• The festival has a duration of four days. The rituals under this festival include a holy bath, keeping the fast, remaining in water for long periods of time, along with offering prayers and food to the setting sun and the rising sun.
 
• The main worshipers are known as Parvaitin,(usually women). Although, it's seen that sometimes men also observe this festival as it is essentially not a gender-specific festival.
 
• The festival is observed primarily in Mithila Province of Nepal, Terai-Madhesh region of Nepal along with the Indian states of Bihar, Jharkhand, and UP.
 
• Moreover, it is also observed in areas where migrants from the above-mentioned areas have their presence. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Madai Festival**

 
 
• The Madai Festival is celebrated primarily by the Gond tribes of Madhya Pradesh and is a significant cultural event that showcases their rich traditions and heritage.
 
• It typically involves vibrant rituals, traditional dance forms, music, and communal feasting, reflecting the community's connection to nature and agriculture.
 
• The festival usually marks the harvesting season and is a time for the tribes to give thanks for the bounty received.
 
 
 
• **Vishwakarma Puja**
 
 
• Vishwakarma Puja is dedicated to Lord Vishwakarma, the divine architect and craftsman of the universe, celebrated by artisans, builders, and craftsmen across India.
 
• This festival often includes the worship of tools, machinery, and vehicles, symbolizing the reverence for craftsmanship and engineering skills.
 
• The Puja is marked by colorful decorations, offerings, and cultural performances, emphasizing creativity and innovation in various trades.
 
 
 
• **Sorath Sabha**
 
 
• Sorath Sabha refers to a cultural and social gathering primarily associated with the Rajput community, particularly in the Sorath region of Gujarat.
 
• These gatherings promote community bonding, sharing of cultural traditions, and discussions on social issues, fostering a sense of unity among members.
 
• The Sabha often features traditional music, dance, and storytelling, highlighting the rich history and heritage of the Rajput community.

question: ‘Sangken’ is a festival celebrated in Arunachal Pradesh by people of which of the following religions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Buddhism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Buddhism**

 
 
• Gautama Buddha, variously termed Sakyamuni or Tathagata, is considered as the founder of Buddhism.
 
• He was born as Siddhartha to Suddhodhana, the ruler of the Sakyan republic, and his wife Maya, on Vaisakha Purnima in the Lumbini gardens near Kapilavasthu (in Nepal) in the 6th century BC.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jainism**

 
 
• Jainism is one of the world’s oldest living religions.
 
• Jainism grounds itself in 24 Tirthankaras.
 
• A ‘Tirthankara’, is the one who revealed religious truth at different times.
 
• The first Tirthankara was Rishabhadev.
 
• The last and 24th tirthankara of the Jainas was Mahaveer Swami or Vardhamana Mahavira.
 
• Jainism gained prominence under the aegis of Mahavira, during the sixth century BC.
 
• He was a kshatriya prince of the Lichchhavis, a group that was part of the Vajji sangha.
 
• At the age of thirty, he left home and went to live in a forest.
 
• For twelve years he led a hard and lonely life, at the end of which he attained enlightenment.
 
• The followers of Mahavira were known as Jainas.
 
• The teachings of Mahavira and his followers were transmitted orally for several centuries.
 
• 
 
They were written down in the form in which they are presently available at a place called Valabhi, in Gujarat, about 1500 years ago.

question: Shab-e-Barat is celebrated by which religious group?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Muslim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shab-e-Barat is a significant Islamic observance that is celebrated by Muslims around the world.
 
• It is observed on the night between the 14th and 15th day of the Islamic month of Sha'ban.
 
• Muslims believe that on this night, God writes the destinies of all individuals for the coming year and forgives the sins of those who seek forgiveness.
 
• It is a night of prayer, reflection, and seeking forgiveness, often involving staying awake all night in devotion and worship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sha'ban**

 
 
• Sha'ban is the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar.
 
• It is considered a significant month for Muslims as it precedes the holy month of Ramadan.
 
• Many Muslims fast during this month and increase their worship in preparation for Ramadan.
 
 
 
• **Islamic Calendar**
 
 
• The Islamic calendar, also known as the Hijri calendar, is a lunar calendar consisting of 12 months in a year of 354 or 355 days.
 
• The calendar is used to determine the proper days of Islamic holidays and rituals, such as the annual period of fasting and the proper time for the pilgrimage to Mecca.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Prayer in Islam**
 
 
• Prayer, or Salah, is one of the Five Pillars of Islam, which are the foundation of a Muslim's faith and practice.
 
• It is a physical, mental, and spiritual act of worship that is observed five times every day at prescribed times.
 
• Prayers are performed facing the Kaaba in Mecca, and include specific recitations and movements.
 
 
 
• **Seeking Forgiveness in Islam**
 
 
• Seeking forgiveness, or Istighfar, is an important concept in Islam.
 
• Muslims believe that God is Merciful and Forgiving, and they regularly seek forgiveness for their sins and shortcomings.
 
• This practice is especially emphasized during significant nights such as Shab-e-Barat.

question: Gangaur Festival, Pushkar Fair, Nagaur Fair and Urs Fair are the popular fairs and festivals of which state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rajasthan is renowned for its vibrant cultural heritage and hosts numerous traditional fairs and festivals.
 
• The Gangaur Festival is celebrated primarily by women to honor the goddess Gauri, the consort of Lord Shiva, and is marked by elaborate processions and rituals.
 
• Pushkar Fair, also known as the Pushkar Camel Fair, is one of the largest camel and livestock fairs in the world and attracts thousands of tourists.
 
• The Urs Fair, held at Ajmer, commemorates the death anniversary of the Sufi saint Moinuddin Chishti and is a significant event for followers of Sufism and Islam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gangaur Festival**

 
 
• This festival is particularly significant in the state of Rajasthan and parts of Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It is dedicated to Gauri, a manifestation of Goddess Parvati, celebrating marital fidelity and conjugal happiness.
 
• Women dress in their finest clothes and jewelry, sing traditional songs, and take part in processions carrying beautifully decorated idols of Gauri.
 
 
 
• **Pushkar Fair**
 
 
• The Pushkar Fair is an annual multi-day livestock fair held in the town of Pushkar, Rajasthan.
 
• It is one of India's largest camel, horse, and cattle fairs, combined with various other events and competitions, such as the "matka phod," "longest mustache," and "bridal competition."
 
• The fair also includes cultural performances, folk dances, and music, making it a major tourist attraction.
 
 
 
• **Nagaur Fair**
 
 
• The Nagaur Fair, also known as the Ramdeoji Cattle Fair, is held annually in the town of Nagaur, Rajasthan.
 
• It is the second-largest cattle fair in India, where animals like camels, cows, bullocks, and horses are traded.
 
• The fair is also famous for its traditional folk music, dance performances, and various local sports and activities.
 
 
 
• **Urs Fair**
 
 
• The Urs Fair is held annually at the Dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti in Ajmer, Rajasthan.
 
• This event marks the death anniversary of the saint, which is celebrated with great fervor by his followers.

The correct answer is __**Lord Jagannath**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rath Yatra of Puri is dedicated to **Lord Jagannath**, who is considered a form of Lord Vishnu.
 
• This annual festival involves a grand procession where the deities are taken out of the Jagannath Temple and placed in chariots, symbolizing their journey to their aunt's house.
 
• The festival is celebrated with much pomp and grandeur, attracting millions of devotees from across the world.
 
• The festival generally occurs in the month of June or July, based on the Hindu lunar calendar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Jagannath:**

 
 
• Lord Jagannath is a deity worshipped primarily in the Indian state of Odisha.
 
• He is considered a form of Lord Vishnu, and is also identified with Krishna and Buddha.
 
• The Jagannath Temple in Puri is one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites, which are considered very sacred by Hindus.
 
• The temple is famous for its annual Rath Yatra, or chariot festival, in which the three main deities are pulled on huge and elaborately decorated temple cars.
 
 
 
• **Rath Yatra:**
 
 
• The Rath Yatra involves the transportation of deities on large chariots from the Jagannath Temple to the Gundicha Temple, which is about 3 kilometers away.
 
• The three deities—Lord Jagannath, his brother Balabhadra, and sister Subhadra—are taken out in three separate chariots.
 
• The chariots are pulled by thousands of devotees who consider it an auspicious act.
 
• The festival lasts for nine days, and the return journey of the deities is known as Bahuda Yatra.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The Rath Yatra symbolizes the journey of Lord Jagannath along with his siblings to their maternal aunt's house.
 
• It represents the idea of the divine coming down to meet the devotees, breaking the barriers of the temple.
 
• The festival promotes the spirit of brotherhood and unity among people, irrespective of their caste or creed.

__
 
• The Chariot Festival, also known as Rath Yatra, is primarily celebrated in the city of Puri in Odisha, India.
 
• It is dedicated to Lord Jagannath, who is considered a form of Lord Krishna, along with his siblings Subhadra and Balabhadra (also known as Balarama).
 
• Balabhadra is the elder brother of Lord Jagannath and Subhadra, and he is often depicted with a plough in his hand, symbolizing agriculture and strength.
 
• The festival involves the procession of deities in chariots, pulled by devotees through the streets, symbolizing the journey of Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra from their temple to their garden temple in the countryside.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Rath Yatra is one of the oldest and largest chariot festivals in the world, attracting millions of devotees and tourists from all over the globe.
 
• It is celebrated annually on the second day of the bright fortnight of the month of Ashadha (June-July).
 
• The three deities, Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra, are taken out in a grand procession from their temple in Puri to the Gundicha Temple, which is considered their aunt's house.
 
• The return journey of the deities to the Jagannath Temple is known as Bahuda Yatra.
 
 
 
• **Lord Jagannath:**
 
 
• Lord Jagannath is a form of Lord Vishnu and is primarily worshipped in the state of Odisha.
 
• He is known for his large, round eyes and is often depicted without limbs.
 
• The Jagannath Temple in Puri is one of the four major Hindu pilgrimage sites in India, known as Char Dham.
 
 
 
• **Balabhadra (Balarama):**
 
 
• Balabhadra, also known as Balarama, is the elder brother of Lord Krishna and is worshipped as an incarnation of Sheshnag, the serpent on whom Lord Vishnu rests.
 
• He is depicted with a fair complexion and is often shown carrying a plough and a mace.
 
• Balarama is considered a deity of agriculture and strength and is revered for his role in various Hindu epics and scriptures.
 
 
 
• **Subhadra:**
 
 
• Subhadra is the younger sister of Lord Jagannath and Balabhadra and is often depicted riding in the middle chariot during the Rath Yatra.
 
• She is worshipped as a manifestation of Goddess Durga and is believed to protect and bless her devotees.

question: Easter festival is celebrated by which community?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Christian**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Easter is one of the most significant festivals in Christianity, marking the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.
 
• This festival is celebrated on the first Sunday after the first full moon following the vernal equinox.
 
• Easter is the culmination of the Passion of Jesus, preceded by Lent, a 40-day period of fasting, prayer, and penance.
 
• The Easter festival also includes traditions such as Easter eggs and the Easter Bunny, which symbolize new life and rebirth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Easter:**

 
 
• Easter is a festival and holiday commemorating the resurrection of Jesus from the dead, described in the New Testament as having occurred on the third day of his burial after his crucifixion by the Romans at Calvary c. 30 AD.
 
• It is the culmination of the Passion of Jesus, preceded by Lent (or Great Lent), a 40-day period of fasting, prayer, and penance.
 
• Most Christians refer to the week before Easter as "Holy Week"—it contains the days of the Easter Triduum, including Maundy Thursday (commemorating the Maundy and Last Supper), as well as Good Friday (commemorating the crucifixion and death of Jesus).
 
• In Western Christianity, Easter is always celebrated on the Sunday following the first full moon that occurs on or after the spring equinox.
 
 
 
• **Christianity:**
 
 
• Christianity is an Abrahamic monotheistic religion based on the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth. It is the world's largest religion, with about 2.4 billion followers.
 
• Its adherents, known as Christians, believe that Jesus is the Christ, whose coming as the Messiah was prophesied in the Hebrew Bible, called the Old Testament in Christianity, and chronicled in the New Testament.
 
• Christian theology is summarized in creeds such as the Apostles' Creed and the Nicene Creed, which state that Jesus suffered, died, was buried, descended into hell, and rose from the dead, and ascended into heaven, from where he will return.
 
• Christianity is divided into three main branches: Catholicism, Orthodoxy, and Protestantism.

• Rongali Bihu is celebrated in April to mark the Assamese New Year and the onset of spring.
 
• Kongali Bihu is observed in October and is a solemn occasion with less merrymaking.

question: Hola Mohalla is a festival associated with which religion/belief?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikhism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Hola Mohalla** is a significant festival celebrated by the Sikh community.
 
• The festival was started by the tenth Sikh Guru, **Guru Gobind Singh**, in 1701.
 
• Hola Mohalla is typically celebrated a day after the Hindu festival of Holi.
 
• It is a week-long festival that involves mock battles, exhibitions, martial arts, poetry, and music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sikhism**

 
 
• Sikhism is a monotheistic religion that originated in the Punjab region of the Indian subcontinent around the end of the 15th century.
 
• The fundamental beliefs of Sikhism, articulated in the sacred scripture Guru Granth Sahib, include faith and meditation on the name of the one creator, unity of all humankind, engaging in selfless service, striving for justice for the benefit and prosperity of all, and honest conduct and livelihood while living a householder's life.
 
• The Sikh community celebrates various festivals like Baisakhi, Guru Nanak Jayanti, and Hola Mohalla.
 
• Sikhism was founded by Guru Nanak and has ten gurus, with Guru Gobind Singh being the last human Guru. Guru Granth Sahib is the eternal Guru of the Sikhs.
 
 
 
• **Guru Gobind Singh**
 
 
• Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth Sikh Guru, a spiritual master, warrior, poet, and philosopher.
 
• He was born on 22 December 1666 in Patna, Bihar, India.
 
• He founded the Khalsa in 1699, a collective body of initiated Sikhs, and introduced the Five Ks, five articles of faith that Khalsa Sikhs wear at all times.
 
• Guru Gobind Singh also declared that the Guru Granth Sahib, the Sikh holy scripture, would be the eternal Guru after him.
 
 
 
• **Holi**
 
 
• Holi is a popular ancient Hindu festival, also known as the "festival of colors" or the "festival of love".
 
• The festival signifies the arrival of spring, the end of winter, the blossoming of love, and for many, it is a festive day to meet others, play and laugh, forget and forgive, and repair broken relationships.
 
• The festival is also celebrated as a thanksgiving for a good harvest.
 
• It lasts for a night and a day, starting on the evening of the Purnima (Full Moon day) falling in the Hindu calendar month of Phalguna, which falls around the middle of March in the Gregorian calendar.

• The festival involves pairs of buffaloes racing across muddy, slushy tracks while being controlled by their handlers, known as "jockeys."
 
• Kambala is celebrated to honor the agricultural traditions and cultural heritage of the region, rooted in the worship of Bhoota (spirits) and nature.
 
• Historically, Kambala was organized by farming communities as a form of thanksgiving to gods for protecting their crops and providing a good harvest.
 
• Over time, the event transformed into a competitive sport, attracting participants and spectators from across Karnataka and neighboring states.

• Examples include the Mysuru Dasara festival and the Meenakshi Temple festival in Tamil Nadu.
 
 
 
• **Classical Music:**

• It focuses on intricate ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic cycles), emphasizing devotion and spirituality.
 
• Prominent Carnatic musicians from Karnataka include Purandara Dasa (known as the father of Carnatic music) and Muthuswami Dikshitar.
 
• Carnatic music is distinct from Hindustani classical music, which developed in North India.
 
 
 
• **Tribal Rituals:**

question: The first recorded origin of Bonalu festival is traced back to which disease outbreak in Hyderabad?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Plague**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__
 
• **The Bonalu festival** is a traditional Hindu festival celebrated annually in Telangana, particularly in Hyderabad and Secunderabad. 
 
• The origins of the festival are traced back to the outbreak of the **plague epidemic** in the twin cities of Hyderabad and Secunderabad in the late 19th century. 
 
• People believed that the epidemic was a result of the anger of the deity **Goddess Mahakali**. As a result, they started offering prayers, sacrifices, and special rituals to appease her. 
 
• The festival involves offering food, which is usually rice cooked with milk and jaggery, placed in a decorated brass or earthen pot, to the goddess as a thanksgiving gesture. 
 
• The outbreak of the plague and subsequent prayers to Goddess Mahakali created a tradition that evolved into what is now celebrated as the Bonalu festival. **Hence, the correct answer is Plague.** 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Historical Context of the Plague:** 
 
 
• The plague was a deadly epidemic that caused widespread panic and loss of life in Hyderabad during the **late 1800s**. 
 
• The epidemic led to the belief that the city needed divine intervention to stop the spread of the disease. 
 
• Goddess Mahakali, a form of Goddess Durga, was believed to be the protector against diseases and calamities. 
 
 
 
• **Significance of Bonalu Festival:** 
 
 
• Bonalu is derived from the word **"Bhojanalu,"** meaning meal or feast, symbolizing the food offering to the goddess. 
 
• The festival typically falls during the **Ashada Masam** (July-August) according to the Hindu calendar. 
 
• The celebrations include vibrant processions, traditional dances like **Potharaju** and the adornment of temples. 
 
 
 
• **Rituals and Practices:** 
 
 
• Women carry decorated pots containing cooked rice, jaggery, milk, and curd, often adorned with neem leaves and turmeric. 
 
• These offerings are made to the goddess in temples, especially the famous **Mahakali temples** in the region. 
 
 
 
• **Modern Celebrations:** 
 
 
• Today, Bonalu is an integral part of Telangana's culture and heritage, celebrated with pomp and grandeur. 
 
• The government of Telangana has recognized it as a **state festival** to promote the region's rich traditions. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Key Temples:** 
 
 
• The most notable temples where Bonalu is celebrated are **Ujjaini Mahakali Temple** in Secunderabad and **Simhavahini Mahakali Temple** in Lal Darwaza, Hyderabad. 
 
• Other significant temples include Akkanna Madanna Temple and Muthyalamma Temple. 
 
 
 
• **Potharaju Role:** 
 
 
• Potharaju is a mythological figure and the brother of the goddess, represented by men dressed in traditional attire. 
 
• He leads the procession, dancing and wielding a whip to ward off evil spirits. 
 
 
 
• **Government Support:** 
 
 
• The Telangana government provides financial assistance and logistical support for the festival. 
 
• The festival attracts tourists, contributing to the promotion of Telangana's cultural tourism.

• The festival typically takes place in the month of **November**, marking the end of the agricultural year.

• The celebration involves **traditional dances**, music, and rituals performed by men and women dressed in colorful traditional attire. The highlight is the rhythmic beating of **100 drums**, which symbolizes unity and joy.

• The Wangala festival not only showcases the rich cultural heritage of the Garo community but also promotes **community bonding** and the preservation of traditional art forms.

• The tribe is known for its **rich cultural traditions**, including music, dance, and handicrafts.

• It symbolizes the transition from hard agricultural labor to a time of relaxation and celebration.

• Through the festival, younger generations learn about traditional customs and rituals, ensuring the preservation of Garo heritage.

• **Mizo:** The Mizo tribe in Mizoram celebrates festivals like **Chapchar Kut**, which is related to the cultivation cycle.

• **Meghalaya:** Meghalaya is known as the "Abode of Clouds" and is home to multiple indigenous tribes, including the Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia.

• The state is rich in biodiversity and cultural heritage, making it a hub for eco-tourism and ethnic festivals.

__

• **Pola festival** is a significant cultural celebration dedicated to **bull worship** in the **Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh** and other parts of India.

• The festival is primarily celebrated by **farmers** to honor and express gratitude to their bulls, which are considered essential for agricultural activities such as plowing and transportation.

• **On the day of Pola**, bulls are bathed, decorated with ornaments, and worshipped. Farmers apply turmeric, oil, and colorful patterns to their bulls as a mark of respect.

• The festival includes **processions**, where bulls are paraded, and cultural activities such as bull races are organized in villages.

• This tradition symbolizes the deep connection between humans and animals in agrarian societies and showcases the importance of bulls in rural livelihoods.

• The term "Pola" is derived from the Marathi language and is widely celebrated in states like **Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Chhattisgarh**.

• On this day, farmers abstain from agricultural work to give their bulls a day of rest and celebration.

• **Significance of Bull Worship:**

• Bulls are considered the backbone of traditional farming in India, especially in rural areas where mechanized farming is less prevalent.

• Worshipping bulls signifies acknowledging their **labor, loyalty, and contribution** to agricultural productivity.

• The festival also emphasizes the harmonious coexistence and respect between humans and animals.

• Communities come together to share meals, celebrate, and strengthen social bonds.

• **Mattu Pongal:** Celebrated in Tamil Nadu, this festival is dedicated to cattle worship and is part of the Pongal celebrations.

• **Gaijatra:** Celebrated in Nepal, it involves processions with cows to commemorate the deceased and honor cattle.

• **Option 4 (Harvest Sale):** Harvest festivals like **Lohri, Baisakhi, and Onam** celebrate the bounty of crops and are unrelated to the theme of Pola.

subject: GK
question:
Which of the following pairs of temple style & region are **correctly **matched?

1. Vesara - Deccan

2. Rekha-Deul - Odisha

3. Bhumija - Malwa

4. Kalinga - Tamil Nadu
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: 1, 2 & 3 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vesara - Deccan:** Vesara style emerged in the Deccan region and represents a hybrid temple architecture combining elements of both Nagara (North Indian) and Dravida (South Indian) styles. It is prominently seen in Karnataka and adjoining areas.
 
• **Rekha-Deul - Odisha:** Rekha-Deul is a specific type of Nagara style temple architecture found in Odisha. It is characterized by its curvilinear tower (Shikhara) and intricate carvings, as seen in temples like the Lingaraja Temple in Bhubaneswar.
 
• **Bhumija - Malwa:** The Bhumija style is prevalent in the Malwa region (present-day Madhya Pradesh). It is distinguished by its vertically rising miniature towers arranged symmetrically around the main Shikhara, giving the temple a pyramidal appearance.
 
• **Kalinga - Tamil Nadu:** The Kalinga style of architecture is associated with Odisha and not Tamil Nadu. Tamil Nadu is known for the Dravidian style of temple architecture characterized by massive gopurams and pillared halls.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vesara Style:**

 
 
• The Vesara style bridges the gap between the Nagara and Dravidian styles, often referred to as a mixed or transitional style.
 
• Examples include the temples of Badami, Pattadakal, and Aihole built during the Chalukya dynasty.
 
 
 
• **Rekha-Deul Style:**
 
 
• Rekha-Deul is a component of the Nagara style specific to Odisha, with temples having tall, curvilinear towers called Shikharas.
 
• Prominent examples include the Sun Temple at Konark and the Mukteshwar Temple in Bhubaneswar.
 
 
 
• **Bhumija Style:**
 
 
• The Bhumija style is notable for its intricate symmetry and miniature towers rising around the central Shikhara.
 
• It was widely adopted in the western and central parts of India, especially under the Paramara dynasty of Malwa.
 
• Examples include the Udayeshwar Temple in Udaipur (Madhya Pradesh).
 
 
 
• **Kalinga Style:**
 
 
• The Kalinga style is indigenous to Odisha and consists of three types: Rekha-Deul (curvilinear towers), Pidha-Deul (pyramidal roof), and Khakhara-Deul (rectangular structures).
 
• It is distinct from Tamil Nadu's Dravidian style, which features large gopurams and open courtyards.

• **Statement 1:** The amalaka is a distinctive, circular, ribbed stone disk that sits atop the shikhara (tower) of Nagara-style temples. This is a defining feature of the Nagara temple architecture.
 
• The amalaka symbolizes the celestial world and serves as a crowning feature of the shikhara, emphasizing verticality and spiritual connection.
 
• **Statement 2:** In Drāviḍa-style temples, the vimana refers to the tower or superstructure directly above the sanctum (garbhagriha), not the gateway tower (gopuram). The gopuram refers to the ornate gateway towers found predominantly in Drāviḍa temples.
 
• The confusion arises because both the vimana and gopuram are tall structures, but their functions and locations within the temple complex differ.
 
• Therefore, Statement 1 is correct, while Statement 2 is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagara Style of Temple Architecture:**

 
 
• The Nagara style is primarily found in northern India and is characterized by its curvilinear shikhara (tower).
 
• The amalaka and kalasha are prominent features atop the shikhara.
 
• The temples have a square base and are often built on a raised platform called a jagati.
 
• Examples include the Kandariya Mahadev Temple in Khajuraho and the Sun Temple in Konark.
 
 
 
• **Drāviḍa Style of Temple Architecture:**
 
 
• The Drāviḍa style is predominant in southern India and is known for its pyramidal vimanas above the sanctum.
 
• The gopurams, or gateway towers, are a unique feature of this style and are often more prominent than the vimana itself.
 
• The temples are enclosed within walls, with multiple gopurams marking the entrances.
 
• Examples include the Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur and the Meenakshi Temple in Madurai.
 
 
 
• **Key Differences Between Nagara and Drāviḍa Styles:**
 
 
• The Nagara style emphasizes verticality with curvilinear shikharas, while the Drāviḍa style has tiered and pyramidal vimanas.
 
• Gopurams are a hallmark of the Drāviḍa style, but they are absent in the Nagara style.
 
• The Nagara temples are relatively smaller and lack boundary walls, unlike the enclosed complexes of Drāviḍa temples.
 
 
 
• **Additional Terminologies:**
 
 
• **Shikhara:** The tower or spire above the sanctum in Nagara-style temples.
 
• **Amalaka:** The circular, ribbed stone disk atop the shikhara, symbolizing the divine.
 
• **Vimana:** The pyramidal structure above the sanctum in Drāviḍa-style temples.
 
• **Gopuram:** Ornate gateway towers, typically found in Drāviḍa temple complexes.
 
• **Garbhagriha:** The innermost sanctum of a temple where the deity resides.

question:
**Which of the following statements is/are true?**

**Statement 1**: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram exemplifies Dravidian architecture built of carved granite blocks.

**Statement 2**: This temple showcases architectural continuity from the Pallava-era rock-cut cave temples to fully structural stone constructions.

options.text: Both statements are true, and Statement 2 is the correct explanation of Statement 1.
Both statements are correct, but Statement 2 is not the correct explanation of Statement 1.
Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is false.

solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Both statements are true, and Statement 2 is the correct explanation of Statement 1.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Statement 1:** The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram exemplifies **Dravidian architecture** built of carved granite blocks. 

• The Shore Temple is located in **Mahabalipuram, Tamil Nadu**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• It was constructed during the reign of the Pallava king **Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha) in the 8th century CE**.

• The temple is made of **granite blocks**, showcasing the brilliance of Pallava-era craftsmanship.

• It is one of the earliest examples of structural stone temples in South India, representing the transition from rock-cut to structural architecture. *Hence, Statement 1 is correct.*

• **Statement 2:** This temple showcases architectural continuity from the Pallava-era rock-cut cave temples to fully structural stone constructions.

• The Pallava dynasty is renowned for its contributions to early South Indian temple architecture.

• The Shore Temple illustrates the **evolution of temple design**, transitioning from rock-cut cave temples like those at Mahabalipuram to fully structural temples.

• The carvings and sculptures reflect the **artistic and architectural continuity** from earlier Pallava creations.

• The temple's aesthetic and construction techniques influenced subsequent Dravidian temple architecture. *Hence, Statement 2 is correct.*

• **Explanation:** Statement 2 correctly explains Statement 1 because it provides the historical and architectural context for the Shore Temple's design and construction.

• ***Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Shore Temple:**

• The Shore Temple complex consists of three shrines dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and **Lord Vishnu**.

• The temple faces the Bay of Bengal and served as a landmark for sailors, hence the name "Shore Temple."

• The intricate carvings depict **mythological stories**, including scenes from the Mahabharata and Ramayana.

• **Pallava Dynasty’s Contribution to Architecture:**

• The Pallavas pioneered rock-cut architecture, as seen in the **Mandapas (cave temples)** and monolithic Rathas (chariots) at Mahabalipuram.

• Examples include **Arjuna's Penance**, the **Pancha Rathas**, and the Mahishasuramardini Cave.

• The Shore Temple marked the beginning of structural temple construction, which became a hallmark of later South Indian dynasties like the Cholas.

• **Dravidian Architecture:**

• Dravidian temple architecture is characterized by **pyramidal towers (Vimanas)**, pillared halls (Mandapas), and enclosed courtyards.

• Intricate carvings and sculptures depicting deities, animals, and mythological scenes are common features.

• Later examples of Dravidian architecture include the **Brihadeshwara Temple** (Chola dynasty) and the **Meenakshi Temple** (Nayaka dynasty).

• **UNESCO World Heritage Status:**

• The Shore Temple is part of the **Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram**, designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in **1984**.

• This recognition highlights its cultural and historical significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Other Notable Pallava Monuments:**

• **Pancha Rathas:** Five monolithic temples, each carved from a single granite block, named after the Pandavas from the Mahabharata.

• **Arjuna’s Penance:** A massive open-air rock relief depicting scenes of devotion and mythology.

• **Mahishasuramardini Cave:** A cave temple featuring carvings of Goddess Durga slaying the demon Mahishasura.

• **Architectural Influence:**

• The Shore Temple and other Pallava structures laid the foundation for later South Indian dynasties' architectural styles, particularly the Cholas and Vijayanagara rulers.

• The use of granite and intricate carvings became defining features of Dravidian temples.

question: The architectural style of ancient temples in Uttarakhand is primarily influenced by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**North Indian Nagara style**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The ancient temples in **Uttarakhand** primarily follow the **Nagara style** of architecture, which is a prominent temple architecture style in **North India**. 
• In Nagara architecture, the temples have a **curvilinear tower (Shikhara)** over the sanctum (Garbhagriha). This distinguishes it from other architectural styles. 
• The temples in Uttarakhand, such as the Kedarnath, Badrinath, and Jageshwar temples, are renowned for their adherence to the **Nagara style** with regional adaptations to suit the Himalayan environment. 
• These temples are constructed using locally available **stone**, ensuring they can withstand the harsh weather conditions of the region. 
• The **Kumaon** and **Garhwal regions** of Uttarakhand are dotted with such temples, showcasing intricate carvings, ornamentation, and a **focus on verticality** as seen in traditional Nagara architecture. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Nagara Style of Architecture:** 
• The Nagara style is one of the three main temple architectural styles in India, along with the Dravidian and Vesara styles. 
• It is prevalent in **North India** and is characterized by a prominent **Shikhara (tower)** that curves inward and upward in a vertical direction. 
• The temples generally have a square base, with intricate carvings on walls and elaborate ornamentation. 
• Examples: **Khajuraho Temples**, **Konark Sun Temple**, and the temples of Uttarakhand. 
• **Other Architectural Styles:** 
• **Indo-Gothic style:** This is a fusion of Indian and Gothic architectural elements, often seen in colonial-era structures like the **Victoria Memorial (Kolkata)**. It is not related to temple architecture. 
• **Vesara Style:** A mix of Nagara and Dravidian styles, prevalent in the **Deccan region**, especially in Karnataka. Examples: **Chalukyan temples**. 
• **Chalukyan Style:** Associated with the Chalukya dynasty, this style is famous for intricate sculptures and **pillared halls**. It is predominantly seen in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh. 
• **Temples in Uttarakhand:** 
• **Kedarnath Temple:** A prime example of Nagara architecture, dedicated to Lord Shiva. 
• **Badrinath Temple:** Dedicated to Lord Vishnu, showcasing the Nagara style with local Himalayan influences. 
• **Jageshwar Temple:** A complex of over 100 small temples built in the Nagara style in the Kumaon region. 
• **Key Features of Uttarakhand Temples:** 
• Use of **stone masonry** to withstand harsh weather. 
• Simple yet elegant designs, with a focus on spiritual symbolism. 
• Integration with natural surroundings, such as rivers and mountains, reflecting the religious significance of the Himalayas. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Historical Significance:** The temples in Uttarakhand are believed to have been built between the **7th and 12th centuries**, during the Katyuri and Chand dynasties. 
• **Religious Importance:** Many of these temples are part of the **Char Dham Yatra**, a significant pilgrimage in Hinduism. 
• **Construction Material:** Locally available **granite and other stones** were used to ensure durability and harmony with the natural environment. 
• **Tourism:** These temples attract millions of pilgrims and tourists annually, contributing to the economy of the region. </ul

question: Abdul Karim Khan was the exponent of which school of Hindustani Music?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kirana Gharana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Abdul Karim Khan was the founder of the Kirana Gharana of classical music.
 
• Kirana Gharana is one of the most prominent Indian classical khayal gharanas and is associated mostly with the perfect intonation of notes.
 
• The Gharana style was further evolved and was established as one of the important styles in modern Indian classical music in the late 19th /early 20th centuries by the musicians Abdul Karim Khan and Abdul Wahid Khan.
 
• The name of this school of music comes from Kirana or Kairana, a town and tehsil of Shamli District in Uttar Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Gharana
 Founder
 Remark
 Exponents
 
 
 
 

 Gwalior Gharana
 Ustad Naththan Pir Bakhsh
 
 
This is the oldest among all the Khayal Gayaki (vocal) styles. The distinctive feature of this style of singing has been noted as its lucidity and simplicity. 

 
 Bal Krishna BaIchal Karanjikar, Vishnu Digambar Paluskar, Pandit Omkarnath Thakur, Veena Sahasrabuddhe and Malini Rajurkar 
 
 

 Benaras Gharana
 Janaki Prasad
 
 
The Benaras Gharana evolved as a result of the great lilting style of khayal singing known by Thumri singers of Benaras and Gaya. 

 
 Rajan Mishra, Sajan Mishra, Girija Devi, and others. 
 
 

 Agra Gharana
 Haji Sujan Khan, Ustad Ghagghe Khuda Baksh
 The Agra Gharana places great importance on developing forcefulness and deepness in the voice so that the notes are powerful and resonant. 
 Faiyyaz Khan, Latafat Hussein Khan, and Dinkar Kakini. 
 
 

 Kirana Gharana 
 Abdul Karim Khan and Abdul Wahid Khan
 The name of this school of music comes from Kirana or Kairana, a town and tehsil of Shamli District in Uttar Pradesh.
 Hirabhai Barodekar, Begum Akhtar, Bhimsen Joshi, Gangubai Hangal, and Prabha Atre. 
 
 

 Patiala Gharana
 Ustad Fateh Ali Khan and Ustad Ali Baksh
 Patiala Gharana is regarded as an offshoot of the Delhi Gharana. The Patiala Gharana is characterized by the use of greater rhythm play and by Layakari with the abundant use of Bols, particularly Bol-tans. 
 Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, Ajoy Chakravarti, Raza Ali Khan, Nirmala Deni, Naina Devi, Parveen Sultana, and others. 
 
 

 Delhi Gharana
 Mia Siddhar Khan Dhadi
 The Delhi Gharana was represented by Tanras Khan and Shabbu Khan. The highlights of Delhi Gharana are pleasing vistaar and exquisite compositions. 
 Chand Khan, Nasir Ahmed Khan, Usman Khan, Iqbal Ahmed Khan, and Krishna Bisht. 
 
 

 Mewati Gharana
 Ghagge Nazir Khan. 
 The Mewati Gharana gives importance to developing the mood of the raga through the notes forming it and its style is Bhava Pradhan. It also gives equal importance to the meaning of the text. 
 Pandit Jasraj, Moti Ram, Mani Ram, Sanjeev Abhyankar, and others.

question: In which season is Sarhul celebrated in Jharkhand?
solution:

__
 
• In the Indian state of** Jharkhand,** there is a** spring festival called Sarhul.**
 
• The festival is observed for **three days**, from **Chaitra Purnima** until the** third day of the Chaitra month **in **Sukla Paksh.**
 
• **Pahan, the village priest, sacrifices flowers, fruit, vermilion, a rooster, and tapan to the Sun, the local deity and ancestor,** during the celebration in order to bring the **village good fortune.**
 
• Then the villagers dance while **clutching sal tree blooms.**
 
• It serves as a reminder that a** new year has begun.**
 
• According to tradition, the marriage of the Earth and the Sun is also symbolized by it.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The festival's **Nagpuri name is Sarhul.**
 
• **The sal tree in Nagpuri is called Sar or Sarai, and Hul means "together" and ****"grove."**
 
• Sal represents a **celebration of nature.**
 
• **Kurukh and Sadan** celebrate Sarhul, a significant holiday. It is referred to as** Khaddi in Kurukh.**
 
• The **Bhumijs and Mundas **call it **Hadi Bonga.**
 
• The **Ho and Santal people** refer to it as **Baha parab.**

question: Which of the following is celebrated as the "Tibetan New Year"?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Losar festival.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Losar festival **marks the beginning of the **Tibetan New Year.**
 
• The Losar Festival is celebrated with **great zeal and fervour in Tibetian border states like Himachal Pradesh, Ladakh, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.**
 
• It is also known as a festival of happiness and prosperity.
 
• The celebrates the** Ladakhi or Tibetan New Year. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Puthandu:

 
 
• It is also known as Puthuvarusham.
 
• Puthandu is observed by Tamils as the traditional "Tamil/Hindu New Year."
 
• It normally occurs on April 14 and this month is known as Chittirai, the first month of the Tamil solar calendar.
 
 
 
• Poila Boisakh:
 
 
• The first day of the first month of Baishakh in the Bengali solar calendar is known as Pohela Boishakh.
 
• It is also known as the Bengali New Year or Nobo Borso.
 
• It is widely observed in Bangladesh and West Bengal.
 
 
 
• Vishu:
 
 
• Due to Malyalam being the dominant language in Kerala, Vishu is sometimes referred to as the Malyalam New Year.
 
• For residents of Kerala and several nearby regions of Tamil Nadu, Vishu signifies the start of the new year.
 
 
 
• Gudi Padwa:
 
 
• Celebrated on the first day of Chaitra month, Gudi Padwa is a New Year day for Maharashtrians and Konkanis.
 
• On this day a gudi can be found hanging out on the right side of the main access of the houses.
 
 
 
• Navreh
 
 
• It is the lunar new year that is celebrated in Kashmir.
 
• It is the Sanskrit word ‘Nav-Varsha’ from where the word ‘Navreh’ has been derived.
 
• It falls on the first day of the Chaitra Navratri.
 
 
 
• Ugadi
 
 
• The festival of Ugadi is celebrated on the first day of Chaitra month as per the Hindu calendar
 
• Ugadi, also known as Yugadi, is a renowned South Indian festival mainly celebrated in Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Telangana to commemorate the beginning of a new year.
 
• For Ugadi, doors in homes are adorned with mango leaf decorations called toranalu or Torana in Kannada
 
 
 
• Pana Sankranti
 
 
• Oriya New Year is also known as Pana Sankranti and it is observed as the first day of the Oriya Calendar.
 
• It is also known as ‘Maha Vishuba Sankranti,’ ‘Maha Sankranti,’ and ‘Mesha Sankranti’ is a festival that is widely celebrated across Odisha as the traditional New Year
 
• Pana Sankranti is named after ‘Pana,’ the main fruit drink which is prepared in Odisha’s traditional culture.

question: In which state is the Maihar court where Baba Allauddin Khan was a musician?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Madhya Pradesh **is the **Maihar court** where **Baba Allauddin Khan** was a musician.
 
• Baba Allauddin Khan was a musician for the Maihar court and was awarded **the Padma Bhushan in 1958 and the Padma Vibhushan in 1971.**
 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar and Nikhil Banerjee,** both deceased, were two more notable artists from this Gharana.
 
• The nal-tarang, jal-tarang, and Chandra-Sarang, among other musical instruments, were created by Baba Allauddin Khan despite the restricted resources in a tiny town like Maihar.
 
• Baba founded the Maihar Band in 1918 with the intention of offering comfort to children who had been left orphaned by an epidemic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Baba Allauddin Khan was appointed as the **Maharaja of Maihar's court musician. **
 
• By creating a number of ragas, fusing the bass sitar and bass sarod with more conventional instruments, and assembling an orchestra, he created the groundwork for the present Maihar Gharana.
 
• He received the Sangeet Natak Akademi's highest honor, the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship, for his lifelong contribution to Indian music in 1954.
 
• He also received India's third and second-highest civilian honors, the Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan, in 1958 and 1971, respectively.

question: Which of the following is celebrated as the New Year in Tamil Nadu?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Puthandu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Tamil calendar's first day** of the year,** Puthandu **is traditionally observed as a festival by **Tamil Hindus**.
 
• The event begins on the first day of the **Tamil month of Chittirai**, according to the lunisolar Hindu calendar's solar cycle.
 
• According to the Gregorian calendar, it occurs every year on or around April 14.
 
• The traditional new year is held on the same day in other parts of South and South East Asia but is referred to by different names there, such as Vishu in Kerala and Vaisakhi or Baisakhi in central and northern India.
 
• The Tamil New Year usually occurs on April 14 of each Gregorian year, immediately after the spring equinox. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Tamils in India and Sri Lanka celebrate **Pongal**, a multi-day Hindu harvest celebration. According to the Tamil solar calendar, it is observed at the beginning of the month, and depending on the sun's orbit that particular year, the festival is typically held on January 14 or January 15.
 
• According to the Hindu calendar, **Ugadi** is New Year's Day, and it is observed in the Indian states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka.
 
• **Onam **is an annual harvest festival in India that is mostly observed by Keralan Hindus. It is the official festival of the state and a significant annual event for people in Kerala, featuring a variety of cultural activities.

question: Wangala festival is celebrated by which of the following tribes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Garo tribe**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Known as the '100 Drum Festival', the Wangala Festival is a traditional festival in the northeastern Indian state of Meghalaya.
 
• The festival kicked off on November 12th, 2021.
 
• The festival lasts from two days to a week. 
 
• It is one of the most important festivals of the Garo Tribe.
 
• The tribesmen make sacrifices to please their god Saljong. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The Wangala festival marks the end of a period of toil, that brings good results to the fields which also signifies the onset of winter.
 
• It is also celebrated in honour of the Sun God that marks the end of the long harvest season.
 
• Wangala is celebrated with different forms of dance.
 
• These dances are performed on the tunes of folk songs that are played on drums and primitive flute.
 
• Additionally, these flutes are made of buffalo horns.
 
• On the first day of the festival, people celebrate it with a ceremony called Ragula.
 
• This ceremony is performed in the house of the village’s chief.
 
• Then on the second day of celebration, which is called Kakkat, people begin the ceremony by dancing to the rhythms of long oval-shaped drums.
 
• In this celebration, young and old join together while men play the drums and women perform traditional dance forms. The dance form is known as Dama Dagota.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​Meghalaya:

 
 
• Lok Sabha seats - 2.
 
• Rajya Sabha seats - 1.
 
• State Animal - Clouded leopard.
 
• State Bird - Common hill myna.
 
• National Parks - Balphakram National Park, Nokrek Ridge National Park.

• It is stated in the Brahma Purana, one of the revered Hindu texts, that Lord Brahma restored the universe after a natural disaster killed everyone and stopped time.
 
• After Brahma's efforts, time was reset on this day, ushering in a new era of truth and justice. On this day, Lord Brahma is worshipped as a result.

• In most cases, when a **loan **is raised by the **government**, the **interest **payment **amount** is also included.
 
• When the principal loan amount is removed from this **sum**, the **primary deficit **is shown.

question:
With reference of Ajivikas, consider the following statements.

a) Makkhali Gosala was the prominent teacher of this sect.

b) Ajivikas believed in fatalism.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both a and b**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Makkhali Gosala** was indeed the prominent teacher of the Ajivika sect, which is a fundamental point in understanding the history of this ascetic sect.
 
• The Ajivikas were known for their belief in **fatalism**, the idea that all events are predetermined and therefore inevitable.
 
• The sect was a contemporary of Buddhism and Jainism and had a significant influence during the time of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• Ajivikas followed a strict ascetic lifestyle and believed in the concept of niyati (destiny).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ajivikas:**

 
 
• The Ajivikas were an ascetic sect that emerged in ancient India around the same time as Buddhism and Jainism. They believed in the doctrine of predetermination, where every event is preordained and humans are powerless to change their destiny.
 
• **Makkhali Gosala:** He was one of the key figures in the Ajivika sect. His teachings emphasized the power of fate over individual effort.
 
• The teachings of the Ajivikas were based on the principle of niyati, which means destiny. This doctrine suggested that everything in the world was predetermined and fixed, and human efforts to change their fate were futile.
 
• The Ajivikas practiced extreme asceticism and renunciation, similar to other contemporary religious movements like Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Fatalism:**
 
 
• Fatalism is the philosophical doctrine suggesting that all events are predetermined and inevitable, a belief that is central to the Ajivika philosophy.
 
• It implies that human actions have no effect on the future, which is already decided by destiny or fate.
 
• This belief can lead to a deterministic outlook on life, where individuals accept whatever happens without trying to change their circumstances.
 
• In the context of Ajivikas, this meant that their ascetic practices were part of adhering to their predetermined path.

question: What makes Chhau a syncretic Indian dance form?

options.text: It uses Sanskrit-only chants in temple rituals
It merges tribal, folk, and classical Hindu elements
It evolved purely from Vaishnav temple dance
It prohibits all forms of theatrical expression

solution:
The correct answer is __**It merges tribal, folk, and classical Hindu elements**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chhau** is a unique Indian dance form that combines elements of tribal, folk, and classical traditions of Hindu culture, creating a syncretic art form.
 
• This dance form is predominantly practiced in the eastern regions of India, particularly in **Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal**.
 
• Chhau incorporates **vigorous martial movements, intricate footwork, and expressive facial gestures** to narrate mythological and folk tales, often drawn from Hindu epics like the **Ramayana and Mahabharata**.
 
• It is recognized for its use of **elaborate masks** (especially in Purulia Chhau) and vibrant costumes, which are integral to the storytelling aspect of the performance.
 
• The dance form has been declared a part of the **UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**, underscoring its cultural significance and historical value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: It uses Sanskrit-only chants in temple rituals**
 
 
• This is incorrect as Chhau is not associated with the exclusive use of Sanskrit chants or temple rituals. While it draws from Hindu mythology, it is a performance art that incorporates folk and tribal traditions rather than being limited to temple worship.
 
• Sanskrit chants are more closely linked with classical dance forms like **Bharatanatyam or Odissi**, which are temple-based traditions.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: It evolved purely from Vaishnav temple dance**
 
 
• This is incorrect as Chhau did not evolve solely from Vaishnav temple dances. While it draws from Hindu religious themes, its origins are rooted in tribal and martial traditions, making it a broader amalgamation of multiple influences.
 
• Vaishnav temple dances are more specifically associated with classical forms like **Kathak** and **Manipuri**.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: It prohibits all forms of theatrical expression**
 
 
• This is incorrect as Chhau is celebrated for its theatrical expressions, including elaborate facial movements, mask work, and dramatic gestures.
 
• Theatrical expression is a defining feature of Chhau, enabling performers to communicate stories effectively.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Chhau Dance**
 
 
• Chhau is a semi-classical Indian dance form that blends classical music with folk and tribal influences.
 
• There are three main styles of Chhau: **Purulia Chhau** (West Bengal), **Mayurbhanj Chhau** (Odisha), and **Seraikella Chhau** (Jharkhand), each with distinct characteristics.
 
• The dance is often performed during festivals, particularly in the spring season, and serves as a medium to preserve cultural heritage.
 
 
</ul

• **Traditional Archery Competitions:** Meghalaya is renowned for its traditional archery competitions, locally known as "Teer." These competitions are deeply rooted in the culture of the Khasi tribe.
