question: Name a reproductive strategy in which parasites take advantage of the care of other individuals of the same species or different species to raise their young.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brood parasitism.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brood parasitism:-**

 
 
• It is a **reproductive strategy **in which a **parasite lays its eggs** in the nest of **another individual **of the same species or different species, and the **host raises the parasite's young.**
 
• This strategy is often used by** birds**, such as cuckoos, cowbirds, and honeyguides, but it can also be observed in** insects, fish, and mammals.**
 
• Brood parasites have evolved various adaptations to increase their chances of success, such as** mimicking the appearance and behavior** of the host's eggs or chicks, laying their eggs at the same time as the host, or removing the host's eggs.
 
• Brood parasitism can have both** costs and benefits** for the host, depending on the **degree of similarity** between the **parasite and the host**, the number of parasites in the host's nest, and the availability of alternative nesting sites.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sexual parasitism:-**

 
 
• It also known as** mate parasitism**, refers to a reproductive strategy in which a** male or female gains access** to a mate or a nest by **deceiving or coercing the other individual. **
 
 
 
• **Klepto parasitism, or kleptoparasitism:-**
 
 
• It​** **refers to a feeding strategy in which a parasite steals food from another individual, often by chasing or harassing it.
 
 
 
• **Competitive parasitism, or social parasitism:-**
 
 
• It** **refers to a reproductive strategy in which a parasite takes over the resources and/or reproduction of a host, often by manipulating its behavior or physiology.

• **Chlorophyceae:-**

 
 
• **It is a class of green algae, distinguished mainly on the basis of ultrastructural morphology. **
 
• They are usually green due to the dominance of pigments chlorophyll a and chlorophyll b.
 
• The chloroplast may be discoid, plate-like, reticulate, cup-shaped, spiral- or ribbon-shaped in different species.
 
• Most of the members have one or more storage bodies called pyrenoids located in the chloroplast.
 
• Pyrenoids contain protein besides starch. Some green algae may store food in the form of oil droplets.
 
 
 
• **Phaeophyceae:-**
 
 
• **It also known as brown algae, is a class of multicellular algae that are found primarily in marine environments. **
 
• They are distinguished by their brown color, which is due to the presence of the pigment fucoxanthin.
 
• Brown algae range in size from microscopic filaments to giant kelp forests that can reach over 60 meters in length.
 
 
 
• **Cyanophyceae:-**
 
 
• It is known as Cyanobacteria, is a class of prokaryotic organisms that obtain energy via photosynthesis.
 
• **It is known as Blue-green algae.**
 
• They are considered to be the oldest form of life on Earth, with fossils dating back over 3.5 billion years.
 
• Cyanobacteria are found in a wide variety of habitats, including freshwater, marine, and terrestrial environments.
 
 
 
• **Rhodophyceae:-**
 
 
• **It also known as red algae, is a class of eukaryotic algae that are found primarily in marine environments. **
 
• They are distinguished by their red color, which is due to the presence of the pigment phycoerythrin.
 
• Red algae range in size from microscopic filaments to large, complex seaweeds.

question: Which is the only living representative of Sphenopsida that has an underground, creeping and perennial rhizome that gives off aerial as well as underground branches?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Equisetum.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer is** option 4, Equisetum**, which is commonly known as** horsetail or scouring rush.**
 
• Equisetum has an **underground, creeping and perennial rhizome** that gives off **aerial **as well as** underground branches**.
 
• It is the only living representative of **Sphenopsida**, a group of **vascular plants **that were dominant during the **Carboniferous period.**
 
• **Adiantum**, also known as** maidenhair fern,** belongs to the group of **ferns **and **does no**t have an underground rhizome.
 
 
• It has **delicate fronds** and is commonly grown as an** ornamental plant.**
 
 
 
• **Dryopteris** is another **group of ferns** that **does not** have an underground rhizome.
 
 
• It is commonly known as **wood fern **and is also grown as an **ornamental plant.**
 
 
 
• **Selaginella, **also known as **spike moss,** is a group of plants that are **similar to ferns** but have** smaller leaves** and are adapted to grow in** dry environments.**
 
 
• They **do not** have an underground rhizome.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f0f43c31587a372f5a7ce0db582a061e8322aa1ad07f7bc85d4b2c70866286b5.png]

• It contains **silica **and other minerals that are believed to have **anti-inflammatory and diuretic properties.**
 
 
 
• **Adiantum** is also used in **traditional medicine** to treat **respiratory and digestive problems.**
 
 
• It is also used in **hair care products** because of its **high silica content.**
 
 
 
• **Dryopteris **is commonly used in landscaping because of its** attractive foliage **and** tolerance to shade.**
 
• **Selaginella** is used in** terrariums and indoor gardens** because of its **small size and unique appearance.**

• **Blue-green Algae (Cyanobacteria)**

 
 
• Blue-green algae are actually** **bacteria** **and are** also known as Cyanobacteria.**
 
• They are** photosynthetic organisms** and can live in a wide variety of environments,** including freshwater, seawater, damp soil, or rocks.**
 
• Cyanobacteria are known for their significant** contribution to the Earth's oxygen atmosphere.**
 
• They can **exist as single cells** or can form colonies.
 
 
 
• **Red Algae (Rhodophyta)**
 
 
• Red algae, often called **Rhodophyta,** have been identified as one of the oldest groups of **eukaryotic algae.**
 
• They are mostly **found in the warmer waters of the ocean.**
 
• Red algae are of great economic value because of their use in the production of **agar and carrageenan**, substances** used as thickening agents** in various food products.
 
• Their **red colour** is due to the **pigment, phycoerythrin.**
 
 
 
• **Green Algae (Chlamydomonas)**
 
 
• Green algae are a diverse** group of algae **from which plants evolved. Chlamydomonas is a genus of **unicellular green algae.**
 
• Chlamydomonas **species are widely distributed worldwide** and are **found in soil and freshwater.**
 
• They have **two flagella** that allow them to move.
 
• They are known for their green colour due to the **presence of chlorophyll.**
 
 
 
• **Brown Algae (Sargassum)**
 
 
• Brown algae are the most complex type of algae; many are **seaweeds.**
 
• Sargassum is a** brown algae**, known for forming massive floating forests in the ocean.
 
• It is **primarily marine** and is** found in warm-temperate and tropical oceans.**
 
• They provide important **ecological functions** such as providing habitats for a wide variety of marine species.
 
• The **brown colour** is due to the presence of a pigment called **fucoxanthin**, which masks the green colour of chlorophyll.

question: What cells help In osmoregulation In platyhelminthes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Flame cells.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Flame cells** are specialized cells that form** part of the excretory system** in these organisms, known as **protonephridia.**
 
• Flame cells play a primary** role in osmoregulation,** the process by which a balance of water and ions is maintained within the body.
 
• Along with osmoregulation, flame cells also help in the **removal of waste products**.
 
• This system is not only found in Platyhelminthes but **also in other types of flatworms and invertebrates**. However, it is most prominent in **Platyhelminthes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nerve cells:**

 
 
• Platyhelminthes have a decentralized nerve cell network and two longitudinal nerve cords running along their body length.
 
• These nerve cells, also known as **neurons**, are responsible for **transmitting signals** across the organism.
 
• They enable **sensing the environment and coordinating the organism's **response to it.
 
 
 
• **Ganglia:**
 
 
• Ganglia are simple forms of** "brains"** or collections of nerve cell bodies that process information in invertebrates such as **Platyhelminthes**.
 
• They serve as the **central nervous system** in these organisms, acting as control centres that coordinate nerve signals.
 
 
 
• **Hooks:**
 
 
• Some Platyhelminthes, specifically parasitic ones, have **hooks and suckers**.
 
• These structures are **not cells, **but adaptations that help the worm to attach to the host's tissue.
 
• The hooks **assist in anchoring the parasite** to its host and facilitate the feeding process.

question: Ferns, horsetails and lycophytes belong to which of the following groups?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pteridophyta.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ferns, horsetails, and lycophytes** all belong to the group referred to as **Pteridophyta.**
 
• These represent some of the** earlier forms of vascular plants on Earth.**
 
• They are classified as a subdivision of the plant kingdom, known as **cryptogams,** which **do not produce seeds or flowers.**
 
• Pteridophyta plants** reproduce via spores, **which are usually located on the underside of the fronds (leaves) in organs or structures called **sporangia.**
 
• The life cycle of Pteridophytes includes two distinct phases – **the large, prominent sporophyte and a less visible**, but still independent gametophyte also known as a **prothallium.**
 
• These plants are typically found in damp, shaded areas, though some have adapted to a variety of other habitats. Ferns, in particular, are known for their feather-like fronds and intricate patterns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bryophyta:**

 
 
• Bryophyta constitute the group of plants known as mosses and liverworts.
 
• They often grow in moist, shaded areas and are non-vascular, meaning they lack tissues for transporting water and nutrients.
 
• Unlike ferns, mosses reproduce using spores but are more primitive, often growing low to the ground.
 
 
 
• **Algae:**
 
 
• Algae is a diverse group of aquatic, photosynthetic organisms.
 
• They form a crucial part of the food chain in aquatic ecosystems and can range from microscopic sizes (microalgae) to massive kelp.
 
• Algae is not a homogeneous group but a term used to describe organisms from different evolutionary backgrounds that share some common features.
 
 
 
• **Fungi:**
 
 
• Fungi are a kingdom of usually multicellular eukaryotic organisms which are heterotrophic, meaning they obtain nutrients by consuming organic matter.
 
• They play a crucial role in nutrient cycling in ecosystems and include yeasts, molds, and mushrooms.
 
• Some fungi form symbiotic relationships with plants, aiding in nutrient absorption, while others can be pathogenic, causing diseases in plants and animals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Typhlops:-**

 
 
• **It is a genus of blind snakes, also known as worm snakes, which belong to the family Typhlopidae. **
 
• These snakes are found in various regions around the world, including Africa, Asia, the Americas, and some islands in the Pacific.
 
• Blind snakes are characterized by their small size, cylindrical bodies, and reduced eyes covered by scales. They are non-venomous and mainly feed on ants and termites, using their specialized jaws and teeth to consume their prey. Due to their fossorial (burrowing) nature and secretive habits, they are not commonly encountered by humans.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **Sea snake:** Sea snakes belong to a completely different family and environment. They are part of the Elapidae family and are adapted to living in marine environments. They are venomous and possess fully functional vision to navigate and hunt in the water.
 
• **Glass snakes**: "Glass snakes" actually refer to legless lizards, primarily belonging to the genus Ophisaurus. They are not snakes at all, despite their snake-like appearance. They differ from snakes in several key ways, such as having eyelids and external ear openings.
 
• **Grass snake:** Grass snakes belong to the genus Natrix, specifically in places like Europe. They are non-venomous snakes that live in terrestrial habitats, often near water sources, and are known for their distinctive collar or ring around the neck. They are not fossorial and have functional eyes.

question: Select the INCORRECT statement about Phylum Arthropoda.

options.text: Class Insecta is the largest class of Phylum Arthropoda.
Lignin is the main component of the exoskeletons of arthropods.
Over 85% of all the known animal species are arthropods.
Phylum Arthropoda comprises a wide diversity of animals with hard exoskeletons and jointed appendages.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Lignin is the main component of the exoskeletons of arthropods.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bacteria are a separate domain of life and are not related to the phylum Arthropoda.
 
• Arthropoda is the phylum that includes insects, spiders, crustaceans, and other similar creatures, all of which are multicellular and have exoskeletons, segmented bodies, and paired, jointed appendages. In contrast, bacteria are unicellular microorganisms in the domain Bacteria.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Phylum Arthropoda**:

 
• Arthropods are the most diverse group of animals, representing over 80% of known living animal species.
 
• Arthropods are characterized by their jointed legs (from which their name derives: 'arthro' means jointed, 'pod' means legs) and a hard exoskeleton made primarily of chitin.
 
• The exoskeleton serves as both a protective structure and a surface for muscle attachment, but it also needs to be periodically shed and regrown through a process called molting as the animal grows.
 
• The specifics of the body plan vary between arthropods, but generally, they possess a segmented body divided into regions such as the head, thorax, and abdomen. Some species may have a fused head and thorax known as a cephalothorax.
 
• Arthropods have specialized, paired appendages. These are often adapted for roles including sensory reception, feeding, and locomotion.
 
• Arthropoda has a broad range of ecological roles, from insects pollinating flowers to spiders acting as predators.
 
• Arthropoda is further divided into several subgroups or classes, like Insecta (insects), Arachnida (spiders and scorpions), Myriapoda (centipedes and millipedes), and Crustacea (crabs, lobsters, shrimp).
 
• In contrast, bacteria refer to microscopic, single-celled organisms belonging to the domain Bacteria. They are completely separate from arthropods and represent one of the most basic forms of life. They have a cell wall but lack organized nuclei and other cell organelles.

question: Meandrina is the generic name of which Coelenterata animal having soft tube-shaped bodies that live together in large groups?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brain coral.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meandrina** is the generic name of **brain coral**, which belongs to the **Coelenterata phylum **of marine animals.
 
• Brain corals are **colonial animals** that have** tube-shaped bodies **with** ridges and valleys **on their surface, resembling the** folds of the human brain.**
 
• They are found in shallow tropical waters of the **Atlantic, Caribbean, and Indo-Pacific regions** and play a vital role in reef-building and ecosystem maintenance.
 
• Brain corals feed on **plankton and organic matter** through their **tentacles **and have a **symbiotic relationship with algae** that provide them with energy through photosynthesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sea anemones** (*Actiniaria*) are also **Coelenterata animals** with **tube-shaped bodies**, but they are** solitary** and have a more delicate structure with tentacles surrounding a central mouth.
 
• **Sea-fans*** (Gorgonia)* are a type of** coral with a fan-shaped structure,** while medusa is a** free-swimming jellyfish** with a bell-shaped body.

question: Identify the animal that does NOT have bilateral symmetry.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cnidarian.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

• They are radially symmetrical, meaning their body parts are arranged around a central axis like the spokes of a wheel.
 
• The absence of bilateral symmetry in cnidarians is due to their simple body plan

question: Which group of Kingdom Animalia has unsegmented, bilaterally symmetrical, soft bodies, with a triploblastic construction (comprising three layers of cells) and a lacking coelom, skeleton, and anus?
solution:
The correct answer is **__Platyhelminthes.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Platyhelminthes are also known as flatworms.
 
• **Flatworms have unsegmented, bilaterally symmetrical, soft bodies, with a triploblastic construction (comprising three layers of cells) and a lacking coelom, skeleton, and anus.**
 
• Example includes Planaria, Liver fluke (Fasciola hepatica), and Tapeworm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cnidaria includes jellyfish, corals, and sea anemones.**

 
 
• **They have radial symmetry, a single body opening, and stinging cells called cnidocytes.**
 
 
 
• **Ctenophora includes comb jellies.**
 
 
• **They have radial symmetry and cilia for movement but also have a complete digestive system.**
 
 
 
• **Porifera includes sponges.**
 
 
• **They have asymmetrical or radial symmetry, no true tissues, and filter food through pores in their bodies.**

question: Sporophyte stage is dominant in which plant group?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vascular plants.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **sporophyte stage** is the dominant phase in** vascular plants,** which includes all plants **except bryophytes **(mosses, liverworts, and hornworts).
 
• In **bryophytes,** the **gametophyte stage** is the dominant phase, while the **sporophyte** is dependent on the gametophyte for **survival. **
 
• **Algae **do not have a well-defined **alternation of generations,** and their life cycles can vary greatly depending on the type of algae.
 
• **Pteridophytes**, which include** ferns and horsetails, **have a **dominant sporophyte stage** that is independent of the gametophyte.
 
• The** dominance of the sporophyte stage** is characterized by the fact that it is the stage that produces the** spores,** which give rise to the next generation of plants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bryophytes **are small,** non-vascular plants** that grow in damp habitats.

 
 
• They** do not** have true roots, stems, or leaves and rely on diffusion to transport water and nutrients.
 
 
 
• **Algae **are a diverse group of **aquatic organisms** that can range from **single-celled organisms** to large seaweeds.
 
 
• They are not considered to be** true plants **because they **lack specialized tissues and organs.**
 
 
 
• **Pteridophytes** are** vascular plants **that reproduce by **spores **instead of seeds.
 
 
• They have** true roots, stems, and leaves,** and can range from small herbaceous plants to large tree ferns.
 
 
 
• The **alternation of generations** is a life cycle that includes both a **haploid (n) gametophyte and a diploid (2n)** sporophyte stage.
 
 
• In plants, the gametophyte produces **gametes (eggs and sperm),** which fuse to form a **diploid zygote** that develops into the sporophyte.
 
• The sporophyte produces **spores,** which give rise to the next generation of gametophytes.

question: Identify an organism that exhibits metagenesis.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Obelia.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Metagenesis **refers to a type of **alternation of generations** where the **life cycle of an organism** involves both **sexual and asexual **reproduction.
 
• In this process, the offspring of the sexual phase undergo a phase of** asexual reproduction** before they mature into the** sexual phase.**
 
• **Obelia **is a genus of **colonial hydrozoans **that exhibit metagenesis.
 
• They have a complex life cycle that involves both **polyp and medusa stages**, and the polyps undergo asexual reproduction to produce medusae.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Spongilla** is a genus of **freshwater sponges** that do not exhibit metagenesis.

 
 
• They reproduce **sexually **by releasing sperm and eggs into the water, which then develop into** larvae **that settle and grow into adult sponges.
 
 
 
• **Sycon** is a genus of **calcareous sponges** that do not exhibit metagenesis.
 
 
• They reproduce **sexually **by releasing sperm and eggs into the water, which then develop into **free-swimming larvae **that settle and grow into adult sponges.
 
 
 
• **Euspongia **is a genus of **marine sponges** that do not exhibit metagenesis.
 
 
• They reproduce sexually by releasing **sperm and eggs i**nto the water, which then develop into **free-swimming larvae** that settle and grow into adult sponges.

• This is a type of** non-vascular plant** that grows in damp habitats such as** forests, bogs, and riverbanks.**
 
• They are commonly found in** temperate and tropical regions** and play an important role in soil formation and nutrient cycling.
 
 
 
• **Phaeophyceae:**
 
 
• This is a **class of brown algae** that are **predominantly marine** and are commonly found in **temperate and cold waters.**
 
• They are important** primary producers in coastal ecosystems **and are also used by humans for food and other purposes.

question: Which of the following statements best defines the monoecious?

options.text: A flower with both androecium and gynoecium

solution:
The correct answer is __**A flower with both androecium and gynoecium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Monoecious plants** have both male (androecium) and female (gynoecium) reproductive organs in the same plant.
 
• This characteristic allows monoecious plants to self-pollinate, although cross-pollination can also occur.
 
• Examples of monoecious plants include maize, cucumbers, and squash.
 
• Monoecious plants are different from dioecious plants, which have male and female reproductive organs on separate plants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Androecium**

 
 
• The androecium is the male reproductive part of a flower.
 
• It consists of stamens, each of which has a filament topped by an anther where pollen is produced.
 
 
 
• **Gynoecium**
 
 
• The gynoecium is the female reproductive part of a flower.
 
• It consists of one or more carpels, each containing an ovary, style, and stigma.
 
• The ovary contains ovules, which develop into seeds upon fertilization.
 
 
 
• **Dioecious**
 
 
• Dioecious plants have male and female reproductive organs on separate plants.
 
• This means that a dioecious plant is either male or female, not both.
 
• Examples of dioecious plants include holly, willow, and asparagus.
 
 
 
• **Pollination**
 
 
• Pollination is the process by which pollen is transferred from the male part of a plant to the female part, allowing fertilization to occur.
 
• Pollination can be carried out by wind, water, insects, birds, and other animals.
 
• Self-pollination occurs within the same flower or plant, while cross-pollination occurs between different plants.

question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECT regarding the grade of organisation and its example?
solution:
The correct answer is **Tissue-organ grade organisation - Euplectella**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cellular grade organisation** refers to a level of organization where cells are functionally differentiated but do not form tissues. Sycon is an example of this grade.
 
• **Protoplasmic grade organisation** is the simplest level of organisation where all life functions are confined within a single cell. Paramecium is an example of this grade.
 
• **Cell-tissue grade organisation** involves groups of similar cells performing a common function. Jellyfish represent this grade.
 
• **Tissue-organ grade organisation** refers to tissues grouped into organs, each performing different functions.** **
 
 
• ​**Euplectella** (Venus's flower basket) is a type of glass **sponge** and does not exhibit tissue-organ grade organization. Instead, it is an example of cellular grade organization, characteristic of Porifera (sponges), where the organization is primarily at the cellular level and not organized into true tissues and organs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cellular Grade Organisation**

 
 
• This refers to organisms whose body is made up of cells that are functionally differentiated but do not form true tissues.
 
• Sponges (Porifera) like Sycon exhibit this type of organisation.
 
• These organisms have a simple body structure with cells specialized for different functions such as feeding, reproduction, and protection.
 
 
 
• **Protoplasmic Grade Organisation**
 
 
• It is the simplest level of organization where all life functions occur within a single cell.
 
• Protozoans like Paramecium demonstrate this type of organization.
 
• These organisms are unicellular and perform all necessary life processes within one cell.
 
 
 
• **Cell-Tissue Grade Organisation**
 
 
• Organisms with this level of organisation have cells grouped into tissues.
 
• Coelenterates, such as jellyfish, exhibit this type of organisation.
 
• These organisms have more complex structures with different tissues performing various functions.
 
 
 
• **Tissue-Organ Grade Organisation**
 
 
• This level of organisation involves tissues grouped into organs, each performing specific functions.
 
• Euplectella, a genus of glass sponges, is an example of cellular grade organisation grade.

question: Which species is known as black lipped pearl oyster found in the Indo-Pacific, within tropical coral reefs?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pinctada margaritiferau**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pinctada margaritifera**, commonly known as the **black-lipped pearl oyster**, is a bivalve mollusc belonging to the family **Pteriidae**
 
• It is **widely distributed in the Indo-Pacific region, particularly within tropical coral reef ecosystems.**
 
• These **environments provide the optimal conditions for its survival, including warm water temperatures and an abundance of plankton for food.**
 
• The term **"black-lipped" refers to the distinct dark colouration found on the inner edges of its shell.**
 
• This **feature distinguishes it from other pearl oysters.**
 
• This species is particularly valued in the pearl industry as it is a primary producer of high-quality Tahitian black pearls, which are renowned for their unique colours and lustre.
 
• Like** other bivalves, it filters water for food, contributing to the clarity and health of its marine environment.**
 
• It also serves as a habitat for various small marine organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aplysia dactylomela:**

 
 
• Also known as the spotted sea hare, it is a sea slug.
 
• These animals are known for their soft, wrinkled bodies, which can have various colours and patterns, including spots.
 
• They **have a distinct head region with tentacles, and their bodies are somewhat flattened.**
 
 
 
• **Dentalium neohexagonum:**
 
 
• **A species of scaphopod mollusk, also known as a tusk shell**
 
• Scaphopods are marine molluscs that have tubular, tapered shells that are open at both ends.
 
• **These shells resemble the shape of an elephant’s tusk, which is how they got the name "tusk shell."**
 
 
 
• **Chatepleura apiculata:**
 
 
• **A type of chiton, which is a class of mollumolluscs **that cling to rocks in intertidal zones
 
• *Chatepleura apiculata* is a small, e**longated gastropod with a conical, smooth shell,** although its size and appearance can vary depending on its environment and the host it attaches to.

question: Which of the following categories does Gonyaulax belong to?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dinoflagellates**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gonyaulax is a genus of dinoflagellates, which are a type of plankton found in marine and freshwater environments.
 
• Dinoflagellates are characterized by their two flagella that allow them to move through the water.
 
• Many dinoflagellates, including Gonyaulax, are bioluminescent and can produce light through chemical reactions within their cells.
 
• Gonyaulax species are often associated with harmful algal blooms, sometimes referred to as "red tides," which can produce toxins harmful to marine life and humans.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Euglenoids**

 
 
• Euglenoids are a group of single-celled organisms that have characteristics of both plants and animals.
 
• They are primarily found in freshwater environments and are known for their ability to photosynthesize using chloroplasts.
 
• Euglena is a well-known example of euglenoids.
 
 
 
• **Chrysophytes**
 
 
• Chrysophytes, also known as golden algae, are a group of algae found in both freshwater and marine environments.
 
• They have a distinctive golden-brown color due to the presence of pigments like carotenoids and xanthophylls.
 
• Chrysophytes can be unicellular or form colonies.
 
 
 
• **Protozoans**
 
 
• Protozoans are a diverse group of single-celled eukaryotic organisms that are primarily heterotrophic.
 
• They can be free-living or parasitic and are found in a variety of environments, including soil, water, and inside other organisms.
 
• Examples of protozoans include amoebas, paramecia, and plasmodia.
 
 
 
• **Dinoflagellates**
 
 
• Dinoflagellates are a group of single-celled organisms that are part of the plankton community.
 
• They possess two flagella which help in their locomotion.
 
• Some dinoflagellates are photosynthetic, while others are heterotrophic.
 
• They play a crucial role in marine ecosystems and can cause harmful algal blooms.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Nucleus: Lipid metabolism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The nucleus is the control center of the cell, storing the cell's DNA and coordinating cellular activities such as growth, metabolism, and reproduction.
 
• Lipid metabolism is primarily associated with the smooth endoplasmic reticulum and not the nucleus.
 
• The nucleus is responsible for the transcription of DNA to mRNA, which is then translated into proteins by ribosomes.
 
• The nucleus also contains the nucleolus, which is involved in ribosome synthesis and assembly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lysosomes:**

 
 
• Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles that contain enzymes to break down biomolecules.
 
• They are often referred to as the "suicidal bags" of the cell because they can digest cellular components when the cell is damaged.
 
• They play a key role in the degradation and recycling of cellular waste, cellular signaling, and energy metabolism.
 
 
 
• **Mitochondria:**
 
 
• Mitochondria are known as the "powerhouses of the cell" because they generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• They are involved in other processes such as signaling, cellular differentiation, and cell death, as well as the control of the cell cycle and cell growth.
 
• Mitochondria have their own DNA and are thought to have originated from ancestral prokaryotes through endosymbiosis.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes:**
 
 
• Ribosomes are the molecular machines responsible for protein synthesis.
 
• They translate messenger RNA (mRNA) into amino acid sequences to build proteins.
 
• Ribosomes can be found floating freely in the cytoplasm or bound to the endoplasmic reticulum, forming the rough ER.
 
• They are made up of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins and consist of two subunits, a large and a small one.

question: What do we mean by Allen’s rule?

options.text: Mammals from colder climates generally have shorter ears and limbs to minimise heat loss.
Desert lizards lack the physiological ability that mammals have to deal with the high temperatures of their habitat.
Some plants have no leaves – they are reduced to spines – and the photosynthetic function is taken over by the flattened stems.
The body compensates low oxygen availability by increasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing the breathing rate.

solution:

__
 
• Allen's Rule is a principle in biology which suggests that animals living in colder regions tend to have shorter appendages (such as ears, tails, and limbs) to conserve body heat, while animals in warmer climates tend to have longer appendages to dissipate excess heat. 
 
• This adaptation helps maintain thermal balance by reducing the surface area through which heat can be lost in colder environments and increasing it in hotter environments to release heat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Statement 3 
 
 
• Refers to adaptations in desert plants, such as succulents, not Allen's Rule.
 
 
 
• Statement 4

question: The organisms that do not have a defined nucleus or organelles are classified in to ______ Kingdom.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Monera**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Monera kingdom:

 
 
• These organisms lack a defined nucleus or organelles and none of them has multicellular bodies.
 
• Some of them have cell walls while some do not.
 
• This group of species may either synthesize their own food (autotrophic) or obtain it from the environment (heterotrophic).
 
• Bacteria, blue-green algae (cyanobacteria), and mycoplasma are examples.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Fungi kingdom:

 
 
• These are heterotrophic eukaryotic organisms. 
 
• Some of them are known as saprotrophs, which feed on decaying organic matter.
 
• Others feed on the living protoplasm of a host organism. They are called parasites.
 
• Many of them have the capacity to become multicellular organisms at certain stages in their lives.
 
• Their cell walls are made of chitin, a tough complex sugar.
 
• Examples are yeasts, moulds, and mushrooms.
 
 
 
• **Protista** kingdom
 
 
• Protista kingdom single-celled eukaryotes.
 
• Characteristics of Protista are given bellow:
 
 
• Unicellular organism.
 
• Normally aquatic.
 
• Reproduction: Asexual & sexual.
 
• Well defined nucleus & membrane-bounded organelles.
 
 
 
• Group of Protista are given bellow:
 
 
• Prokaryotic: Dinoflagellate, Diatoms, Euglenoids.
 
• Consumer: Slime moulds, Myxomycetes.
 
• Protozoans: Slime moulds, Myxomycetes.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Plantae**
 
 
• Kingdom plantae includes all eukaryotic, chlorophyll-containing organisms called plants.
 
• Some of these members are primarily heterotrophic, such as insectivorous plants or parasites.
 
• Kingdom plantae is divided into 5 major divisions:
 
 
• Algae (Thallophyta)
 
• Bryophytes
 
• Pteridophytes
 
• Gymnosperms and
 
• Angiosperms
 
 
 
• 
 
Algae (Thallophyta)

 
 
• Algae are chlorophyll-containing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic (both freshwater and marine) organisms.
 
• Algae are self-feeders.
 
• 
 
Bryophytes

 
 
• The bryophytes are generally classified into two main groups
 
• Liverworts
 
 
• Liverworts usually grow in moist, shady places such as banks of streams, marshy ground, damp soil, the bark of trees, and deep in the woods.
 
 
 
• Mosses
 
 
• Mosses grow in dense mats over moist shady places, especially during rainy seasons.
 
 
 
• 
 
Pteridophytes

 
 
• Pteridophytes are primitive seedless vascular plants also called cryptogams.
 
• The pteridophytes are found in cool, damp shady places though some may flourish well in sandy-soil conditions.
 
• 
 
Gymnosperms

 
 
• Gymnosperms are vascular plants having naked seeds.
 
• The gymnosperms are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation.
 
• 
 
Angiosperms

 
 
• Angiosperms are seed bearing plants or flowering plants.
 
• Unlike gymnosperms where the ovules are naked, in angiosperms the sporophylls are organized into flowers and seeds are produced inside fruits,

question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Starch: Egg yolk**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Starch is a carbohydrate consisting of a large number of glucose units joined by glycosidic bonds.
 
• It is produced by most green plants as an energy store.
 
• Egg yolk does not contain starch; it is rich in proteins and fats.
 
• Common sources of starch include potatoes, rice, wheat, and corn.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lactose**

 
 
• Lactose is a disaccharide sugar derived from galactose and glucose that is found in milk.
 
• It makes up around 2-8% of milk (by weight).
 
• Lactose is important for the proper digestion of milk in mammals.
 
 
 
• **Fructose**
 
 
• Fructose is a simple sugar found in many plants, where it is often bonded to glucose to form the disaccharide sucrose.
 
• It is one of the three dietary monosaccharides, along with glucose and galactose, that are absorbed directly into the bloodstream during digestion.
 
• Fructose is commonly found in fruits such as grapes, apples, and honey.
 
 
 
• **Maltose**
 
 
• Maltose, also known as malt sugar, is a disaccharide formed from two units of glucose joined with an α(1→4) bond.
 
• It is found in germinating grains like wheat, cornmeal, and barley.
 
• Maltose is used in the brewing of beer and is a component of malt.

question: Which of the following is NOT related to reticulate venation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maize**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Maize** exhibits parallel venation, which is typical of monocotyledonous plants.
 
• In parallel venation, veins run parallel to each other, which is different from reticulate venation where veins form a network.
 
• Examples of plants with parallel venation include grasses, lilies, and maize.
 
• Reticulate venation is commonly found in dicotyledonous plants like China rose and Tulsi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Venation**

 
 
• Venation refers to the arrangement of veins in the leaf blade.
 
• It is important for the identification of plant species and helps in the distribution of nutrients and water throughout the leaf.
 
 
 
• **Reticulate Venation**
 
 
• Reticulate venation is characterized by a net-like pattern of veins.
 
• It is commonly found in dicots such as China rose, Tulsi, and Coriander.
 
• In this type of venation, the main vein (midrib) branches into secondary veins which further branch into tertiary veins forming a network.
 
 
 
• **Parallel Venation**
 
 
• Parallel venation is characterized by veins running parallel to each other.
 
• It is typical of monocots such as Maize, wheat, and other grasses.
 
• In this type of venation, veins do not form a network but run parallel from the base to the tip of the leaf.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Plants**
 
 
• **China Rose (Hibiscus rosa-sinensis)** - Exhibits reticulate venation.
 
• **Tulsi (Ocimum tenuiflorum)** - Exhibits reticulate venation.
 
• **Maize (Zea mays)** - Exhibits parallel venation.
 
• **Coriander (Coriandrum sativum)** - Exhibits reticulate venation.

question: Who published Systema Naturae in 1735 classifying the three kingdoms of nature and outlining the sexual system for the classification of plants?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Carolus Linnaeus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Carolus Linnaeus, also known as Carl Linnaeus or Carl von Linné, was a Swedish botanist, zoologist, and physician.
 
• He published the landmark book "Systema Naturae" in 1735, which laid the foundations for the modern biological naming scheme of binomial nomenclature.
 
• Linnaeus classified nature into three kingdoms: animal, vegetable, and mineral, and introduced the sexual system for the classification of plants.
 
• His work in "Systema Naturae" is considered one of the most significant contributions to the field of taxonomy and systematics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Systema Naturae**

 
 
• Systema Naturae is one of the major works of Carl Linnaeus and was first published in 1735.
 
• It introduced a hierarchical classification system, which is the basis for the modern system of taxonomy.
 
• The book included a classification of all known plants, animals, and minerals, and established the use of binomial nomenclature, where each species is given a two-part Latin name (genus and species).
 
• The sexual system of plant classification was based on the number and arrangement of reproductive organs (stamens and pistils).
 
 
 
• **Binomial Nomenclature**
 
 
• Binomial nomenclature is a formal system of naming species of living things by giving each a name composed of two parts, both of which use Latin grammatical forms.
 
• The first part of the name identifies the genus to which the species belongs, and the second part identifies the species within the genus.
 
• This system was developed by Carolus Linnaeus and is used universally in the scientific community.
 
 
 
• **Taxonomy**
 
 
• Taxonomy is the science of defining and naming groups of biological organisms based on shared characteristics.
 
• Organisms are grouped into taxa, which are then grouped into larger taxa, creating a hierarchical structure.
 
• Linnaeus' classification system included ranks such as kingdom, class, order, family, genus, and species, which are still used today.
 
 
 
• **Sexual System**
 
 
• The sexual system was a method of classifying plants based on the number and arrangement of their reproductive organs.
 
• This system was part of Linnaeus' work in "Systema Naturae" and was revolutionary at the time, providing a clear and structured way to classify plants.

question: By which of the following methods do red algae reproduce?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Fragmentation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fragmentation is a form of asexual reproduction where the parent organism breaks into fragments, and each fragment can grow into a new organism.
 
• Red algae, which are primarily aquatic organisms, commonly reproduce by fragmentation.
 
• This method of reproduction ensures that red algae can quickly colonize an area, especially when conditions are favorable.
 
• Fragmentation in red algae can occur naturally due to water currents, or it can be induced by external factors such as being grazed by herbivores.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Grafting**

 
 
• Grafting is a horticultural technique where tissues from one plant are inserted into those of another so that the two sets of vascular tissues may join together.
 
• It is commonly used in agriculture and horticulture to propagate clones of desired plants.
 
 
 
• **Cutting**
 
 
• Cutting is a method of plant propagation where a piece of the plant, typically a stem or leaf, is cut and placed in a suitable environment to grow into a new plant.
 
• It is widely used for the propagation of houseplants and garden plants.
 
 
 
• **Micropropagation**
 
 
• Micropropagation is a method used to multiply plants under sterile conditions, often from very small plant parts, such as cells or tissues.
 
• It is used for the rapid multiplication of plants and the production of disease-free plants.
 
 
 
• **Fragmentation**
 
 
• As mentioned, fragmentation is a form of asexual reproduction where an organism is split into fragments, each capable of growing independently into a new organism.
 
• It is a common method of reproduction in many algae, including red algae, as well as in some plants and fungi.

question: Which types of gametes are found in Spirogyra?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Isogamous and non-flagellated**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Spirogyra** is a genus of filamentous green algae that is commonly found in fresh water.

• The gametes in Spirogyra are **isogamous**, meaning they are morphologically similar or identical.

• Isogamous gametes in Spirogyra are **non-flagellated**, meaning they do not have flagella and thus do not have the ability to move independently.

• During reproduction, Spirogyra undergoes a process called **conjugation**, where gametes from different filaments join together to form a zygote.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Isogamy:** 

• Isogamy refers to a type of sexual reproduction involving gametes of similar morphology (shape and size), differing only in their allelic composition.

• In isogamous species, the gametes are often referred to as "+" and "-" types rather than male and female.

• **Flagella:**

• Flagella are long, whip-like appendages that protrude from the cell body and enable many protozoa, bacteria, and spermatozoa to swim.

• Non-flagellated gametes lack these appendages and thus rely on other means for movement, such as water currents.

• **Conjugation in Spirogyra:**

• Conjugation in Spirogyra is a form of sexual reproduction where two filaments align side by side and form conjugation tubes.

• Protoplasts from one filament move through these tubes and fuse with the protoplasts of the other filament to form zygospores.

• Zygospores are thick-walled and can survive harsh conditions. Upon germination, they undergo meiosis to produce new haploid filaments.

• **Spirogyra:**

• Spirogyra is known for its spiral arrangement of chloroplasts, which is unique and easily identifiable.

• It is commonly referred to as "pond scum" and can form dense mats on the surface of freshwater bodies.

• Spirogyra plays an important role in the ecosystem by producing oxygen through photosynthesis and serving as food for aquatic organisms.

question: Which of the following classes includes the family of turtles?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Reptilia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Turtles belong to the class **Reptilia**, which also includes snakes, lizards, and crocodiles.
 
• Reptiles are characterized by their **cold-blooded metabolism**, scaly skin, and the laying of eggs with leathery shells.
 
• Turtles have a distinctive feature known as a **shell**, which is developed from their ribs and acts as a shield.
 
• Most reptiles, including turtles, are **ectothermic** (rely on external sources of temperature to regulate their body heat).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chondrichthyes**

 
 
• Chondrichthyes is a class that includes **cartilaginous fishes** such as sharks, rays, and skates.
 
• These fishes have a skeleton made of cartilage rather than bone.
 
• They are characterized by having paired fins, paired nostrils, scales, a heart with its chambers in series, and skeletons made of cartilage.
 
 
 
• **Amphibia**
 
 
• Amphibia is a class that includes **amphibians** such as frogs, toads, salamanders, and newts.
 
• Amphibians are characterized by their ability to live both in water and on land.
 
• They have a life cycle that includes both an aquatic larval stage and a terrestrial adult stage.
 
• Amphibians have moist, permeable skin that assists in respiration.
 
 
 
• **Aves**
 
 
• Aves is a class that includes **birds**.
 
• Birds are characterized by their feathers, beaks, and laying of hard-shelled eggs.
 
• They have a high metabolic rate, a four-chambered heart, and a lightweight but strong skeleton.
 
• Most birds are capable of flight, though some species are flightless.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Pteropus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pteropus** is a genus of bats commonly known as flying foxes or fruit bats.
 
• They are the largest bats in the world, with some species having a wingspan of up to 1.5 meters.
 
• Pteropus species are primarily found in tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, Australia, East Africa, and some oceanic islands.
 
• These bats are not classified under the class Aves (birds) but belong to the order Chiroptera in the class Mammalia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aves (Birds)**

 
 
• Aves is a class of vertebrates that includes all birds.
 
• Birds are characterized by feathers, a beak without teeth, the laying of hard-shelled eggs, a high metabolic rate, a four-chambered heart, and a strong yet lightweight skeleton.
 
• Examples of birds include species like Psittacula (parrots), Neophron (vultures), and Struthio (ostriches).
 
 
 
• **Psittacula**
 
 
• Psittacula is a genus of parrots, commonly known as parakeets.
 
• They are characterized by their bright plumage and strong, curved beaks.
 
• These birds are primarily found in Asia and Africa.
 
 
 
• **Neophron**
 
 
• Neophron is a genus of vultures, commonly known as the Egyptian vulture.
 
• They are scavengers and are known for their distinctive bald heads and hooked beaks.
 
• These birds are found in Europe, Asia, and Africa.
 
 
 
• **Struthio**
 
 
• Struthio is a genus of birds that includes the ostrich.

• They are native to Africa and are the largest and heaviest living birds.

question: Which of the following sets of locations in India is known for having significant coral reef ecosystems?

options.text: Bay of Bengal coast and deltas
East coast of India near major river mouths
​Gulf of Kutch, Gulf of Mannar, Lakshadweep, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands
Deep-sea trenches in the Indian Ocean

solution:
The correct answer is __**Gulf of Kutch, Gulf of Mannar, Lakshadweep, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Coral reefs in India** are primarily found in tropical and subtropical regions and are biodiversity hotspots that support a wide range of marine life.
 
• The major coral reef ecosystems in India are located in the **Gulf of Kutch** (western India), **Gulf of Mannar** (southeastern India), the **Lakshadweep Islands**, and the **Andaman & Nicobar Islands**.
 
• The **Gulf of Mannar** hosts fringing reefs and supports one of the richest marine biodiversity hotspots in India.
 
• The **Lakshadweep Islands** are known for their atolls and coral lagoons, which provide habitat for various marine species.
 
• The **Andaman & Nicobar Islands** support fringing and barrier reefs, contributing significantly to India’s coral reef biodiversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bay of Bengal coast and deltas**

 
 
• The Bay of Bengal coast and deltas are primarily known for their mangroves, such as the Sundarbans, which is one of the largest mangrove forests in the world.
 
• While these areas are rich in biodiversity, they are not significant locations for coral reef ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **East coast of India near major river mouths**
 
 
• The east coast of India, especially near river mouths like the Ganges and Mahanadi, is dominated by sedimentation, making it unsuitable for the growth of coral reefs.
 
• Instead, these regions are better known for their estuarine ecosystems and mangrove forests.
 
 
 
• **Deep-sea trenches in the Indian Ocean**
 
 
• Deep-sea trenches in the Indian Ocean are not suitable for coral reef growth as corals require sunlight for photosynthesis, which is facilitated by their symbiotic relationship with zooxanthellae algae.
 
• These trenches are characterized by extreme depths and pressures.

question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding plants?

options.text: Roots take water from the soil
Phloem tubes of cells specialized for water transport
Chlorophyll, the green pigment in the leaves, absorbs light
Stomata are the little pores in the leaves required for gaseous exchange

solution:
The correct answer is __**Phloem tubes of cells specialized for water transport**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Roots take water from the soil:** This statement is correct. Roots are specialized structures in plants that absorb water and nutrients from the soil. The water is then transported upward through the xylem tissue to other parts of the plant.

• **Phloem tubes of cells specialized for water transport:** This statement is incorrect. Phloem is responsible for transporting food (mainly sugar) produced during photosynthesis from leaves to other parts of the plant. Water transport is carried out by the xylem tissue, not phloem. Hence, this option is incorrect.

• **Chlorophyll, the green pigment in the leaves, absorbs light:** This statement is correct. Chlorophyll is a vital pigment found in chloroplasts of plant cells. It absorbs light, primarily in the blue and red wavelengths, to carry out photosynthesis by converting light energy into chemical energy.

• **Stomata are the little pores in the leaves required for gaseous exchange:** This statement is correct. Stomata are tiny openings present on the surface of leaves that facilitate gaseous exchange, allowing oxygen to exit and carbon dioxide to enter for photosynthesis. They also play a role in transpiration.

• ***Hence, the correct answer is Phloem tubes of cells specialized for water transport.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Xylem vs. Phloem:**

• **Xylem:** Responsible for transporting water and dissolved minerals from roots to other parts of the plant. It consists of vessels and tracheids, which are specialized cells for water conduction.

• **Phloem:** Transports organic nutrients, especially sucrose, from leaves (where photosynthesis occurs) to other parts of the plant. It consists of sieve tubes and companion cells.

• **Water transport mechanism:**

• Water is absorbed by roots through osmosis and transported upward via capillary action in the xylem.

• The transpiration process creates a suction force, pulling water upward through the plant.

• **Photosynthesis:**

• Chlorophyll absorbs light energy and uses it to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.

• This process occurs in the chloroplasts, primarily in leaf cells.

• **Stomata and transpiration:**

• Stomata regulate the exchange of gases (CO₂ and O₂) and water vapor through the process of transpiration.

• They are controlled by guard cells, which open and close the stomatal pores depending on environmental conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Functions of Xylem and Phloem:**

• **Xylem:** One-way transport system for water and minerals from roots to leaves.

• **Phloem:** Bidirectional transport system for nutrients between leaves and other parts of the plant.

• **Role of chlorophyll:**

• Chlorophyll absorbs light most efficiently in the blue and red wavelengths, making leaves appear green due to the reflection of green light.

• It is essential for converting light energy into glucose during photosynthesis.

• **Stomatal regulation:**

• Stomata play a key role in maintaining plant water balance and enabling photosynthesis.

• Environmental factors like humidity, temperature, and light intensity affect stomatal opening and closing.

</ul

question: Which of the following does **NOT **figure among the main functions of the root system of a plant?

options.text: Absorption of water from the soil
Absorption of mineral from the soil
Providing a proper anchorage to the plant parts
Supply of food to plant parts

solution:
The correct answer is __**Supply of food to plant parts**__.

__
 
• **The supply of food to plant parts is not the main function of the root system of a plant**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Plants have specialized organs that help them survive and reproduce in a great diversity of habitats. The major organs of most plants include roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• Roots are important organs in all vascular plants.
 
 
• Most vascular plants have two types of roots: primary roots that grow downward and secondary roots that branch out to the side.
 
• Together, all the roots of a plant make up a root system.
 
 
 
• A root is a complex organ consisting of several types of tissue. The structure of roots helps them perform their primary functions, which are-
 
 
• **Absorbing water and minerals**
 
 
• Thin-walled epidermal cells and root hairs are well suited to absorb water and dissolved minerals from the soil. The roots of many plants also have a mycorrhizal relationship with fungi for greater absorption.
 
 
 
• **Anchoring and supporting the plant**
 
 
• Root systems help anchor plants to the ground, allowing plants to grow tall without toppling over. A tough covering may replace the epidermis in older roots, making them ropelike and even stronger.
 
 
 
• **Storing food**
 
 
• In many plants, ground tissues in roots store food produced by the leaves during photosynthesis. The bloodroot stores food in its roots over the winter.

subject: GK
question: Productivity of an ecosystem is composed of which of the following?

options.text: Net prime productivity and gross prime productivity

solution:
The correct answer is __**Net primary productivity and gross primary productivity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Primary production **is defined as the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis.
 
• It is expressed in terms of **gm–² yr –¹ or (kcal m–² ) yr –¹ **to compare the productivity of different ecosystems
 
• It can be divided into **gross primary productivity (GPP)** and** net primary productivity (NPP)**.
 
• The gross primary productivity of an ecosystem is the** rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis**
 
• Net primary productivity, or NPP, is gross primary productivity **excluding the rate of energy loss to metabolism and maintenance**.
 
• Net primary productivity is the rate at which energy is stored as biomass by plants or other primary producers and made available to consumers.
 
• **GPP – R = NPP** ( R represents the Respiration losses)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Primary productivity depends on the plant species inhabiting a particular area.
 
• **Secondary productivity **is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.
 
• The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately **170 billion tons** (dry weight) of organic matter.
 
• Despite occupying about **70 per cent of the surface**, the productivity of the oceans is only **55 billion tons**.

• **Stomata**

 
 
• In leaves transpiration takes place through **stomata**.
 
• The little **apertures** known as stomata are found on the **epidermis of leaves**.
 
• **Stomata** are visible under a **light microscope.**
 
• Stomata can be found on the **stems and other portions** of various plants.
 
• In **gaseous exchange and photosynthesis,** stomata are crucial. Via opening and closing, they regulate the **rate of transpiration.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Water is lost from the **aerial regions of plants **in the form of water vapour through a **biological process called transpiration.**
 
• Like all other living things, plants need an **excretory system** to remove extra water from their bodies.
 
• **Transpiration** is the term for this process of removing extra water from the body of the plant. Typically, it is the** evaporation of water from the leaf surface.**
 
• The plants only use a small portion of the water they absorb for **growth and development**.

question: Most of the Chlorophyceae have one or more storage bodies called _______ located in the chloroplasts.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pyrenoids**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pyrenoids**

 
 
• Pyrenoid is a protein-rich body found in the members of Chlorophyceae or green algae. It is used for the storage of reserved food material.
 
• It may be one to many in number in different species of algae.
 
• The chloroplast is a double membrane-bound cell organelle.
 
• Out of the two membranes, the inner membrane is relatively less permeable (the outer membrane contains porins)
 
• The number & shape of chloroplast also varies from one species of algae to another.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Stomata ​

 
 
• Stomata are the tiny pores on the leaves which play a major role in the exchange of gases.
 
• The intake of carbon dioxide and the outtake of oxygen both takes place through these pores.
 
• The respiration in leaves takes place through these tiny pores.
 
• Evaporation of water from the leaf surface occurs through the stomata.
 
• Thus, the stomata help in the process of transpiration.
 
• It also closes or opens its pores based on climatic conditions to maintain the moisture balance.
 
• It remains open during the day and closed at night. This closure at night prevents water from escaping through open pores.
 
 

 
• **Carotenoids**

 
 
• arotenoids also called tetraterpenoids, are yellow, orange, and red organic pigments__ that are produced by plants and algae, as well as several bacteria and fungi.
 
• Carotenoids give the characteristic color to pumpkins, carrots, corn, tomatoes, canaries, flamingos, salmon, lobster, shrimp, and daffodils.
 
 
 
• **Chlorophyll**
 
 
• **​**Chlorophyll or leaf green is a porphyrin derivative with magnesium (Mg) as the central atom and is hence a metal complex dye.
 
• It is present in the chloroplasts in all green parts of plants as a mixture of blue-green chlorophyll a and yellow-green chlorophyll b and constitutes the catalyst for photosynthesis.
 
• Chlorophylls are porphyrins, whose molecules contain a flat ring of four-linked heterocyclic groups, based upon magnesium.
 
• Chlorophyll is a green photosynthetic pigment found in plants, algae, and cyanobacteria.

subject: GK
question: Microbes like Rhizobium, Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter are used for:
solution:
The correct answer is __**nitrogen cycling**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 Nitrogen Cycle-

 
 
• Nitrogen is an essential constituent of protein and is a basic building block of all living tissue. It constitutes nearly 16% by weight of all the proteins that is, converted to ammonia, nitrites or nitrates before it can be taken up by plants.
 
• Nitrogen fixation on earth is accomplished in three different ways:

 a) By microorganisms (bacteria and blue-green algae)

 b) By man using industrial processes (fertilizer factories) and

 c) To a limited extent by atmospheric phenomena such as thunder and lighting
 
• Certain microorganisms are capable of fixing atmospheric nitrogen into ammonium ions. These include free-living nitrifying bacteria (e.g. aerobic Azotobacter and anaerobic Clostridium) and symbiotic nitrifying bacteria living in association with leguminous plants and symbiotic bacteria living in non-leguminous root nodule plants (e.g. Rhizobium) as well as blue-green algae (e.g. Anabaena, Spirulina).
 
• Ammonium ions can be directly taken up as a source of nitrogen by some plants, or are oxidized to nitrites or nitrates by two groups of specialised bacteria: Nitrosomonas bacteria promote the transformation of ammonia into nitrite. Nitrite is then further transformed into nitrate by the bacteria Nitrobacter.
 
• The nitrates synthesised by bacteria in the soil are taken up by plants and converted into amino acids, which are the building blocks of proteins. These then go through higher trophic levels of the ecosystem. During excretion and upon the death of all organisms nitrogen is returned to the soil in the form of ammonia.
 
• Certain quantities of soil nitrates, being highly soluble in water, are lost to the system by being transported away by surface run-off or groundwater. In the soil as well as oceans there are special denitrifying bacteria (e.g. Pseudomonas), which convert the nitrates/nitrites to elemental nitrogen. This nitrogen escapes into the atmosphere, thus completing the cycle.
 
• The periodic thunderstorms convert the gaseous nitrogen in the atmosphere to ammonia and nitrates which eventually reach the earth’s surface through precipitation and then into the soil to be utilized by plants.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Carbon Cycle

 
 
• The carbon cycle involves several processes, including photosynthesis, respiration, decomposition, and combustion. Plants absorb carbon dioxide (CO₂) during photosynthesis, while animals release CO₂ through respiration.
 
• Carbon is stored in various reservoirs, including the atmosphere (as CO₂), oceans (as dissolved CO₂ and organic carbon), soil (as organic matter), and living organisms. These reservoirs play a crucial role in regulating global climate.
 
• Human activities, such as fossil fuel combustion and deforestation, significantly alter the carbon cycle by increasing atmospheric CO₂ levels, contributing to global warming and climate change.​
 
 
 
• Water Cycle-
 
 
• The hydrologic cycle is the continuous circulation of water in the Earth-atmosphere system which is driven by solar energy. Water on our planet is stored in major reservoirs like atmosphere, oceans, lakes, rivers, soils, glaciers, snowfields, and groundwater. Water moves from one reservoir to another by the processes of evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, deposition, runoff, infiltration, and groundwater flow.
 
• Water as an important ecological factor determines the structure and function of the ecosystem. Cycling of all other nutrients is also dependent upon water as it provides their transportation during the various steps. It acts as a solvent medium for their uptake of nutrients by organisms.
 
 
 
• Sulphur Cycle-
 
 
• The sulphur reservoir is in the soil and sediments where it is locked in organic (coal, oil and peat) and inorganic deposits (pyrite rock and sulphur rock) in the form of sulphates, sulphides and organic sulphur.
 
• It is released by weathering of rocks, erosional runoff and decomposition of organic matter and is carried to terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems in a salt solution.
 
• The sulphur cycle is mostly sedimentary except two of its compounds hydrogen sulphide (H2S) and sulphur dioxide (SO2) add a gaseous component to its normal sedimentary cycle.
 
• Sulphur enters the atmosphere from several sources like volcanic eruptions, combustion of fossil fuels, from the surface of the ocean and from gases released by decomposition. Atmospheric hydrogen sulphide also gets oxidised into sulphur dioxide.
 
• Atmospheric sulphur dioxide is carried back to the earth after being dissolved in rainwater as weak sulphuric acid.

question: ______ leaves are used to make bidis.

The correct answer is __**Tendu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Tendu leaves are primarily used to make bidis, which are a traditional type of hand-rolled cigarette in India.
 
• The leaves are known for their strength and elasticity, making them ideal for rolling bidis.
 
• Tendu, also known as Diospyros melanoxylon, is a tree found widely in central India.
 
• The collection and sale of tendu leaves are a significant source of income for forest-dwelling communities in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bidis**

 
 
• Bidis are traditional Indian cigarettes made by rolling dried tobacco flakes in a tendu leaf and securing the roll with a thread.
 
• They are often cheaper and smaller than regular cigarettes, making them accessible to a larger population.
 
• Despite their small size, bidis deliver a higher amount of nicotine, tar, and carbon monoxide compared to conventional cigarettes.
 
• The bidi industry is labor-intensive, providing employment to millions of people, especially women and children in rural areas.
 
 
 
• **Tendu (Diospyros melanoxylon)**
 
 
• Tendu is a species of flowering tree in the family Ebenaceae, native to India and Sri Lanka.
 
• The tree produces small, sweet fruits that are edible, but its leaves are more commercially valuable.
 
• Tendu leaves are collected during the summer months and are dried and processed for use in bidi production.
 
• The economic importance of tendu leaves has led to government regulation and control over their collection and trade in various states of India.

question: The growth form of a plant, comprising its size, shape and orientation is known as:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term "habit" in botany refers to the general growth form of a plant, including its size, shape, and orientation.
 
• It describes whether the plant is a tree, shrub, herb, or vine.
 
• Habit is an important characteristic used to identify and classify plants.
 
• Understanding the habit of a plant helps in determining its ecological role and adaptability to specific environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Environment:**

 
 
• The environment is the surrounding conditions in which an organism lives, including air, water, land, and other living beings.
 
• It influences the growth, development, and survival of organisms but is not specific to the growth form of a plant.
 
 
 
• **Habitat:**
 
 
• The habitat is the natural environment in which a particular species lives.
 
• It includes all the living and non-living factors that affect the species.
 
• It is more about the location and environment where a species is found rather than its growth form.
 
 
 
• **Growth Pattern:**
 
 
• Growth pattern refers to the developmental process of an organism, including stages of growth and changes in form over time.
 
• It is a broader term that can include habit but also encompasses other aspects of growth dynamics.

question: What kind of phyllotaxy was examined in the Guava plant?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Opposite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In an opposite phyllotaxy, two leaves arise at the same level from opposite sides of the stem.
 
• Each pair of leaves is typically perpendicular to the next pair above or below, providing a crisscross pattern.
 
• Opposite phyllotaxy ensures maximum light exposure for each leaf, which is beneficial for photosynthesis.
 
• This type of leaf arrangement is common in plants such as guava (Psidium guajava), calotropis, and jamun.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phyllotaxy**

 
 
• Phyllotaxy refers to the arrangement of leaves on a plant stem.
 
• The primary types of phyllotaxy are alternate, opposite, and whorled.
 
• This arrangement plays a significant role in maximizing light capture and minimizing shading of lower leaves.
 
 
 
• **Alternate Phyllotaxy**
 
 
• In alternate phyllotaxy, each leaf arises at a different level on the stem, and the leaves are not directly opposite each other.
 
• Examples include sunflower and mustard.
 
 
 
• **Whorled Phyllotaxy**
 
 
• In whorled phyllotaxy, three or more leaves grow at the same level around the stem.
 
• This arrangement is less common and can be seen in plants like Nerium (oleander).

question: Which of the following is NOT a component of a flower?

__
 
• **Spines** are not a component of a flower; they are modified leaves, stems, or stipules that are typically hard, pointed, and meant for protection.
 
• Flowers are reproductive structures in angiosperms (flowering plants) and typically consist of four main parts: androecium, corolla, calyx, and gynoecium.
 
• The primary role of spines is to protect the plant from herbivores and reduce water loss, especially in arid environments.
 
• Unlike the other options listed (androecium, corolla, and calyx), spines do not play a role in the reproductive process of the flower.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Androecium**

 
 
• The androecium is the collective term for the stamens in a flower. Each stamen typically consists of a filament and an anther, where pollen is produced.
 
• It is the male reproductive part of the flower.
 
 
 
• **Corolla**
 
 
• The corolla is the collective term for the petals of a flower.
 
• Petals are often brightly colored to attract pollinators.
 
 
 
• **Calyx**
 
 
• The calyx is the collective term for the sepals of a flower.
 
• Sepals are typically green and provide protection to the flower bud before it opens.
 
 
 
• **Gynoecium**
 
 
• The gynoecium is the collective term for the female reproductive parts of a flower, consisting of one or more carpels.
 
• Each carpel typically includes an ovary, style, and stigma.
