question:
Match the terms in Column A with their respective properties in Column B

 
 

 **Column-A**
 **Column-B**
 
 
 
 

 i. Glucose
 a. Intermediate substance in breakdown of glucose
 
 

 ii. Yeast
 b. Glucose is converted into pyruvic acid
 
 

 iii. Glycolysis
 c. Uses nutrients for fermentation process
 
 

 iv. Pyruvic acid
 d. Best organic substrate for respiration
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **i. Glucose - d. Best organic substrate for respiration:** Glucose is a primary source of energy and is considered the best substrate for respiration in cells.

• **ii. Yeast - c. Uses nutrients for fermentation process:** Yeast cells use glucose and other nutrients to carry out fermentation, producing ethanol and carbon dioxide.

• **iii. Glycolysis - b. Glucose is converted into pyruvic acid:** Glycolysis is the metabolic pathway that converts glucose into pyruvate, yielding ATP and NADH.

• **iv. Pyruvic acid - a. Intermediate substance in breakdown of glucose:** Pyruvic acid (pyruvate) is a key intermediate in the metabolic pathways of glucose breakdown and energy production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Glycolysis:**

• Glycolysis is the first step in the process of cellular respiration, where one molecule of glucose is broken down into two molecules of pyruvate.

• This process occurs in the cytoplasm and does not require oxygen, making it an anaerobic pathway.

• It produces a net gain of 2 ATP molecules and 2 NADH molecules, which are used in further metabolic processes.

• **Fermentation:**

• Fermentation is a metabolic process that converts sugar to acids, gases, or alcohol in the absence of oxygen.

• It is used by yeast and some bacteria to produce energy anaerobically.

• Common products of fermentation include ethanol (in alcoholic beverages) and lactic acid (in yogurt and sourdough).

• **Respiration:**

• Cellular respiration is the process by which cells convert biochemical energy from nutrients into ATP, and release waste products.

• It involves three main stages: glycolysis, the citric acid cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation.

• Glucose is the most common substrate for respiration, but other carbohydrates, fats, and proteins can also be used.

• **Pyruvic Acid (Pyruvate):**

• Pyruvate is a key intermediate in several metabolic pathways.

• It can be converted into acetyl-CoA, which enters the citric acid cycle, or it can be fermented to lactate or ethanol.

• Pyruvate is also involved in gluconeogenesis and the synthesis of amino acids.

subject: GK
question: Which pathway in cellular respiration generates the most ATP?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Electron Transport Chain**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **electron transport chain (ETC)** is a crucial pathway in cellular respiration that generates the most **ATP (adenosine triphosphate).**
 
• It occurs in the inner membrane of the **mitochondria** in eukaryotic cells.
 
• The ETC uses high-energy electrons from molecules like **NADH and FADH₂**, which are produced during earlier stages of respiration.
 
• Electrons are transferred through a series of protein complexes, including **cytochromes**, which pump **protons (H⁺)** across the mitochondrial membrane, creating a **proton gradient.**
 
• This proton gradient powers the enzyme **ATP synthase** to synthesize ATP via a process called **oxidative phosphorylation.**
 
• The ETC is responsible for producing approximately **34 ATP molecules** per glucose molecule, making it the most efficient pathway in energy production.
 
• Oxygen acts as the final electron acceptor in the ETC, combining with protons and electrons to form **water**, which is essential to the process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Glycolysis**__

 __
 
• **Glycolysis** is the first step in cellular respiration, occurring in the **cytoplasm** of the cell.
 
• It breaks down **glucose** into two molecules of **pyruvate**, producing a net gain of **2 ATP** molecules and **2 NADH** molecules.
 
• Though it is an essential step, it generates far less ATP compared to the ETC.
 
 
 
• **Krebs Cycle**__
 __
 
• The **Krebs cycle**, also known as the **citric acid cycle**, occurs in the mitochondrial matrix.
 
• It produces **NADH** and **FADH₂**, which are used in the electron transport chain.
 
• The cycle directly generates only **2 ATP** molecules per glucose molecule.
 
 
 
• **Fermentation**__
 
 
• **Fermentation** is an anaerobic process that occurs in the absence of oxygen.
 
• It produces ATP through **glycolysis** and regenerates **NAD+** for continued glycolysis.
 
• However, it generates only **2 ATP** molecules per glucose molecule, making it far less efficient than aerobic respiration.

subject: GK
question: Which of the below statements on the plant hormones is **INCORRECT**?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethylene promotes seed germination**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ethylene is primarily known as a gaseous plant hormone responsible for regulating processes such as fruit ripening, leaf abscission, and flower senescence.
 
• It is not directly linked with promoting seed germination; instead, other hormones such as gibberellins play a more dominant role in this process.
 
• The role of ethylene is often associated with responses to stress conditions and the promotion of senescence rather than germination.
 
• Studies have shown that ethylene can inhibit seed germination under certain conditions, contrary to the statement in the question.
 
• Thus, the statement "Ethylene promotes seed germination" is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Auxins promote growth:**

 
 
• Auxins are a class of plant hormones that play a critical role in cell elongation, root formation, and overall plant growth.
 
• They are primarily produced in the shoot apical meristem and transported to other parts of the plant.
 
• Auxins stimulate cell division and elongation, especially in the stem and roots, contributing to phototropism and gravitropism.
 
• Indole-3-acetic acid (IAA) is the most common naturally occurring auxin in plants.
 
 
 
• **Cytokinins delay aging:**
 
 
• Cytokinins are plant hormones that promote cell division and delay senescence (aging) in leaves and other plant tissues.
 
• They work antagonistically with auxins in regulating plant growth and development.
 
• Cytokinins help maintain chlorophyll levels in leaves, delaying leaf yellowing and promoting nutrient mobilization.
 
• Natural cytokinins include zeatin, which is derived from adenine and plays a role in promoting shoot initiation and growth.
 
 
 
• **Gibberellins promote stem elongation:**
 
 
• Gibberellins are a group of plant hormones that stimulate stem elongation, seed germination, and flowering.
 
• They break seed dormancy by promoting the synthesis of enzymes required for mobilizing stored nutrients.
 
• Gibberellins also influence the development of fruits and delay senescence in certain plants.
 
• They are widely used in agriculture to improve crop yield and quality.

question:
Read the following statements about aerobic respiration:

1. Glycolysis occurs in the mitochondria.

2. Kreb's cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix.

3. The final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration is oxygen.

Which of the above statements are **correct**?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 2 and 3 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Glycolysis** does not occur in the mitochondria; it takes place in the **cytoplasm** of the cell.
 
• **Kreb's cycle** (or citric acid cycle) occurs in the mitochondrial matrix, where acetyl-CoA is oxidized to produce energy carriers like NADH and FADH2.
 
• The final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration is **oxygen**, which combines with hydrogen ions and electrons to form water at the end of the electron transport chain.
 
• Aerobic respiration is a multi-step process that includes glycolysis, Kreb's cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation, with mitochondria playing a central role in the latter two stages.
 
• Energy in the form of ATP is produced primarily during the electron transport chain, a process that is dependent on oxygen as the terminal electron acceptor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kreb's Cycle (Statement 2):**

 
 
• This cycle occurs in the **mitochondrial matrix** and is a key step in aerobic respiration.
 
• It oxidizes acetyl-CoA derived from pyruvate to produce NADH, FADH2, and ATP (or GTP).
 
• The cycle also releases carbon dioxide as a byproduct.
 
• Statement 2 is correct as it accurately describes the location of the Krebs' cycle.
 
 
 
• **Final Electron Acceptor (Statement 3):**
 
 
• In the electron transport chain, electrons are passed through a series of protein complexes in the mitochondrial inner membrane.
 
• The final acceptor of electrons is **oxygen**, which combines with protons (H+) to form water.
 
• This step is essential for maintaining the flow of electrons and ensuring the production of ATP.
 
• Statement 3 is correct.

question:
Read the below statements about transpiration:

1. Transpiration is highest in dry and windy conditions.

2. It helps in the ascent of sap through cohesion-tension.

3. Transpiration always results in wilting. Which of the above statements are **correct**?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: Only 1 and 2 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1:** Transpiration is highest in dry and windy conditions because these conditions enhance the evaporation of water from the leaf surface, increasing the transpiration rate.
 
• **Statement 2:** Transpiration helps in the ascent of sap through the plant’s vascular system by creating a negative pressure in the xylem, which is supported by the cohesion-tension theory.
 
• The process of transpiration is essential for water movement in plants as it aids in nutrient uptake and maintains plant temperature.
 
• Both statements 1 and 2 are scientifically correct and aligned with modern botanical principles.
 
• **Statement 3 is incorrect:** Transpiration does not always result in wilting. Wilting occurs only when water loss due to transpiration exceeds the water absorption by roots, leading to a water deficit in plant cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transpiration:**
 
 
• It is the process by which plants lose water vapor through stomata in their leaves.
 
• Transpiration plays a critical role in nutrient transport, temperature regulation, and maintaining water balance in plants.
 
• Factors like temperature, humidity, wind speed, and soil water availability influence the rate of transpiration.
 
 
 
• **About Statement 3:**
 
 
• Wilting occurs when transpiration exceeds water absorption, leading to a loss of turgor pressure in plant cells.
 
• However, in normal conditions, plants regulate transpiration effectively and do not wilt.
 
• Guard cells play a key role in controlling the opening and closing of stomata to balance water loss and gas exchange.
 
 
 
• **Cohesion-Tension Theory:**
 
 
• It explains the movement of water through the xylem of plants.
 
• Water molecules are cohesive (stick to each other) and adhesive (stick to xylem walls), enabling the ascent of sap.
 
• Transpiration creates a negative pressure in the leaves, pulling water upward from the roots.
 
 
 
• **Dry and Windy Conditions:**
 
 
• Low humidity and high wind speed increase the water vapor concentration gradient between the leaf and the surrounding air, enhancing transpiration.

question: Which of the following is a characteristic of permanent tissue?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Intercellular spaces are present.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The characteristic features of permanent tissue are:
 
 
• **Cells have intercellular spaces to keep them separated.**
 
• The cells may be living or dead, i.e.the protoplasm is either present or absent.
 
• Tissue may have only one type of cell or may have different kinds of cells.
 
• The cell wall is either cellulosic or along with cellulose other complex carbohydrates may be present.
 
• Cells may** vary in shape, **i.e., either** round or oval or polygonal, **etc.
 
• In the living cells, the cytoplasm is present surrounding** a large central vacuole.**
 
• **Cells do not divide at all.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of permanent tissue: **
 
• **Permanent tissues are of three types, namely –**
 
 
• **(a) Simple tissue, (b) Complex tissue and (c) Secretory tissue.**
 
 
 
• **​Simple permanent tissue**
 
 
• Simple permanent tissue is composed of a single type of cells that have comparable origin, structure, and function.
 
 
 
• **Types of simple permanent tissue**
 
 
• **Parenchyma** – It provides temporary support and maintains the shape of the plant body. They have thin-walled cells with large vacuoles.
 
• **Collenchyma** – It provides mechanical support and elasticity and flexibility to young dicotyledonous plants. They have thickened cell walls at corners, giving mechanical strength.
 
• **Sclerenchyma **– It provides strength and toughness to plant parts. They have dead cells with extremely thick walls (lignin deposition). Sclerenchyma may be either fibres or sclereids
 
 
 
• **Complex permanent tissue**
 
 
• Complex permanent tissue is composed of two or more two types of cells and contributes to a general function.
 
• They organize together to carry out similar particular functions in the plant body.
 
• It is also known as vascular tissue.
 
 
 
• **Types of complex tissue:**
 
 
• **Xylem **– The xylem tissue is accountable for the transmission of water and minerals from the roots to the leaves and stems.
 
• **Phloem** – This complex permanent tissue helps in the translocation of food that is prepared by photosynthesis in the leaves to diverse parts of the plant.

__
 
• Water is a cyclic resource, as it is present in different states and abundant supplies around the globe.
 
• **A cyclic resource** is what can be **formed, again and again, Similarly water is a cyclic resource.**
 
• **The water** from the sea, river, ocean, etc. evaporates and condenses to form clouds.
 
• When the rain occurs water from these clouds comes onto earth and flows down into water resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The hydrological cycle is also known as the **water cycle;** it is the normal water recycling system on Earth. 
 
• It is the total of all processes in which water moves from the land and ocean surface to the atmosphere and back in form of precipitation.
 
• Though water is an** abiotic component of the environment**, it is not described as one since water carries many biotic components in it which are often crucial for the sustenance of life on earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Water is, indeed a** renewable resource.**
 
• Water has** three states.**
 
• Water or Fresh Water is a renewable Natural Resource.
 
• However, it should be noted that freshwater is a non-renewable energy resource.
 
• Water is used as a power generation tool by using turbines and steam boilers.
 
• Water also acts as one of the five elements which enable humans to live on this planet.
 
• Water is a **cyclic resource as it is used and reused.**
 
• **About 71% **of the planetary water is found in the oceans.
 
• The remaining is held as freshwater in glaciers and ice caps, groundwater sources, lakes, soil moisture, atmosphere, streams, and within life.
 
• **About 59% **of the water on the land surface evaporates and returns to the atmosphere.
 
• The remaining run-off on the surface penetrates the ground or a part of it becomes glaciers.

question: Which of the following greenhouse gases is most abundant in the atmosphere?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Water Vapour**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Greenhouse gasses**

 
 
• A **greenhouse gas**, often known as a greenhouse gas **(GHG or GhG)**, is a gas that creates the **greenhouse** **effect** by **absorbing **and **radiating **heat **infrared** light.
 
• **Water vapour **(H2O), **carbon dioxide** (CO2), **methane **(CH4), **nitrous oxide** (N2O), and **ozone** are the planet's main **greenhouse gases **(O3).
 
• Without **greenhouse gases, the average surface temperature of the Earth **would be closer to -**18 °C (0 °F)** than it is today, which is **15 °C (59 °F)**.
 
• **Greenhouse gases** are found in the atmospheres of **Venus**, **Mars**, and **Titan**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Water Vapour **

 
 
• **Water vapour**, or aqueous vapour are all terms for the **gaseous** state of **water**.
 
• It is a particular kind of water condition inside the **hydrosphere**.
 
• **Water vapour** can be created by the boiling or evaporation of **liquid water **as well as by the sublimation of ice. 
 
• **Water vapour **is continuously produced by **evaporation **and eliminated by **condensation** in a normal **atmosphere**.
 
• It causes convection currents that can result in clouds since it is less dense than the majority of the other **air constituents**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Carbon dioxide**

 
 
• The **most significant contributor to the warming effect**, accounting for 64% of the total.
 
• Carbon dioxide is long-lived in the atmosphere, with 40% remaining after 100 years, 20% after 1,000 years, and 10% after 10,000 years.
 
 
 
• **Methane**
 
 
• The** second-largest contributor,** accounting for 19% of the total.
 
• Methane is more potent than carbon dioxide, with a global warming impact that's almost 30 times greater over 100 years.
 
 
 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**
 
 
• The **third-largest contributor,** accounting for 8.1% of the total.
 
• CFCs were widely used in the mid-1900s, but they are still long-lived in the atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Nitrous oxide**
 
 
• A powerful greenhouse gas with a GWP that's around 270 times that of carbon dioxide.
 
• It remains in the atmosphere for a little more than a century. 
 
 
 
• **Other greenhouse gases include:**
 
 
• Fluorinated gases
 
• Hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs)
 
• Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs)
 
• Perfluorocarbons (PFCs)
 
• Sulfur hexafluoride (SF6)
 
• Nitroge n triflouride (NF3)

question: Identify the function of the enzyme trypsin.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Digesting Proteins.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Trypsin**

 
 
• **​**The function of the enzyme **trypsin** is** to digest proteins**.
 
• By breaking up lengthy chains of** amino acids** into smaller pieces, the enzyme trypsin in the early part of the small intestine initiates the breakdown of **protein **molecules.
 
• It is a serine protease from the PA clan superfamily that **hydrolyzes proteins** in the digestive tracts of numerous animals.
 
• When the **pancreatic** **enzyme **trypsinogen, in the proenzyme form, is activated, **trypsin **is generated in the **small intestine**.
 
• The **carboxyl** side of the amino acids lysine or arginine is where trypsin primarily breaks peptide chains. It is employed in a variety of **biotechnological procedures**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One significant** protease, trypsin**, has the unique ability to **catalyze** the **hydrolysis** of **peptide** and **ester** **bonds** with **lysine** and arginine amino acids at the **carboxyl-terminus.**
 
• Additionally, an autocatalytic, trypsin produces additional trypsin by converting **trypsinogen**.
 
• In addition to its basic function of breaking down dietary protein, trypsin also transforms the other two zymogens into **chymotrypsin and carboxypeptidase.**

__
 
• **Tissue**

 
 
• **​Tissue** is a group of cells similar in structure and function.
 
• A **biological **organisational level between cells and an entire organ, **tissue **is historically derived.
 
• Hence, a tissue is frequently considered to be an amalgamation of comparable cells and their extracellular matrix from the same origin that work together to perform a certain **function**.
 
• Afterwards, various tissues are functionally grouped together to form **organs**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Organ system**

 
 
• ​A group of **organs** that cooperate to carry out one or more functions is known as an **organ system i**n biology.
 
• Each organ in a plant or animal body is composed of certain **tissues** and serves a specific purpose.
 
 
 
• **Organ**
 
 
• ​**Organs** are groups of **tissues** that serve the same purpose. The brain, heart, kidneys, liver, and lungs are the five main organs that humans need to survive. Organs with similar functions frequently work together to create whole **organ systems**.
 
• **Parenchyma** and stroma make up an organ. The primary tissue that is peculiar to an organ, such as the myocardium, the primary tissue of the heart, is known as the **parenchyma**. **Nerves, blood vessels**, and **connective tissues** can all be found in the stroma, which is **sporadic tissue.**
 
 
 
• **Molecule**
 
 
• ​According to the context, the term may or may not include ions that meet this requirement. A **molecule** is a collection of two or more atoms held together by attractive forces known as **chemical bonds.**
 
• When speaking of **polyatomic** **ions**, the distinction between them and ions is frequently ignored in the fields of quantum physics, organic chemistry, and biochemistry.

• The **cell **creates a full copy of the **DNA **in its nucleus during the **S phase**. Moreover, it makes duplicates of the **centrosome**, a structure that organises **microtubules**. During **M phase**, the **centrosomes **aid in the separation of **DNA**.

question: What do you call the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Secondary productivity.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Primary productivity **is the pace at which producers - plants and other photosynthetic organisms - create new organic matter.
 
• The **rate at which consumers are creating new organic matter** is known as **secondary productivity. **Protists, fungi, bacteria, Deer, cows, goats, horses, etc. are a few examples.
 
• The entire **dry biomass of all living things at a certain trophic level** is referred to as a **standing crop.**
 
• It stands for biomass that is above ground. It could vary during the course of the year.
 
• There are** two forms of primary productivity:**
 
 
• Gross primary productivity, which measures the total rate of photosynthesis and the amount of organic matter consumed during respiration and is influenced by chlorophyll content.
 
• The difference between gross primary production and ecosystem organisms' respiration is known as net primary production.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tertiary productivity:****​**

 
 
• **​**The quantity of fresh biomass (weight) that carnivores (animals that eat meat) create over a certain amount of time.
 
 
 
• **Primary Productivity:**
 
 
• **​**The process by which organisms produce their own sustenance from inorganic sources is known as primary productivity. Terrestrial plants and microbiological life, such as algae, make up the majority of primary producers.
 
 
 
• **Net Productivity:**
 
 
• **​**The total amount of food or biomass produced by primary producers minus energy losses, which is also the total amount of food stored by producers, is referred to as net primary productivity.

question: Which enzyme in the pancreatic juice helps in breaking down fats?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lipase.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lipase,** 

 
 
• **Triglycerides are broken down by a class of enzymes called lipases into free fatty acids and glycerol.**
 
• They are present and functional in a variety of tissues; for instance, hepatic lipases are found in the liver, hormone-sensitive lipases in adipocytes, lipoprotein lipase is found on the surface of vascular endothelial cells, and pancreatic lipase is found in the small intestine.
 
• This enzyme functions in conjunction with the bile your liver produces.
 
• Your body will have problems absorbing fat and the crucial fat-soluble vitamins if you don't have enough lipase (A, D, E, K).
 
• Poor fat absorption is characterized by diarrhea and greasdiarrheay bowel motions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protease,**

 
 
• Proteases have more specialised uses in the extraction of mucopolysaccharides and carbohydrate gums, which are nonprotein compounds made from animal or plant extracts.
 
• Proteases can be employed to dissolve keratin-containing materials, such as feather debris, to provide protein concentrates for animal diets. Streptomyces species' alkaline proteases have potent keratinolytic activity as well.
 
• Your diet's protein is broken down by this enzyme.
 
• Also, it aids in defending you against microorganisms like certain bacteria and yeast that could reside in your intestines.
 
 
 
• **Amylase,**
 
 
• Any member of the class of enzymes known as amylases is responsible for catalysing the breakdown of starch into smaller carbohydrate molecules like maltose (a molecule composed of two glucose molecules). 
 
• Alpha-amylase is present in many biological things.
 
• Ptyalin, an alpha-amylase produced by salivary glands in the digestive tracts of humans and many other mammals, is secreted into the small intestine by pancreatic amylase.
 
• The undigested carbs may cause diarrhea if you don't have enough amylase.
 
 
 
• **Pepsin,**
 
 
• Pepsin, a potent digestive enzyme found in gastric juice, breaks down proteins found in foods including meat, eggs, seeds, and dairy products.
 
• The mature active version of the inactive protein pepsinogen is called pepsin.
 
• Pepsinogen is produced and stored by glands in the mucous membrane lining of the stomach. Pepsinogen is released into the stomach under the influence of vagus nerve impulses and the hormonal secretions gastrin and secretin, where it is combined with hydrochloric acid and quickly transformed into the active enzyme pepsin.

question: ______ is the fundamental structural unit of living organisms.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Cell.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **smallest and most basic unit **of life is the cell.
 
• Cells make up the **majority **of living things, and it is the processes that cells perform that allow **life to continue**.
 
• Because of this, cells are also referred to as the** fundamental building block **of living things.
 
• The smallest building blocks of all living things are called **cells.**
 
• A cell has the ability to live independently and do all the tasks required of a living thing.
 
• **Nutrition, respiration, excretion, transportation, and reproduction are all carried out by a cell.**
 
• Since they contribute to the structure of the organism, cells are structural units.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cell:**

 
 
• Unicellular organisms are able to I live **independently** and carry out the** fundamental tasks of life**.
 
• Independent living cannot be guaranteed if a cell's structure is incomplete.
 
• As a result, the cell is the **basic structural and functional unit **of all living things.
 
• **Cells **come together to form the body of every organism, much as how bricks come together to form a house.
 
• A tissue is made up of a number of cells that have a certain job to do.
 
• An organ is made up of a** group of tissues**, while an organism is made up of a group of organs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wuchereria **— This is a genus of parasitic filarial nematodes (tiny worms). Wuchereria bancrofti is one of the three types of roundworms that cause lymphatic filariasis, an infection of the lymphatic system. The two other roundworms are Brugia malayi and Brugia timori. Humans contract these through bites by infected mosquitoes. Wuchereria bancrofti is commonly referred to as Filaria worm.
 
• **Ancylostoma** — This is a genus of nematodes, commonly called the hookworms, which usually infect the intestines of their hosts. Ancylostoma duodenale (old world hookworm) and Necator americanus (new world hookworm), are the two species common to humans. They feed on the blood of the host and cause condition known as hookworm disease or ancylostomiasis. Contrary to the incorrect match, Ancylostoma does not refer to pinworm.
 
• **Taenia** — This genus of flatworms, commonly known as tapeworms, includes some important parasites of livestock and humans. Species like Taenia solium (pig tapeworm) and Taenia saginata (beef tapeworm) can cause taeniasis and cysticercosis in humans. Humans become infected when they consume undercooked beef or pork that contains larval cysts.
 
• **Ascaris** — Ascaris lumbricoides, commonly known as the "giant roundworm", is a species of roundworm that lives in the human intestine. subject: GK
question: Mitochondria is NOT found in ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**bacteria**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mitochondria are not found in bacteria**.
 
• Bacteria are prokaryotic cells and do not contain organelles, such as mitochondria, that are found in eukaryotic cells.
 
• It's interesting to note that it's widely accepted that mitochondria originated from a type of prokaryote due to a symbiotic event in the distant past, a theory known as endosymbiosis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****​​Mitochondria:**

 
• **Cell Organelle**: Mitochondria are cell organelles in eukaryotic cells. They are not present in prokaryotic cells like bacteria.
 
• Structure: Each mitochondrion is a double-membrane-bound structure with the outer membrane being smooth and the inner one thrown into folds or cristae.
 
• **Powerhouse of the Cell**: Mitochondria are often referred to as the 'powerhouse of the cell'. They are the sites of cellular respiration and produce energy in the form of ATP (adenosine triphosphate).
 
• **Semi-Autonomous**: Mitochondria are semi-autonomous organelles. They have their own DNA and ribosomes, meaning they can manufacture their own proteins and replicate independently of the cell in which they reside. This suggests a symbiotic origin to the mitochondria, supporting the endosymbiotic theory.
 
• **Number of Mitochondria**: The number of mitochondria in a cell can vary greatly depending on the cell type. For example, cells with high energy needs like muscle cells have more mitochondria, while other cells may have very few.
 
• **Size and Shape**: Mitochondria are typically rod-shaped or oval in nature. Their size ranges from 0.5 to 1.0 micrometre in diameter.
 
• **Role in Metabolism**: Mitochondria are not only the energy factories of the cell, but also participate in other metabolic tasks such as the synthesis of certain components of blood and hormones, the metabolism of cholesterol, and the regulation of calcium concentration in the cell.
 
• **Cytochromes**: Mitochondria contain a number of enzymes, including the cytochromes, which participate in electron transport during aerobic respiration.
 
• **Matrix Space**: The space within the inner membrane of a mitochondrion is known as the matrix. It contains a number of enzymes, the mitochondrial DNA, ribosomes, and granules that store calcium phosphate.
 
• **Oxysomes or F1 Particles**: The inner membrane of mitochondria bears some spherical bodies called oxysomes or F1 particles. These particles are involved directly in ATP synthesis.
 
• **Krebs Cycle**: The process by which energy is produced in the mitochondria, the Krebs (or citric acid) cycle, is a series of biochemical reactions that generate energy through the oxidation of acetate—derived from carbohydrates, fats, and proteins—into carbon dioxide.
 
• **Mitochondrial Disorders**: Certain genetic disorders have been linked to mutations in mitochondrial DNA. These include some forms of heart disease, diabetes, and Leigh's syndrome, a progressive neurometabolic disorder.
 
• **Role in Aging**: Some theories suggest a role for mitochondria in the aging process. The free-radical theory of aging suggests that accumulated damage from oxidative stress (the imbalance between the production of free radicals and the ability of cells to counteract their harmful effects), largely caused by mitochondria, results in the physiological changes we associate with aging.
 
• **Mitophagy**: The process in which defective mitochondria are destroyed by cellular machinery is termed 'mitophagy'. This is a vital process as it assists in maintaining the proper functioning of cells by removing damaged mitochondria that could potentially harm the cell.

question: Identify the function of lipase in the process of digestion.
solution:
The correct answer is__** Breaking down emulsified fats.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lipase** is an **enzyme** that plays a crucial role in the **digestion of fats in the body.**
 
• The **breakdown of fats** is essential for the **absorption and utilization** of essential **fatty acids and fat-soluble vitamins**.
 
• **Lipase breaks down emulsified fats**:
 
 
• The process of digestion starts in the** mouth** where the food is chewed and mixed with** saliva.**
 
• Saliva contains an enzyme called **salivary lipase **that starts breaking down fats.
 
• However, the majority of **fat digestion** happens in the** small intestine** where the emulsified fats are acted upon by **pancreatic lipase.**
 
• This enzyme breaks down the emulsified fats into** fatty acids and glycerol, **which can be absorbed by the body.
 
 
 
• **Lipase works with bile:**
 
 
• Bile is a **digestive fluid** produced by the** liver **and stored in the **gallbladder.**
 
• Bile contains bile salts that help in the **emulsification of fats**, making them easier for** lipase to break down.**
 
• Lipase and bile work together to **digest fats **and ensure their **absorption **in the body.
 
 
 
• **Lipase deficiency can lead to malabsorption:**
 
 
• In some cases, people may have a **deficiency of lipase,** which can result in **malabsorption of fats.**
 
• This can lead to symptoms like **bloating, gas, diarrhea, and weight loss.**
 
• People with conditions like c**ystic fibrosis, pancreatitis, and celiac disease **may have a deficiency of lipase.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Breaking down roughage:** This is the function of enzymes like **cellulase**, which break down the fiber in plant foods.

 
 
• Lipase **does not** play a role in breaking down roughage.
 
 
 
• **Secreting intestinal fluids:** This is the function of the **intestinal glands**, which secrete fluids that help in the digestion and absorption of nutrients.
 
 
• Lipase is **not** involved in this process.
 
 
 
• **Digesting proteins**: This is the function of enzymes like** pepsin and trypsin**, which break down proteins into amino acids.
 
 
• Lipase does **not** play a role in digesting proteins.
 
 
 
• Hence, the** correct **option is 2) Breaking down emulsified fats.

• **Cushing's syndrome is a condition that is caused by the overproduction of cortisol, a steroid hormone that is produced by the adrenal glands.**
 
• Diabetes is a condition that is characterized by high levels of glucose (sugar) in the blood.
 
 
• **It is caused by a lack of insulin, a hormone that is produced by the pancreas.**
 
 
 
• **Thyroxin**, which is associated with goitre, is involved in regulating **metabolism and growth**. 
 
 
• **It helps to regulate the body's energy production and influences the development of the brain, bones, and muscles.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cortisol,** which is associated with Cushing's syndrome, is involved in regulating a variety of bodily functions, including **metabolism, immune response, and stress response.**
 
• Insulin, which is associated with diabetes, regulates the levels of glucose (sugar) in the blood.
 
 
• **It allows cells to use glucose for energy and helps to store excess glucose in the liver and muscles.**
 
 
 
• Goitre is a condition that is characterized by an enlarged thyroid gland.
 
 
• **It is often caused by a deficiency of iodine, which is necessary for the production of thyroid hormones.**

question: In the early 1800s, who discovered that each chemical element is made up of a unique type of atom and that atoms differ by their mass?
solution:
The correct answer is __**John Dalton.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **John Dalton** discovered that each chemical element is made up of a **unique type of atom **and that atoms **differ by their mass **in the early 1800s.
 
• Dalton proposed the **atomic theory** which explained the **behavior of atoms** and their interactions with other atoms.
 
• **Dalton's atomic theory** also stated that atoms **cannot be created or destroyed** in a chemical reaction and that compounds are formed by the combination of **atoms in fixed ratios.**
 
• Dalton's work laid the foundation for **modern atomic theory **and the** periodic table** of elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Antoine Lavoisier **is known as the **father of modern chemistry.**

 
 
• He made significant contributions to the understanding of **combustion** and the **law of conservation of mass.**
 
 
 
• **Amedeo Avogadro **proposed **Avogadro's law.**
 
 
• The law states that **equal volumes of gases** at the **same temperatur**e and **pressure** contain equal numbers of molecules.
 
 
 
• **Robert Boyle** is known for **Boyle's law.**
 
 
• The law states that the volume of a gas is **inversely proportional** to its pressure at a constant temperature.

question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding cell membrane?

I. The membrane is selectively permeable to some molecules present on either side of it.

II. Water may also move across this membrane from lower to higher concentration.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The cell membrane is a thin, flexible barrier that separates the inside of a cell from its external environment.**
 
• It is selectively permeable, meaning that it allows some substances to pass through while preventing others from entering or leaving the cell.
 
• This selectivity is achieved through various mechanisms such as **ion channels, transporters, and pumps.**
 
• **Water can also move across the membrane through a process called osmosis, but it always moves from an area of higher concentration to an area of lower concentration.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The lipid bilayer that makes up the cell membrane is composed of two phospholipid layers with cholesterol, a lipid component, strewn in between to maintain the proper fluidity of the membrane at different temperatures.**
 
• Additionally, membrane proteins are present in the membrane.
 
• These proteins include integral proteins, which span the membrane and function as membrane transporters, and peripheral proteins, which cling slackly to the cell membrane's outer (peripheral) side and function as enzymes to promote interaction with the surrounding milieu.
 
• The function of glycolipids embedded in the outer lipid layer is comparable. 
 
• **Furthermore, cell membranes act as the attachment surface for a number of extracellular structures, including the cell wall, and are involved in a number of cellular activities including cell adhesion, ion conductivity, and cell signaling. **

• This is because mitochondria are typically depicted as oval or bean-shaped organelles with an inner membrane folded into cristae, which helps in energy production within the cell.
 
• The mitochondrion is an essential organelle found in eukaryotic cells, often referred to as the "powerhouse of the cell" because it produces energy in the form of ATP (adenosine triphosphate).
 
• The structure of the mitochondrion includes the following key features:

• Matrix: The space inside the inner membrane is filled with a gel-like substance called the matrix. It contains enzymes that are essential for the Krebs cycle (part of cellular respiration).

question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the **correct **options:

**Assertion (A):** Delhi frequently records the highest AQI levels among Indian cities.

**Reason (R):** It lies in a low-lying basin surrounded by the Himalayas.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Delhi frequently records the highest Air Quality Index (AQI) levels** among Indian cities due to severe air pollution caused by vehicular emissions, industrial pollutants, burning of crop stubble, and construction dust.
 
• The city's geographical location contributes significantly to its poor air quality as it lies in a **low-lying basin surrounded by the Himalayas**, which traps pollutants and prevents their dispersal.
 
• Delhi's air pollution worsens during the winter months due to **temperature inversion**, where cold air near the ground traps pollutants and prevents their upward movement.
 
• The Himalayas act as a barrier, preventing the movement of polluted air masses away from the region, resulting in stagnation of pollutants over Delhi.
 
• Local factors such as population density, unregulated industrial activities, and lack of green cover further exacerbate the air quality crisis in Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The AQI (Air Quality Index) measures the concentration of pollutants in the air, including PM2.5, PM10, sulfur dioxide (SO2), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), and ozone (O3).
 
• Delhi's air pollution crisis is a significant environmental challenge, impacting public health and necessitating urgent policy interventions.
 
• Geographical features, seasonal factors, human activities, and lack of effective pollution control measures contribute to Delhi’s high AQI levels.

question: Which of these is an odd one out?
solution:
The correct answer is __**DNA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid)** is the odd one out as it is a molecule that carries genetic information, unlike the other options which are involved in energy metabolism.
 
• DNA is a nucleic acid, made up of nucleotide monomers, and its primary role is to store and transfer genetic information in living organisms.
 
• It is not directly involved in cellular energy transfer or metabolism, which is the primary function of ATP, NADH, and Glucose.
 
• The structure of DNA consists of a double helix made of two strands held together by complementary base pairing (adenine-thymine and cytosine-guanine).
 
• DNA is crucial for processes like replication, transcription, and translation, which are central to heredity and protein synthesis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate):**
 
 
• ATP is often called the "energy currency" of the cell as it provides energy for various cellular processes.
 
• It is composed of adenine, ribose, and three phosphate groups. The energy is released during the hydrolysis of its terminal phosphate bond.
 
• ATP is synthesized in the mitochondria during cellular respiration and in chloroplasts during photosynthesis.
 
• It is critical for muscle contraction, active transport, and biochemical reactions.
 
 
 
• **Glucose:**
 
 
• Glucose is a simple sugar and a primary source of energy for most organisms.
 
• It is a monosaccharide with the chemical formula C6H12O6.
 
• Glucose undergoes metabolic processes like glycolysis, the citric acid cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation to produce ATP.
 
• It is obtained from dietary carbohydrates and is regulated in the body by hormones like insulin and glucagon.
 
 
 
• **NADH (Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide - Reduced Form):**
 
 
• NADH is an electron carrier that plays a crucial role in cellular respiration and energy production.
 
• It is produced during glycolysis and the citric acid cycle and donates electrons to the electron transport chain in mitochondria.
 
• Through oxidative phosphorylation, NADH contributes to the generation of ATP.
 
• NADH is essential for maintaining redox balance in the cell and for metabolic pathways.

question: What is the name of the inflammatory condition that causes cracks, crusting and scaling at the corners of the mouth due to vitamin B2 deficiency?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cheilosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Cheilosis**, also known as angular cheilitis, is an inflammatory condition that affects the corners of the mouth.
 
• It is characterized by the formation of cracks, crusting, and scaling at the mouth corners.
 
• Cheilosis is commonly caused by a deficiency in Vitamin B2 (riboflavin).
 
• Other contributing factors can include fungal infections and poor oral hygiene.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vitamin B2 (Riboflavin)**

 
 
• Riboflavin is a water-soluble vitamin that is essential for energy production and cellular function.
 
• It helps in the metabolism of fats, drugs, and steroids and is crucial for the conversion of carbohydrates into ATP (adenosine triphosphate).
 
• Deficiency in riboflavin can lead to symptoms such as sore throat, redness and swelling of the lining of the mouth and throat, and cheilosis.
 
 
 
• **Psoriasis**
 
 
• Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune condition that causes the rapid buildup of skin cells.
 
• This buildup of cells causes scaling on the skin’s surface.
 
• Inflammation and redness around the scales are fairly common.
 
 
 
• **Urticaria (Hives)**
 
 
• Urticaria, commonly known as hives, is a skin reaction that causes itchy welts.
 
• It is usually caused by an allergic reaction to food, medicine, or other irritants.
 
 
 
• **Atopic Dermatitis**
 
 
• Atopic dermatitis, also known as eczema, is a condition that makes the skin red and itchy.
 
• It is common in children but can occur at any age.
 
• Atopic dermatitis is long-lasting (chronic) and tends to flare periodically.

question: Burning of coal is an example of ______.
solution:
The correct answer is a __Combination Reaction.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• The combustion of coal is an example of Combination Reaction.
 
• A combination reaction is a reaction where two or more elements or compounds combine to form a single compound. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: X + Y → XY.
 
• The combination of two or more elements to form one compound is called a combination reaction.

​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

Other types of Chemical Reactions:

__
 
• Decomposition reaction__:

 __
 
• The opposite of a combination reaction, a complex molecule breaks down to make simpler ones. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: AB → A + B.
 
 
 
• Precipitation reaction__: 
 __
 
• Two solutions of soluble salts are mixed resulting in an insoluble solid (precipitate) forming. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: A + Soluble salt B → Precipitate + soluble salt C.
 
 
 
• Neutralization reaction__: 
 __
 
• An acid and a base react with each other. Generally, the product of this reaction is salt and water. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: Acid + Base → Salt + Water.
 
 
 
• Combustion reaction__: 
 __
 
• Oxygen combines with a compound to form carbon dioxide and water. These reactions are exothermic, meaning they give off heat. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: A + O2 → H2O + CO2.
 
 
 
• Displacement reaction__: 
 __
 
• One element takes place with another element in the compound. Such reactions are represented by equations of the following form: A + BC → AC + B.
 
 
 
• Double displacement reaction__:
 
 
• Double displacement reactions occur when a part of two ionic compounds is exchanged and makes two new components.
 
• Double displacement reactions take place mostly in aqueous solutions wherein the ions precipitate and the exchange of ions takes place.

question: Buckminsterfullerene is a nanoparticle characterised by spherical geometry and a hollow interior which contains how many carbon atoms?
solution:
The correct answer is** **__**60**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **60 carbon atoms** are organized in interlocking **hexagonal and pentagonal rings** to form the spherical molecule known as **buckminsterfullerene.**
 
• The spherical carbon allotrope known as a **buckminsterfullerene (C60) **has 60 atoms arranged in pentagons and hexagons, giving it a soccer ball-like form.
 
• A type of fullerene with the chemical formula C60 is buckminsterfullerene. It is shaped like a football and has a fused-ring construction that resembles a cage.** It is made up of twenty hexagons and twelve pentagons**. Its 60 carbon atoms are all linked to three of their neighbours.
 
• Each carbon atom generates three sigma bonds with three other carbon atoms in the fullerene's **sp2 hybridization state**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Carbon fullerene molecules can take on a variety of **geometries**, including tubes, spheres, cubes, and other pure solids comprised of just one type of atom. A feature of fullerenes is their hollow core, which is an area of empty space inside the molecule.
 
• Consider a basketball; it has a** spherical, leather outside**, but a hollow interior where air is trapped to give it its **bouncing motion**. With a fullerene, the situation is identical. It is entirely composed of carbon, and the interior of the structure is always hollow.
 
• HIV proteases' hydrophobic cavity can accommodate fullerene, which prevents substrates from reaching the** enzyme's catalytic site**. It has **antioxidant** and **radical scavenger properties**. Fullerene can also produce significant quantum yields of singlet oxygen when exposed to light.

question: In organic chemistry, which of the following is an empirical rule used to predict the regioselectivity of electrophilic addition reactions of alkanes and alkynes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Markovnikov's rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Markovnikov's rule:
 
 
• Markovnikov's rule is a principle that predicts the outcome of an addition reaction of an unsymmetrical alkene.
 
• It states that in the addition of a polar reagent to an unsymmetrical alkene, the electrophile will add to the carbon atom that has the most hydrogen atoms attached to it, while the nucleophile will add to the carbon atom that has the least hydrogen atoms attached to it.
 
• This is because the more substituted carbocation intermediate is more stable due to the electron-donating effect of the alkyl groups.
 
• This rule is named after Russian chemist Vladimir Markovnikov who first proposed it in 1869.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Rule
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Cornforth's rules
 
 
A set of rules that predict the stereochemistry of certain types of organic reactions.

 
Rule 1: In an electrocyclic reaction, the new sigma bond is formed in such a way as to maximize the overlap of the interacting orbitals.

 
Rule 2: In a cycloaddition reaction, the new sigma bonds are formed in such a way as to minimize the number of four-membered rings formed.

 
 
 

 Bredt's rule
 
 
A rule that states that a double bond cannot be located at the bridgehead of a bridged bicyclic system if it leads to a strained conformation.

 
This is because the double bond would introduce additional ring strain, making the molecule less stable.

 
 
 

 Baldwin's rules
 
 
A set of rules that describe the feasibility and stereochemistry of intramolecular reactions.

 
The rules specify the minimum number of atoms in the transition state of a reaction, as well as the angles between the reacting bonds.

 
The rules are as follows:

 
Rule 1: The number of atoms in the transition state of a reaction cannot exceed the number of atoms in the smallest ring that can be drawn around the reacting bonds.

 
Rule 2: The angles between the reacting bonds must correspond to bond angles in stable molecules.

 
Rule 3: The reaction must proceed through a transition state that is no more strained than the reactant or product.

• Covalent bond: The chemical bond formed by sharing of two valence electron between the two atoms. There are 8 carbon-hydrogen covalent bonds and 2 carbon-carbon covalent bonds present in the propane molecule. So, the total number of covalent bonds present in propane is (8 + 2 = 10)
 
 
• A covalent bond is represented clearly by drawing an electron - dot structure.
 
 
 
• Hybridization: sp² hybridized around the carbon of the double bond; sp³ hybridized around the last carbon.
 
• Polarity: Non-polar because of its symmetric geometric structure and the similar electronegativity of Carbon and Hydrogen.
 
• In terms of reactions, propene is commonly involved in addition reactions due to the presence of the double bond:
 
• Combustion: Like all hydrocarbons, propene burns in oxygen to produce water and carbon dioxide.
 
 
• C₃H₆ + 4.5 O₂ -> 3 CO₂ + 3 H₂O
 
 
 
• Addition of Halogens: When reacted with halogens like Bromine (Br2), the bromine molecule adds across the double bond.
 
 
• C₃H₆ + Br₂ -> C₃H₆Br₂
 
 
 
• Hydrogenation: Propene can undergo hydrogenation to produce propane, in the presence of a metallic catalyst.
 
 
• C₃H₆ + H₂ -> C₃H₈
 
 
 
• Polymerization: Propene is particularly important in the industry as a monomer in the production of polypropylene, a versatile plastic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Alkenes are hydrocarbons that contain a carbon-carbon double bond. Here are some common alkenes:

 
• **Ethene (ethylene)**: This is the simplest alkene and is utilized broadly in the chemical industry. Its chemical formula is C2H4 and its structural formula is H2C=CH2.
 
• **Butene**: There are three isomers of butene; 1-butene, 2-butene (cis and trans). The chemical formula for Butene is C₄H8. The structural formulas are CH₂=CH-CH₂-CH₃ for 1-butene and CH₃-CH=CH-CH₃ for 2-butene.
 
• **Pentene**: There are three isomers of pentene; 1-Pentene, 2-Pentene (cis and trans). The chemical formula for Pentene is C5H10. The structural formulas are CH2=CH-(CH2)3-CH3 for 1-Pentene and CH3-CH=CH-(CH2)2-CH3 for 2-Pentene.
 
• These molecules are important in both natural processes (such as ripening of fruits) and industrial processes (such as polymer production, preparation of alcohols, etc.). The "cis" and "trans" prefixes refer to the geometry of the substituents around the double bond. In "cis" isomers, the larger substituents are on the same side of the double bond, while in "trans" isomers, they are on opposite sides.
 
• All alkenes have similar chemical properties due to the presence of the carbon-carbon double bond. They all can undergo addition reactions where a molecule can add across the double bond, and polymerization reactions where individual alkene molecules (monomers) combine to form long chains (polymers), such as polyethylene and polypropylene plastics.

__
 
• Grignard reagents are organomagnesium compounds which are commonly represented as **R-Mg-X**, where R is an organic group and X is a halogen.
 
• In the given options, **CH₃-Mg-Cl** (Methylmagnesium chloride) fits this representation.
 
• Grignard reagents are highly reactive and are used in various organic synthesis reactions, particularly for forming carbon-carbon bonds.
 
• They were discovered by the French chemist Victor Grignard, who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1912 for this discovery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Grignard Reagent:**

 
 
• Grignard reagents are typically prepared by reacting an alkyl or aryl halide with magnesium metal in an anhydrous ether solvent.
 
• They are strong nucleophiles and strong bases, making them very useful in organic chemistry for forming new carbon-carbon bonds.
 
• The general formula for a Grignard reagent is R-Mg-X, where R can be an alkyl, aryl, or vinyl group, and X is usually a halogen like chlorine, bromine, or iodine.
 
• Due to their high reactivity, Grignard reagents must be handled under an inert atmosphere (such as nitrogen or argon) to prevent them from reacting with moisture or oxygen in the air.
 
 
 
• **Victor Grignard:**
 
 
• François Auguste Victor Grignard was a French chemist who discovered the Grignard reagent, which revolutionized the field of organic chemistry.
 
• His discovery allowed for the formation of carbon-carbon bonds, which is fundamental in the synthesis of a wide variety of organic compounds.
 
• He was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1912 for this significant contribution.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Grignard Reagents:**
 
 
• Grignard reagents are used to form various types of carbon-carbon bonds, making them invaluable in the synthesis of alcohols, acids, and other organic compounds.
 
• They can react with carbonyl compounds (such as aldehydes and ketones) to form secondary and tertiary alcohols.
 
• They are also used in the synthesis of carboxylic acids by reacting with carbon dioxide.
 
• In addition to their use in academic research, Grignard reagents are also used in the pharmaceutical and chemical industries for the synthesis of complex organic molecules.

question: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
solution:
The correct answer is __**C3H8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• C3H8 is the chemical formula for propane, which is a saturated hydrocarbon.
 
• Saturated hydrocarbons contain only single bonds between carbon atoms.
 
• Propane is an alkane, which is a type of saturated hydrocarbon.
 
• Alkanes have the general formula CnH2n+2, and propane (C3H8) fits this formula.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saturated Hydrocarbons:**

 
 
• Saturated hydrocarbons are hydrocarbons in which all the carbon atoms are connected by single bonds. They are also known as alkanes.
 
• Alkanes have the general formula CnH2n+2, where n is the number of carbon atoms.
 
• Examples include methane (CH4), ethane (C2H6), and propane (C3H8).
 
 
 
• **Unsaturated Hydrocarbons:**
 
 
• Unsaturated hydrocarbons contain at least one double or triple bond between carbon atoms.
 
• Alkenes are hydrocarbons with one or more double bonds (general formula CnH2n), such as ethene (C2H4) and propene (C3H6).
 
• Alkynes are hydrocarbons with one or more triple bonds (general formula CnH2n-2), such as ethyne (C2H2) and propyne (C3H4).
 
 
 
• **Benzene (C6H6):**
 
 
• Benzene is an aromatic hydrocarbon, characterized by a ring of six carbon atoms with alternating double bonds.
 
• Aromatic hydrocarbons have unique stability and properties due to their conjugated pi-electron systems.
 
 
 
• **Hydrocarbon Classes:**
 
 
• Hydrocarbons can be classified into alkanes (saturated), alkenes (unsaturated), alkynes (unsaturated), and aromatic hydrocarbons.
 
• Each class has distinct chemical properties and reactivities.

question: Which of the following elements’ salts are most soluble?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The** solubility** is the **ability **of a **compound**, it may be a liquid, solid or gaseous substance to **dissolve **in the **solvent **and there is a **formation **of a **solution**.

 
 
• The **solubility **is mainly **dependent **upon the **solvent**, **hydration energy**, **lattice energy**, **temperature**, and **pressure**.
 
• The **solubility **of a compound mainly depends upon the **hydration energy **and **lattice energy**.
 
• If the **hydration energy **of the compound is **greater **than **lattice energy**, the **solubility **is **more**.
 
 
• **Hydration energy **(also hydration enthalpy) is the amount of energy released when one mole of ions undergo hydration.
 
• **Lattice energy **is defined as the amount of energy required to completely separate one mole of a solid ionic compound into a gaseous constituent.
 
 
 
• The **hydration energy **of **sodium **is **greater **than its **lattice energy**. 
 
• And the **size of sodium ions** is **smaller **than potassium and other ions. 
 
• Therefore, the **sodium ion can easily create a hydration sphere** around the ion than other ions.
 
• The sodium atom readily reacts with water and it dissolves in it.

• It is used as an** important reagent in lanthanide **chemistry.
 
• It is** used in creams/ointments **that are used for rehydration.
 
• It is used in** hair removal creams** and dish soaps.
 
• It is used as a **browning agent for pretzels.**
 
• It is used in **manufacturing melamine.**
 
• It is used to** detect the bacteria in the stomach** through the urea breath test.

question: What kind of forces arise from transient dipoles in atoms that induce transient dipoles in nearby atoms, produce an attractive force and are significant only over short distances (~500 pm)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**London dispersion forces**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Atoms and nonpolar molecules are electrically symmetrical and have **no dipole moment** because their electronic charge cloud is symmetrically distributed. But a dipole may develop momentarily even in such atoms and molecules.
 
• This force of attraction was first proposed by the **German physicist Fritz London**, and for this reason force of attraction between two temporary dipoles is known as the **London force**.
 
• These forces are always **attractive and interaction energy** is inversely proportional to the sixth power of the distance between two interacting particles (i.e., 1/r 6 where r is the distance between two particles)
 
• These forces are important only at **short distances **(~500 pm) and their magnitude depends on the polarisability of the particle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4be81f64d3a1eb024bd7521af78d34a6d5c3d494070630c186585d9a93aec973.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dipole-dipole forces**

 
 
• **​**Dipole-dipole forces act between the molecules possessing permanent dipole. Ends of the dipoles possess “partial charges” and these charges are shown by the Greek letter delta (δ)
 
• The polar molecules interact with neighboring molecules.
 
• This interaction is stronger than the London forces but is weaker than ion-ion interaction because only partial charges are involved.
 
 
 
• D**ipole–Induced Dipole Forces**
 
 
• **​**This type of attractive force operates between the polar molecules having permanent dipole and the molecules lacking permanent dipole.
 
• The permanent dipole of the polar molecule induces a dipole on the electrically neutral molecule by deforming its electronic cloud.
 
• Thus an induced dipole is developed in the other molecule.
 
• Induced dipole moment depends upon the dipole moment present in the permanent dipole and the polarisability of the electrically neutral molecule.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen bond**
 
 
• **​**This is a special case of dipole-dipole interaction found in the molecules in which highly polar N–H, O–H or H–F bonds are present. Although hydrogen bonding is regarded as being limited to N, O and F; species such as Cl may also participate in hydrogen bonding

question: In which year did Langmuir reform the Lewis concept by abandoning the idea of a stable cubical arrangement of the octet and introducing the term ‘covalent bond’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1919**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Langmuir in 1919** refined the Lewis postulation by abandoning the idea of the stationary cubical arrangement of the octet, and by introducing the team covalent bond.
 
• **Covalent bonds****;-**
 
 
• They are formed by the sharing of electrons between **two atoms** so that both can achieve a filled outermost shell.
 
• When two atoms share one electron pair they are said to be joined by a single covalent bond.
 
 
 
• In many compounds, we have multiple bonds between atoms. The formation of multiple bonds envisages the sharing of more than one electron pair between two atoms.
 
• If two atoms share two pairs of electrons, the covalent bond between them is called a** double bond**.
 
• When combining atoms share **three electrons** Paris as in the case of two nitrogen atoms in the N₂ molecule and the two carbon atoms in the ethyne molecule, a triple bond is formed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** first description of covalent bonding was provided by Gilbert N. Lewis **in terms of the sharing of electron pairs between atoms
 
• He related the process to the attainment of noble gas configurations by reacting atoms as a result of sharing of electrons.
 
• Kossel and Lewis in **1916 **developed a theory of chemical combination between atoms known as the electronic theory of chemical bonding.

question: Which theory discusses the relationship between ligand bonding and degradation of d orbitals in metal complexes and the geometry of metal complexes and the splitting of d orbitals?
solution:
The correct answer is **Crystal field theory (CFT).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Crystal field theory (CFT)**

 
 
• ​**Crystal field theory (CFT) discusses the relationship between ligand binding and degradation of d orbitals in metal complexes, the geometry of metal complexes, and the splitting of d orbitals.**
 
• The **propensity of transition metals **to form complexes is one of their key characteristics. A complex can be thought of as having several ligands encircling a core metal atom or ion.
 
• **Crystal field** **theory** governs how these ligands interact with the central **metal atom or ion.**
 
• The interaction between a **metal ion and ligand** is viewed by the 1929-founded crystal field theory as essentially an electrostatic phenomenon, with the ligands being considered as point charges close to the **atomic orbitals of the central atom.**
 
• Using **molecular orbital theory**, crystal field theory was developed and expanded to consider the partially covalent nature of bonding between the **ligand and metal atom.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **metal-ligand bond** was defined by crystal field theory as an ionic bond that solely results from **electrostatic interactions between the metal ions and ligands.**
 
• In the crystal field theory, anions are viewed as **point charges**, whereas neutral molecules are viewed as dipoles. **Transition metals' d orbitals degenerate**, or have the same energy, when they are not bound to any ligands.
 
• Due to the varied **symmetries of the d orbitals** and the inductive influence of the ligands on the electrons, the d orbitals split apart and become non-degenerate when they begin bonding with other ligands.

question: How many anions surround a sodium ion in a crystal lattice of sodium chloride?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Six.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cations and anions **are combined to **form ionic molecules**. \
 
• In sodium chloride, the** cation** is **sodium (Na+)** and the** anion** is **chloride (Cl-).**
 
• The** anion (Cl-) and the cation (Na+)** in the **crystal structure** alternate back and forth in a **predictable pattern.**
 
• The** cubic lattice of sodium ions** and a related** cubic lattice of chlorine ions** are entangled in the **crystal structure of sodium chloride.**
 
• **Thirteen sodium ions** and **fourteen chloride ions** make up each unit cell of sodium chloride.
 
• **Eight unit cells **share an ion at a corner, **two unit cells **share one at the **face's center, and four unit cells **share one at the edge.
 
• **Each sodium ion **is surrounded by **six chloride ions**, and **each chloride ion** is surrounded by **six sodium ions.**
 
• The** sodium chloride unit cell **contains** four sodium ions** and **four chloride ions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9475ac0ab2383687f41741c01bb369d13e84e80996f9ed9f9571911950d50259.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **symmetrical three-dimensional **structural groupings of **atoms, ions, or molecules** inside a crystalline solid as points are known as the **crystal lattice.**
 
• It can be characterized as the **spatial geometrical arrangement** of the **atoms, ions, or molecules** that make up the crystalline solid.
 
• A **crystal lattice** is created by **substituting a representative point** for each group of atoms.

• **Calcium hydrogen carbonate**

 
 
• **​Ca(HCO3)2** is the chemical formula for **calcium bicarbonate**, often known as **calcium hydrogencarbonate**.
 
• It only exists in aqueous solutions containing calcium **(Ca2+)**, bicarbonate ions, and dissolved carbon dioxide; the word does not refer to a known solid substance** (CO2)**.
 
• The **pH **affects the relative quantities of these **carbon-containing species**, with **bicarbonate **predominating in fresh water between **6.36 **and **10.25**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• As these waters interact with rocks and **sediments **they pick up metal ions, most frequently **calcium** and **magnesium**.
 
• These hard **fluids **often result in **carbonate **scale building up in boilers and **pipes**, and when they interact with **soap**, they create an unfavourable **scum**.

question: What type of isomerism exists in compounds containing two or more complexes, each of which contains a different set of ligands that can in principle be replaced with a ligand of the other complex?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Coordination isomerism.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coordination isomerism**

 
 
• **​**A type of structural **isomerism **known as** coordination isomerism** occurs when the coordination** complex ion'**s makeup changes.
 
• The overall **ligand **to metal ratio in a **coordination isomer **doesn't vary, but the **ligands **bound to a particular **metal **ion do.
 
• Instances of a whole series of **coordination** **isomers **call for two or even more** metal ions**.
 
• The **exchange **of one or more ligands between the cationic complex ion and the anionic complex ion is known as coordination isomerism, and it happens in **compounds **that have** complex anionic** and **cationic components**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Two or more **coordination compounds **having a difference in composition within the **coordination **sphere are said to be **coordination isomers**.
 
• This kind of **isomerism **is caused by the exchange of **ligands **between anionic and cationic entities of various metal ions that are present in the complex.
 
• **Coordination isomerism**, which can be thought of as an exchange of some **ligands **from the **cation **to the anion, occurs in **compounds **that contain complex cationic and **anionic components**.
 
• As a result, two **complicated chemicals **that have opposite charges one **negative **and the other **positive **are linked together.

question: In 1931, who recognised that an aromatic compound must have an odd number of pairs of electrons, which can mathematically be written as 4n + 2 (n = 0, 1, 2, 3 etc.)?
solution:
The correct answer is __Erich Huckel__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Erich Huckel was a German chemist and physicist.
 
• He proposed a theory in 1931 to help determine if a planar ring molecule would have aromatic properties.
 
• Erich Huckel recognized that an aromatic compound must have an odd number of pairs of electrons.
 
• His rule states that a cyclic, planar molecule is considered aromatic if it has 4n+2 pi electrons.
 
• This rule is known as Huckel's Rule.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Pi bond:- Bond formed by the same phase overlap of atomic orbitals along a direction perpendicular to the internuclear axis is called pi bond.
 
• Pi electrons:- An electron that resides in the pi bond (s) of a double bond or a triple bond or in a conjugated p orbital is called pi electron.
 
• ​System is divided into aromatic, anti-aromatic, and non-aromatic based on no. of pi electrons-
 
 
• ​​​Aromatic system - The number of pi electrons in an aromatic system is determined by N = 4n+2 (n is an integer)
 
• Anti-aromatic system - The number of pi electrons in an anti-aromatic system is determined by N = 4n (n is an integer)
 
• Non-aromatic - If a compound does not have a continuous ring of conjugated p orbitals in a planar module, then it is called non-aromatic.
