question: The color order in a secondary rainbow is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Reversed compared to primary rainbow**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• A **secondary rainbow** occurs due to **double reflection** of sunlight inside water droplets, unlike the **primary rainbow**, which happens due to a single reflection. 
• The color order in the secondary rainbow is **reversed** compared to the primary rainbow. In the primary rainbow, the sequence is **red on the outer edge** and **violet on the inner edge**, while the secondary rainbow has **violet on the outer edge** and **red on the inner edge**. 
• The reversing of colors in the secondary rainbow is caused by the **additional internal reflection** within the raindrop, which changes the direction of light rays and flips the color sequence. 
• Secondary rainbows are generally **fainter** than primary rainbows because of the **double reflection**, which results in more light being lost during the process. 
• The secondary rainbow appears **higher in the sky** than the primary rainbow and forms at an angle of approximately **50–53 degrees** from the direction opposite to the sun. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Primary Rainbow:** 
• Formed due to **single internal reflection** of sunlight within raindrops. 
• The color sequence is **red** (outer edge) to **violet** (inner edge). 
• The angle of formation is typically **40–42 degrees** from the direction opposite to the sun. 
• **Secondary Rainbow Characteristics:** 
• Formed due to **two internal reflections** of sunlight within raindrops. 
• Color sequence is **reversed**, with **violet** on the outer edge and **red** on the inner edge. 
• Appears **fainter** than the primary rainbow due to additional light dispersion. 
• **Light Dispersion and Reflection:** 
• Rainbows are created due to **dispersion of light**, where white sunlight splits into its component colors when passing through water droplets. 
• Reflection and refraction within the raindrops lead to the bending and focusing of light to form the rainbow. 
• **Supernumerary Rainbow:** 
• In rare cases, **supernumerary rainbows** may form as additional faint and closely spaced bands inside the primary rainbow. 
• These are caused by **wave interference** of light rather than simple refraction and reflection. 
• **Important Facts:** 
• Rainbows only appear when the sun is **low in the sky**, typically early morning or late afternoon. 
• Rainbows are always seen in the direction opposite to the sun. 
• Rainbows are **circular**, but only the upper portion is visible due to the horizon; a full circle can be seen from higher altitudes, such as in an airplane. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Scientific Explanation:** 
• The reversal of colors in the secondary rainbow is explained by **Snell’s law**, which governs refraction of light. 
• The additional internal reflection leads to more **light scattering**, causing the secondary rainbow to appear dimmer. 
• **Historical Observations:** 
• The phenomenon of rainbows has been studied since ancient times by scientists like **René Descartes** and **Isaac Newton**, who explained the principles of light dispersion. 
• Newton’s **prism experiments** demonstrated how light splits into its constituent colors. 
• **Applications:** 
• Rainbows are used in teaching concepts of **optics** and **light behavior**, including refraction, reflection, and dispersion. 
• The study of rainbows helps understand **weather patterns** and the **formation of raindrops** in the atmosphere.

subject: GK
question: How does a concave mirror form an image when an object is located at its center of curvature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Real, inverted, and same size.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Concave mirror and its image formation:** A concave mirror forms images based on the position of the object relative to its principal focus (**F**) and center of curvature (**C**).

• **Object at the center of curvature (C):** When an object is placed at the center of curvature of a concave mirror, the image is formed at the same location as the object, i.e., at **C**.

• **Nature of the image:** The image formed is **real, inverted, and of the same size** as the object.

• **Reflection mechanics:** In this position, light rays originating from the object strike the mirror and converge at the same distance, creating an image identical in size and orientation (except inverted).

• **Ray diagram:** A ray diagram of a concave mirror with the object at **C** clearly shows the reflected rays intersecting at the same point on the other side of the mirror, confirming the image characteristics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Concave Mirror Basics:**

• A concave mirror is a spherical mirror with its reflective surface curving inward, resembling the interior of a sphere.

• It is also known as a **converging mirror** because it converges light rays that fall on its surface.

• **Image Characteristics by Object Position:**

• **Beyond C:** Image is real, inverted, and diminished.

• **At C:** Image is real, inverted, and of the same size.

• **Between C and F:** Image is real, inverted, and magnified.

• **At F:** Image is highly magnified and formed at infinity.

• **Between F and Mirror:** Image is virtual, erect, and magnified.

• **Applications of Concave Mirrors:**

• **Shaving mirrors:** Provide a magnified and upright image.

• **Telescope:** Used in reflecting telescopes to gather and focus light.

• **Headlights:** Used in car headlights to focus light into a beam.

• **Real vs. Virtual Images:**

• **Real images:** Formed when light rays converge and can be projected on a screen.

• **Virtual images:** Formed when light rays only appear to diverge and cannot be projected on a screen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Mirror Equation:** The mirror equation is given by **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**, where:

• **f:** Focal length of the mirror.

• **v:** Image distance from the mirror.

• **u:** Object distance from the mirror.

• **Magnification:** The magnification (M) of a mirror is given by **M = -v/u**. For an object at **C**, magnification is **-1** (image is of the same size but inverted).

• **Principal Focus and Radius of Curvature:**

• The distance between the mirror and the principal focus is called the **focal length (f)**.

• The radius of curvature (**R**) is twice the focal length (**R = 2f**).

</ul

subject: GK
question: A person needs spectacles with a power of -2.5 D. This indicates that the person is suffering from:

options.text: Hypermetropia (farsightedness) and needs a converging lens.
Myopia (nearsightedness) and needs a diverging lens.
Presbyopia and needs a bifocal lens.
Astigmatism and needs a cylindrical lens.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Myopia (nearsightedness) and needs a diverging lens**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Myopia (Nearsightedness)** is a vision condition in which a person can see nearby objects clearly but struggles to see distant objects clearly. This is caused by the excessive elongation of the eyeball or excessive curvature of the cornea. 
• The power of the lens in spectacles is denoted by diopters (D). A negative lens power (-2.5 D in this case) indicates the use of a **diverging (concave) lens**, which is used to correct myopia. 
• The diverging lens functions by spreading out light rays before they enter the eye so that the focus point shifts backward onto the retina, correcting the blurred vision for distant objects. 
• The spectacle prescription (-2.5 D) signifies the degree of myopia, and the higher the negative value, the more severe the condition. 
• Myopia can occur due to **hereditary factors**, excessive screen time, or prolonged near work, and it is commonly diagnosed in childhood or adolescence. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Hypermetropia (Farsightedness):** 
• In this condition, a person can see distant objects clearly but struggles to see nearby objects clearly. 
• It is corrected using a **converging (convex) lens**, which helps in focusing light rays onto the retina. 
• This condition is often caused by a shorter-than-normal eyeball or a less curved cornea. 
• **Presbyopia:** 
• This is an age-related condition where the eye's lens loses flexibility, causing difficulty in focusing on nearby objects. 
• It commonly occurs after the age of **40 years** and is corrected using **bifocal or progressive lenses**. 
• **Astigmatism:** 
• Astigmatism is caused by an irregularly shaped cornea or lens, leading to distorted or blurred vision at all distances. 
• This condition is corrected using a **cylindrical lens**, which compensates for the uneven curvature of the cornea or lens. 
• **Important Points:** 
• Corrective lenses (like concave or convex lenses) are prescribed after an eye examination by an optometrist or ophthalmologist. 
• Regular eye check-ups are crucial to detect and manage vision-related issues early. 
• Uncorrected refractive errors, such as myopia or hypermetropia, can lead to complications like eye strain, headaches, or progressive worsening of vision. </ul

question: What do you call the effect of splitting of a spectral line into several components in the presence of a static magnetic field?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Zeeman effect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zeeman Effect**__

 __
 
• It is the name of the phenomena in physics and astronomy which involves the **splitting of a spectral line into two or more components of slightly different frequencies when the light source is placed in a magnetic field**.
 
• It is named after the Dutch physicist Pieter Zeeman.
 
• The effect is caused due to the distortion of the electron orbitals because of the magnetic field.
 
• This effect is very useful in investigating the charge/mass ratio and magnetic moment of an electron.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3960b9d2557a20b6a3f2c8a2a9c04c064ebafe04ec585bb3abd1d9311f3406d9.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Askaryan effect**

 
 
• It is the phenomenon whereby a particle travelling faster than the phase velocity of light in a dense dielectric medium (such as salt, ice) produces a shower of secondary charged particles.
 
• The Askaryan effect describes coherent electromagnetic radiation from high-energy cascades in dense media with a collective charge.
 
 
 
• **Bezold effect**
 
 
• It is an optical illusion.
 
• It is named after a German professor of meteorology, Wilhelm von Bezold.
 
• He discovered that a colour may appear different depending on its relation to adjacent colours.
 
• It happens when small areas of colour are interspersed.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2cde349b3d6197f7479ca03c197be9eb4ae9c5550bda653d74182c53cf2913f8.png] 

 
• **Domino effect**

 
 
• It is a cumulative effect produced when one event initiates a succession of similar events.

question: Who conducted an X-ray spectroscopic study of a large number of elements and showed that the frequency of X-rays emitted by an element is related to the atomic number, Z, rather than the atomic mass?
solution:
The correct option is __**Henry Moseley**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 1913 AD, the English scientist** Henry Moseley **demonstrated, with the help of experiments done using an X-ray tube, that the **atomic number (Z) of an element corresponds to the positive charge on the nucleus or the number of the protons in the nucleus of the atom of that element**.
 
• This revealed that the atomic number is a more fundamental property of an element than its atomic mass.
 
• Henry Moseley observed **regularities in the characteristic** X-ray spectra of the elements. A plot frequency of X-ray emitted against **atomic number gave a straight line and the plot of the frequency of X-rays emitted vs atomic mass was not a straight line**.
 
• Based on the above experiments he proposed that the physical and chemical properties of the elements are periodic functions of their atomic number.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A German chemist, **Julius Lothar Meyer** 1869, was looking at the physical properties of elements along with their valence states. He made a table that contained a preliminary tabulation of 28 elements. The table showed how the integral valence changed as the atomic weight of elements increase
 
• On 17 February 1869, **Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev** jotted down the symbols for the chemical elements, putting them in order according to their atomic weights and inventing the periodic table. He wrote down the sequence in such a way that they ended up grouped on the page according to known regularities or ‘periodicities’ of behaviour. It was perhaps the greatest breakthrough in the history of chemistry
 
• In 1829** Johann Wolfgang Dobereiner** discovered the **existence of families of elements with similar chemical** properties. Because there always seemed to be three elements in these families, he called them triads.

question: In the Right-Hand Thumb Rule, the thumb is directed towards the direction of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**current**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b72937cf535ccde879f48f3c0a69560cb6e29a846b9275f66f205b5affbd5db4.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Right-Hand Thumb Rule is used to determine the direction of the magnetic field relative to the direction of the current.
 
• In this rule, the thumb points in the direction of the current, and the fingers curl around the conductor, indicating the direction of the magnetic field lines.
 
• The Right-Hand Thumb Rule helps visualize the 3-dimensional relationship between current and magnetic fields, crucial in electromagnetism.
 
• This rule is fundamental in understanding the behavior of electromagnets, electric motors, and generators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Current**

 
 
• Current is the flow of electric charge in a conductor, typically measured in amperes (A).
 
• It is the movement of electrons through a conductive material, such as a wire.
 
• The direction of conventional current is taken as the direction in which positive charge carriers would move.
 
• In most practical scenarios, electrons (negative charge carriers) move in the opposite direction to the conventional current.
 
 
 
• **Electric Field**
 
 
• An electric field is a region around a charged particle or object within which a force would be exerted on other charged particles or objects.
 
• It is represented by field lines that point in the direction a positive test charge would move if placed in the field.
 
• The strength of the electric field is measured in volts per meter (V/m).
 
• Electric fields are fundamental to the behavior of electric charges and the operation of capacitors.
 
 
 
• **Motion of the Conductor**
 
 
• The motion of a conductor in a magnetic field induces a voltage across the conductor.
 
• This phenomenon is described by Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction.
 
• The direction of the induced voltage is given by Lenz's Law, which states that the induced voltage will oppose the change in magnetic flux.
 
• This principle is applied in the operation of electric generators.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field**
 
 
• A magnetic field is a vector field that describes the magnetic influence on moving electric charges, electric currents, and magnetic materials.
 
• It is represented by field lines that indicate the direction and strength of the magnetic force.
 
• The strength of a magnetic field is measured in teslas (T) or gauss (G).
 
• Magnetic fields are fundamental to the operation of electromagnets, transformers, and magnetic storage devices.

options.text: Electric Generator : Converts electrical energy to mechanical energy.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Electric Bell: Uses the magnetic effect of electric current.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An electric bell operates on the principle of the **magnetic effect of electric current**, where an electromagnet is created by passing an electric current through a coil of wire.
 
• The magnetic field generated attracts a metal armature, causing it to strike the bell and produce sound.
 
• The electric bell consists of components like an electromagnet, armature, contact screw, and hammer, all working in synchronization to create the ringing sound.
 
• When the circuit is complete, the current flows through the coil, magnetizing the core, and pulling the armature, which simultaneously breaks the circuit and causes the hammer to strike the bell.
 
• This cycle repeats rapidly as long as the switch is pressed, producing a continuous ringing sound.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electric Generator: Converts electrical energy to mechanical energy**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect. An electric generator actually converts **mechanical energy into electrical energy**.
 
• It operates on the principle of electromagnetic induction, as discovered by Michael Faraday, where a conductor moving through a magnetic field induces an electric current.
 
• Generators are widely used in power plants to produce electricity for homes, industries, and businesses.
 
 
 
• **Transformer: Operates on DC current to change voltage**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect because transformers **only work with alternating current (AC)**, not direct current (DC).
 
• Transformers are used to step up (increase) or step down (decrease) the voltage levels in an AC circuit.
 
• They function based on the principle of mutual induction between two coils of wire.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnet: A permanent magnet**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect because an electromagnet is a **temporary magnet** that only exhibits magnetic properties when an electric current flows through its coil.
 
• Once the current is stopped, the magnetic field disappears, unlike a permanent magnet that retains its magnetism.
 
• Electromagnets are widely used in devices like motors, relays, and magnetic cranes.

• Auroras occur due to the** interaction between charged particles from the solar wind** and Earth's magnetic field.
 
• When these charged particles (mostly electrons and protons) collide with gases in Earth's atmosphere, such as oxygen and nitrogen, they excite these gases, causing them to emit light, which we see as auroras.
 
• Earth's **magnetosphere directs the solar wind particles** toward the polar regions, leading to the phenomenon predominantly occurring near the poles.
 
• The distinct colors of auroras, such as green, red, and purple, are due to different gases in the atmosphere and their altitude of interaction. For example, oxygen produces green or red hues, while nitrogen emits blue or purple light.
 
• Auroras are known as the **Aurora Borealis (Northern Lights)** in the northern hemisphere and **Aurora Australis (Southern Lights)** in the southern hemisphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Earthquake Waves**:

 
 
• Earthquake waves are seismic waves generated by the sudden release of energy in Earth's crust during an earthquake.
 
• There are two main types of seismic waves: **body waves** (P-waves and S-waves) that travel through Earth's interior and **surface waves** that move along Earth's surface.
 
• Seismic waves have no direct connection to the formation of auroras, as they are related to geological activity, not atmospheric or solar phenomena.
 
 
 
• **Lightning Discharges**:
 
 
• Lightning is a sudden electrostatic discharge caused by the imbalance of electrical charges between clouds, the air, or the ground.
 
• It produces light, heat, and sound (thunder) but does not involve solar wind or Earth's magnetic field.
 
• Although lightning occurs in Earth's atmosphere, it is unrelated to the mechanisms that create auroras.
 
 
 
• **Volcanic Ash Dispersion**:
 
 
• Volcanic ash dispersion refers to the spread of fine particles of ash into the atmosphere during a volcanic eruption.
 
• These particles can affect air travel, weather patterns, and climate but do not emit light or involve charged particles from the solar wind.
 
• While volcanic eruptions can produce phenomena like lightning within the ash plume, they are unrelated to auroras.

question:
Two resistors, one with a resistance of 2 ohms and the other with a resistance of 4 ohms, are connected in parallel to a 6-volt battery.

What is the total current flowing through the circuit?
solution:
The correct answer is __**4.5 Amperes**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The two resistors of **2 ohms** and **4 ohms** are connected in **parallel**. In a parallel circuit, the total resistance is calculated using the formula: 
**1/Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂**. 
• Substituting the values: 
**1/Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4**. 
Thus, **Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 4/3 ohms**. 
• The circuit is powered by a **6-volt battery**. Using **Ohm’s Law** (**V = IR**), the total current can be calculated: 
**Iₜₒₜₐₗ = V/Rₜₒₜₐₗ**. 
Substitute the values: 
**Iₜₒₜₐₗ = 6 / (4/3) = 6 × 3/4 = 4.5 Amperes**. 
• Hence, the total current flowing through the circuit is **4.5 Amperes**. 
• Each resistor shares the current based on its resistance. The **current through the 2-ohm resistor** is: 
**I = V/R = 6/2 = 3 Amperes**. 
The **current through the 4-ohm resistor** is: 
**I = V/R = 6/4 = 1.5 Amperes**. 
Adding these gives **4.5 Amperes**, verifying the calculation. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Ohm’s Law:** 
• **Ohm’s Law** states that the current flowing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points, provided the temperature remains constant. 
• The formula is: **V = IR**, where **V** is voltage, **I** is current, and **R** is resistance. 
• **Parallel Circuit Properties:** 
• In a parallel circuit, the **voltage across all components remains the same**. 
• The total resistance in a parallel circuit is always **less than the smallest individual resistance**. 
• The total current is the **sum of the currents through each parallel branch**. 
• **Resistor Applications:** 
• Resistors are widely used in electrical circuits for **current regulation, voltage division, and protection against overcurrent**. 
• They are categorized as **fixed resistors** (constant resistance) or **variable resistors** (adjustable resistance). 
• **Battery Characteristics:** 
• A battery is a device that converts chemical energy into electrical energy. The **voltage rating** of a battery determines the electric potential difference it can provide. 
• Common batteries include **AA, AAA, lithium-ion, and lead-acid batteries**, used in various applications like household electronics, vehicles, and industrial equipment. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Series vs. Parallel Circuits:** 
• **Series Circuit:** The current remains constant throughout the circuit, and the total resistance is the sum of individual resistances (**Rₜₒₜₐₗ = R₁ + R₂ + …**). 
• **Parallel Circuit:** The voltage remains constant across all branches, and the total resistance is calculated using **1/Rₜₒₜₐₗ = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + …**. 
• **Electrical Safety:** 
• To prevent electrical hazards, circuits are often equipped with **fuses, circuit breakers, and insulation materials**. 
• Proper resistance calculations are critical to ensure **safe operation and avoid overheating**. 
• **Practical Examples:** 
• Parallel circuits are commonly found in **home electrical systems**, ensuring that individual appliances function independently. 
• Series circuits are used in applications like **string lights**, where the current flows through all components sequentially.

question: A person standing on a railway platform notices that the sound of an approaching train's whistle changes in pitch (frequency) as the train passes by. This phenomenon is best explained by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Doppler effect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Doppler effect is the change in the frequency or wavelength of a wave concerning an observer moving relative to the wave source.
 
• It occurs for all types of waves, including sound, light, and water waves, and is commonly experienced in the case of sound waves.
 
• In the given scenario, as the train approaches, the sound waves compress, causing an increase in frequency (higher pitch), and as it moves away, the sound waves spread out, causing a decrease in frequency (lower pitch).
 
• The mathematical expression for the Doppler effect in sound is given by: f' = f(v + vo) / (v + vs), where f' is the observed frequency, f is the source frequency, v is the speed of sound, vo is the observer’s velocity, and vs is the source velocity.
 
• This phenomenon has practical applications in various fields, such as astronomy (to study the motion of stars and galaxies), radar technology, and medical imaging (Doppler ultrasound).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refraction of Sound**

 
 
• Refraction refers to the bending of sound waves as they pass from one medium to another, where the speed of sound differs.
 
• For instance, sound waves bend towards cooler regions where the speed of sound is slower.
 
• While refraction affects the propagation direction of sound, it does not explain the change in pitch observed in the given scenario.
 
 
 
• **Diffraction of Sound**
 
 
• Diffraction is the bending of sound waves around obstacles or through openings.
 
• It allows sound to be heard even when the source is not in the direct line of sight.
 
• This phenomenon is unrelated to the change in frequency or pitch caused by relative motion between the source and observer.
 
 
 
• **Resonance**
 
 
• Resonance occurs when an object vibrates at its natural frequency due to an external force of the same frequency.
 
• This results in a significant increase in amplitude, as seen in musical instruments or structures like bridges.
 
• Resonance does not explain the change in pitch when the train passes by, as it is unrelated to relative motion or frequency shifts.

• The **speed of sound increases** significantly in water compared to air due to the higher density and elasticity of water.
 
• The **wavelength of the sound wave changes** because wavelength is directly proportional to the speed of sound in the medium (wavelength = speed/frequency).
 
• In water, due to the increased speed of sound, the wavelength becomes longer compared to its value in air.
 
• This phenomenon adheres to the principle of wave mechanics, where the product of frequency and wavelength equals the speed of the wave.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Behavior of Sound Waves in Different Media**

 
 
• Sound is a mechanical wave that requires a medium to propagate and travels as a longitudinal wave.
 
• The speed of sound depends on the medium's density and elasticity. It travels faster in solids, slower in liquids, and slowest in gases.
 
• The relationship between speed, frequency, and wavelength is given by the equation: speed = frequency × wavelength.
 
• The change in speed and wavelength occurs to maintain the same frequency as the wave moves from one medium to another.

question: If the speed of sound in a medium is 340 m/s and a sound wave has a frequency of 680 Hz, what is its wavelength?

The correct answer is __**Option 1) 0.5 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The relationship between the speed of sound, frequency, and wavelength is given by the formula: **speed = frequency × wavelength**.
 
• Here, the speed of sound is 340 m/s, and the frequency is 680 Hz.
 
• To calculate the wavelength, rearrange the formula: **wavelength = speed ÷ frequency**.
 
• Substituting the values: wavelength = 340 ÷ 680 = **0.5 m**.
 
• Thus, the wavelength of the sound wave is **0.5 meters**, which corresponds to Option 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speed, Frequency, and Wavelength:**

 
 
• The speed of a wave is the product of its frequency and wavelength: **speed = frequency × wavelength**.
 
• Frequency is the number of wave cycles passing through a point in one second, measured in Hertz (Hz).
 
• Wavelength is the distance between two consecutive points in phase (e.g., crests or troughs) on a wave, measured in meters.
 
• This relationship is fundamental in the study of wave mechanics and applies to all types of waves, including sound waves, light waves, and water waves.

• The **perceived frequency**, also known as the apparent frequency, is determined by the **Doppler Effect**, which explains how the frequency of a wave changes in relation to an observer who is moving relative to the source of the wave. 
 
• If the **source and the listener move with the same speed in the same direction**, the relative velocity between them remains constant. This means there is **no relative motion** between the source and the listener in the direction of the wave.

• The **Doppler Shift formula** for perceived frequency is given by: 
 *f' = f * (v + vₒ) / (v + vₛ)*

question:
A sound wave travels from air into water.
How do its speed and wavelength change?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Speed increases, wavelength increases.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• When a sound wave travels from **air to water**, its **speed increases**. This is because the speed of sound depends on the **medium's density and elasticity**. Water, being denser and more elastic than air, allows sound to travel faster.

• The **wavelength** of the sound wave also increases when it enters water. This is because the wavelength is proportional to the speed of the wave when the frequency remains constant.

• **Frequency** of the sound wave does not change during the transition between two media. It remains constant because frequency is determined by the source of the sound and not by the medium.

• The relationship between the speed, wavelength, and frequency is given by the formula: **v = f × λ**, where **v** is the speed, **f** is the frequency, and **λ** is the wavelength. When speed (**v**) increases and frequency (**f**) remains constant, the wavelength (**λ**) must also increase.

• As water is a denser and more elastic medium compared to air, sound travels approximately **4.3 times faster** in water than in air.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Speed of Sound in Different Media**: 

• The speed of sound in air (at 20°C) is approximately **343 m/s**.

• In water, the speed of sound is about **1482 m/s** (at 25°C), which is much faster than in air.

• In solids like steel, sound travels even faster, at around **5000 m/s**.

• **Factors Affecting Speed of Sound**: 

• **Density:** Higher density generally decreases speed; however, in liquids and solids, elasticity plays a more significant role.

• **Elasticity:** Greater elasticity increases the speed of sound.

• **Temperature:** In gases, an increase in temperature increases the speed of sound.

• **Why Frequency Remains Constant**: 

• The frequency of a wave is determined by its source and does not change when the wave moves between different media.

• As a result, changes in the wave's speed directly affect its wavelength in the new medium.

• **Applications of Sound Wave Properties**: 

• Sonar systems use the increased speed of sound in water for underwater navigation and communication.

• Medical ultrasonography leverages the varying speeds of sound in different tissues for imaging.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Formula for Wave Behavior:** The equation **v = f × λ** is critical for understanding how speed, frequency, and wavelength are interrelated.

• **Why Sound Travels Faster in Water:** Water molecules are more tightly packed compared to air molecules, allowing sound waves to transfer energy more efficiently.

• **Effect of Medium on Amplitude:** While speed and wavelength may change, the amplitude of the sound wave can also vary, affecting the wave's intensity.

• **Real-Life Phenomena:** This principle explains why sounds underwater (like a dolphin's echolocation clicks) can be heard over long distances.

 **Conductor__**

 __
 
• 
 
**​__**A substance or material that permits the flow of electricity is known as an electrical conductor. When voltage is provided, electrical charge carriers, often electrons or ions, travel effortlessly from atom to atom in a conductor.

 
 
• 
 
Several types of electrical conductors include - Human Body, Copper, Aluminium, Silver, Gold, Graphite, Platinum.

 
 
• 
 
Electric charges can easily pass through an electrical conductor. Conductivity is the ability of conductors to "conduct" electricity. Such materials provide less barrier to the movement of charges. Because electrons can freely flow through conducting materials, charge transfer is simple. Such materials offer less opposition or “resistance” to the flow of charges. Conducting materials allows easy charge transfer because of the free movement of electrons through them.

 
 
 
 
• **__Electrical Conductor Properties__**
 __
 
• 
 
The flow of electrons and ions via a conductor is constant.

 
 
• 
 
Since there is no electric field inside a conductor, electrons can move around freely.

 
 
• 
 
Inside a conductor, the charge density is zero.

 
 
• 
 
Free charges are only present on the conductor's surface.

 
 
• 
 
A conductor's points are all at the same potential.

 
 
• 
 
Many metals are effective electrical conductors. This is the rationale behind the use of metals in electrical appliance parts. Insulators are the plastic casings that shield electrical conductors. We won't experience an electric shock thanks to it.

• Alloy Conductor: Brass, Bronze, etc.
 
• __**Liquid Conductor**__
 
• Metallic Conductor: Mercury
 
• Non Metallic Conductor: Saline Water, Acid Solution, etc.
 
• Copper Conductor is the most common material used for electrical wiring.

question: If Q = net charge, t = time, then which of the following equations is correct?
solution:
The correct answer is **I =Q over t**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Current, charge and time**

 
 
• How much electric charge is transferred each second defines electrical current, giving the following relationship:

 **Current= charge/ time**

 Rearranging this we get,

 charge= current * time
 
• The symbol for charge is **Q**, it is measured in **coulombs (C).**
 
• The symbol for current is** I**, it is measured in **amperes (A).**
 
• The symbol for time is** t**, it is measured in **seconds (t).**
 
• This gives the relation:

 **Q= I* t**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Current**

 
 
• A stream of charged particles, like **electrons or ions**, moving through an electrical conductor or space is called an electric current.
 
• The net rate of electric **charge flow** through a surface or into a control volume is how it is measured.
 
• Depending on the conductor, the **moving particles** are referred to as charge carriers, which can be any one of a number of different types of particles.
 
 
 
• **Charge**
 
 
• A charge in physics can be any of a number of different quantities, such as the color charge in **quantum** chromodynamics or the electric charge in **electromagnetism.**
 
• The time-invariant generators of a symmetry group, and more specifically, the generators that commute with the **Hamiltonian**, are represented by charges.
 
• The charge invariance corresponds to the vanishing commutator **[Q,H]=0**, where H is the Hamiltonian because **charges** are frequently denoted by the letter Q.
 
• As a result, charges and **conserved quantum** numbers are linked; these are the **eigenvalues q **of the generator Q.
 
 
 
• **Time**
 
 
• From the past through the present and into the future, time is the ongoing sequence of existence and events that appears to be** irreversible.**
 
• It is a component quantity of various measurements used to order events, compare their **durations or intervals**, and quantify rates of change of quantities in material reality or conscious experience.
 
• Along with the three spatial dimensions, time is frequently referred to as a **fourth dimension.**

question: Seismograph is used to measure:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Earthquakes**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plate Tectonics**:

 
 
• Seismographs can provide indirect evidence supporting the theory of plate tectonics.
 
• By recording earthquake patterns and magnitudes around the world, they help illustrate the world’s tectonic plate boundaries where earthquakes are common.
 
 
 
• **Epicenter and Focus of Earthquakes**:
 
 
• Seismographs play a crucial role in locating the epicenter (geographical location directly above the focus on the surface) and the focus (actual location within the earth where the earthquake originates) of an earthquake.
 
• Data collected from minimum three seismograph stations is used to triangulate the epicenter of an earthquake.
 
 
 
• **Seismic Wave Speed Variations**:
 
 
• P-waves (primary waves) and S-waves (secondary waves) recorded by seismographs travel at different speeds and through different parts of the Earth's interior.
 
• Based on their arrival times at seismograph stations, we can infer properties of the Earth's interior, such as the presence of a molten outer core (which S-waves cannot travel through).
 
 
 
• **Seismicities**:
 
 
• Analysis of seismographs can help identify areas known as seismicities - geographical zones with a high frequency of earthquakes.
 
• Historical data from seismographs can therefore be used to predict regions where future earthquakes may occur.
 
 
 
• **Earth's Interior Structure**:
 
 
• Seismograph readings help scientists understand the Earth's interior structure better.
 
• For instance, changes in seismic wave velocity indicate interfaces between different layers of the Earth's interior, such as the crust, mantle, and core.
 
 
 
• **Human-Induced Seismic Activity**:
 
 
• Seismographs not only capture natural seismic activity, but also man-made seismic events such as those resulting from mining, reservoir-induced seismicity, nuclear tests, and construction work.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Earthquake Waves**:

 
• Earthquake waves are vibrations in the Earth's crust caused by seismic events like earthquakes or volcanic activity.
 
• Two main types: body waves and surface waves.

**Body Waves**:

 
• Generated at the earthquake's focus and travel in all directions through the Earth's interior.
 
• Interact with surface rocks, generating surface waves.
 
• Changes in velocity and direction due to material density differences.
 
• **Two types**: P-waves (primary waves) and S-waves (secondary waves).

**P-Waves (Primary Waves)**: 

 
• Fastest seismic waves, reaching the surface first.
 
• Similar to sound waves, they travel through gaseous, liquid, and solid materials.
 
• Provide important information about the Earth's interior structure.

**S-Waves (Secondary Waves)**:

 
• Arrive at the surface after P-waves.
 
• Can only travel through solid materials, not liquids or gases.
 
• Vital for understanding the Earth's interior composition and structure.

**Surface Waves**:

 
• ​Generated by interaction between body waves and surface rocks.
 
• Slowest seismic waves, causing significant damage.
 
• Displace rocks and contribute to structural collapses.

subject: GK
question: A key characteristic of nuclear fission is that the total mass of the products is:

options.text: Greater than the mass of the reactants
Equal to the mass of the reactants
Less than the mass of the reactants
Dependent on the temperature of the reaction

solution:
The correct answer is __**Less than the mass of the reactants**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Nuclear fission** is a process in which the nucleus of a heavy atom, such as uranium-235 or plutonium-239, splits into two smaller nuclei, along with the release of energy and free neutrons. 
• During nuclear fission, a small amount of the **mass of the reactants** (original atom and neutron) is converted into energy according to **Einstein's mass-energy equivalence formula: E = mc²**, where **E** is energy, **m** is the mass lost, and **c** is the speed of light. 
• As a result, the **total mass of the products** (the resulting smaller nuclei and neutrons) is **less than the mass of the reactants**. 
• This difference in mass, referred to as the **mass defect**, is the source of the immense energy released during nuclear fission. 
• The energy released in nuclear fission is utilized in **nuclear reactors** and **nuclear weapons**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Energy Release in Nuclear Fission:** 
• When a nucleus such as uranium-235 absorbs a neutron, it becomes unstable and splits into two smaller nuclei (fission fragments) like krypton-92 and barium-141, along with the release of 2-3 neutrons and energy. 
• The energy released is approximately **200 MeV per fission reaction**, which is significantly higher than energy released in chemical reactions. 
• This energy is primarily in the form of **kinetic energy of the fission fragments** and is later converted into thermal energy in reactors. 
• **Mass-Energy Equivalence:** 
• The principle of mass-energy equivalence, given by **Albert Einstein** in 1905, states that mass can be converted into energy and vice versa. 
• The formula **E = mc²** explains how even a small mass defect results in a large amount of energy due to the large value of the speed of light (**c ≈ 3 × 10⁸ m/s**). 
• **Chain Reaction in Fission:** 
• The neutrons released in fission can trigger further fission reactions in nearby uranium or plutonium nuclei, leading to a self-sustaining process known as a **chain reaction**. 
• In nuclear reactors, this chain reaction is controlled using materials like **control rods** (made of boron or cadmium) to regulate the number of neutrons. 
• **Applications of Nuclear Fission:** 
• Fission is used in **nuclear power plants** to generate electricity by converting the thermal energy produced into electrical energy. 
• It is also used in **nuclear weapons**, where uncontrolled chain reactions lead to massive explosions. 
• **Fission vs. Fusion:** 
• While fission involves splitting a heavy nucleus, **nuclear fusion** involves combining two light nuclei (e.g., hydrogen isotopes) to form a heavier nucleus with the release of energy. 
• Fusion reactions power the **Sun and stars**, but achieving controlled fusion on Earth remains a challenge due to the extremely high temperatures and pressures required. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Fissionable Materials:** The most commonly used fissionable materials are **uranium-235** and **plutonium-239**. 
• **Neutron Moderators:** Materials like **graphite** or **heavy water** are used in reactors to slow down neutrons, making them more effective in causing fission. 
• **Waste Management:** Nuclear fission produces radioactive waste, which requires careful handling and long-term storage to prevent environmental contamination. 
• **Global Usage:** As of **2023**, nuclear power contributes about **10%** of the world's electricity production.

subject: GK
question: What happens during beta-plus (β⁺) decay in a nucleus?

options.text: Proton number decreases by 1, mass number remains unchanged
Proton number increases by 1, mass number remains unchanged
Both proton number and mass number decrease
Proton number decreases by 2, mass number decreases by 4

solution:
The correct answer is __**Proton number decreases by 1, mass number remains unchanged**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Beta-plus (β⁺) decay** occurs when a proton in a nucleus transforms into a neutron, emitting a **positron (β⁺)** and a **neutrino**. This process is mediated by the weak nuclear force. 
• As a result of β⁺ decay, the **proton number decreases by 1**, while the **mass number remains unchanged**. This is because a proton is converted to a neutron, and both particles have nearly equal masses. 
• The emitted positron is the antimatter counterpart of an electron, carrying a **positive charge**. 
• The process leads to the formation of a new element with an atomic number **lower by 1** than the original element, but the total number of nucleons (mass number) in the nucleus remains the same. 
• For example, during the β⁺ decay of carbon-11: 
• **Carbon-11 (6 protons, 5 neutrons)** transforms into **Boron-11 (5 protons, 6 neutrons)**, with the emission of a positron and a neutrino. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Other Types of Radioactive Decay:** 
• **Beta-minus (β⁻) decay:** A neutron transforms into a proton, emitting an electron and an antineutrino. In this case, the proton number increases by 1, and the mass number remains unchanged. 
• **Alpha (α) decay:** The nucleus emits an alpha particle (2 protons and 2 neutrons), leading to a decrease in both the mass number (by 4) and the atomic number (by 2). 
• **Gamma (γ) decay:** The nucleus releases excess energy in the form of gamma radiation without changing its composition (proton and neutron numbers remain the same). 
• **Applications of β⁺ Decay:** 
• β⁺ decay is utilized in **positron emission tomography (PET)**, a medical imaging technique used to study metabolic processes in the human body. 
• It plays a role in the synthesis of certain isotopes used in medical diagnostics. 
• **Characteristics of Positron:** 
• A positron is the **antiparticle of an electron**, having the same mass but carrying a positive charge. 
• When a positron encounters an electron, they annihilate each other, producing **gamma rays**. 
• **Important Facts:** 
• β⁺ decay typically occurs in proton-rich nuclei, where the proton-to-neutron ratio is too high for stability. 
• The weak nuclear force is responsible for β⁺ decay, as it governs the transformation of quarks within protons and neutrons. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Mass Number:** The total number of protons and neutrons in a nucleus. It remains constant during β⁺ decay as no nucleons are lost. 
• **Proton Number (Atomic Number):** The number of protons in the nucleus, which decreases by 1 during β⁺ decay. 
• **Weak Nuclear Force:** One of the four fundamental forces in nature, responsible for processes like β⁺ decay and β⁻ decay. 
• **Neutrino:** A nearly massless, electrically neutral particle emitted during β⁺ decay, which carries away energy and momentum.

• This reduces the **atomic number by 2** and the **mass number by 4**.

• It occurs in heavy nuclei, such as uranium or radium, to achieve stability.

• **Gamma Decay:**

• Gamma decay involves the emission of gamma rays (high-energy photons) from an excited nucleus.

• It does not change the atomic number or mass number but releases excess energy from the nucleus.

• This often accompanies alpha or beta decay.

• **Fission:**

• Nuclear fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus into two lighter nuclei, accompanied by the release of energy and neutrons.

• It significantly changes both the atomic and mass numbers of the original nucleus.

• Fission is commonly used in nuclear reactors and weapons.

• **Key Characteristics of Beta Decay:**

• There are two types: Beta-minus (β⁻) and Beta-plus (β⁺) decay.

• In β⁻ decay, a neutron is converted into a proton, emitting an electron and an antineutrino.

• In β⁺ decay, a proton is converted into a neutron, emitting a positron and a neutrino.

• Beta decay plays a critical role in processes like radioactive decay chains and nuclear reactions in stars.

• Helps in carbon dating to determine the age of archaeological artifacts (e.g., Carbon-14 decay).

• Used in studying nuclear reactions and understanding stellar processes.

• **Examples of Beta Decay:**

• **Carbon-14 (C-14):** Undergoes β⁻ decay to form Nitrogen-14 (N-14).

• **Potassium-40 (K-40):** Undergoes β⁺ decay to form Argon-40 (Ar-40).

__
 
• The SI unit of electric current is the **Ampere**, symbolized as **A**.
 
• It is named after **André-Marie Ampère**, a French physicist and mathematician who is considered one of the founders of the science of classical electromagnetism.
 
• One Ampere is defined as the flow of one coulomb of charge per second.
 
• It is a fundamental unit in the International System of Units (SI), and it is used to quantify the amount of electric charge passing a point in an electric circuit per unit time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm (Ω)**

 
 
• The Ohm is the SI unit of electrical resistance.
 
• Named after German physicist Georg Simon Ohm, it quantifies the resistance in a circuit.
 
• One Ohm is defined as the resistance between two points of a conductor when a constant potential difference of 1 Volt, applied to these points, produces a current of 1 Ampere.
 
 
 
• **Volt (V)**
 
 
• The Volt is the SI unit of electric potential, electric potential difference, and electromotive force.
 
• Named after the Italian physicist Alessandro Volta, it measures the potential difference between two points.
 
• One Volt is defined as the potential difference that will drive one Ampere of current against one Ohm of resistance.
 
 
 
• **Metre (m)**
 
 
• The Metre is the SI unit of length.
 
• It is defined as the distance traveled by light in a vacuum in 1/299,792,458 seconds.
 
• It is a fundamental unit in the metric system and is used to measure distance.

subject: GK
question: For a rigid body, the angular velocity of any particle about a given axis of rotation is:

options.text: Proportional to its distance from the axis
Inversely proportional to its distance from the axis

solution:
The Correct answer is __**The same for all particles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **rigid body**, all particles are fixed relative to each other and move collectively during rotation.
 
• The angular velocity is a measure of the rate of rotation of a body about a given axis and is denoted as **ω (omega)**.
 
• For a rigid body, the angular velocity of all particles is **the same** because they rotate together about the same axis at the same rate.
 
• While the linear velocity of particles depends on their distance from the axis of rotation, the angular velocity remains **constant** for all particles of the rigid body.
 
• This uniformity of angular velocity ensures that the body remains rigid and its shape does not change during rotation.
 
• Angular velocity is a **vector quantity**, having both magnitude and direction, where the direction is determined by the right-hand rule.
 
• The concept of angular velocity is widely used in **mechanics, engineering, and physics** to study rotational motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Proportional to its distance from the axis**__

 __
 
• The linear velocity of a particle in a rigid body is **proportional to its distance** from the axis of rotation. However, angular velocity is the same for all particles.
 
• This is because linear velocity (v) is calculated as v = ω × r, where **r** is the distance from the axis, and ω is the angular velocity.
 
 
 
• **Inversely proportional to its distance from the axis**__
 __
 
• This statement is incorrect because angular velocity does not depend on the distance from the axis. However, other properties, like torque, can depend inversely on certain factors.
 
 
 
• **Always zero**__
 
 
• For a rigid body in rotational motion, angular velocity is never zero unless the body is at rest.
 
• If angular velocity were zero, the body would not exhibit any rotational motion.

question:
A ball is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity of 10 m/s.

Ignoring air resistance, what is the maximum height it will reach?

(Assume g = 9.8 m/s²)
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Initial velocity** of the ball is given as **10 m/s**, and it is thrown vertically upward. 
• The maximum height can be determined using the **equation of motion:** v² = u² - 2gh , where: 
• **v** is the final velocity at the maximum height (0 m/s). 
• **u** is the initial velocity (10 m/s). 
• **g** is the acceleration due to gravity (9.8 {m/s}²). 
• **h** is the maximum height (to be calculated). 
• Substitute the values into the equation: 0 = (10)² - 2(9.8)h . 
• Rearranging: h = ((10)²)/(2 times 9.8) . 
• Calculate: h = (100)/(19.6) = 5.10 {m} . 
• **Maximum height reached by the ball is 5.10 m.** 
• *Hence, the correct answer is Option 2.* 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Equations of motion:** 
• The equations of motion are used to analyze objects in uniform acceleration. These are: 
• v = u + gt (velocity-time relation). 
• s = ut + (1)/(2)gt² (displacement-time relation). 
• v² = u² - 2gh (velocity-displacement relation). 
• **Gravity:** The acceleration due to gravity ( g ) is a constant value of 9.8 {m/s}² on the Earth’s surface. It acts downward toward the center of the Earth. 
• **Maximum height:** At the maximum height, the velocity of the ball becomes zero ( v = 0 ) because gravity completely decelerates the upward motion. 
• **Ignoring air resistance:** The calculations assume that air resistance is negligible, meaning the only force acting on the ball is gravity. 
• **Practical applications:** Understanding projectile motion is essential in sports, engineering, and physics, such as designing ballistics, rockets, and predicting motion trajectories. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Initial velocity:** The speed at which an object is launched determines its trajectory and maximum height. 
• **Effect of gravity:** Gravity causes the object to decelerate while moving upward and accelerates it while descending. 
• **Zero velocity at maximum height:** The object's upward motion halts momentarily before reversing direction. 
• **Air resistance:** In real-world scenarios, air resistance can significantly affect the motion, but here it is neglected for simplicity. 
• **Equation derivation:** The equations of motion are derived from Newton's laws of motion, providing a mathematical framework for analyzing linear motion under constant acceleration.

question: The 'Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan' (PM-AASHA) has________ components to rationalise the government agricultural produce price and policy for efficiency, savings by way of reduction of wastages and leakages in storage and make fiscal gains.
solution:
The correct answer is __**three.**__

__
 
• The **'Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan' (PM-AASHA)** has **three **components to rationalise the government agricultural produce price and policy for efficiency, savings by way of reduction of wastages and leakages in storage and making fiscal gains.
 
• It is a scheme that guarantees a **Minimum support price (MSP)** to the farmers.
 
• The scheme is an effort of the government’s commitment to ensure remunerative prices to farmers for their produce as announced in the **Union Budget for 2018. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The scheme comprises three sub-schemes:**

 
 
• Price Support Scheme (PSS)

 
 
• ​Under this, physical procurement of pulses, oilseeds, and Copra is to be done by Central Nodal Agencies in collaboration with state governments.
 
 
 
• Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS)
 
 
• ​This is based on the recommendations of NITI Aayog which suggested “Price Deficiency Payment” for implementation of MSP in crops where procurement is poor.
 
• Direct payment of the difference between the MSP and the selling price will be made to pre-registered farmers selling their produce in the notified market yard and thus it does not involve any physical procurement.
 
 
 
• The pilot of the Private Procurement & Stockist Scheme (PPPS)
 
 
• Under this scheme, participation of the private sector in procurement operations will be piloted.
 
• States have the option to roll out the scheme on a pilot basis in selected districts/APMCs involving private stockists.

__
 
• The Immunization Programme introduced in India as the 'Expanded Programme of Immunization' (EPI) by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare was introduced in India in the year **1978**.

• The **objective** of the programme was:
 
 
• To reduce morbidity and mortality from diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, poliomyelitis and childhood tuberculosis by providing immunization services to all eligible children and pregnant women by 1990.

• **Universal Immunization Programme (UIP)** is one of the largest public health programmes targeting close to 2.67 crore newborns and 2.9 crore pregnant women annually.
 
• It is one of the most cost-effective public health interventions and is largely responsible for the reduction of vaccine-preventable under-5 mortality rate.
 
• Under UIP, immunization is provided free of cost against **12 vaccine-preventable diseases**.
 
• Nationally against 9 diseases - **Diphtheria, Pertussis, Tetanus, Polio, Measles, Rubella, a severe form of Childhood Tuberculosis, Hepatitis B and Meningitis & Pneumonia** caused by Hemophilus Influenza type B.

question: MUDRA is a financial institution set up by the Government of India for the development and refinancing of micro unit enterprises. The full form of MUDRA is:

options.text: Micro Finance Usage Development & Refinance Agent

solution:
The correct answer is __**Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **MUDRA **stands for **Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency.**

• **Option 1 **(Micro Urban Development & Refinance Agency) and **Option 4** (Medium Units Development & Refinance Agency) are** incorrect** as MUDRA focuses on** micro and small enterprises** only.
 
• **Option 3** (Micro Finance Usage Development & Refinance Agent) is also** incorrect **as it does not represent the full form of MUDRA.
 
• Hence, the **correct** answer is option 2.

• It​ is a **government initiative **aimed at improving the **nutritional status **of** pregnant and lactating mothers, infants, and children **under the age of** 6 years.**

• It utilizes technology for real-time monitoring, data collection, and assessment of nutritional interventions, aiding in better planning and implementation.
 
• The mission focuses on behavior change communication, aiming to promote better nutritional practices and habits at the community level.
 
• Adequate budget allocation is crucial for the successful implementation of the mission's strategies and interventions.

question: Which of the following schemes is available to people in the age group of 18 to 50 years and provides risk coverage of ₹2 lakh in case of death of the insured, due to any reason, at an annual premium of ₹436?

options.text: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)
Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-SYM)

solution:
The correct answer is **Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)__ 

 __
 
• The government of India launched Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) on 09 May 2015.
 
• It was proposed by the Finance(Arun Jaitley) Minister in the 2015 budget speech.
 
• It comes under the Ministry of Finance.
 
• It was a government-backed life insurance scheme in India
 
• In case of the death of the insured person, the next eligible beneficiary is provided with a death benefit including a **death coverage of Rs. 2,00,000.**
 
• Aim - PMJJBY was launched to increase the reach of life insurance among citizens.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other details of PMJJBY;

 
 

 
 
Primary KYC

 
 
 
Aadhaar will be the primary KYC

 
 
 

 
 
Entry age

 
 
 
Min – 18 yrs (on the date of enrollment),

 
Max- 50 yrs(Age near Birthday)

 
 
 

 
 
Maximum maturity age

 
 
 
Completion of 55 years (Age near Birthday)

 
 
 

 
 
Coverage terms

 
 
 
1 year (renewable) – June 1 to May 31 each year

 
 
 

 
 
Sum assured

 
 
 
Maximum coverage of Rs. 2,00,000 per life irrespective of multiple accounts/multiple certificates of insurance held under the PMJJBY scheme.

 
The cover of Rs 2 lakh comes at less than one rupee per day.

 
 
 

 
 
Premium

 
 
 
Rs. 436

 
 
 

 Premium payment mode
 Annual. However, the 1st-year premium depends on the quarter in which the scheme is opted for.

• Under the mission, all villages, Gram Panchayats, Districts, States and Union Territories in India declared themselves "open-defecation free" (ODF) by 2 October 2019 in First Phase.
 
• On the 150th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, by constructing over 100 million toilets in rural India.
 
• To ensure that the open defecation-free behaviours are sustained, no one is left behind, and that solid and liquid waste management facilities are accessible.

Jawaharlal Nehru

• He was born on November 14, 1889, in Allahabad.
 
• November 14 is celebrated as Children's Day in India.
 
• He is the Prime Minister who has had the longest term in office.
 
• He served as the prime minister of India from 15th August 1947 to 1964.
 
• He is the architect of the Preamble of the Indian constitution.
 
• He was the Prime Minister of India during the Indo-China war in 1962.
 
• He served as the first chairman of the planning commission of India.
 
• He was honoured with the Bharat Ratna in 1955.
 
• The name Panchayati raj was given by Jawaharlal Nehru.

• He died on May 27, 1964, in New Delhi​​ 

Lal Bahadur Shastri

• Participated in the freedom movement since 1930.
 
• He joined the Kashi Vidyapeeth in Varanasi, one of the many national institutions set up in defiance of British rule.
 
• ‘Shastri’ was the bachelor’s degree awarded to him by the Vidya Peeth but has stuck in the minds of the people as part of his name.
 
• He was a minister in the Union Cabinet from 1951 to 1956 when he resigned taking responsibility for the railway accident and later from 1957-1964.
 
• He was India’s second Prime Minister (1964-66).
 
• He signed an agreement with then Ceylon (now Sri Lanka) on persons of Indian origin there, in 1964 — an endorsement of the importance of neighbourhood.
 
• He was the first person to be posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna (1966).

Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel

 
• He was the first Deputy Prime Minister of India.
 
• He was often called Sardar.
 
• He was also called an Indian Bismarck.
 
• Served as the first Home Minister of India.
 
• He was appointed as the President of the Indian National Congress during the Karachi session in 1931.

question: When was the Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme for Least Developed Countries (LDCs) announced by India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2008**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme for Least Developed Countries (LDCs) was announced by India in **2008**.
 
• This scheme aims to provide preferential market access for exports from LDCs to the Indian market.
 
• Under this scheme, India offers duty-free access to a wide range of products originating from LDCs.
 
• The initiative is part of India's commitment to support the economic development of LDCs and integrate them into the global trading system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Least Developed Countries (LDCs)**

 
 
• LDCs are a group of countries recognized by the United Nations as the poorest and most vulnerable in the world.
 
• These countries face severe structural impediments to sustainable development.
 
• They are characterized by low income, weak human assets, and economic vulnerability.
 
• As of 2023, there are 46 countries classified as LDCs by the United Nations.
 
 
 
• **Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme**
 
 
• The DFTP Scheme was announced by India in 2008 to promote trade with LDCs.
 
• It provides duty-free access to 98% of India's tariff lines for products originating from LDCs.
 
• The scheme covers a wide range of products including agricultural goods, textiles, and industrial products.
 
• This initiative aims to enhance the export capabilities of LDCs and foster economic growth through trade.
 
 
 
• **India's Trade Policy for LDCs**
 
 
• India's trade policy for LDCs is guided by the principles of South-South cooperation.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of providing market access to LDCs to support their economic development.
 
• India has been actively involved in providing technical assistance and capacity-building support to LDCs.
 
• India's trade policy aligns with its broader foreign policy objectives of promoting inclusive growth and development.
 
 
 
• **Global Trading System**
 
 
• The global trading system refers to the international framework that governs trade between countries.
 
• It includes agreements, institutions, and practices that facilitate the exchange of goods and services across borders.
 
• The World Trade Organization (WTO) plays a central role in regulating the global trading system.
 
• Efforts to integrate LDCs into the global trading system aim to ensure that these countries benefit from globalization and trade liberalization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

question: In which year was the Digital India mission launched?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2015**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Digital India mission was launched by the Government of India on **1st July 2015**.
 
• It aims to ensure that Government services are made available to citizens electronically by improving online infrastructure and by increasing Internet connectivity or by making the country digitally empowered in the field of technology.
 
• The initiative includes plans to connect rural areas with high-speed internet networks.
 
• Digital India consists of three core components: the development of secure and stable digital infrastructure, delivering government services digitally, and universal digital literacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Digital Infrastructure**

 
 
• One of the primary objectives of the Digital India initiative is to create a robust digital infrastructure that ensures high-speed internet connectivity across the country.
 
• It involves laying optical fiber cables, promoting mobile connectivity, and establishing Wi-Fi hotspots in rural and urban areas.
 
• This initiative also includes the establishment of common service centers (CSCs) that provide digital access points for various government services.
 
 
 
• **Governance and Services on Demand**
 
 
• Digital India aims to transform the way government services are delivered to citizens by making them available online.
 
• This includes services such as online filing of taxes, applying for government schemes, accessing educational resources, and availing healthcare services.
 
• The initiative promotes the use of e-governance to enhance transparency and efficiency in the delivery of public services.
 
 
 
• **Digital Literacy**
 
 
• Ensuring digital literacy for all citizens is a key component of the Digital India mission.
 
• The initiative focuses on providing digital education and training to individuals, especially in rural areas, to empower them with the skills needed to navigate the digital world.
 
• Various programs and campaigns are conducted to promote digital literacy and bridge the digital divide.

question: In which year was Smart Cities Mission launched?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2015**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Smart Cities Mission was launched by the Government of India in **2015**.
 
• The initiative aims to promote sustainable and inclusive cities that provide core infrastructure and give a decent quality of life to their citizens.
 
• It focuses on sustainable and inclusive development by creating replicable models which act like lighthouses to other aspiring cities.
 
• The mission targets the development of smart solutions that leverage digital and information technologies, urban planning best practices, public-private partnerships, and policy changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Smart Cities Mission**

 
 
• It is an urban renewal and retrofitting program by the Government of India with the mission to develop smart cities across the country, making them citizen-friendly and sustainable.
 
• The Smart Cities Mission was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on June 25, 2015.
 
• The goal is to promote sustainable and inclusive cities that provide core infrastructure, a clean and sustainable environment, and give a decent quality of life to their citizens.
 
• The mission focuses on sustainable and inclusive development by creating replicable models which act like lighthouses to other aspiring cities.
 
• The mission is operated as a centrally sponsored scheme and the central government has allocated Rs. 48,000 crore for the development of 100 smart cities.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Smart Cities**
 
 
• **Smart Mobility:** Efficient and sustainable transport system, smart traffic management, and public transportation.
 
• **Smart Environment:** Sustainable waste management, pollution control, and green spaces.
 
• **Smart Governance:** E-governance, citizen participation, and digital services.
 
• **Smart Economy:** Digital economy, innovation hubs, and entrepreneurship support.
 
• **Smart Living:** High quality of life, health, education, and safety services.
 
 
 
• **Implementation Strategy**

question:
Which of the following statements about the aims of National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) of India is/are correct?

1. To make agriculture more productive.

2. To make agriculture more sustainable.

3. To promote organic farming.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2 and 3 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) aims to make agriculture more productive, sustainable, remunerative, and climate-resilient by promoting location-specific integrated/composite farming systems.
 
• It also focuses on improving soil health and water use efficiency, as well as enhancing seed quality and promoting the use of organic farming practices.
 
• The NMSA is designed to cover both rainfed and irrigated areas to ensure comprehensive coverage of all agricultural zones.
 
• It supports the adoption of sustainable agricultural practices that help in conserving natural resources while maintaining agricultural productivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soil Health Management (SHM)**

 
 
• SHM is one of the major components of the NMSA. It aims to promote Integrated Nutrient Management (INM) through judicious use of chemical fertilizers, including secondary and micronutrients, in conjunction with organic manure and bio-fertilizers.
 
• The objective is to improve soil health and its productivity, thus supporting sustainable agriculture.
 
 
 
• **Rainfed Area Development (RAD)**
 
 
• RAD focuses on Integrated Farming Systems (IFS) for enhancing productivity and minimizing risks associated with climatic variability.
 
• It includes crop diversification, horticulture, livestock, fishery, and agroforestry to make agriculture more resilient to climate change.
 
 
 
• **Climate Change and Sustainable Agriculture: Monitoring, Modeling and Networking (CCSAMMN)**
 
 
• This initiative aims to build and strengthen the capacity of farmers and other stakeholders in addressing climate change impacts on agriculture.
 
• It involves the development of climate-resilient agricultural practices and technologies, and promoting their adoption.
 
 
 
• **Organic Farming**
 
 
• The NMSA promotes organic farming through the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY). PKVY aims to support and encourage farmers to adopt organic farming practices and certifications.
 
• It also focuses on marketing organic produce to ensure better returns to farmers.

__
 
• The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is a crop insurance scheme launched by the Government of India.
 
• The maximum premium payable by the farmers is 2% for all kharif food and oilseeds crops.
 
• The scheme aims to provide insurance coverage and financial support to farmers in the event of crop failure due to natural calamities, pests, and diseases.
 
• It helps stabilize the income of farmers to ensure their continuance in farming.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)**

 
 
• The scheme was launched on 18th February 2016 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
• It aims to provide a comprehensive insurance cover against the failure of crops, thus helping in stabilizing the income of farmers.
 
• Farmers are required to pay a uniform premium of only 2% for all Kharif crops and 1.5% for all Rabi crops. For annual commercial and horticultural crops, the premium is 5%.
 
• The remaining premium is paid by the Government to provide full insured amount to the farmers against crop loss on account of natural calamities.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)**
 
 
• PMKSY was launched to improve farm productivity and ensure better utilization of the resources in the country.
 
• The scheme’s motto is "Har Khet Ko Pani" (Water for every field).
 
• It focuses on efficient water conveyance and precision water application devices like drips, sprinklers, pivots, rain-guns, etc.
 
• The scheme aims at improving on-farm water use efficiency through a proper combination of surface and ground water.
 
 
 
• **Soil Health Card Scheme**
 
 
• The Soil Health Card Scheme was launched by the Government of India in February 2015.
 
• The scheme aims at promoting soil test-based and balanced use of fertilizers to enable farmers to realize higher yields at lower cost.
 
• Under the scheme, farmers are provided with Soil Health Cards, which will carry crop-wise recommendations of nutrients and fertilizers required for the individual farms.
 
• The Soil Health Cards will be issued once every three years for all land holdings in the country.
