• RSBY aims to provide health insurance coverage for Below Poverty Line (BPL) families.
 
• Under this scheme, beneficiaries are entitled to hospitalization coverage up to Rs. 30,000 for most of the diseases that require hospitalization.
 
• The scheme was designed to protect poor families from financial liabilities arising out of health shocks that involve hospitalization.

• The scheme provides for cashless insurance for hospital services through an empaneled network of healthcare providers.
 
• Beneficiaries need to pay a registration fee of Rs. 30, and the government pays the premium to the insurer selected by the state government on the basis of a competitive bidding.
 
• The scheme covers all pre-existing conditions and there is no age limit for the beneficiaries.
 
• Transport expenses are also provided to the patient, within an overall limit of Rs. 1000.
 
 
 
• **Health Insurance in India**
 
 
• Health insurance in India is a type of insurance that covers medical expenses incurred by the insured due to health conditions.
 
• Health insurance policies can be purchased by individuals or families to cover a wide range of medical expenses, including hospitalization, surgery, and other medical treatments.
 
• Several government schemes like Ayushman Bharat, PM-JAY, and others aim to provide health insurance coverage to various segments of the population.
 
• The goal of these schemes is to reduce the financial burden of medical expenses and ensure access to quality healthcare services for all.

• Both measures are critical in controlling the spread of infectious diseases like COVID-19.

question: In Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awaas Yojana, the cost of unit assistance is shared between Central and State Governments in the ratio ________ for the North-Eastern and the Himalayan states.
solution:
The correct answer is __**90 : 10**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awaas Yojana (PMGAY) is a social welfare flagship program created by the Indian Government to provide housing for the rural poor.

• For the North-Eastern and the Himalayan states, the cost sharing ratio between the Central and State Governments is 90:10.

• This scheme aims to provide financial assistance to the homeless and those living in kutcha houses to construct pucca houses.

• It ensures that people living in difficult areas such as hilly terrains and remote regions also have access to housing support.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awaas Yojana (PMGAY)**

• Formerly known as Indira Awaas Yojana, it was revamped in 2016 as Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G).

• It aims to provide financial assistance for constructing pucca houses with basic amenities to homeless families and those living in dilapidated houses.

• The cost of unit assistance is shared between the Central and State Governments for various states in different ratios.

• In plain areas, the cost sharing ratio is 60:40 between Central and State Governments.

• For the North-Eastern and the Himalayan states, the cost sharing ratio is 90:10 between the Central and State Governments.

• For Union Territories, the entire cost is borne by the Central Government.

• **Other Similar Schemes:**

• **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban)**

• This scheme is aimed at addressing the urban housing shortage among the Economically Weaker Section (EWS)/Low Income Group (LIG) and Middle Income Group (MIG) categories including the slum dwellers by ensuring a pucca house to all eligible urban households by the year 2022.

• The scheme is implemented through four verticals: In-situ Slum Redevelopment, Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme, Affordable Housing in Partnership, and Subsidy for beneficiary-led individual house construction/enhancement.

• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana**

• This is a financial inclusion program aimed at ensuring affordable access to financial services such as bank accounts, remittances, credit, insurance, and pensions.

• Launched on 28 August 2014, it aims to provide universal access to banking facilities with at least one basic banking account for every household.

options.text: Preservation of ancient Indian heritage sites
To promote values of local communities in conserving wetland ecosystem

solution:
The correct answer is __**To promote values of local communities in conserving wetland ecosystem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Amrit Dharohar' scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on World Environment Day, 2023.
 
• The scheme aims to encourage the preservation and restoration of wetlands in India by involving local communities.
 
• It focuses on the sustainable use of wetland resources while ensuring ecological balance and biodiversity conservation.
 
• Local communities are key stakeholders in this initiative, and their traditional knowledge and practices play a crucial role in wetland conservation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Wetlands**

 
 
• Wetlands are areas where water covers the soil, or is present either at or near the surface of the soil all year or for varying periods of time during the year.
 
• They include swamps, marshes, bogs, and similar areas.
 
• Wetlands provide numerous ecosystem services such as water purification, flood control, and habitat for a wide variety of wildlife.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Balance**
 
 
• Ecological balance refers to a state of dynamic equilibrium within a community of organisms in which genetic, species, and ecosystem diversity remain relatively stable.
 
• It is achieved through the interactions among organisms and their environment.
 
• Conservation efforts like the 'Amrit Dharohar' scheme help maintain ecological balance by protecting and restoring natural habitats.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity Conservation**
 
 
• Biodiversity conservation is the practice of protecting and preserving the variety of species in a particular habitat.
 
• It ensures the survival of species and the health of ecosystems.
 
• Efforts to conserve biodiversity include protecting natural habitats, restoring degraded ecosystems, and implementing sustainable resource management practices.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Knowledge**
 
 
• Traditional knowledge refers to the knowledge, innovations, and practices of indigenous and local communities developed from experience gained over the centuries and adapted to the local culture and environment.
 
• This knowledge is passed down through generations and is an integral part of their cultural heritage.
 
• In the context of wetland conservation, traditional knowledge can provide valuable insights into sustainable management practices and the maintenance of ecological balance.

question:
Which of the following objectives are part of the National Population Policy (NPP) 2000?

1. Providing free and compulsory education up to 14 years of age

2. Increasing fertility rate to ensure demographic dividend

3. Reducing infant mortality rate below 30 per 1000 live births

4. Promoting delayed marriage for girls
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1, 3 and 4 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Population Policy (NPP) 2000** was formulated with the objective of stabilizing the population of India while ensuring sustainable development and improving the quality of life of its citizens.
 
• One of the key goals of the policy is providing **free and compulsory education up to 14 years of age**, as outlined in the **Directive Principles of State Policy** under the **Indian Constitution**. This helps address population issues through better awareness and education.
 
• The policy aims to reduce the **infant mortality rate (IMR) below 30 per 1000 live births** by improving healthcare services, immunization programs, and maternal health facilities.
 
• Promoting **delayed marriage for girls** is another critical goal of the policy. Encouraging marriage at a later age not only helps in reducing fertility rates but also allows women to pursue education and professional opportunities.
 
• The policy focuses on several other measures such as addressing unmet needs for contraception, improving maternal healthcare, and achieving population stabilization by 2045.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Incorrect Option: Increasing fertility rate to ensure demographic dividend**__

 __
 
• This is incorrect as the **National Population Policy (NPP) 2000** focuses on reducing the fertility rate, not increasing it.
 
• Reducing fertility rates helps to stabilize population growth and improve socioeconomic indicators.
 
• Achieving a stable Total Fertility Rate (TFR) is one of the major goals of the policy, aiming for a replacement-level TFR of **2.1**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Infant Mortality Rate Reduction**__
 
 
• Reducing the **infant mortality rate (IMR)** is a key indicator of healthcare quality in a country.
 
• It reflects improvements in areas such as **nutrition, immunization, sanitation, and access to healthcare services.**

Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

__
 
• The **One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC)** scheme ensures the portability of food grains under the **National Food Security Act (NFSA).**
 
• Portability allows eligible beneficiaries to access their entitled food grains from any **Fair Price Shop (FPS)** in India, irrespective of their location.
 
• It particularly benefits **migrant workers** and their families who relocate to different states or regions for work or other reasons.
 
• The scheme uses **Aadhaar-enabled biometric authentication** to verify the identity of beneficiaries at FPS outlets. This ensures that food grains are delivered to the rightful beneficiaries.
 
• The integration of **Aadhaar** with the Public Distribution System (PDS) helps in preventing **leakages, duplication, and fraud** in the system.
 
• ONORC was introduced to support the vision of a **unified India** and address food security challenges faced by the **migrant population.**

• This option is incorrect because **Reason (R) is true**. The Aadhaar-enabled biometric authentication plays a crucial role in ensuring portability under the scheme.
 
 
 
• **A is false, but R is true**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect because **Assertion (A) is correct**. The One Nation One Ration Card indeed ensures portability of food grains.
 
 
 
• **Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect because **Reason (R) directly supports Assertion (A)**. The Aadhaar-enabled system is a core component of ensuring portability.

__
 
• **Assertion (A): UDAN Scheme improves regional air connectivity:**

 
 
• The UDAN Scheme, known as **Ude Desh Ka Aam Nagrik**, is a flagship regional air connectivity scheme launched by the Government of India in **2016**.
 
• Its primary aim is to make air travel affordable and accessible for common citizens, especially in tier-2 and tier-3 cities.
 
• By connecting underserved and remote regions of India, UDAN improves regional connectivity and fosters economic growth. ***Hence, the assertion is correct.***
 
 
 
• **Reason (R): It provides financial viability gap funding to airlines:**
 
 
• Under the UDAN scheme, airlines operating on regional routes receive **Viability Gap Funding (VGF)** from the government.
 
• The VGF reduces the financial burden on airlines to operate flights on less profitable routes, ensuring sustained operations.
 
• This funding is critical to achieving the goals of UDAN by incentivizing airlines to cover underserved routes. ***Hence, the reason is correct.***
 
 
 
• The reason (R) directly explains the assertion (A), as the financial VGF mechanism is integral to improving regional air connectivity through the UDAN scheme. ***Thus, both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **UDAN Scheme:**

• **Viability Gap Funding (VGF):**

• Under UDAN, VGF is funded through a levy collected from airlines operating on metro routes.
 
• It ensures that airlines can operate on regional routes without incurring significant losses.
 
 
 
• **Impact of UDAN:**
 
 
• Boosts tourism and trade in remote and underserved areas.
 
• Generates employment opportunities in aviation and related sectors.
 
• Strengthens socioeconomic development by connecting regions with the rest of the country.
 
 
 
• **Other Regional Connectivity Efforts:**
 
 
• Development of regional airports under **Regional Connectivity Infrastructure Investment**.
 
• Promotion of private sector investments in aviation infrastructure.
 
• Collaboration with state governments to enhance last-mile connectivity.

• **UDAN Achievements:**

 
 
• As of **October 2023**, the UDAN scheme has connected **over 70 airports** and initiated **425 routes** in India.
 
• It has made air travel accessible to millions of citizens, especially in remote regions.
 
 
 
• **Future Goals:**

• Plans to expand infrastructure and increase the number of operational airports to **100+**.

question: The primary aim of the Soil Health Card Scheme is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Assess nutrient status**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Soil Health Card Scheme was launched by the Government of India in **February 2015** to promote sustainable agriculture.
 
• The primary objective is to **assess the nutrient and health status of soil** across the country.
 
• The scheme provides farmers with soil health cards that include detailed information on soil nutrients, deficiencies, and recommendations for improving soil fertility.
 
• The soil health card suggests **crop-specific fertilizers and integrated nutrient management practices** to enhance productivity.
 
• By promoting scientific soil management, the scheme aims to reduce dependency on chemical fertilizers and ensure sustainable agricultural practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Improve seed quality**

 
 
• Improving seed quality refers to providing farmers with high-yielding, pest-resistant, and drought-tolerant seed varieties.
 
• Although improving seed quality is important for increasing agricultural productivity, it is not the direct focus of the Soil Health Card Scheme.
 
• Other government programs, such as the National Seed Policy, cater to the development and distribution of quality seeds.
 
 
 
• **Promote organic farming**
 
 
• Organic farming involves the use of natural inputs like compost, green manure, and biological pest control to enhance soil and crop health.
 
• While the Soil Health Card Scheme indirectly supports organic farming by reducing chemical fertilizer use, its primary focus is on soil nutrient assessment.
 
• Initiatives like the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) are specifically designed to promote organic farming practices in India.
 
 
 
• **Prevent land acquisition**
 
 
• Preventing land acquisition refers to safeguarding agricultural land from being acquired for non-agricultural purposes.
 
• This is not related to the Soil Health Card Scheme, as the scheme focuses on soil health and nutrient management, not land ownership or acquisition issues.
 
• Land acquisition laws and policies are governed under the Land Acquisition Act, 2013, which is unrelated to this scheme.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Soil Health Card Scheme**
 
 
• The Soil Health Card Scheme is a flagship program by the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare to address declining soil fertility and productivity.
 
• It involves soil testing, preparation of soil health cards for individual farmers, and providing recommendations for efficient nutrient management.
 
• By ensuring balanced fertilizer use, the scheme helps reduce input costs for farmers and promotes sustainable agricultural practices.

question: Which government scheme aims to provide financial support to senior citizens who may have lost their means of sustenance?

options.text: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS)

solution:
The correct answer is __**Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS)** is a component of the **National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP)**, launched by the Government of India.

• It was introduced in **1995** and revised in **2007** under the Ministry of Rural Development.

• The scheme provides a **monthly pension** to senior citizens aged **60 years and above** who belong to families living **below the poverty line (BPL)**.

• The amount of pension varies depending on the beneficiary's age:

• **60–79 years**: ₹200 per month from the central government (states can top up).

• **80 years and above**: ₹500 per month from the central government.

• IGNOAPS aims to provide **social security** and ensure the financial well-being of economically weaker sections of senior citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Atal Pension Yojana (APY):**

• Launched in **2015**, it is focused on providing a **guaranteed monthly pension** to workers in the **unorganized sector**.

• The entry age is **18–40 years**, and the pension amount ranges from ₹1,000 to ₹5,000, depending on contributions.

• It is co-contributory, with the government adding 50% of the contribution or ₹1,000 per year (whichever is lower) for eligible subscribers.

• **Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (PMVVY):**

• Implemented by the **LIC of India**, this scheme aims to provide **pension security** to senior citizens aged **60 years and above**.

• It guarantees a fixed interest rate of **7.4% per annum** for 10 years, payable monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, or yearly.

• The maximum purchase price under the scheme is ₹15 lakh.

• **National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP):**

• Launched in **1995**, it is an umbrella scheme aimed at providing **social security** to the poor, including old age pension, widow pension, and disability pension.

• IGNOAPS is one of its key components, specifically targeted at senior citizens.

• **Key Differences:**

• **IGNOAPS:** Focuses on senior citizens in BPL families, providing small pensions.

• **APY:** Caters to unorganized workers, offering a range of pensions based on contributions.

• **PMVVY:** A fixed-income scheme for senior citizens with higher financial security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **IGNOAPS Implementation:**

• The scheme is implemented through **state governments and union territories**.

• Each state can add additional funds to the pension amount to enhance benefits.

• **Eligibility Verification:**

• BPL status is verified through the **Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC)**.

• Beneficiaries need to provide proof of age and BPL status to avail of the benefits.

• **Challenges:**

• Low pension amounts under IGNOAPS remain a concern for ensuring adequate financial support.

• Coverage gaps and beneficiary identification issues persist in certain regions.

1. It aims to make India a global hub for production and export of green hydrogen.

2. The mission targets production of 10 MMT by 2030.

3. Green hydrogen is produced by electrolysis using renewable energy.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 3 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Statement 1: It aims to make India a global hub for production and export of green hydrogen.** 

• This statement is correct. The **National Green Hydrogen Mission** was introduced to position India as a key player in the global green hydrogen market, encouraging both domestic production and export opportunities.

• The initiative aligns with India’s commitment to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and achieving **net-zero carbon emissions by 2070**.

• **Statement 2: The mission targets production of 10 MMT by 2030.**

• This statement is incorrect. While the mission has ambitious production targets, the actual target for green hydrogen production by 2030 is **5 MMT (Million Metric Tonnes)** as per the official framework of the National Green Hydrogen Mission.

• The focus is to enhance domestic production and reduce reliance on fossil fuels.

• **Statement 3: Green hydrogen is produced by electrolysis using renewable energy.**

• This statement is correct. Green hydrogen is generated through the process of **electrolysis**, where water is split into hydrogen and oxygen using electricity sourced from **renewable energy** like solar or wind power.

• This makes green hydrogen a sustainable and clean alternative to conventional hydrogen production methods, which rely on fossil fuels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **National Green Hydrogen Mission:**

• Launched by the **Government of India** in **2022**, the mission aims to make India a leader in the production and use of green hydrogen.

• The mission will help in reducing India’s dependency on imported energy and contribute significantly to its energy transition efforts.

• It is expected to attract investments worth **Rs. 8 lakh crore** and create over **6 lakh jobs**.

• The mission is part of India’s strategy to meet its **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)** under the Paris Agreement.

• **Green Hydrogen:**

• It is hydrogen produced through **electrolysis** using electricity generated from renewable energy sources.

• This hydrogen has a variety of applications, including in industries like steel, cement, and chemicals, as well as in transportation and energy storage.

• It is considered a key fuel for the future due to its potential to decarbonize sectors that are difficult to electrify directly.

• **Key Environmental Benefits:**

• Green hydrogen reduces carbon emissions significantly compared to grey hydrogen, which is derived from natural gas.

• It supports the global transition to **clean energy** and helps combat climate change.

• **Current Global Scenario:**

• Countries like Germany, Japan, and Australia are investing heavily in green hydrogen technologies.

• India’s mission places it among the leading nations aiming to scale up green hydrogen production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Green Hydrogen Production Technologies:**

• **Electrolysis:** The most common method for producing green hydrogen using water and renewable electricity.

• **Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting:** Uses sunlight to split water into hydrogen and oxygen.

• Research is ongoing to improve the efficiency of these technologies and reduce production costs.

• **Challenges in Green Hydrogen Adoption:**

• The high cost of production and lack of infrastructure for storage and distribution are key barriers.

• Scaling up requires significant investments and technological advancements.

• **Future Prospects:**

• With global emphasis on achieving net-zero emissions, green hydrogen is expected to play a pivotal role in transforming the energy landscape.

• India’s proactive initiatives under the Green Hydrogen Mission aim to position the country as a major player in this emerging sector.

question: The "Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM)" scheme has a focus on the energy sector within agriculture. What is the primary objective of this scheme?

options.text: To provide free electricity to all agricultural consumers.

To encourage the installation of solar pumps and grid-connected solar power plants in rural areas.

solution:
The correct answer is __**To encourage the installation of solar pumps and grid-connected solar power plants in rural areas**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM)** scheme was launched by the Government of India to promote the use of renewable energy in the agricultural sector. 
• The primary focus of the scheme is to encourage the installation of **solar-powered pumps** and **grid-connected solar power plants** in rural areas. 
• It aims to provide energy security to farmers by reducing their dependence on expensive diesel or unreliable electricity grids. 
• Under this scheme, farmers can install **solar irrigation pumps** and even sell surplus electricity generated from solar plants to the grid, thus generating additional income. 
• The scheme is divided into three components: 
• **Component A:** Setting up 10,000 MW of decentralized grid-connected renewable energy plants. 
• **Component B:** Installation of 20 lakh standalone solar pumps. 
• **Component C:** Solarization of 15 lakh existing grid-connected agricultural pumps. 
• The scheme also aligns with the government’s vision of achieving **175 GW of renewable energy capacity** by 2022. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __

• Reduces dependency on **fossil fuels** and promotes the use of **clean energy**. 
• Provides an alternative source of income for farmers by enabling them to sell surplus power to the grid. 
• Improves access to reliable energy for irrigation, boosting agricultural productivity. 
• Helps in achieving the government’s **climate goals** by reducing greenhouse gas emissions. 
• **Key Features of Solar Pumps:** 
• Solar pumps are powered by energy from the sun, which is a renewable and sustainable energy source. 
• Standalone solar pumps eliminate the need for grid electricity or diesel, reducing operational costs. 
• They are ideal for remote areas where electricity supply is unreliable or unavailable. 
• **Implementation and Funding:** 
• The scheme is implemented by the **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)**. 
• It provides a combination of **Central Financial Assistance (CFA)**, state government subsidies, and farmer contributions. 
• The central government provides up to **30% subsidy**, while the state government contributes another 30%, and the farmer bears the remaining cost. 
• **Global Perspective:** 
• Globally, solar-powered irrigation systems are gaining popularity as a sustainable solution to water and energy challenges in agriculture. 
• Countries like **India, Kenya, and Bangladesh** have embraced solar irrigation to support smallholder farmers and reduce reliance on traditional energy sources. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• The **PM-KUSUM scheme** contributes significantly to the government’s goal of doubling farmers’ income by **2022**. 
• It also supports the **National Solar Mission**, which aims to increase the share of solar energy in India’s energy mix. 
• By replacing diesel pumps with solar pumps, the scheme can save approximately **1.2 billion liters of diesel** annually, reducing the import burden and foreign exchange expenditure.

question: The "Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme" has been introduced for various sectors in India. What is the primary goal behind the implementation of this scheme?

options.text: To reduce the fiscal deficit of the government.
To boost domestic manufacturing and attract investments.
To promote exports of agricultural commodities.
To improve the skill development of the workforce.

solution:
The correct answer is __**To boost domestic manufacturing and attract investments**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 __ 
• The **Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme** was launched by the Government of India to enhance the country’s **manufacturing capabilities** and increase the competitiveness of Indian industries in the global market. 
• The primary goal of this scheme is to **boost domestic manufacturing** by providing financial incentives to companies for incremental production in specified sectors. 
• The scheme aims to attract both **domestic and foreign investments** to build a robust manufacturing ecosystem in India, particularly in sectors like electronics, pharmaceuticals, textiles, automobiles, and more. 
• The PLI scheme is designed to **reduce import dependency**, promote export growth, and make India a global manufacturing hub. 
• By focusing on sectors with high growth potential, the scheme also contributes to the generation of **employment opportunities** and the development of cutting-edge technologies within the country. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Key Features of the PLI Scheme:** 
• The PLI scheme provides **financial incentives** in the form of subsidies or cash benefits based on incremental sales or production of goods in specific sectors. 
• It is targeted at **key sectors** that are critical for India’s economic growth, such as mobile and electronic components, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and more. 
• The scheme is implemented with a budgetary allocation from the government and has a time-bound framework to achieve its objectives. 
• **Benefits of the Scheme:** 
• Encourages the development of a **self-reliant India** (Aatmanirbhar Bharat) by reducing reliance on imports. 
• Supports the creation of a globally competitive manufacturing base in India, promoting **export growth**. 
• Helps in the development of **advanced manufacturing technologies** and innovation. 
• Leads to large-scale **employment generation** across various sectors, benefiting both skilled and unskilled workers. 
• **Examples of Sectors Covered Under PLI:** 
• **Electronics Manufacturing:** The scheme covers mobile phones, semiconductor components, and other electronics to make India a global manufacturing hub for these products. 
• **Pharmaceuticals:** PLI incentives support the production of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) and key starting materials (KSMs) to strengthen the healthcare sector. 
• **Automobile and Auto Components:** Focuses on the production of advanced automotive technologies to promote green mobility and electric vehicles. 
• **Textiles:** Includes incentives for the production of technical textiles and man-made fiber-based products. 
• **Global Context:** 
• Many countries use similar schemes to promote domestic manufacturing, such as China’s **Made in China 2025** initiative. 
• India’s PLI scheme is a strategic step to compete with such global initiatives and improve its share in the global manufacturing supply chain. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Launch Year:** The PLI scheme was first introduced in the **Union Budget 2020-21** and later expanded to cover multiple sectors. 
• **Budget Allocation:** The government has allocated **INR 1.97 lakh crore** over five years for the implementation of the scheme. 
• **Targeted Outcomes:** The scheme aims to increase India’s **manufacturing GDP** contribution to 25% by 2025 from the current 16-17%. 
• **Monitoring and Implementation:** The scheme is monitored by **respective ministries** and involves collaboration with industries to achieve its targets. 
• **Global Recognition:** The PLI scheme has been acknowledged as a transformative initiative to position India as a global manufacturing leader. 
5e:T2aae

question: Which government scheme aims to provide social security to workers in the unorganized sector?

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)

solution:
The correct answer is __**Atal Pension Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Atal Pension Yojana (APY)** is a government-backed pension scheme in India aimed at providing **social security for workers in the unorganized sector.**

• Launched in **May 2015** by the Government of India, the scheme operates under the **Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA).**

• The scheme is open to all Indian citizens aged between **18 to 40 years**, with a focus on workers in the unorganized sector, such as laborers, drivers, domestic workers, and street vendors.

• Under APY, subscribers receive a **guaranteed monthly pension ranging from Rs. 1,000 to Rs. 5,000**, depending on their contribution and age at the time of joining.

• The contributions are made till the age of **60 years**, after which the pension benefits are disbursed.

• The scheme allows **spouses** to continue receiving the pension or claim the accumulated corpus in case of the subscriber's demise.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Eligibility for Atal Pension Yojana:**

• The subscriber must be an **Indian citizen** and have a **savings bank account** or a post office savings account.

• The entry age is restricted to **18-40 years**, ensuring a minimum contribution period of 20 years before receiving benefits.

• **Key Features:**

• The scheme guarantees a fixed monthly pension, with the government providing **co-contribution** for eligible subscribers who are not covered under any statutory social security scheme and are not income taxpayers.

• It is especially beneficial for workers in the **unorganized sector**, which constitutes around **85% of India's workforce**.

• **Funding and Management:**

• The scheme is managed by the **Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA)** under the **National Pension System (NPS).**

• The government's **co-contribution** is 50% of the subscriber's contribution or Rs. 1,000 per annum, whichever is lower, for a period of 5 years for eligible subscribers enrolled between June 1, 2015, and December 31, 2015.

• **Benefits to the Unorganized Sector:**

• The scheme provides a social safety net for individuals without formal pension coverage, especially those working in **low-income, informal jobs.**

• It ensures **financial stability** and promotes savings for old age among economically vulnerable sections of society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Other Government Schemes for Social Security:**

• **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA):** Provides guaranteed 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to rural households.

• **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY):** Focuses on financial inclusion by providing access to banking services like savings accounts, credit, insurance, and pensions.

• **National Health Mission (NHM):** Aims at providing accessible, affordable, and quality healthcare services to rural and urban populations.

• **Global Perspective:**

• Similar schemes exist globally, such as **Social Security in the United States** and the **National Pension Scheme in South Korea**, which aim to provide financial stability and old-age security to workers.

__

• The capital city **Port Blair** is situated in the South Andaman.
 
• **10º Channel** separates the Andaman islands from Nicobar.
 
• The** Barren Island**, India's only active volcano is in the Middle Andaman and** Narcondam** is also a volcanic island.
 
• **Saddle Peak** is the highest point of this Archipelago.
 
• **Indira Point**, India's southernmost tip is part of Greater Nicobar.
 
• Andaman and Nicobar islands are one of the biodiversity hotspots of India.

**Lakshadweep Islands:**__

 
• This archipelago consists of 36 islands and atolls that are of** Coral origin**.
 
• The capital of Lakshadweep is** Kavaratti**.
 
• These were earlier known as** Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands**.
 
• **Andrott** is the largest island of this group.

question: The Centre introduced a new bill called the Criminal Procedure (Identification) Bill 2022. This Bill will repeal the Identification of Prisoners Act which was established in _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1920**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Criminal Procedure (Identification) Bill 2022 seeks to repeal the Identification of** Prisoners Act 1920**. The said Act, in its present form, provides **access to a limited category of persons** whose body measurements can be taken
 
• As per the Bill, any person convicted, arrested, or held under any preventive detention law will be required to provide “**measurements**” to a police officer or a prison official.
 
• Resistance to or refusal to allow the taking of measurements under this Act shall be deemed to be an offense under **section 186 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC)**.
 
• It authorizes law enforcement agencies to collect, store and analyze physical and biological samples of convicts and other persons for the purposes of identification and investigation in criminal matters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• This was done in the backdrop of the** State of UP vs Ram Babu Misra**, where the Apex Court had highlighted the need for amending this law.
 
• The **Criminal Procedure (Identification) Bill, 2022 **was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 28th March 2022. It was passed by the Rajya Sabha on 6th April.
 
• The **National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB)** will be the central agency to maintain the records

question: The Appropriation bill, 2022 was passed in Lok Sabha on ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**March 24, 2022**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Appropriation Bill gives power to the government to **withdraw funds from the Consolidated Fund** of India for fulfilling the expenditure during the financial year.
 
• The government cannot withdraw money from the **Consolidated Fund of India** till the implementation of the appropriation bill.
 
• To meet the direct expenses the Constitution has authorized the Lok Sabha to make any grant in advance for a part of the financial year. This provision is known as the ‘**Vote on Account**
 
• As per **Article 114** of the Constitution, the government can withdraw money from the Consolidated Fund only after receiving approval from Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **defeat of an Appropriation Bill in Loksabha would lead to the resignation of the government**.
 
• The unique feature of the Appropriation Bill is its **automatic repeal clause**, whereby the Act gets repealed by itself after it meets its statutory purpose.
 
• Both appropriation and finance bills are classified as money bills that **do not require the explicit consent of the Rajya Sabha**. The Rajya Sabha only discusses them and returns the bills,
 
• Appropriation bills specify the quantum and purpose for withdrawing money, while the **Finance bill contains a provision for financing the expenditure of the government**.

question: In October 2022, ‘Tele-MANAS’ initiative was launched by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. What does ‘M’ stand for in MANAS?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mental health.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tele MANAS**

 
 
• **The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare** started the "**Tele-MANAS**" project in October 2022. **M stands for mental health in MANAS.**
 
• In October 2022, the **Tele-MANAS (Telemental Health Assistance and Networking Across States)** initiative was launched by the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare.
 
• In order to provide free, round-the-clock tele-mental health services to everyone in the country,** Tele-MANAS **is concentrating on underprivileged or isolated communities.
 
• The plan includes a network of 23 centres for tele-mental health excellence, with NIMHANS acting as the scheme's nodal body and the **International Institute of** **Information Technology-Bangalore (IIITB)** offering technical support.
 
• **The National Health Systems Resource Center (NHRSC) **and the **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT)** Bangalore would provide technical support.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mental health**

 
 
• Our mental health includes all aspects of our** emotional, psychological, and social well-being**. It has an impact on our attitudes, feelings, and actions. It also affects how we deal with stress, communicate with others, and make wise decisions.
 
• From childhood and youth to adulthood, every stage of life is important for maintaining mental health.
 
• Despite the fact that the terms are commonly used interchangeably, poor mental health and mental illness are not the same. A person can have poor mental health even if they do not have a mental condition.
 
• A person who suffers from a mental illness may also experience periods of excellent physical, mental, and** social health.**

question:
Consider the following statements associated with the India Infrastructure Project Development Fund (IIPDF).

1. IIPDF was set up in 2017.

2. The funds for IIPDF are provided by the Central Government?

3. This scheme is notified under the Department of Economic Affairs.

Which of the above statements is/are INCORRECT?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **IIPDF was set up in 2007** to support the development of quality infrastructure projects.
 
• The fund provides financial support for project development activities of the Central Government and State Governments.
 
• The scheme is **notified under the Department of Economic Affairs**, which plays a crucial role in the economic development of the country.
 
• The funds for IIPDF are provided by the **Central Government** to assist in creating a pipeline of viable infrastructure projects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **India Infrastructure Project Development Fund (IIPDF)**

 
 
• The IIPDF was established to provide financial support for the development of public-private partnership (PPP) projects.
 
• The fund is intended to assist project authorities by providing the necessary resources for project preparation, including feasibility studies, detailed project reports, and other preparatory activities.
 
• The IIPDF aims to enhance the quality and bankability of infrastructure projects, making them more attractive to private sector investments.
 
• This initiative is part of the government's broader strategy to improve infrastructure and promote economic growth through increased private sector participation.
 
 
 
• **Department of Economic Affairs (DEA)**
 
 
• The DEA is a department under the Ministry of Finance, Government of India.
 
• It is responsible for formulating and monitoring the country's economic policies and programs, including fiscal policy, monetary policy, and financial regulations.
 
• The DEA plays a pivotal role in managing the country's economic infrastructure, ensuring sustainable growth and development.
 
• The department also oversees international economic relations, including India's participation in multilateral financial institutions.
 
 
 
• **Public-Private Partnership (PPP)**
 
 
• PPP is a collaborative arrangement between the government and private sector entities for the provision of public infrastructure and services.
 
• It leverages the expertise, efficiency, and capital of the private sector to deliver public projects, while the government provides regulatory and policy support.
 
• PPP models are used in various sectors, including transportation, healthcare, education, and utilities, to enhance service delivery and infrastructure development.
 
• The success of PPP projects depends on effective project planning, risk-sharing mechanisms, and transparent contractual agreements.

question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct statement(s) from the following:

1. The UDAN scheme has completed five years since its implementation in 2017.

2. It is the flagship scheme of the Ministry of Science and Technology.

3. The Airports Authority of India is the implementing agency of this scheme.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only statements 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1 is incorrect**: The UDAN scheme, also known as Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik, was launched in 2017, and it has completed seven years of its implementation in 2024.
 
• **Statement 2 is incorrect**: The UDAN scheme is not the flagship scheme of the Ministry of Science and Technology. It is the flagship scheme of the Ministry of Civil Aviation.
 
• **Statement 3 is correct**: The Airports Authority of India (AAI) is the implementing agency of the UDAN scheme.
 
• The UDAN scheme aims to make air travel affordable and widespread, thereby boosting inclusive national economic growth, job growth, and air transport infrastructure development in all regions and states of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UDAN Scheme (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik)**

 
 
• UDAN is a regional airport development and "Regional Connectivity Scheme" (RCS) of Government of India, aimed at making air travel affordable and widespread.
 
• The scheme is jointly funded by the central government and state governments.
 
• Under the scheme, financial incentives in terms of concessions from the central and state governments and airport operators are extended to selected airlines to encourage operations from unserved and underserved airports, and keep airfares affordable.
 
• The UDAN scheme envisions the enhancement of aviation infrastructure and air connectivity in tier II and tier III cities.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Civil Aviation**
 
 
• The Ministry of Civil Aviation of Government of India is responsible for formulating national policies and programmes for the development and regulation of the Civil Aviation sector in the country.
 
• It oversees airport facilities, air traffic services, and maintenance of the air transportation system.
 
• The Ministry also ensures the implementation of various schemes, including the UDAN scheme, to promote regional connectivity and affordable air travel.
 
 
 
• **Airports Authority of India (AAI)**
 
 
• The Airports Authority of India (AAI) is a statutory body, working under the Ministry of Civil Aviation, Government of India.
 
• AAI is responsible for creating, upgrading, maintaining, and managing civil aviation infrastructure in India.
 
• It manages a total of 137 airports, which include 24 International Airports, 10 Customs Airports, 80 Domestic Airports, and 23 Civil Enclaves at Defence airfields.
 
• AAI also provides air traffic management (ATM) services over the entire Indian airspace and adjoining oceanic areas.

• The NIPUN Bharat scheme specifically targets the attainment of FLN by children at the primary level.
 
• FLN is crucial for the overall cognitive development of a child and impacts their ability to learn more complex subjects in higher grades.
 
 
 
• **Implementation of NIPUN Bharat**

question: On 29th October 2020, the Ministry of Science and Technology launched the SERB-POWER Scheme. What is the objective of the scheme?

To strengthen the solar programme of India with France
To mitigate gender disparity in science and engineering research funding in various academic programmes and laboratories
To allow reservation for women in the Ministry of Science and Technology

solution:
The correct answer is __**To mitigate gender disparity in science and engineering research funding in various academic programmes and laboratories**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The SERB-POWER (Promoting Opportunities for Women in Exploratory Research) Scheme was launched by the Ministry of Science and Technology on 29th October 2020.
 
• The primary objective of the scheme is to mitigate gender disparity in science and engineering research funding in various academic programs and laboratories.
 
• The scheme aims to empower women researchers by providing them with structured support in their research endeavors.
 
• It focuses on creating a conducive environment for women scientists to excel in their respective fields through grants, fellowships, and other supportive measures.

• **Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB)**

 
 
• SERB is a statutory body under the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India.
 
• It was established through an Act of Parliament in 2008 and came into existence in 2009.
 
• The primary mandate of SERB is to promote basic research in emerging areas of science and engineering.
 
• The board supports research through various programs, grants, and fellowships.
 
 
 
• **Gender Disparity in Science and Engineering**
 
 
• Gender disparity in science and engineering refers to the underrepresentation of women in these fields.
 
• Several factors contribute to this disparity, including societal biases, lack of role models, and unequal access to resources and opportunities.
 
• Efforts to address gender disparity include providing scholarships, mentorship programs, and creating inclusive policies.
 
• Encouraging women's participation in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) is crucial for achieving gender equality and fostering innovation.

• Academic programs refer to structured courses and curricula offered by educational institutions to impart knowledge and skills.
 
• Laboratories are facilities equipped for scientific research, experiments, and measurement, providing hands-on experience and practical training.
 
• Both academic programs and laboratories play a vital role in advancing scientific knowledge and fostering research and development.
 
• Ensuring equal access and opportunities in these settings is essential for promoting diversity and inclusion in the scientific community.

solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• This scheme is implemented under the Ministry of Women and Child Development.
 
• It is not just limited to children aged below 6 years but also includes pregnant women and lactating mothers.
 
• Six services provided under this scheme include supplementary nutrition, pre-school non-formal education, nutrition & health education, immunization, health check-up, and referral services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0**

 
 
• This is a flagship program of the Government of India aimed at improving the nutritional and health status of children, pregnant women, and lactating mothers.
 
• It is a Centrally-Sponsored Scheme and not under the National Food Security Act, 2003.
 
• The scheme is designed to address the challenges of malnutrition and to ensure holistic development of children.
 
• It integrates supplementary nutrition, early childhood care, and education, maternal care, and various health services.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)**
 
 
• Launched on 2nd October 1975, ICDS is one of the world's largest programs for early childhood care and development.
 
• ICDS aims to provide food, preschool education, primary healthcare, immunization, health check-up, and referral services to children under 6 years of age and their mothers.
 
• It is a significant step towards meeting the nutritional and health needs of the most vulnerable sections of society.
 
 
 
• **National Food Security Act, 2013**
 
 
• The National Food Security Act, 2013 (also known as the Right to Food Act), was legislated by the Indian Parliament in 2013.
 
• The Act aims to provide subsidized food grains to approximately two-thirds of India's 1.2 billion people.
 
• It includes provisions for both rural and urban populations and covers a range of food security measures.

question: Which of the following is a component of the SHG-bank linkage program in India?

options.text: Microfinance institutions providing loans directly to SHGs
Banks providing loans to individual members of SHGs
Non-governmental organisations providing capacity building training to SHGs
State government providing subsidies to SHGs for credit

solution:
The correct answer is __**Banks providing loans to individual members of SHGs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme (SBLP) was launched by NABARD in 1992 as a pilot project to provide a cost-effective mechanism for providing financial services to the unreached and underserved rural poor.
 
• The program allows Self-Help Groups (SHGs) to open savings accounts in banks and avail loans.
 
• The SHG members collectively guarantee the repayment of loans, which reduces the risk for banks.
 
• This program has been instrumental in promoting financial inclusion and improving the socioeconomic conditions of rural women.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**

 
 
• SHGs are informal associations of people who come together to find ways to improve their living conditions.
 
• They are usually composed of 10-20 members who meet regularly to save and lend money to each other.
 
• The primary objective of SHGs is to promote savings and provide credit facilities to their members.
 
• SHGs play a crucial role in enhancing the socio-economic status of their members, especially women, by fostering a sense of community and collective responsibility.
 
 
 
• **NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)**
 
 
• NABARD is an apex development bank in India, established on 12 July 1982.
 
• It is responsible for providing and regulating credit and other facilities for the promotion and development of agriculture, small-scale industries, cottage and village industries, handicrafts, and other rural crafts.
 
• NABARD also supports rural development projects by providing financial assistance and guidance.
 
• One of its significant initiatives is the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, which aims to link SHGs with banks to facilitate access to financial services.
 
 
 
• **Financial Inclusion**
 
 
• Financial inclusion refers to the process of ensuring access to financial services and timely and adequate credit where needed by vulnerable groups such as weaker sections and low-income groups at an affordable cost.
 
• It aims to eliminate barriers to financial services and create opportunities for all individuals, especially the underprivileged, to participate in the formal financial system.
 
• Key components of financial inclusion include access to savings accounts, credit, insurance, remittances, and financial literacy.
 
• Promoting financial inclusion is crucial for achieving inclusive growth and reducing poverty.

question: The ________ portal is a platform provided by the Govt. of India for farmers to attain any information related to agriculture.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Farmer's**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Farmer's portal** is a platform provided by the Government of India to facilitate easy access to information related to agriculture for farmers.
 
• It offers comprehensive details on various aspects of farming including **crop management, pest control, weather forecasts, and government schemes.**
 
• The portal is designed to **empower farmers** with knowledge and information that can help them make better decisions and improve their agricultural practices.
 
• This platform also acts as a **single window for agricultural information** from various governmental departments and agencies, making it easier for farmers to access the necessary data.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agricultural Portals and Their Importance**

 
 
• **eNAM** - The National Agriculture Market (eNAM) is an online trading platform for agricultural commodities in India. It aims to create a unified national market for agricultural products by connecting existing APMC mandis.
 
• **Kisan Call Center** - This initiative provides farmers with information and advice on agriculture through toll-free calls. Farmers can get answers to their queries on agriculture-related issues from experts.
 
• **M-Kisan** - This platform uses mobile technology to provide farmers with critical information such as weather updates, pest control measures, and best practices for crop management.
 
• **PM-KISAN** - The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) scheme provides financial assistance to farmers. The scheme aims to supplement the financial needs of farmers in procuring various inputs to ensure proper crop health and appropriate yields.
 
 
 
• **Government Schemes for Farmers**
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)** - This crop insurance scheme provides financial support to farmers in the event of crop failure due to natural calamities, pests, and diseases.
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY)** - It aims to enhance water use efficiency through various measures including the creation of protective irrigation facilities, the promotion of efficient water conveyance, and the adoption of water-saving technologies.
 
• **Soil Health Card Scheme** - This scheme aims to provide farmers with soil health cards that carry crop-wise recommendations for nutrients and fertilizers to help improve productivity.
 
• **Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY)** - This scheme aims to promote decentralized planning for agriculture and allied sectors and to ensure the holistic development of agriculture and allied sectors.

question:
Which of the following pairs of Government Scheme and its associated Nodal Ministry/Department is correctly matched?

1. PM-AASHA - Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution

2. e-NAM - Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare

3. PMKSY - Ministry of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation

4. RODTEP - Ministry of Finance
solution:
The correct answer is __**e-NAM - Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)** is an online trading platform developed to create a unified national market for agricultural commodities.
 
• It is spearheaded by the **Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare**, aiming to connect farmers, traders, and buyers digitally.
 
• e-NAM was launched by the Government of India on **14th April 2016** as a major step towards agricultural reforms.
 
• The platform facilitates better price discovery through transparent auction processes and eliminates intermediaries, benefiting farmers directly.
 
• As of October 2023, e-NAM has integrated over **1,000 mandis** across India, enhancing the efficiency of agricultural marketing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PM-AASHA - Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution**

 
 
• PM-AASHA (Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan) is a scheme launched in 2018 aimed at ensuring remunerative prices for farmers' produce.
 
• It comprises three components: **Price Support Scheme (PSS)**, **Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS)**, and **Pilot of Private Procurement and Stockist Scheme (PPPS)**.
 
• However, the nodal ministry for PM-AASHA is the **Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare**, not the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution.
 
 
 
• **PMKSY - Ministry of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation**
 
 
• Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) aims to improve irrigation efficiency and increase agricultural productivity.
 
• The nodal ministry for PMKSY is the **Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare**, not the Ministry of Water Resources.
 
• It includes components such as **Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (AIBP)** and **Har Khet Ko Pani**.
 
 
 
• **RODTEP - Ministry of Finance**
 
 
• Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products (RODTEP) is a scheme launched in January 2021 to boost exports by reimbursing taxes and duties incurred during manufacturing and transport.
 
• The nodal ministry for RODTEP is the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry**, not the Ministry of Finance.
 
• It replaced the earlier **MEIS (Merchandise Exports from India Scheme)** to align with World Trade Organization (WTO) rules.

question: Objective of India's new Eco-Tourism Policy in protected areas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Balance conservation and livelihoods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India's new Eco-Tourism Policy aims to balance **environmental conservation and sustainable livelihoods** for local communities residing in protected areas.
 
• The policy promotes **community-based tourism**, involving local stakeholders to ensure their active participation and equitable benefit-sharing.
 
• It emphasizes **responsible tourism practices** that minimize negative ecological impacts while enhancing awareness about biodiversity conservation.
 
• Protected areas under this policy, including wildlife sanctuaries and national parks, will integrate **sustainable economic activities** to support local communities.
 
• The Eco-Tourism Policy aligns with India's **National Biodiversity Action Plan** and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 15 (Life on Land) and SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ban human activity**

 
 
• Banning human activity entirely in protected areas is not feasible or practical as many local communities depend on these areas for their livelihoods.
 
• While certain activities like poaching and deforestation are prohibited, regulated human activity, such as eco-tourism, is encouraged to strike a balance between conservation and community needs.
 
• India's wildlife protection laws, including the Wildlife Protection Act 1972, allow for controlled human interaction to support conservation efforts.
 
 
 
• **Maximize profit without community**
 
 
• This approach contradicts the principles of sustainable and responsible tourism.
 
• Ignoring local communities in eco-tourism policies can lead to social unrest and environmental degradation.
 
• India's Eco-Tourism Policy emphasizes community involvement to ensure equitable distribution of benefits and preservation of ecological integrity.
 
 
 
• **Turn areas into resorts**
 
 
• Turning protected areas into resorts is against the principles of conservation and can lead to habitat destruction.
 
• Eco-tourism promotes low-impact accommodations, such as eco-lodges, rather than large-scale resorts.
 
• The policy strictly avoids commercialization and prioritizes preserving the natural environment.

question: Which of these schemes is implemented to promote organic farming?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) is a sub-component of the Soil Health Management (SHM) scheme under the National Mission of Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA).
 
• The scheme was launched in 2015 to promote organic farming and improve soil health by reducing the dependence on chemical fertilizers and pesticides.
 
• PKVY helps farmers adopt organic farming practices such as the use of bio-fertilizers, vermicomposting, and traditional techniques to improve crop productivity sustainably.
 
• Under the scheme, farmers are incentivized to form clusters of 20 hectares to take up organic farming collectively, thereby reducing input costs and improving yields.
 
• The scheme also focuses on creating market linkages for organic produce, promoting Participatory Guarantee Systems (PGS), and assisting farmers in getting organic certification.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY)**

 
 
• PM-KMY is a pension scheme introduced in 2019 for small and marginal farmers.
 
• Farmers aged between 18 and 40 years can enroll in this scheme, contributing a small monthly premium based on their age.
 
• On attaining the age of 60, enrolled farmers receive a minimum fixed pension of Rs. 3,000 per month.
 
• The scheme aims to provide social security to farmers after their retirement.
 
 
 
• **Soil Health Card Scheme (SHC)**
 
 
• The Soil Health Card Scheme was launched by the Government of India in 2015 to promote soil testing and balanced use of fertilizers.
 
• Under this scheme, farmers receive soil health cards containing detailed information about the nutrient content of their soil.
 
• The cards provide recommendations on the type and quantity of fertilizers required to improve soil health and crop productivity.
 
• The scheme aims to reduce overuse of fertilizers, increase crop yields, and improve soil fertility.
 
 
 
• **Agricultural Technology Management Agency (ATMA)**
 
 
• ATMA is a central sector scheme launched in 2005 as part of the National Mission on Agricultural Extension and Technology (NMAET).
 
• It aims to strengthen extension services by integrating research and extension activities at the district level.
 
• ATMA focuses on capacity-building, training, and dissemination of technology to farmers through Farmer Field Schools (FFS) and demonstrations.
 
• The scheme emphasizes participatory and bottom-up planning for agricultural development.

question: The slogan "Har Khet Ko Pani" belongs to:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The slogan **"Har Khet Ko Pani"** is associated with the **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)**, launched by the Government of India in 2015.
 
• The scheme aims to **enhance irrigation coverage** and improve water use efficiency in agriculture across the country.
 
• PMKSY focuses on providing **water to every farm** ("Har Khet Ko Pani") and improving on-farm water management to minimize wastage.
 
• The program integrates multiple schemes such as **Accelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme (AIBP)**, **Watershed Development**, and **On-Farm Water Management**.
 
• The scheme is implemented by the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**, Ministry of Agriculture, and Ministry of Rural Development.
 
• It addresses critical issues like **rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge**, and the adoption of sustainable water conservation practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)**

 
 
• PKVY was launched in 2015 by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare to **promote organic farming practices**.
 
• It aims to reduce dependency on chemical fertilizers and pesticides while increasing soil fertility and productivity.
 
• The scheme encourages farmers to form clusters and adopt organic farming techniques, which are environmentally sustainable.
 
• Financial assistance is provided for organic farming certification, marketing, and cluster formation.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)**
 
 
• Launched in 2016, PMFBY is a crop insurance scheme that aims to **provide financial support to farmers** in case of crop losses due to natural calamities.
 
• The scheme covers risks such as drought, floods, hailstorms, pests, and diseases.
 
• Farmers pay a **nominal premium** (1.5% for rabi crops, 2% for kharif crops, and 5% for commercial crops), while the government provides the remaining subsidy.
 
• It ensures **timely claim settlement** and provides coverage for post-harvest losses.
 
 
 
• **Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY)**
 
 
• RKVY was launched in 2007 to incentivize states to invest more in agriculture and allied sectors.
 
• The scheme aims to achieve **4% annual growth** in the agriculture sector by addressing production constraints.
 
• It focuses on infrastructure development, crop diversification, and promoting value addition in agriculture.
 
• States are provided flexibility to design and implement projects based on local needs.

__
 
• The Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) was launched in 2007 by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare to incentivize states to increase their investment in agriculture and allied sectors.
 
• The scheme focuses on **promoting crop diversification** through cluster-based planning, enabling farmers to adopt high-value and market-driven crops.
 
• RKVY supports projects that promote sustainable agriculture practices, including better crop management and diversification to enhance farmers' income.
 
• Under RKVY, funds are allocated to states based on their agricultural performance and the level of investment made in the sector.
 
• The scheme has been restructured into RKVY-RAFTAAR (Remunerative Approaches for Agriculture and Allied sector Rejuvenation) to focus more on pre- and post-harvest infrastructure, value addition, and innovation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PM-AASHA (Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan)**

 
 
• Launched in 2018, PM-AASHA aims to **ensure remunerative prices** to farmers for their produce.
 
• The scheme has three components: Price Support Scheme (PSS), Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS), and Private Procurement & Stockist Scheme (PPSS).
 
• Its primary objective is to strengthen procurement mechanisms and provide price assurance for crops.
 
 
 
• **SMAM (Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization)**
 
 
• Launched in 2014, SMAM aims to promote the mechanization of agricultural activities to reduce drudgery and enhance productivity.
 
• The scheme focuses on providing subsidies to farmers for purchasing farm machinery and implements.
 
• It aims to increase the reach of farm mechanization to small and marginal farmers and regions with low mechanization levels.
 
 
 
• **AIF (Agriculture Infrastructure Fund)**
 
 
• The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund, launched in 2020, is a medium to long-term debt financing facility for agricultural infrastructure projects.
 
• The fund provides support to farmers, primary agricultural credit societies (PACS), startups, and agri-entrepreneurs for building post-harvest infrastructure like cold storage, warehouses, and collection centers.
 
• It aims to improve the overall agricultural value chain and reduce post-harvest losses.

subject: GK
question: The "National Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) Policy" aims to foster creativity and innovation in India. Which of the following is a key objective of this policy?

options.text: To discourage the filing of patents by domestic inventors to reduce bureaucratic hurdles.
To create public awareness about the economic, social, and cultural benefits of IPRs.
To solely focus on strengthening the enforcement mechanisms against counterfeiting and piracy.
To advocate for the abolition of international treaties related to intellectual property.

solution:
The correct answer is __**To create public awareness about the economic, social, and cultural benefits of IPRs.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) Policy aims to **promote awareness about IPRs** among all sections of society, emphasizing their economic, social, and cultural significance.
 
• It focuses on **enhancing the understanding** of intellectual property rights to foster a culture of innovation and creativity in India.
 
• The policy encourages the **active participation of stakeholders**, including educational institutions, industries, and the public, in promoting IPR awareness.
 
• It seeks to **integrate IPR education** into the academic curriculum to build a knowledge-driven society.
 
• The goal is to **increase the number of IPR filings** in India by creating a more informed public and facilitating innovation-driven economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: To discourage the filing of patents by domestic inventors to reduce bureaucratic hurdles**

 
 
• This option is incorrect as the IPR policy aims to **encourage, not discourage, the filing of patents** by domestic inventors.
 
• The policy seeks to simplify and streamline procedures for filing patents and other IPRs to reduce bureaucratic hurdles.
 
• The government has introduced initiatives like the **Startup Intellectual Property Protection (SIPP) scheme** to assist startups in filing patents and trademarks.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: To solely focus on strengthening the enforcement mechanisms against counterfeiting and piracy**
 
 
• While strengthening enforcement mechanisms is a key component of the IPR policy, the policy does not focus solely on this aspect.
 
• It also emphasizes **IPR awareness, capacity building, and innovation promotion** to create a balanced IPR ecosystem.
 
• Measures include the establishment of **Commercial Courts** and the modernization of IPR offices to ensure timely and effective enforcement.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: To advocate for the abolition of international treaties related to intellectual property**
 
 
• This option is incorrect as the IPR policy supports India's active participation in international treaties and agreements related to intellectual property.
 
• The policy emphasizes **aligning India's IPR framework with global standards** while safeguarding national interests.
 
• India is a signatory to various international IPR treaties, such as the **Paris Convention, Berne Convention, and TRIPS Agreement**.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: National IPR Policy**
 
 
• The National IPR Policy was **adopted by the Government of India in May 2016** to create a robust IPR framework in the country.
 
• The policy is based on **seven objectives**, including IPR awareness, generation, legal and legislative framework, administration, commercialization, enforcement, and human capital development.
 
• It aims to position India as a **global leader in innovation** by building a dynamic and balanced IPR ecosystem.
