question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the **correct **options:

**Assertion (A)**: The Human Development Index can increase even if income drops.

**Reason (R)**: Improvements in life expectancy and education can offset income decline.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 
 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):** The HDI is a composite index used to measure a country's overall achievement in its social and economic dimensions. It combines three key dimensions: **life expectancy at birth** (health), **mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling** (education), and **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita** (income). 
 
• **Assertion (A) - The Human Development Index can increase even if income drops:** This statement is **true** as the HDI is a composite measure. Even if the income component declines, improvements in life expectancy or education can compensate for the income drop, resulting in a net increase in HDI. 
 
• **Reason (R) - Improvements in life expectancy and education can offset income decline:** This statement is also **true**. In the HDI calculation, all three components (health, education, and income) are weighted equally. A significant improvement in life expectancy or education can balance or even outweigh the adverse effects of a decline in income. 
 
• **R is the correct explanation of A:** Since the HDI is calculated using a weighted approach, any improvement in one or more dimensions (like health or education) can counterbalance a drop in income, validating that Reason (R) explains Assertion (A). 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 
 
• **Components of HDI:** 
 
 
• **Health:** Measured by life expectancy at birth, it reflects the ability to lead a long and healthy life. 
 
• **Education:** Calculated using two indicators – mean years of schooling (average number of years of education received by people aged 25 and older) and expected years of schooling (years of education a child entering school can expect). 
 
• **Income:** Measured by Gross National Income (GNI) per capita (adjusted for purchasing power parity), reflecting the standard of living. 
 
 
 
• **Calculation of HDI:** HDI is calculated as the geometric mean of normalized indices for each of the three dimensions (health, education, and income). 
 
• **Weightage of Dimensions:** Each dimension contributes equally (one-third weightage) to the overall HDI value. This ensures that no single dimension dominates the calculation. 
 
• **Country Comparison:** HDI enables the comparison of development levels between countries, focusing on human well-being rather than just economic growth. 
 
• **Global Trends:** Countries like Norway, Switzerland, and Ireland often top the HDI rankings due to their strong performance in health, education, and income indicators. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
 
• **Criticism of HDI:** HDI does not capture inequality, poverty, or environmental sustainability. To address these gaps, the **Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI)** was introduced. 
 
• **HDI vs GDP:** While GDP focuses solely on economic output, HDI provides a broader perspective, incorporating health and education dimensions. 
 
• **India’s HDI Rank:** As per the latest Human Development Report, India ranks **132** among **191 countries**, with significant improvements in life expectancy and education over the years. 
 
• **Example of Offset:** In countries with declining income but improving healthcare and education (e.g., post-communist nations), HDI values may still rise. 
 
a5

question:
**Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct option:**

**Assertion (A)**: In macroeconomics, treating a single commodity as representative of all goods allows simplification of aggregate analysis.

**Reason (R)**: This is because all individual goods always behave identically under inflationary trends.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

solution:
The correct answer is __**A is true, but R is false**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 
 
• **Assertion (A):** In macroeconomics, treating a single commodity as representative of all goods allows simplification of aggregate analysis. 
 
 
• This statement is **true** because macroeconomics often uses a representative commodity to analyze aggregate trends, such as inflation, output, or consumption. 
 
• Using a single representative good or aggregate measure simplifies the complexities of dealing with numerous individual goods. 
 
• For example, the concept of an "aggregate price level" is used to study inflation, even though it combines the prices of multiple goods and services. 
 
 
 
• **Reason (R):** This is because all individual goods always behave identically under inflationary trends. 
 
 
• This statement is **false** because different goods behave differently under inflationary trends. 
 
• For instance, luxury goods, essential goods, and non-essential goods may show varied price elasticity and responses during inflation. 
 
• The demand and supply dynamics of individual goods are influenced by factors such as consumer preferences, production costs, and market conditions, which do not always align uniformly under inflation. 
 
 
 
• Since the assertion is correct but the reason provided does not justify the assertion, the correct option is **A is true, but R is false**. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 
 
• **Macroeconomics and Aggregation:** 
 
 
• **Macroeconomics** studies the economy as a whole, focusing on aggregate indicators like GDP, inflation, and unemployment. 
 
• To simplify analysis, macroeconomics often uses aggregate variables like "aggregate demand," "aggregate supply," and "price levels." 
 
• The concept of treating a single commodity as representative is a methodological tool to make the analysis of complex economies more manageable. 
 
 
 
• **Inflationary Trends:** 
 
 
• **Inflation** refers to the general increase in prices of goods and services over a period of time. 
 
• Not all goods are affected equally by inflation; for example, prices of necessities like food and fuel may rise faster compared to luxury items. 
 
• Inflation impacts consumer purchasing power, but the degree of impact varies across different sectors and goods. 
 
 
 
• **Representative Commodity:** 
 
 
• The use of a representative commodity or index (e.g., Consumer Price Index) helps study the overall behavior of the economy. 
 
• Indices like CPI and GDP Deflator are examples of aggregate measures created by combining data from multiple goods and services. 
 
 
 
• **Micro vs. Macro Behavior:** 
 
 
• In microeconomics, the behavior of individual goods is studied, which often varies based on market structure, demand elasticity, and other factors. 
 
• In macroeconomics, the focus shifts to aggregate behavior, which is a summary of the entire economy, rather than individual goods. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
 
• **Consumer Price Index (CPI):** 
 
 
• CPI measures changes in the price level of a basket of consumer goods and services purchased by households. 
 
• It is widely used as an indicator of inflation and cost of living. 
 
 
 
• **Price Elasticity of Demand:** 
 
 
• Price elasticity measures how sensitive the quantity demanded of a good is to a change in its price. 
 
• Essential goods tend to have low elasticity, while luxury goods often have higher elasticity. 
 
 
 
• **Inflation Types:** 
 
 
• Demand-pull inflation occurs when demand outpaces supply. 
 
• Cost-push inflation arises due to increased production costs, such as raw materials and wages.

question:
**Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct option:**

**Assertion (A):** Increase in autonomous investment leads to a multiplied rise in national income.

**Reason (R):** This happens because of the marginal propensity to save being less than one.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• **Assertion (A): Increase in autonomous investment leads to a multiplied rise in national income:** 
 
 
• This is correct because when there is an increase in autonomous investment, it triggers additional economic activities in various sectors. 
 
• Autonomous investments are those that are not influenced by income levels, such as government spending on infrastructure or private investments in innovation. 
 
• These investments increase demand for goods and services, leading to higher production and, consequently, a rise in national income. 
 
 

 
• **Reason (R): This happens because of the marginal propensity to save (MPS) being less than one:** 
 
 
• This is also correct. The marginal propensity to save (MPS) refers to the fraction of additional income that is saved rather than spent. 
 
• If MPS is less than one, it means that a portion of the income is spent on consumption, which generates further economic activity through the multiplier effect. 
 
• The multiplier effect ensures that an initial increase in investment leads to a larger overall increase in national income. 
 
 

 
• **The relationship between A and R:** 
 
 
• The reason (R) is the correct explanation for the assertion (A) because the concept of the multiplier effect is directly tied to the marginal propensity to save being less than one. 
 
• The larger the marginal propensity to consume (MPC), which is the complement of MPS, the greater the multiplier effect on national income. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Autonomous Investment:** 
 
 
• Autonomous investments are those that are made irrespective of the current level of income or economic activity, such as investments in infrastructure, education, or healthcare. 
 
• They are often initiated by governments or large organizations to stimulate economic growth. 
 
• These investments are crucial for kick-starting economic activity, especially in stagnant economies. 
 
 

 
• **Marginal Propensity to Save (MPS):** 
 
 
• MPS is the fraction of additional income that a household saves. It is calculated as MPS = ΔSavings/ΔIncome. 
 
• If MPS is less than one, it implies that the remaining portion of additional income is spent on consumption. 
 
• For example, if MPS is 0.2, it means that 20% of additional income is saved, and 80% is spent on consumption. 
 
 

 
• **Multiplier Effect:** 
 
 
• The multiplier effect explains how an initial increase in investment leads to a larger increase in national income. 
 
• It is calculated as Multiplier = 1/(1 - MPC) or 1/MPS. 
 
• For example, if MPC is 0.8, the multiplier is 1/(1 - 0.8) = 5. This means that every unit of investment leads to a 5-unit increase in national income. 
 
 

 
• **Relationship Between MPS and MPC:** 
 
 
• MPS and MPC are complementary, i.e., MPS + MPC = 1. 
 
• A higher MPC (lower MPS) leads to a stronger multiplier effect, amplifying the impact of autonomous investments on national income. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Key Formula:** The multiplier is inversely related to MPS. A smaller MPS leads to a larger multiplier effect, emphasizing the importance of consumption in driving economic growth. 
 
• **Real-World Examples:** During economic downturns, governments often increase autonomous investments (e.g., stimulus packages) to boost national income through the multiplier effect. 
 
• **Consumption-Driven Growth:** Economies with high marginal propensities to consume tend to experience faster growth due to the enhanced impact of investment on income levels.

question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct option:

Assertion (A): GDP doesn't really tell the whole story when it comes to how well people in a country are actually doing.

Reason (R): That's mainly because it doesn't take into account stuff like wear and tear of machines, pollution, or even how the money is divided among people.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Assertion (A): GDP doesn't really tell the whole story when it comes to how well people in a country are actually doing.** 
• Gross Domestic Product (**GDP**) measures the total economic output of a country but does not reflect the overall well-being of citizens. 
• It does not account for factors such as income inequality, environmental degradation, or the quality of life. ***Hence, the assertion is correct.*** 
• **Reason (R): That's mainly because it doesn't take into account stuff like wear and tear of machines, pollution, or even how the money is divided among people.** 
• **GDP** primarily measures economic activity and ignores externalities like **pollution**, **resource depletion**, or **income distribution.** 
• It also excludes factors such as the depreciation of capital goods (wear and tear of machines) and how wealth is distributed among individuals. ***Hence, the reason is correct.*** 
• The reason directly explains why GDP fails to fully capture the well-being of citizens. ***Thus, it is the correct explanation of the assertion.*** 
• ***Therefore, both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.*** 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Limitations of GDP as an Indicator:** 
• **Environmental Costs:** GDP does not consider the negative effects of economic activities, such as **pollution** or depletion of natural resources. 
• **Income Inequality:** GDP measures total output but does not show how income is distributed across the population. High GDP can coexist with **widespread poverty**. 
• **Non-Market Activities:** Informal sector activities, household labor, and volunteer work are excluded from GDP calculations, despite their contribution to society. 
• **Depreciation:** GDP does not account for the wear and tear of capital goods (known as **depreciation**), which can affect future productivity. 
• **Quality of Life:** GDP focuses on quantity rather than quality. Factors like **healthcare**, **education**, or **happiness** are not directly measured. 
• **Alternative Measures of Well-Being:** 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):** Combines measures of **health**, **education**, and **income** to provide a broader perspective on well-being. 
• **Gross National Happiness (GNH):** Used by countries like Bhutan to prioritize **happiness** and quality of life over economic output. 
• **Genuine Progress Indicator (GPI):** Adjusts GDP by considering factors such as **environmental costs**, **social costs**, and income inequality. 
• **Green GDP:** Accounts for environmental degradation and resource depletion alongside economic growth. 
• **Important Points:** 
• Economists and policymakers often use GDP as a benchmark but recognize the need for supplementary indicators to assess a country’s overall progress. 
• In recent years, global organizations like the **United Nations** and **World Bank** have emphasized the importance of inclusive growth and sustainable development. 
• Countries are increasingly adopting multidimensional indices to address the limitations of GDP and focus on long-term well-being.

subject: GK
question: Which of the following is usually excluded when measuring a country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP)?

options.text: Consumer spending on final goods and services.
The value of intermediate goods used in production.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The value of intermediate goods used in production.**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 __ 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** measures the total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a specific time period. 
• The **value of intermediate goods** is excluded from GDP calculations to avoid **double counting**, which would otherwise inflate GDP figures. 
• Intermediate goods are those **used as inputs** in the production of other goods and services, such as raw materials or components. 
• Only the value of **final goods and services**, which are sold to the end-user, is included in GDP measurements. 
• For instance, if a car manufacturer buys steel to produce a car, the value of steel is not separately added to GDP, as it is already accounted for in the final price of the car. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Components of GDP:** 
• **Consumer Spending:** Includes household expenditures on goods and services like food, clothing, and entertainment. 
• **Government Expenditure:** Includes government spending on public services such as education, defense, and infrastructure. 
• **Net Exports:** Calculated as exports minus imports. A positive net export contributes to GDP, while a negative net export reduces it. 
• **Why Intermediate Goods Are Excluded:** 
• Including intermediate goods in GDP would lead to **double counting**, as their value is already embedded in the final goods. 
• This exclusion ensures an accurate and undistorted representation of a country's economic output. 
• **Examples of Intermediate and Final Goods:** 
• **Intermediate Goods:** Steel used in construction, flour used by bakeries to make bread. 
• **Final Goods:** Cars sold to consumers, bread sold at grocery stores. 
• **Methods of GDP Calculation:** 
• **Production Approach:** Calculates GDP based on the value added at each stage of production. 
• **Income Approach:** Summarizes all incomes earned in the economy, such as wages, rents, and profits. 
• **Expenditure Approach:** Totals all expenditures on final goods and services. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Consumer Spending:** Largest component of GDP in many economies, reflecting the purchasing power and demand of households. 
• **Government Expenditure:** Includes spending on infrastructure projects and public services, crucial for economic development. 
• **Net Exports:** A key indicator of a country's trade balance, influencing its economic health and GDP. 
• **Intermediate Goods in Context:** Their exclusion highlights the importance of focusing on value addition in GDP metrics. 
• **Relevance of GDP:** Used as an indicator of economic performance and to compare economic activity across nations. </ul

question: Which of the following is **NOT** a feature of food security?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Acceptability**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Food security, as defined by the United Nations’ Committee on World Food Security, means that all people, at all times, have physical, social, and economic access to sufficient, safe, and nutritious food that meets their food preferences and dietary needs for an active and healthy life.
 
• **Food security is the combination of the following three elements:**
 
 
• **Food availability **i.e. food must be available in sufficient quantities and on a consistent basis. It considers stock and production in a given area and the capacity to bring in food from elsewhere, through trade or aid.
 
• **Food access** i.e. people must be able to regularly acquire adequate quantities of food, through purchase, home production, barter, gifts, borrowing, or food aid.
 
• **Food utilization**: Consumed food must have a positive nutritional impact on people. It entails cooking, storage and hygiene practices, individuals health, water and sanitation, feeding and sharing practices within the household.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__

 
• The **National Development Council (NDC)** in its 53rd meeting held on 29th May 2007 adopted a resolution to launch a Food Security Mission comprising rice, wheat, and pulses to increase the annual production of rice by 10 million tonnes, wheat by 8 million tonnes, and pulses by 2 million tonnes by the end of the Eleventh Plan (2011-12).

 
 
• Accordingly, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, 'National Food Security Mission (NFSM)', was launched in October 2007.
 
• The approximate percentage of funds allocated for pulses under the National Food Security Mission for 2017-18 is 60%.

question: Unemployment arising due to mismatch between Job availability in the market and skills of available worker is called?
solution:
The correct option is __**Structural**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term unemployment refers to a situation where a person **actively searches for employment but is unable **to find work.
 
• **Structural **unemployment comes about through a **technological change in the structure of the economy** in which labour markets operate. 
 
• Technological changes can lead to unemployment among workers displaced from jobs that are no longer needed
 
• Examples of such changes include the replacement of horse-drawn transport with automobiles and the automation of manufacturing,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frictional Unemployment**

 
 
• This type of unemployment is usually short-lived. It is also the least problematic from an economic standpoint. It occurs when people voluntarily change jobs.
 
 
 
• **Seasonal unemployment**
 
 
• It occurs at different points over the year because of seasonal patterns that affect jobs. Some examples include ski instructors, fruit pickers and holiday-related jobs.
 
 
 
• **Economic Unemployment**
 
 
• During an economic downturn, a shortfall of demand for goods and services results in a lack of jobs available for those who want to work. Businesses experiencing weaker demand might reduce the number of people they employ by laying off existing workers or hiring fewer new workers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **According to the Rangarajan committee**, the poverty ratio has **declined from 39.6% in 2009-10 to 30.9% in 2011-12 in rural India and from 35.1% to 26.4% in urban India.** The decline was thus a uniform 8.7 percentage points over the two years.
 
• The all-India poverty ratio fell from 38.2% to 29.5%. Totally, 91.6 million individuals were lifted out of poverty during this period.
 
• States such as Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, and Uttarakhand saw about a 10 per cent decline in poverty over the past years.
 
• In Odisha, the decrease is 24.6 %, Bihar 20.7 %, Rajasthan 19.7 %, and Jharkhand 8.3%.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The poverty rate is the ratio of the number of people (in a given age group) whose income falls below the poverty line; taken as half the median household income of the total population.
 
• It is also available by broad age group: child poverty (0-17 years old), working-age poverty and elderly poverty (66 year-olds or more).
 
• However, two countries with the same poverty rates may differ in terms of the relative income-level of the poor.
 
• An expert group constituted by the Planning Commission and, chaired by Suresh Tendulkar, was constituted to review methodology for poverty estimation and to address the shortcomings of the previous methods.

Recommendations of the Tendulkar Committee

 
• The shift from Calorie Consumption-based Poverty Estimation:

 
 
• It based its calculations on the consumption of the items like cereal, pulses, milk, edible oil, non-vegetarian items, vegetables, fresh fruits, dry fruits, sugar, salt & spices, other food, intoxicants, fuel, clothing, footwear, education, medical (non-institutional and institutional), entertainment, personal & toilet goods.
 
 
 
• Uniform Poverty line Basket: 
 
 
• Tendulkar Committee computed new poverty lines for rural and urban areas of each state based on the uniform poverty line basket and found that all India poverty line (2004-05) was:
 
 
• ₹446.68 per capita per month in rural areas
 
• ₹578.80 per capita per month in urban areas
 
 
 
 
 
• Private Expenditure: Incorporation of private expenditure on health and education while estimating poverty.
 
• Price Adjustment Procedure: The Committee also recommended a new method of updating poverty lines, adjusting for changes in prices and patterns of consumption, using the consumption basket of people close to the poverty line.
 
• Tendulkar committee computed poverty lines for 2004-05 at a level that was equivalent, in Purchasing Power Parity (PPP) terms to Rs 33 per day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ef88204c8ac1d482f20c172de58a625007a5e9520bcece0b4a7236cc62194ece.png] 

Note- Purchasing Power Parity model refers to a method used to work out the money that would be needed to purchase the same goods and services in two countries.

question:
Consider the following statements about unemployment in India:

a) Seasonal unemployment is mainly found in urban areas.

b) Educated unemployed people are mainly found in rural areas of India.

c) Higher cropping intensity is desirable for reducing unemployment in the rural economy.

Which of the given statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only c**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct choice is: c)** Higher cropping intensity (greater number of crops grown in a year on the same land) can indeed help reduce unemployment in rural areas by providing more continuous work for agricultural laborers.Higher cropping intensity (greater number of crops grown in a year on the same land) can indeed help reduce unemployment in rural areas by providing more continuous work for agricultural laborers.
 
• The given statements **a) and b) are typically incorrect **based on the general understanding of these terms:
 
 
• a) Seasonal Unemployment is primarily found in agriculture-dominated rural areas, not urban areas. This is because agriculture in India is largely dependent on the monsoon season, creating periods of high activity and low activity.
 
• b) Educated unemployment, or a situation where educated individuals are unable to find suitable jobs, is typically associated with urban areas rather than rural areas. This is due to higher access to education in urban regions and the propensity for educated individuals to look for employment in urbanized, industrial, or service-based sectors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structural Unemployment**: This type of unemployment occurs when there is a mismatch between the skills possessed by job seekers and the skills demanded by employers. It often results from changes in technology or shifts in the economy, leaving some workers with obsolete skills.
 
• **Frictional Unemployment**: Frictional unemployment refers to the temporary period of unemployment that arises when individuals are transitioning between jobs or entering the workforce for the first time. It's often considered natural as people search for better opportunities.
 
• **Cyclical Unemployment**: This type of unemployment is linked to the business cycle. It occurs when economic downturns lead to reduced demand for goods and services, resulting in reduced production and layoffs. As the economy improves, this type of unemployment tends to decrease.
 
• **Seasonal Unemployment**: Seasonal unemployment arises due to the seasonal nature of certain industries. Workers in agriculture, tourism, and other sectors experience joblessness during off-peak seasons when demand for their services declines.
 
• **Disguised Unemployment**: This situation occurs when more people are engaged in a task or job than actually required, leading to inefficiencies and reduced productivity. It's often seen in rural areas where multiple family members work on a farm but could be replaced by fewer workers using modern techniques.
 
• **Educational Unemployment**: This is when individuals are unemployed due to the lack of necessary education or skills required for available jobs. It highlights the importance of aligning education and training with the demands of the job market.
 
• **Underemployment**: Underemployment refers to a situation where workers are employed in jobs that are below their skill levels or that don't utilize their full capabilities. This often leads to lower income and job dissatisfaction.
 
• **Long-Term Unemployment**: Long-term unemployment occurs when individuals remain unemployed for an extended period, typically more than 27 weeks. It can have adverse effects on skills, self-esteem, and employability.
 
• **Technological Unemployment**: This type of unemployment results from technological advancements that replace human labor with automation or machinery. While technology can boost efficiency, it can also lead to job losses in certain industries.

question: Which of the following can be referred to in the estimation of poverty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Monthly Per Capita Expenditure.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Monthly Per Capita Expenditure:-**

 
 
• 
 
It is used in economics and personal finance to describe the average monthly spending of each person in a defined population, such as a household, city, province, or country.

 
 
• 
 
This is calculated by taking the total monthly expenditure of the population and dividing it by the total number of people in that population.

 
 
• 
 
Formula:- **Monthly Per Capita Expenditure = Total monthly expenditure / Total population**.

 
 
• 
 
It can be referred to in the estimation of poverty.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marginal utility:-**

 
 
• It refers to the additional satisfaction or benefit (utility) that a consumer derives from consuming an additional unit of a good or service.
 
• The principle of diminishing marginal utility suggests that as a person consumes more and more of a good, the incremental benefit experienced from consuming another unit declines.
 
 
 
• **Minimum Support Price:-**
 
 
• It is generally used in the context of agricultural policies.
 
• MSP is a form of market intervention by the government to insure agricultural producers against any sharp fall in farm prices.
 
• The minimum support prices are announced by the government at the beginning of the sowing season for certain crops.

question: Which of the following types of unemployment is found in India when people are employed for a certain period of a year in tourist resorts and various tourism-related activities in the mountain regions, but are unemployed in off-seasons?

The correct answer is __**Seasonal unemployment**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Seasonal unemployment is the type of unemployment that occurs when people are employed for a certain period of the year but are unemployed during other times.
 
• This is the type of unemployment that occurs in India when people are employed in the tourism sector but are unemployed during the off-season. 
 
• Seasonal unemployment is common in industries and occupations that are subject to seasonal demand or weather, such as tourism, farming, and construction.
 
• In the tourism sector, some months of the year have more tourists than others, which can lead to seasonal unemployment. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other types of unemployment include:
 
• Frictional unemployment: Occurs when someone is unemployed by choice while looking for a better job opportunity. 
 
• Underemployment
 
 
• When people are employed but want or are available to work more hours.
 
• This can include part-time workers who want to work full-time or people who usually work full-time but are currently working part-time. 
 
 
 
• Disguised unemployment
 
 
• When people are employed but not to their full potential due to a lack of opportunities.
 
• This can include people who are working below their skill set, or people who are doing part-time work but want to work full-time.
 
• Disguised unemployment is also known as underemployment
 
 
 
• Cyclical unemployment is a type of unemployment that occurs when the economy changes, such as during a recession or period of economic growth.
 
 
• It's characterized by a short-term increase in unemployment, usually lasting from one month to 1.5 years.

question: Which of the following options is the most appropriate cause for unemployment in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Over population**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Overpopulation** leads to a larger number of individuals competing for the same number of jobs, which increases the unemployment rate.
 
• With a high population growth rate, the **number of job seekers increases** faster than the number of available jobs.
 
• Overpopulation also puts a strain on resources and infrastructure, which can limit job creation and economic growth.
 
• In many cases, the education system and skill development programs cannot keep up with the growing population, leading to a **mismatch of skills** and available jobs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unemployment**

 
 
• Unemployment occurs when individuals who are capable of working and are actively seeking work remain un-hired. It is often used as a measure of the health of the economy.
 
• Types of unemployment include:
 
 
• **Structural Unemployment:** Caused by changes in the industrial makeup (structure) of the economy.
 
• **Frictional Unemployment:** Short-term unemployment that arises from the process of matching workers with jobs.
 
• **Cyclical Unemployment:** Resulting from economic downturns (recessions).
 
• **Seasonal Unemployment:** Occurs when industries slow or shut down for a season or make seasonal shifts in their production schedules.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Overpopulation**
 
 
• Overpopulation refers to a situation where the population exceeds the carrying capacity of the environment or the available resources.
 
• It results in environmental degradation, depletion of natural resources, and a higher level of competition for jobs, housing, and other services.
 
• Overpopulation can lead to higher levels of poverty and a lower quality of life for the population.
 
• Efforts to control overpopulation include family planning, education, and policies aimed at reducing birth rates.
 
 
 
• **Economic Growth**
 
 
• Economic growth refers to an increase in the production of goods and services in an economy over a period of time.
 
• It is often measured by the increase in Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
 
• Economic growth can lead to higher employment levels, improved living standards, and an increase in the overall wealth of a country.
 
• Sustainable economic growth is essential for reducing unemployment and alleviating poverty.

__

• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)** are typically small, community-based organisations that are formed by individuals coming together voluntarily.

• **Microfinance Institutions (MFIs)** are larger and more formal institutions that provide financial services to low-income individuals or groups.

• SHGs often operate at the grassroots level, focusing on mutual help and social solidarity among members.

• MFIs operate on a larger scale and often have a formal structure and regulatory framework guiding their operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)**

• SHGs are small, informal groups of people who come together to address common problems and pool their resources for mutual benefit.

• They are often formed with the aim of improving the economic and social conditions of their members.

• SHGs are usually supported by Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs) and government agencies.

• They often focus on savings and credit activities to help members improve their financial stability.

• **Microfinance Institutions (MFIs)**

• MFIs are financial institutions that provide microcredit and other financial services to low-income individuals or groups who do not have access to traditional banking services.

• They offer a range of financial products, including loans, savings, insurance, and remittance services.

• MFIs aim to promote financial inclusion and empower economically disadvantaged individuals by providing them with access to financial resources.

• They operate under formal regulatory frameworks and are often registered as Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) or other legal entities.

question: Which of the following sectors in India faces seasonal unemployment?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Agriculture is a sector that is highly dependent on seasons and climatic conditions, leading to **seasonal unemployment**.
 
• During the off-season, agricultural workers may not find work, leading to **temporary unemployment**.
 
• This type of unemployment typically affects rural areas where agriculture is the primary occupation.
 
• Seasonal unemployment in agriculture can be mitigated by providing alternate employment opportunities during the off-season.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seasonal Unemployment:**

 
 
• Seasonal unemployment occurs when people are unemployed at certain times of the year because their work is seasonal in nature.
 
• Common sectors that face seasonal unemployment include **agriculture, tourism, and construction**.
 
• In agriculture, this type of unemployment happens between planting and harvesting seasons.
 
• To mitigate seasonal unemployment, workers often seek **alternative employment** during the off-season or may participate in government employment schemes.
 
 
 
• **Cyclical Unemployment:**
 
 
• Cyclical unemployment occurs due to the **fluctuations in the business cycle**—during recessions, demand for goods and services decreases, leading to job losses.
 
• This type of unemployment is typically **temporary** and can be addressed through economic policies that stimulate demand.
 
 
 
• **Structural Unemployment:**
 
 
• Structural unemployment is caused by **mismatches between the skills of the unemployed and the skills needed for available jobs**.
 
• This can be due to technological changes, shifts in the economy, or other long-term changes.
 
• Re-training and education programs can help reduce structural unemployment.
 
 
 
• **Frictional Unemployment:**
 
 
• Frictional unemployment occurs when people are temporarily unemployed while transitioning from one job to another.
 
• This is a natural form of unemployment and is often short-term.
 
• It is also considered a sign of a healthy economy as workers move to jobs that better match their skills and preferences.

question:
**Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are given below. Choose the correct option:**

**Assertion (A):** Population growth can be measured in absolute numbers and percentage change per year.

**Reason (R):** Measuring growth only in absolute numbers provides detailed insights into population trends over time.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3: A is true, but R is false**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Assertion (A): Population growth can be measured in absolute numbers and percentage change per year.**
 
• This statement is correct as population growth is commonly assessed using both absolute numbers (total increase in population) and percentage change (growth rate relative to the total population).
 
• Absolute numbers give the actual increase in population size, while percentage change provides a standardized measure to compare growth rates across regions or time periods.
 
• **Reason (R): Measuring growth only in absolute numbers provides detailed insights into population trends over time.**
 
• This statement is incorrect because measuring growth only in absolute numbers does not provide a complete or detailed picture of population trends. For example, it does not account for variations in population size or growth rates across regions or timeframes.
 
• Therefore, while the assertion is true, the reason does not correctly explain it, making Option 3 the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Growth Measurement**

 
 
• Population growth can be influenced by factors such as birth rate, death rate, immigration, and emigration.
 
• Absolute numbers are useful for understanding the total increase in population size but do not account for population distribution or density.
 
• Percentage change provides a relative measure, enabling comparison across regions or time periods.

Assertion (A): Demographic statistics like birth and death rates rely on accurate reporting by households.

Reason (R): Birth and death registration is mandatory and always accurately followed in all parts of India.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation

solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Demographic statistics** like birth and death rates depend heavily on accurate reporting from households to maintain the reliability of population data.
 
• Birth and death registration in India is governed by the **Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969**, which mandates recording these events.
 
• Despite the legal requirement, the implementation of birth and death registration varies widely across regions due to factors like literacy levels, infrastructure, and accessibility.
 
• The claim in the reason (R) that registration is "always accurately followed in all parts of India" is incorrect. Challenges such as lack of awareness, geographical inaccessibility, and resource constraints often result in underreporting or delayed registration.
 
• Thus, while the assertion (A) is correct, the reason (R) is false, as it does not accurately explain the situation of registration compliance in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Importance of Birth and Death Registration**

 
 
• Accurate registration is crucial for demographic analysis, policy-making, and resource allocation at both national and state levels.
 
• Birth certificates serve as proof of age, identity, and nationality, which are essential for accessing various benefits and rights.
 
• Death registration helps track mortality rates, causes of death, and contributes to public health planning.
 
• Efforts are being made to improve registration rates in India through awareness campaigns and the digitization of records.

question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:

Assertion (A): Human Development Index (HDI) in India improved significantly post-2010.

Reason (R): The methodology was revised globally to include inequality-adjusted Human Development Index (HDI).

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Human Development Index (HDI) in India has shown significant improvement post-2010 due to progress in areas such as health, education, and income.
 
• Globally, the HDI methodology was revised in 2010 to include the Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index (IHDI), which accounts for inequality in each dimension of HDI.
 
• However, India’s improvement in HDI post-2010 is primarily attributed to socio-economic growth and policy interventions rather than just the inclusion of IHDI.
 
• The IHDI adjustment reflects the actual level of human development after accounting for inequality, but it is not the sole reason for India's HDI improvement.
 
• Thus, while both the assertion and reason are true, the reason does not directly explain the assertion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inequality-adjusted Human Development Index (IHDI):**

 
 
• The IHDI was introduced in 2010 to address the limitations of the HDI by considering inequality in each dimension.
 
• It provides a more accurate representation of human development by accounting for disparities in health, education, and income.
 
• If inequality is high, the IHDI value will be much lower than the HDI value.
 
 
 
• **India’s Socio-Economic Policies:**
 
 
• Post-2010, India implemented various schemes focusing on education (e.g., Right to Education Act), healthcare (e.g., Ayushman Bharat), and income generation (e.g., MNREGA).
 
• These policies collectively contributed to the improvement in India’s HDI.

subject: GK
question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding population stabilization?

options.text: Stabilization occurs when birth rate exceeds death rate
Stabilization is reached when fertility rate drops to zero
Stabilization occurs when birth and death rates are nearly equal
Stabilization refers to doubling of population every decade

solution:
The correct answer is __**Stabilization occurs when birth and death rates are nearly equal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Population stabilization refers to a stage where the number of births is approximately equal to the number of deaths over a specific period.
 
• This balance ensures that the total population remains constant or changes very slightly, avoiding rapid growth or decline.
 
• Stabilization is achieved when the Total Fertility Rate (TFR) is at or slightly below the replacement level (approximately 2.1 children per woman).
 
• Population stabilization is a critical goal for sustainable development as it helps reduce pressure on resources like food, water, healthcare, and education.
 
• Countries like Japan and many European nations have achieved population stabilization through effective policies and societal changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: Stabilization occurs when birth rate exceeds death rate**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect because when the birth rate exceeds the death rate, the population grows rather than stabilizes.
 
• High birth rates without corresponding death rate reduction lead to population explosions, which are often unsustainable in the long term.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Stabilization is reached when fertility rate drops to zero**
 
 
• This is inaccurate as a fertility rate of zero would result in no births, causing a population decline and eventual extinction over time.
 
• Population stabilization requires a fertility rate around the replacement level (2.1), not zero.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Stabilization refers to doubling of population every decade**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect as doubling the population every decade signifies rapid growth, not stabilization.
 
• Rapid population growth can strain resources and hinder economic and social development.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Population Stabilization**
 
 
• Population stabilization is essential for sustainable development, reducing environmental degradation, and improving living standards.
 
• Policies like family planning, education, and access to healthcare play a vital role in achieving population stabilization.
 
• Global organizations, including the United Nations, emphasize the importance of stabilizing population growth to meet sustainable development goals (SDGs).

question: What was the aim of the Sixth Plan (1980-85)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Poverty reduction and modernization**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-85)** was focused on achieving **poverty reduction** and **modernization of industries** in India. It aimed to improve the living standards of people and ensure balanced economic development. 
• The plan emphasized the importance of **economic self-reliance** and targeted reducing the percentage of people living below the **poverty line** through employment generation and rural development. 
• Key sectors prioritized under this plan included **agriculture, energy, industry, and human resource development**, which were seen as critical for modernization and sustainable growth. 
• The government introduced several schemes and programs to foster rural development, including **Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP)** and **National Rural Employment Programme (NREP)**. 
• The Sixth Plan also emphasized **technological upgradation** and modernization in industries to make them more competitive globally. This was aimed at reducing dependency on imports and achieving **self-reliance**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP):** 
• Launched in **1980**, the IRDP aimed to provide **employment opportunities** and improve the quality of life in rural areas by offering productive assets to the poor. 
• The program targeted individuals below the **poverty line**, including small farmers, landless laborers, and rural artisans. 
• **National Rural Employment Programme (NREP):** 
• Introduced during the Sixth Plan, this program focused on creating **employment opportunities** in rural areas through labor-intensive projects like road construction, irrigation, and afforestation. 
• The program also aimed at improving rural infrastructure to support economic development. 
• **Modernization of Industries:** 
• The Sixth Plan promoted the adoption of **modern technologies** to enhance industrial efficiency and productivity. 
• It aimed at reducing import dependency and fostering **self-reliance** in key sectors like energy, steel, and engineering goods. 
• **Poverty Reduction:** 
• The Sixth Plan sought to reduce the percentage of people living below the **poverty line** from 48% to 30% by the end of the plan period. 
• This was to be achieved through a combination of employment generation, rural development, and targeted welfare programs. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Planning Commission:** The Sixth Plan was prepared and implemented by the **Planning Commission of India**, which has since been replaced by **NITI Aayog** in 2015. 
• **Self-Reliance:** A key feature of the Sixth Plan was its focus on achieving **economic self-reliance** through domestic production and reduced import dependency. 
• **Achievements:** The Sixth Plan successfully achieved a growth rate of **5.4%**, exceeding its target of 5.2%, and made significant contributions to poverty alleviation and industrial modernization. 
• **Legacy:** The initiatives introduced during this period laid the foundation for several future programs and policies aimed at rural development and poverty reduction in India. </ul

question: Terrace farming is done on which of the following types of land?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Terrace Farming:**

 
 
• **This is practiced on hill slopes that do not have enough flat terrain for growing crops. Hence, Option 4 is correct.**
 
• In this, the slopes of the **hills are converted into horizontal terraces of regular intervals which allow the cultivation of crops.**
 
• They also reduce the surface runoff along the slopes and help in preventing soil erosion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **In this, a series of checks are put in place across the slope of a hilly surface.**
 
• The bunds divide the entire slope into numerous smaller segments which help in reducing the runoff along the slopes, ensure greater absorption of rainwater on the slopes thus controlling soil erosion.
 
• Sometimes, the bunds can be in the form of retaining walls.
 
 
 
• **Contour Ploughing**
 
 
• **On slopy areas, ploughing of land must be done across the contours, at right angles to the slope.**
 
• This will prevent the formation of gullies along the slopes which could erode the topsoil through runoff.
 
• This also helps in ensuring that the crops along the slopes get adequate water.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

I. Only marketed goods are considered while estimating Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

II. The work done by a woman at her home is outside the purview of Gross Domestic Product.

III. In estimating GDP, only final goods and services are considered.
solution:
The correct answer is __**I, II and III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The total monetary or market worth **of all finished goods and services produced inside a country's borders in a certain time period is known as **Gross Domestic Product(GDP)**. 
 
• GDP includes the total value of final products that are produced and sold (and not resold) within the current year.
 
• It serves as a comprehensive scorecard of a country's economic health because it is a wide measure of entire domestic production.
 
• 
 In a free market economy, GDP includes only those products that are sold through the market. That is, consumers are willing to pay prices for the products they consume. In principle, GDP does NOT include those products consumers do not pay for. ***Hence statement 1 is correct.***
 
 
• Non-monetary goods and services (e.g. cooking by a housewife) are not included in GDP calculation. *Hence statement 2 is correct.*
 
• To avoid double-counting (adding the value of output to the GDP more than once), GDP only counts the ultimate output of commodities and services, not intermediary items or labour value in the supply chain. *Hence statement 3 is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **GDP represents the monetary value of a country's** final goods and services—those that are purchased by the end-user—produced over a specific period of time (say a quarter or a year).
 
• It counts all of the products produced within a country's borders. GDP is made up of commodities and services generated for market sale as well as certain nonmarket production, such as government-provided defence and education services.
 
• Gross national product, or GNP, is an alternative definition that counts all of a country's residents' productivity.

question: According to the Output Method, GDP is calculated as:

options.text: GDP at Constant Prices - Taxes + Subsidies
GDP at Constant Prices + Taxes - Subsidies

solution:
The correct answer is__** GDP at Constant Prices - Taxes + Subsidies.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the Output Method, GDP is calculated as GDP at Constant Prices - Taxes + Subsidies.__
 
• The **GDP Output Method measures** the monetary or market value of all the goods and services produced within the borders of the country.
 
• In order to avoid a distorted measure of GDP due to price level changes, GDP at constant prices or Real GDP is computed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• GDP is the final value of the final goods and services produced within the geographic boundaries of a country during a specified period of time, normally a year.
 
• It counts the goods and services produced within the country and hence does not consider the products that the country imports from another country.
 
• **GDP calculation through income approach**:
 
 
• The GDP income approach formula starts with the income earned from the production of goods and services.
 
• GDP=Total National Income +Sales Taxes+Depreciation +Net Foreign Factor Income.
 
 
 
• **GDP calculation through Expenditure method:**
 
 
• ​This measures the total expenditure incurred by all entities on goods and services within the domestic boundaries of a country.
 
• GDP= Consumption expenditure + Investment expenditure + Government expenditure + (Exports - Imports).

question: The poverty ratio declined to ________ in 2011-12 in rural India.
solution:
The correct answer is __**30**____**.9%**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the "Rangarajan Report on Poverty", **the poverty ratio has declined from 39.6% in 2009-10 to 30.9% in 2011-12 in rural India**__ and from 35.1% to 26.4% in urban India.
 
• The all-India ratio was 29.5%. In rural India, 260.5 million individuals were below poverty and in urban India 102.5 million were under poverty. Totally, 363 million were below poverty in 2011-12.
 
• 
 
 The Methodology recommended by the Expert Group (Rangarajan) for estimation of poverty is as follows:

 __
 
• 
 
The poverty line should be based on certain normative levels of adequate nourishment, clothing, house rent, conveyance and education, and a behaviorally determined level of other non-food expenses.

 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Poverty **

 
 
• When a person lacks the means of support and necessities for a given level of living, they are said to be in a state or condition of poverty.

__
 
• **Expenditure method **

 
 
• The expenditure method is a system for calculating gross domestic product (GDP) that combines consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports.
 
• It is the most common way to estimate GDP. It says everything that the private sector, including consumers and private firms, and government spending within the borders of a particular country, must add up to the total value of all finished goods and services produced over a certain period of time.
 
• This method produces nominal GDP, which must then be adjusted for inflation to result in the real GDP.
 
 
 
• **Product Method:**
 
 
• The product or value-added method is a way of computing the national income of a country.
 
• This system is also known as the output or inventory method. This method calculates national income by adding value to a product at every stage of its production.
 
 
 
• **Income Method:**
 
 
• In the income method, the national income is measured by adding up the pretax income generated by the individuals and companies in the economy.
 
• It consists of income from wages, rent of buildings and land, interest on capital, profits, etc.

subject: GK
question: What was the duration of Rolling Plan in India?
solution:
Correct answer **1978 to 1980**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points:__**

__
 
• Rolling Plan in India was started in 1978__.
 
• The rolling plan concept was coined by **Gunnar Myrdal.**
 
• This plan was rejected again by the** Indian National Congress government** when it came to power in **1980** and **a new sixth plan was made.**
 
• The main advantage of the rolling plans is that they are flexible.
 
• The Rolling Plan is a plan in which every year the performance of the plan is assessed and a new plan is made next year based on this assessment.
 
• Thus, both the allocation and targets are revised during this plan.
 
• In India, the **Janta Government terminated the fifth five-year plan in 1977-78** and launched its own sixth five-year plan for the period 1978-83 and called it a Rolling Plan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information:__**

​A brief summary of the 5-year plans are: 

 
 

 Five-year plan
 
 
Time Period

 
 Comment
 
 

 First Plan
 1951-56
 During the initial years of independence, the economy was facing the problem of large-scale foodgrains import (1951) and there was the pressure of price rise. In the plan, the highest priority was given to agriculture including irrigation and power projects. 

 

 
 
 

 Second Plan
 1956-61
 The plan period was 1956–61. The plan laid emphasis on rapid industrialization with a focus on heavy industries and capital goods. The architect of this plan was Professor Mahalanobis. 
 
 

 Third Plan
 1961-65
 This plan incorporated the development of agriculture as one of the objectives of planning in India. It also for the first time, considered the aim of balanced, regional development. Significant events like the war with China in 1961– 62 and with Pakistan in 1965–66 affected the performance of this plan. Also, severe drought-led famine in 1965–66 led to a heavy drain and diversion of funds, so this plan utterly failed to meet its targets.
 
 

 Three annual plans
 1966-69
 The fourth plan was ready for implementation in 1966- still the government opted for three annual plans due to weak financial situation and low morale after the defeat by China. Experts, as well as the opposition, called this period as a discontinuity in the planning process. So they named it a period of “Plan Holiday”, i.e., a period when no planning was carried out.
 
 

 Fourth Plan
 1969-74
 The Plan was based on the Gadgil strategy (named after Dhananjay Ramchandra Gadgil, who was a social scientist who had helped in determining the allocation of central assistance for state plans in India.). There was a focus on the ideas of growth with stability and progress towards self-reliance. This plan led to the beginning of the politicisation of planning in India. This led to frequent double-digit inflations, unchecked increase in the fiscal deficits etc. Also, there was a first move in the direction of ‘nationalisation’. Greater control and regulation of the economy were some of the salient features of this plan
 
 

 Fifth Plan
 1974-79
 This plan had its focus on poverty alleviation and self-reliance. The popular rhetoric of poverty alleviation was sensationalised a lot to the extent that the then Indira Gandhi government came out with a fresh plan, i.e., the Twenty-point Programme (1975).

 Twenty point programme gave little importance to the objective of ‘growth with stability’ (one of the major objectives of the Fourth Plan).
 
 

 Twenty Point programme
 1975
 
 

 Sixth Plan
 1980-85
 Due to the draconian emergency, there was a change in the government at the centre. The new government cut-short the fifth plan by a year to the fiscal 1977–78 and came up with the sixth Plan for the period 1978–83 it was called the ‘Rolling Plan’

 In 1980, again government changed at the Centre, Indira led congress came back and it abandoned the rolling plan and came up with a fresh sixth plan (1980-85). This Plan was launched with the slogan of ‘Garibi Hatao’ (alleviate poverty).
 
 

 Seventh Plan
 1985-90
 This plan greatly emphasized on rapid foodgrain production, increased employment creation and productivity in general. The basis of planning, i.e., growth, self-reliance and social justice and modernization in this plan too were the guiding principles. In 1989 the government launched the Jawahar Rojgar Yojana (JRY) to create wage-employment for the rural poor.
 
 

 Two annual Plans
 1990-92
 
 
Due to the fast-changing political situation at the central level also due to the pathbreaking and restructuring-oriented suggestions which were there in the eighth plan, the eighth plan could not take off. The new government, which came in the power in 1991 decided to commence the Eighth Plan for the period 1992–97 and that the fiscals 1990–91 and 1991–92 were then decided as two separate annual plans.

 
 
 

 Eighth Plan
 1992-97
 This was the first plan in the new economic environment after the opening of the economy. The economic reforms which began in 1991 led to structural adjustment and macro-stabilization policies. As the economy moved towards liberalization, there was also severe criticism directed at the move. The opinion was that as the country was now entering into the market economy zone and the state is ‘rolling back’, planning makes no sense.
 
 

 Ninth Plan
 1997-2002
 This plan was launched when due to the South East Asian Financial Crisis in 1996-97, there was an all-round ‘slowdown’ in the economy. But by now the economy was almost out of the fiscal imbroglio of the early 1990s. The plan targeted an ambitious high growth rate of per cent and also aimed towards time-bound ‘social’ objectives. There was an emphasis on the seven identified Basic Minimum Services (BMS). 
 
 

 Tenth Plan
 2002-07
 The Plan mandated greater participation of the NDC in the formulation of planning. Some highly important steps like doubling of per capita income in 10 years; improving quality of life should also come with higher growth rates. Also, ‘Governance’ was considered a factor of development. 
 
 

 Eleventh Plan
 2007-12
 This plan targeted a growth rate of 10 per cent and also voiced the idea of ‘inclusive growth’. 
 
 

 Twelfth Plan
 2012-17
 This plan was prepared by the Planning Commission after the widest and most comprehensive consultation to date as the government believed that citizens are now better informed and literate and are also keen to engage. The plan aimed at a growth rate of 9 per cent. It also emphasized the need to intensify efforts to have a 4 per cent average growth in the agriculture sector.

question:
Which of the following statements is true?

A) Wage bill of the government is a capital expenditure.

B) Disinvestment by the government in a company is a capital receipt.
solution:
The correct answer is__** Option 4**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Disinvestment by the government in a company can be either a capital receipt or a revenue receipt, depending on the nature of the transaction.**
 
• If the government sells its equity shares in a company to the public or to another entity, the proceeds from the sale are considered a capital receipt.
 
• This is because the government is selling a **capital asset **(i.e., its ownership stake in the company) and receiving cash in return.
 
• However, if the government sells its goods or services to a company, such as land or buildings, the proceeds from the sale would be considered a revenue receipt.
 
• This is because the government is receiving cash for the sale of goods or services, which is a normal business transaction and not the sale of a capital asset.
 
• In summary, **the classification of disinvestment receipts as capital or revenue depends on the nature of the transaction and the asset being sold.**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In accounting and finance, capital expenditures refer to investments made by a company or government that are expected to provide long-term benefits, such as the acquisition of fixed assets like** land, buildings, equipment, and machinery.**
 
• These assets are expected to generate revenue or other economic benefits over a long period of time.
 
• On the other hand, the wage bill of the government is typically considered an operating expenditure because it represents the cost of the government's day-to-day operations.
 
• This includes the salaries and wages paid to government employees, which are necessary to keep the government functioning and to provide public services.
 
• While there may be instances where the government's wage bill is considered a capital expenditure, such as when it is tied to a specific capital project, such as the construction of a new building or infrastructure project, in general, it is considered an operating expenditure rather than a capital expenditure.

question: Which of the following is an example of revenue receipt of the government?

options.text: Receipts from sale of shares of public sector companies

solution:

__
 
• **Revenue receipt** refers to the** income** received by the government in the normal course of its business activities, such as** taxes, duties, fees,** and other charges.
 
• **GST (Goods and Services Tax)** is a tax levied on the **supply of goods and services **in India.
 
• It is a **revenue receipt** for the government, as it is collected o**n behalf of the government** by the businesses that are registered under GST.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Receipts from **sale of shares of public sector **companies is a** capital receipt** as it involves the sale of assets.
 
• **Recovery of loans** is also a** capital receipt **as it involves the recovery of loans given by the government.
 
• **Borrowings from public** is a **capital receipt** as it involves the borrowing of funds by the government from the public.
 
• Capital receipts are those that either** increase the government's liabilities** or** lower **the **value of its assets**.
 
 
• In essence, these are the loans that the government has obtained from a variety of sources to pay for **long-term developmental requirements.**
 
• They are **non-recurring** in nature.

subject: GK
question: What was a significant negative environmental impact of the Green Revolution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Soil degradation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Green Revolution led to the extensive use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, which resulted in the degradation of soil quality.
 
• Overuse of these chemicals destroyed beneficial soil microorganisms, making the soil less fertile over time.
 
• High-yielding varieties of crops required more water and nutrients, leading to the depletion of soil nutrients and increased soil salinity.
 
• Monocropping practices associated with the Green Revolution reduced the organic matter in the soil, further contributing to soil degradation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution**

 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to a set of research, development, and technology transfer initiatives that increased agricultural production worldwide, particularly in developing countries, starting in the 1960s.
 
• Key components included the development of high-yielding varieties (HYVs) of staple crops, the use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, and the introduction of modern farming techniques.
 
• The main aim was to achieve food security and reduce hunger by increasing crop yields.
 
 
 
• **Soil Degradation**
 
 
• Soil degradation is the decline in soil quality caused by its improper use, usually for agricultural, industrial, or urban purposes.
 
• It involves the loss of soil's physical, chemical, and biological properties, which affects its ability to sustain plant life and provide ecosystem services.
 
• Factors contributing to soil degradation include erosion, salinization, compaction, loss of soil organic matter, and contamination by toxic substances.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Fertilizers and Pesticides**
 
 
• Chemical fertilizers are substances that supply essential nutrients to plants in the form of compounds like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.
 
• Pesticides are chemicals used to kill or control pests that can damage crops.
 
• Excessive use of these chemicals can lead to environmental issues such as soil degradation, water pollution, and harm to non-target organisms.
 
 
 
• **Monocropping**
 
 
• Monocropping is the agricultural practice of growing the same crop on the same piece of land year after year.
 
• This practice can lead to soil nutrient depletion, increased vulnerability to pests and diseases, and reduced biodiversity.
 
• It often requires higher inputs of fertilizers and pesticides to maintain crop yields, contributing to soil degradation and environmental pollution.

question: In which five-year plan was the 'food, work, and productivity' slogan used?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Seventh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The slogan 'food, work, and productivity' was used during the **Seventh Five-Year Plan** of India.
 
• This plan was implemented during the period from **1985 to 1990**.
 
• The main focus was on increasing agricultural production, employment, and productivity in various sectors.
 
• It aimed to achieve self-sufficiency in food grains and increase employment opportunities to reduce poverty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans of India**

 
 
• India's Five-Year Plans were centralized and integrated national economic programs. These plans aimed at economic development and were formulated by the Planning Commission of India.
 
• The **First Five-Year Plan** (1951-1956) focused on agriculture and energy.
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan** (1956-1961) aimed at the rapid industrialization of the country.
 
• The **Third Five-Year Plan** (1961-1966) focused on agriculture and improving production of wheat.
 
• The **Fourth Five-Year Plan** (1969-1974) aimed at growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance.
 
• The **Fifth Five-Year Plan** (1974-1979) focused on poverty alleviation and achieving self-reliance.
 
• The **Sixth Five-Year Plan** (1980-1985) emphasized the elimination of poverty and technological self-reliance.
 
• The **Seventh Five-Year Plan** (1985-1990) focused on "food, work, and productivity."
 
• The **Eighth Five-Year Plan** (1992-1997) aimed at improving the quality of life, generating employment, and reducing inequality.
 
• The **Ninth Five-Year Plan** (1997-2002) aimed at achieving a rapid and sustainable growth rate.
 
• The **Tenth Five-Year Plan** (2002-2007) focused on reducing poverty and achieving a growth rate of 8% per annum.
 
• The **Eleventh Five-Year Plan** (2007-2012) aimed at inclusive growth.
 
• The **Twelfth Five-Year Plan** (2012-2017) focused on faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth.
 
 
 
• **Planning Commission of India**
 
 
• The Planning Commission was an institution in the Government of India, which formulated India's Five-Year Plans, among other functions.
 
• It was established in March 1950 by an executive resolution of the Government of India, on the recommendation of the Planning Commission's Report.
 
• The Planning Commission was replaced by the **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) in 2015.
