subject: GK
question: Who among the following, while praising the amending feature of the Indian Constitution said that 'This variety in the amending process is wise but is rarely found'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**K C Wheare**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• K C Wheare was a distinguished constitutional scholar known for his work on federalism and constitutional law.
 
• He praised the Indian Constitution's amending process for its variety and flexibility, which he considered wise and unique.
 
• Wheare emphasized that such variety in the amending process is rare among the world's constitutions.
 
• His observations highlight the robustness and adaptability of the Indian Constitution in accommodating changes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Granville Austin**

 
 
• Granville Austin was an American historian who studied the Indian Constitution extensively.
 
• He is known for his seminal work, "The Indian Constitution: Cornerstone of a Nation," which examines the making and functioning of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Austin's work is highly regarded for its in-depth analysis and insight into the Indian constitutional process.
 
 
 
• **Ivor Jennings**
 
 
• Sir Ivor Jennings was a British lawyer and academic who made significant contributions to the study of constitutional law.
 
• He was involved in the drafting of several constitutions in the Commonwealth countries, including India.
 
• Jennings emphasized the importance of conventions and practices in the functioning of a constitution.
 
 
 
• **HM Seervai**
 
 
• H.M. Seervai was a prominent Indian jurist and constitutional expert.
 
• He authored the influential book "Constitutional Law of India," which is a comprehensive commentary on the Indian Constitution.
 
• Seervai's work is widely cited in legal circles and has greatly contributed to the understanding of the Indian constitutional law.
 
 
 
• **Amending Process in the Indian Constitution**
 
 
• The Indian Constitution provides a detailed procedure for its amendment in Part XX, Article 368.
 
• The amending process is categorized into three types: simple majority, special majority, and special majority with ratification by states.
 
• This flexibility allows the Constitution to be both rigid and flexible, accommodating necessary changes while maintaining stability.
 
• Amendments require different levels of parliamentary support and, in some cases, ratification by state legislatures, ensuring a broad consensus.

__
 
• Article 80 of the Indian Constitution deals with the composition of the Council of States, which is commonly known as the Rajya Sabha.
 
• The Rajya Sabha is the upper house of the Parliament of India.
 
• As per Article 80, the Rajya Sabha consists of not more than 250 members.
 
• Out of these, 12 members are nominated by the President of India from among persons having special knowledge or practical experience in fields such as literature, science, art, and social service, and the remaining members are representatives of the States and Union territories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 76**

 
 
• Article 76 of the Indian Constitution deals with the office of the Attorney General of India.
 
• The Attorney General is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India and has the right to participate in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament, but without a right to vote.
 
 
 
• **Article 84**
 
 
• Article 84 of the Indian Constitution specifies the qualifications required to be a member of Parliament.
 
• These qualifications include being a citizen of India, being not less than 30 years of age in the case of the Rajya Sabha and 25 years in the case of the Lok Sabha, and possessing such other qualifications as may be prescribed by law by the Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Article 92**
 
 
• Article 92 of the Indian Constitution deals with the provisions for the Chairman or Deputy Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
 
• It states that while the office of Chairman or Deputy Chairman is vacant, or in the absence of the Chairman from any sitting of the Council, the duties of the office shall be performed by the Deputy Chairman, or if the Deputy Chairman is also absent, by such member of the Council as may be determined by the rules of procedure of the Council.

question: Which article of the Constitution of India lays down that it shall be the duty of the Advocate-General to give advice to the Government of the State upon legal matters?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 165**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 165 of the Indian Constitution specifies the duties of the Advocate-General for the State.
 
• It mandates that the Advocate-General shall give advice to the State Government upon legal matters referred to him.
 
• The Advocate-General is the highest law officer in the state and corresponding to the Attorney General of India at the central level.
 
• Article 165 also allows the Advocate-General to perform any other legal duties assigned to him by the Governor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Advocate-General of the State:**

 
 
• The Advocate-General is appointed by the Governor of the State.
 
• He must be a person who is qualified to be appointed as a judge of a High Court, which means he must be an Indian citizen and must have been an advocate of a High Court for ten years or a judge of two or more such courts in succession for a similar period.
 
• The Advocate-General's functions are comparable to those of the Attorney General of India, but he operates at the state level.
 
 
 
• **Legal Advice to the Government:**
 
 
• Article 165(2) mentions that the Advocate-General shall perform duties of a legal character assigned to him by the Governor.
 
• He has the right to speak and participate in the proceedings of both Houses of the State Legislature, but without the right to vote.
 
 
 
• **Other Relevant Articles:**
 
 
• **Article 168**: Deals with the Constitution of Legislatures in states.
 
• **Article 166**: Specifies the conduct of business of the Government of a State.
 
• **Article 167**: Discusses the duties of the Chief Minister as respects the furnishing of information to the Governor.

question:
Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India lays down that ‘The allocation of seats in the Council of States to

be filled by representatives of the States and of the Union territories shall be in accordance with the provisions in that behalf contained in the fourth Schedule’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 80**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 80 of the Constitution of India deals with the composition of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
 
• The Council of States is to be composed of representatives of the States and Union territories.
 
• The allocation of seats in the Council of States is specified in the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution.
 
• This article ensures that the representation of states and union territories in the Rajya Sabha is in accordance with the provisions laid out in the Fourth Schedule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 81**

 
 
• Article 81 of the Constitution of India deals with the composition of the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
• It specifies the maximum number of seats in the Lok Sabha and the allocation of these seats among the States.
 
 
 
• **Article 82**
 
 
• Article 82 pertains to the readjustment of seats in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies after each census.
 
• This article ensures periodic readjustments to reflect changes in the population.
 
 
 
• **Article 83**
 
 
• Article 83 specifies the duration of the Houses of Parliament.
 
• The Lok Sabha has a term of five years, unless dissolved sooner, while the Rajya Sabha is a permanent body with one-third of its members retiring every two years.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Schedule**

• This schedule ensures balanced representation of the States and Union territories in the Council of States.

question: The Epidemic Diseases (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020 amended which of the following Acts?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 was enacted to provide for better prevention of the spread of dangerous epidemic diseases.
 
• The Act gives special powers to state and central governments to take measures necessary to prevent the outbreak or spread of an epidemic.
 
• The Epidemic Diseases (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020 was introduced to include protections for healthcare personnel combatting epidemic diseases.
 
• The Ordinance also provides for stricter penalties for acts of violence against healthcare service personnel and damage to property during epidemics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897**

 
 
• The Act was passed by the British colonial government in India in 1897 in response to the bubonic plague outbreak in Mumbai (then Bombay).
 
• The Act allows the central and state governments to take special measures and prescribe regulations to prevent the spread of epidemic diseases.
 
• The Act also provides the legal framework for the implementation of containment measures such as quarantine, isolation, and restrictions on the movement of people.
 
• The Act has been invoked several times in India, including during the outbreaks of H1N1 influenza (swine flu), dengue, and COVID-19.
 
 
 
• **The Epidemic Diseases (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020**
 
 
• The Ordinance was promulgated by the President of India on April 22, 2020, in response to the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• It amends the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 to include protections for healthcare service personnel combating epidemic diseases.
 
• The Ordinance defines "healthcare service personnel" to include healthcare professionals, nurses, paramedical workers, and any other person empowered under the Act to take measures to prevent the outbreak or spread of an epidemic disease.
 
• It provides for imprisonment and fines for acts of violence against healthcare service personnel and damage to property during epidemics.
 
 
 
• **Other Important Terminologies**
 
 
• **Quarantine:** A restriction on the movement of people and goods intended to prevent the spread of disease or pests.
 
• **Isolation:** The separation of people who are infected with a contagious disease from those who are healthy to prevent the spread of the disease.
 
• **Containment Measures:** Strategies and actions taken to prevent the spread of a disease within a community, including quarantine, isolation, and restrictions on movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 75** of the Indian Constitution deals with the appointment of the Prime Minister and other ministers by the President.
 
• It states that **the Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President** and the other Ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
• The article also discusses the **collective responsibility of the Council of Ministers to the House of the People (Lok Sabha)**.
 
• It mentions that the Ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the President.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 62**

 
 
• Article 62 deals with the time of holding election to fill a vacancy in the office of President and the term of office of the elected person.
 
• It specifies that an election to fill the vacancy caused by the expiration of the term of office of President shall be completed before the expiration of the term.
 
• It also states that an election to fill a vacancy in the office of President occurring by reason of his death, resignation, or removal, or otherwise, shall be held as soon as possible after, and in no case later than six months from, the date of occurrence of the vacancy.
 
 
 
• **Article 66**
 
 
• Article 66 deals with the election of the Vice-President of India.
 
• The Vice-President is elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament.
 
• The election is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote and the voting is by secret ballot.
 
 
 
• **Article 71**
 
 
• Article 71 deals with matters relating to, or connected with, the election of a President or Vice-President.
 
• It states that all doubts and disputes arising out of or in connection with the election of a President or Vice-President shall be inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court whose decision shall be final.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Articles 245 to 255 in Part XI of the Indian Constitution deal with the **legislative relations between the Centre and the states**.
 
• These provisions outline the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the State legislatures.
 
• Article 245 states the extent of laws made by Parliament and by the Legislatures of States.
 
• Article 246 deals with the subject-matter of laws made by Parliament and by the Legislatures of States, emphasizing the three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Emergency Provisions (Articles 352 to 360)**

 
 
• These articles cover the proclamation of emergency by the President of India.
 
• They include National Emergency (Article 352), President's Rule (Article 356), and Financial Emergency (Article 360).
 
 
 
• **Financial Relations (Articles 268 to 293)**
 
 
• These articles outline the financial relations between the Centre and the States.
 
• They cover topics such as distribution of revenues, grants-in-aid, and borrowing powers of the Centre and States.
 
 
 
• **Tribunals (Articles 323A to 323B)**
 
 
• These articles provide for the establishment of administrative tribunals for the adjudication or trial of disputes and offenses.
 
• Article 323A deals with administrative tribunals, while Article 323B deals with tribunals for other matters.

question: Which of the following is the most controversial Article in the Indian Constitution, which provides for President's rule in an state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 356**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 356 of the Indian Constitution deals with the imposition of President's Rule in states.
 
• This article is also known as the "President's Rule" or "State Emergency."
 
• It allows the President of India to take over the functions of the state government if the state government is unable to function according to the provisions of the Constitution.
 
• President's Rule can be imposed for a maximum period of six months at a time and can be extended with the approval of the Parliament, but not beyond three years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 352**

 
 
• Article 352 of the Indian Constitution deals with the proclamation of National Emergency.
 
• It can be declared due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• During a National Emergency, the central government gains sweeping powers, and the state governments come under the direct control of the central government.
 
• This can be proclaimed by the President of India based on the written advice of the Cabinet.
 
 
 
• **Article 358**
 
 
• Article 358 provides for the suspension of the rights guaranteed by Article 19 during a National Emergency.
 
• It states that while a National Emergency is in operation, nothing in Article 19 shall restrict the power of the State to make any law or to take any executive action abridging or taking away the rights conferred by Article 19.
 
 
 
• **Article 360**
 
 
• Article 360 of the Indian Constitution deals with the proclamation of Financial Emergency.
 
• The President can declare a Financial Emergency if the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
 
• During a Financial Emergency, the executive authority of the Union extends to giving directions to any state to observe such canons of financial propriety as may be specified in the directions.
 
• However, no Financial Emergency has been declared in India so far.

question: Which of the following Constitution Amendment Bills is related to the provision of modifying the list of Scheduled Caste in Tamil Nadu?

options.text: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order Amendment Act, 2013

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order (Amendment) Bill, 2021**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order (Amendment) Bill, 2021, was introduced to modify the list of Scheduled Castes in Tamil Nadu.
 
• This amendment bill aims to include certain communities in the list of Scheduled Castes in Tamil Nadu, thereby enabling them to avail benefits and protections guaranteed under the Constitution.
 
• The bill was introduced in the Rajya Sabha on February 8, 2021, by the Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment.
 
• Such amendments are periodically made to address the demands and needs of various communities to ensure equitable development and social justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scheduled Castes**

 
 
• Scheduled Castes (SCs) are specific groups of people who are historically disadvantaged and have been subjected to untouchability and social exclusion.
 
• The Constitution of India provides various safeguards to protect and promote the socio-economic interests of SCs, including reservation in education and employment.
 
• The President of India, in consultation with the Governor of a state, issues orders specifying the SCs in that state.
 
• From time to time, amendments are made to the list of SCs to include or exclude communities based on social, educational, and economic criteria.
 
 
 
• **Constitution Amendment Bills**
 
 
• Constitution Amendment Bills are proposed changes to the Constitution of India.
 
• Such bills can be introduced in either house of Parliament and require a two-thirds majority of the members present and voting for passage.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution address various issues, including the rights of marginalized communities, electoral reforms, and changes in the structure of government.
 
• The Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order (Amendment) Bill is one such amendment aimed at updating the list of SCs.
 
 
 
• **Rajya Sabha**
 
 
• Rajya Sabha, or the Council of States, is the upper house of India's Parliament.
 
• Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of State Legislative Assemblies, and by the members of the Electoral college for Union Territories, using a single transferable vote system.
 
• The Rajya Sabha has a maximum membership of 250 members, of which 12 are nominated by the President of India.
 
• The Rajya Sabha plays a crucial role in the legislative process, including the passage of amendment bills.

question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts led to formation of the Goods and Services Tax Council?
solution:
The correct answer is __**101st Constitutional Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act was passed by the Indian Parliament in August 2016.
 
• This amendment led to the introduction of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India, which came into effect on 1st July 2017.
 
• The GST Council was formed as per Article 279A of the Indian Constitution, inserted by the 101st Amendment.
 
• The GST Council is responsible for making recommendations on the rates of taxes, goods and services that may be subjected or exempted from GST, and other related matters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **102nd Constitutional Amendment Act**

 
 
• This amendment came into effect in 2018.
 
• It granted constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC).
 
• Article 338B was inserted to provide for the NCBC.
 
 
 
• **100th Constitutional Amendment Act**
 
 
• This amendment was passed in 2015.
 
• It dealt with the exchange of certain enclaves between India and Bangladesh and the demarcation of the boundary between the two countries.
 
• It facilitated the implementation of the Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) between India and Bangladesh.
 
 
 
• **103rd Constitutional Amendment Act**
 
 
• This amendment came into effect in 2019.
 
• It introduced a 10% reservation for economically weaker sections (EWS) in government jobs and educational institutions.
 
• Articles 15(6) and 16(6) were added to the Constitution to enable this reservation.
 
 
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**
 
 
• GST is a comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based tax that is levied on every value addition.
 
• It replaced multiple indirect taxes previously levied by the central and state governments.
 
• GST is categorized into Central GST (CGST), State GST (SGST), Integrated GST (IGST), and Union Territory GST (UTGST).
 
• The GST Council, chaired by the Union Finance Minister, is a federal body where both the center and the states participate in the decision-making process.

question: Which of the following most **accurately **describes the legal character of the right to property under Article 300A of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: It is a fundamental right that guarantees compensation for all property acquisitions.
It allows the State to deprive a person of property by any law, even without due process.
It is a constitutional legal right that permits deprivation only by authority of law.
It permits citizens to claim property protection under Article 32 before the Supreme Court.

solution:
The Correct answer is __**It is a constitutional legal right that permits deprivation only by authority of law.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **Article 300A** of the **Indian Constitution**, the right to property is no longer a **fundamental right**. It was demoted to a constitutional legal right by the **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.**
 
• This article states that no person shall be deprived of their property except by the **authority of law.**
 
• This ensures that property can only be taken by the state through a legally established process, providing protection against arbitrary deprivation.
 
• As a constitutional legal right, this provision primarily ensures that property rights are safeguarded as long as the deprivation occurs through proper legislation.
 
• Unlike fundamental rights, violations of Article 300A cannot be directly challenged under **Article 32** in the **Supreme Court**.
 
• However, if property is taken away without following the due process of law, remedies can be sought through the **High Courts under Article 226** or other legal avenues.
 
• The transformation of the right to property from fundamental to constitutional legal right reflects the state's ability to regulate property for public welfare, subject to legal procedures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **It is a fundamental right that guarantees compensation for all property acquisitions.**__

 __
 
• Before the **44th Amendment Act**, the right to property was a fundamental right under **Articles 19(1)(f)** and **31**. However, post-amendment, Article 300A does not guarantee compensation for all acquisitions, and the right to property is now a constitutional legal right.
 
 
 
• **It allows the State to deprive a person of property by any law, even without due process.**__
 __
 
• This statement is incorrect as Article 300A explicitly requires deprivation to occur through the **authority of law**. Arbitrary deprivation without legal procedures violates the article.
 
 
 
• **It permits citizens to claim property protection under Article 32 before the Supreme Court.**__
 
 
• Property rights under Article 300A cannot be enforced through **Article 32**, as they are not fundamental rights. Remedies for violations must be sought through **High Courts under Article 226** or other legal mechanisms.

question: Education is now placed under which list after the 42nd Amendment?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Concurrent List**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act of 1976** is one of the most comprehensive amendments to the Indian Constitution. It brought about significant changes in various provisions.
 
• One of the key changes was the transfer of **Education** from the **State List** to the **Concurrent List**.
 
• By placing education in the **Concurrent List**, both the **Union Government** and the **State Governments** can legislate on matters related to education.
 
• This amendment was aimed at achieving a **uniform educational policy** across the country, ensuring better coordination and implementation of educational reforms.
 
• The **Concurrent List** is one of the three legislative lists under the **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution of India. It contains subjects on which both the Union and State Governments can make laws.
 
• Other important subjects in the Concurrent List include **criminal law, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy, and forests**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Union List**__

 __
 
• The **Union List** contains subjects on which only the **Parliament** has exclusive powers to make laws.
 
• Examples of subjects in the Union List include **defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, banking, and communications**.
 
• It is mentioned in the **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution and includes **100 subjects**.
 
 
 
• **State List**__
 
 
• The **State List** contains subjects on which only the **State Legislatures** have the authority to legislate.
 
• Examples of subjects in the State List include **police, public health, agriculture, and local government**.
 
• This list also falls under the **Seventh Schedule** and contains **61 subjects**.

question: Article 370, which granted special status to Jammu and Kashmir, was abrogated by which constitutional mechanism?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Presidential Order under Article 370(3)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 370** granted special status to Jammu and Kashmir, providing autonomy over its internal matters except for defense, foreign affairs, finance, and communications.
 
• The abrogation of Article 370 was executed using a **Presidential Order** issued under **Article 370(3)**, which allowed the President of India to make modifications or exceptions to Article 370.
 
• The Presidential Order **C.O. 272**, issued on **5th August 2019**, replaced the previous Presidential Order from 1954, extending all provisions of the Indian Constitution to Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019, was passed by Parliament, bifurcating Jammu and Kashmir into two Union Territories: **Jammu and Kashmir** and **Ladakh**.
 
• The procedure involved obtaining the concurrence of the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly, which was absent at the time due to President's Rule. Consequently, the concurrence was given by the **Governor**, who was acting on behalf of the state legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 370:**

 
 
• Article 370 was part of the Indian Constitution that provided special autonomy to Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It was incorporated as a temporary provision under Part XXI of the Constitution, which deals with “Temporary, Transitional, and Special Provisions.”
 
• Under Article 370, the state had its own Constitution and decision-making rights in all matters except defense, foreign affairs, finance, and communications.
 
• It also allowed Jammu and Kashmir to have a separate flag and denied property rights to outsiders.
 
 
 
• **Presidential Order and Article 370(3):**
 
 
• Article 370(3) empowered the President of India to declare Article 370 inoperative or modify it, provided the recommendation of the Constituent Assembly of Jammu and Kashmir was obtained.
 
• Since the Constituent Assembly of Jammu and Kashmir ceased to exist in 1957, the Indian government used the provision of President's Rule in the state to bypass this requirement.
 
• The Presidential Order issued on 5th August 2019 extended all provisions of the Indian Constitution to Jammu and Kashmir, effectively nullifying its special status.
 
 
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act, 2019:**
 
 
• Passed on 6th August 2019, this Act reorganized the state of Jammu and Kashmir into two Union Territories: Jammu and Kashmir (with a Legislative Assembly) and Ladakh (without a Legislative Assembly).
 
• The Act came into effect on **31st October 2019**.
 
• The bifurcation aimed to improve governance and integrate the region fully with the rest of India.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Abrogation:**
 
 
• The abrogation of Article 370 has led to the extension of all Indian laws and provisions to Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It has sparked debates on federalism, autonomy, and the rights of states under the Indian Constitution.
 
• While some argue it has brought greater integration, others highlight concerns over political representation and regional identity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 368:** This article pertains to the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution, including fundamental rights. However, it was not used for the abrogation of Article 370.
 
• **Article 356:** This article allows the imposition of President's Rule in a state due to the failure of constitutional machinery. While President's Rule was in effect in Jammu and Kashmir, Article 356 was not directly used for the abrogation.
 
• **Ordinance by the President:** Ordinances are temporary laws issued by the President when Parliament is not in session. This mechanism was not employed for abrogating Article 370.
 
• It is important to understand that the abrogation of Article 370 followed a unique constitutional process, combining Presidential Orders and Parliamentary legislation.

question: Which Article enables the President to establish an Inter-State Council?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 263**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 263 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President of India to establish an Inter-State Council.
 
• The primary function of the Inter-State Council is to inquire into and advise upon disputes that may arise between states.
 
• It also aims to investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between states or between the Union and one or more states.
 
• The Inter-State Council promotes coordination and cooperation among the states and the Union of India, ensuring smooth governance and resolving inter-state disputes.
 
• The council may also be assigned the responsibility to formulate policies and improve the implementation of laws and schemes for national integration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 264**:

 
 
• This article deals with the provisions related to the "definition" of the territory of India for taxation purposes.
 
• It defines the jurisdiction of the Union and States in terms of taxes and duties, but it does not relate to the Inter-State Council.
 
 
 
• **Article 312**:
 
 
• Article 312 provides for the creation of All India Services, such as the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS).
 
• It allows Parliament to create new All India Services by passing a law, if deemed necessary in the national interest.
 
 
 
• **Article 262**:
 
 
• Article 262 grants Parliament the power to adjudicate disputes related to inter-state rivers or river valleys.
 
• It also provides that Parliament may, by law, bar the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court or any other court in such disputes.

question: Which of the following correctly reflects the legal implication of Article 255 regarding presidential or governor's assent to bills?

options.text: State law is void without written Governor assent.
Mention of assent is mandatory for validity.
Omission of prior recommendation doesn't invalidate law if assent is given.
President's assent must precede legislative passage to be valid.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Omission of prior recommendation doesn't invalidate law if assent is given**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 255 of the Indian Constitution states that the absence of prior recommendation or sanction required by the Constitution does not invalidate a law if it has received the assent of the President or the Governor.
 
• The provision ensures that minor procedural lapses do not obstruct the legislative process, provided the bill has been duly assented to.
 
• For example, even if a recommendation from the President or Governor is not obtained at the time of introducing a bill, the law remains valid if subsequent assent is granted.
 
• This article upholds the principle of legislative supremacy by ensuring that procedural errors do not nullify valid legislative acts.
 
• It applies to both state and central legislation, ensuring uniformity in the treatment of procedural lapses related to assent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Constitutional Articles (Part VI, Chapter II)**

 
 
• Article 153: Establishes the office of the Governor for each state (one person can be Governor for two or more states).
 
• Article 154: Vests the executive power of the state in the Governor.
 
• Article 155: Appointment by the President (warrant under hand and seal).
 
• Article 156: Term of office (holds office during President's pleasure).
 
• Article 157: Qualifications for appointment (Citizen of India, 35 years old).

question: Article 246A of the Constitution of India gives power to both Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws on ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Taxation of Goods and Services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 246A of the Indian Constitution was introduced through the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016**, which enabled the implementation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST).
 
• It grants **concurrent powers** to both the Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws with respect to GST.
 
• Under this article, the Parliament has exclusive power to make laws on **inter-state trade or commerce of goods and services**, while both Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate on intra-state transactions.
 
• GST subsumes multiple indirect taxes such as VAT, Service Tax, Excise Duty, and others, simplifying India's indirect taxation system.
 
• The introduction of Article 246A aimed to promote a unified market, enhance ease of doing business, and eliminate the cascading effects of taxes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Property Rights (Option 1):**

 
 
• Property rights in India are addressed under Article 300A of the Indian Constitution, which states that no person shall be deprived of their property except by the authority of law.
 
• Initially, property rights were a fundamental right under Article 31, but it was abolished by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, and made a legal right under Article 300A.
 
• This provision ensures that private property cannot be taken away without due process of law or proper compensation.
 
 
 
• **Emergency Provisions (Option 3):**
 
 
• Emergency provisions are detailed under Part XVIII (Articles 352 to 360) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These provisions enable the government to assume greater control during times of crisis and include three types of emergencies: National Emergency (Article 352), State Emergency/President’s Rule (Article 356), and Financial Emergency (Article 360).
 
• These provisions are invoked to safeguard the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India during extraordinary situations.
 
 
 
• **Criminal Law (Option 4):**
 
 
• Criminal law in India is primarily governed by the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860, the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973, and various special laws.
 
• The Parliament and state legislatures can legislate on criminal law under the Concurrent List (List III) of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution.
 
• Criminal law ensures the maintenance of public order, punishment for offenses, and the protection of citizens’ rights.

question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is Hindi in Devanagari script declared as the official language of the Union?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 343**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 343** of the Indian Constitution declares Hindi written in the Devanagari script as the official language of the Union.
 
• It also specifies that the numerals used for official purposes must be in the international form of Indian numerals.
 
• The Constitution initially allowed English to continue as an official language of the Union for a period of 15 years from the commencement of the Constitution (1950), which was later extended through amendments.
 
• Article 343(2) empowers Parliament to provide for the continued use of English for official purposes, alongside Hindi, even after the initial 15-year period.
 
• The Official Languages Act of 1963 extended the use of English as an associate official language indefinitely, ensuring bilingual usage for administrative purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 348**:
 
 
• It provides for the language to be used in the Supreme Court and High Courts and for Acts, Bills, and other official documents.
 
• According to this Article, English shall be used for all proceedings in the Supreme Court and High Courts, as well as for authoritative texts of laws and bills at the Union and State levels unless otherwise specified by Parliament or the State Legislature.
 
 
 
• **Article 344**:
 
 
• This Article deals with the Constitution and functions of the Official Language Commission.
 
• The Commission is tasked with making recommendations regarding the progressive use of Hindi for official purposes and the restrictions on using English.
 
• It also advises on measures to promote the spread and development of Hindi throughout the country.
 
 
 
• **Article 351**:
 
 
• It directs the Union Government to promote the spread of the Hindi language and develop it to serve as a medium of expression for all elements of India's composite culture.
 
• The Government is also instructed to enrich Hindi by assimilating its forms, style, and expressions from other Indian languages and Sanskrit.

question: What does Article 268 of the Indian Constitution primarily deal with?

options.text: Service tax levied by Union and collected by States
Income tax levied and collected by States
Stamp duties levied by Union but collected by States
Excise duties on medicinal products collected by States

solution:
The correct answer is __**Stamp duties levied by Union but collected by States**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 268 of the Indian Constitution primarily deals with **duties levied by the Union Government but collected and appropriated by the States**.
 
• It includes **stamp duties on certain instruments** and **excise duties on medicinal and toilet preparations** that are levied by the Union but collected by the State.
 
• The revenue collected from these duties does not form part of the Consolidated Fund of India but is **assigned to the States** where it is collected.
 
• This provision ensures that certain revenue sources are shared between the Union and State Governments to balance fiscal responsibilities.
 
• Examples of stamp duties include duties on transactions such as sale deeds, transfer of property, promissory notes, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fiscal Federalism in India:**

 
 
• The Indian Constitution establishes a clear division of fiscal powers between the Union and State Governments to ensure financial autonomy and accountability.
 
• Articles 268 to 281 of the Constitution outline the distribution of tax revenues between the Union and the States.
 
• Article 268 specifically ensures that certain duties levied by the Union are collected and utilized by the States to support their fiscal responsibilities.

question: Which Article allows Parliament to legislate on a subject in the State List during a National Emergency?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 250**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 250** of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to legislate on matters enumerated in the State List under exceptional circumstances, such as during a National Emergency.
 
• While a National Emergency is in operation (as per Article 352), Parliament can make laws on subjects in the State List for the entire country or part of its territory.
 
• Such laws made by Parliament under Article 250 remain valid only during the period of the emergency and up to six months after it ceases to operate.
 
• This provision ensures that Parliament can address urgent national concerns that might require overriding state authority during an emergency.
 
• Article 250 is a crucial component of the emergency provisions in the Indian Constitution, allowing the central government to maintain legislative control during extraordinary situations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 256**

 
 
• Article 256 deals with the obligation of states and the Union to ensure compliance with laws made by Parliament.
 
• It mandates that the executive power of every state shall be exercised to ensure compliance with the laws made by Parliament.
 
• It does not specifically address the legislative powers of the Parliament during an emergency.
 
 
 
• **Article 254**
 
 
• Article 254 addresses inconsistencies between laws made by Parliament and laws made by state legislatures.
 
• If there is a conflict between a central law and a state law on a subject in the Concurrent List, the central law prevails.
 
• It is unrelated to Parliament’s ability to legislate on State List subjects during a National Emergency.
 
 
 
• **Article 352**
 
 
• Article 352 provides for the proclamation of a National Emergency in India.
 
• The President can declare a National Emergency if there is a threat to the security of India or any part of it due to war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• While Article 352 enables the declaration of an emergency, it is Article 250 that specifically allows Parliament to legislate on State List subjects during such emergencies.

question:
**Consider the following statements: **

1. Article 131A gave High Courts exclusive power to decide on central laws' validity.

2. It was repealed by the 43rd Constitutional Amendment. Which of the above is/are **correct**?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 131A** was introduced by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 during the Emergency period in India.
 
• This article granted the Supreme Court exclusive jurisdiction to decide the constitutional validity of any Central law, bypassing High Courts.
 
• The provision aimed to centralize judicial power in the Supreme Court, reducing the role of High Courts in this matter.
 
• The 43rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1977 repealed Article 131A, restoring the original balance of judicial power between the High Courts and the Supreme Court.
 
• Thus, Statement 2 is correct, while Statement 1 is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976:**

 
 
• Known as the "Mini-Constitution," this amendment introduced sweeping changes to the Constitution, increasing the power of the Central government.
 
• It added Article 131A, which centralized the adjudication of the validity of Central laws in the Supreme Court.
 
• Other changes included the addition of the Fundamental Duties (Part IVA) and the extension of the term of Lok Sabha and State Assemblies from 5 to 6 years.
 
 
 
• **43rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1977:**
 
 
• This amendment reversed many provisions of the 42nd Amendment, reflecting the shift in political power after the Emergency.
 
• It repealed Article 131A, restoring the High Courts' jurisdiction in deciding the validity of Central laws.
 
• The amendment also reinstated judicial review and reduced the power of the executive in certain areas.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review:**
 
 
• Judicial review is the power of the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of legislative and executive actions.
 
• In India, both the Supreme Court and High Courts have the power of judicial review under Articles 32 and 226 of the Constitution.
 
• It ensures the supremacy of the Constitution and protects fundamental rights.

question: Which Article empowers the Parliament to create laws on State List subjects under national interest?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 249**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 249 of the Indian Constitution** empowers Parliament to legislate on matters enumerated in the State List if the Rajya Sabha declares by a resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of its members present and voting that it is necessary in the national interest.
 
• This resolution remains valid for one year and can be extended by one year at a time through further resolutions.
 
• The laws made under Article 249 are only applicable as long as the resolution is in force and cease to have effect after six months once the resolution expires.
 
• The provision ensures that Parliament can address matters of national interest even in areas under the State List, maintaining the unity and integrity of the country.
 
• Examples of matters in the State List include public order, police, public health, and agriculture, among others.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 253:**

 
 
• Article 253 enables Parliament to make laws for implementing any treaty, agreement, or convention with other countries or for implementing decisions made at international conferences, associations, or other bodies.
 
• This article primarily deals with India's compliance with international obligations and agreements.
 
• It serves as a basis for enacting laws on matters that may fall in the State List if required for implementing international commitments.
 
 
 
• **Article 248:**
 
 
• Article 248 provides Parliament with exclusive power to make laws on matters not enumerated in the State List or the Concurrent List, referred to as the residuary powers of legislation.
 
• This article ensures that any subject not explicitly mentioned in the Constitution can still be legislated upon by Parliament.
 
• It reflects the flexibility of the Indian Constitution in adapting to emerging issues and challenges.
 
 
 
• **Article 254:**
 
 
• Article 254 resolves conflicts between laws made by Parliament and laws made by the State Legislature on matters in the Concurrent List.
 
• If there is inconsistency between the two, the law made by Parliament prevails, and the state law becomes void to the extent of the repugnancy.
 
• However, a state law on the same subject can prevail if it has received Presidential assent, unless Parliament later enacts a law inconsistent with it.

question: By which Constitutional Amendment was education transferred to the Concurrent List?
solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd Constitutional Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**, also known as the "Mini Constitution," brought significant changes to the Constitution of India.
 
• It transferred the subject of **education** from the State List to the Concurrent List, enabling both the Center and States to legislate on matters related to education.
 
• This amendment was enacted during the tenure of Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi** and reflected the growing importance of education in achieving national development goals.
 
• The 42nd Amendment introduced several other changes, including the incorporation of **Fundamental Duties** for citizens and provisions strengthening the central government.
 
• This shift to the Concurrent List was aimed at ensuring uniformity in educational policies across the country, promoting national integration, and addressing disparities in access to education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **24th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971:**
 
 
• It was enacted to affirm Parliament’s power to amend any part of the Constitution, including Fundamental Rights.
 
• This amendment was passed to counter the Supreme Court’s judgment in the Golaknath case (1967), which restricted Parliament’s power to amend Fundamental Rights.
 
• It also made it mandatory for the President to give assent to Constitutional Amendment Bills.
 
 
 
• **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978:**
 
 
• This amendment was enacted to reverse some provisions of the 42nd Amendment, particularly to restore the balance of powers between the central and state governments.
 
• It abolished the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right and made it a legal right under Article 300A.
 
• The amendment also strengthened the protection of Fundamental Rights during emergencies by limiting the scope of Article 352 (National Emergency).
 
 
 
• **61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988:**
 
 
• This amendment reduced the voting age for Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections from 21 years to 18 years.
 
• It sought to enhance youth participation in the electoral process and strengthen democratic governance in India.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Education in India**
 
 
• Education plays a crucial role in national development, fostering human resource growth and innovation.
 
• By including education in the Concurrent List, the 42nd Amendment ensured a collaborative approach between the Center and States for policy formulation and implementation.
 
• This move was instrumental in addressing disparities and ensuring equitable access to education across all regions of the country.
 
 

77:T

question:
Fill in the blanks:

Taxes on interstate trade are restricted by Article ____ unless Parliament otherwise provides.
solution:
The correct answer is __**286**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 286** of the Indian Constitution restricts the imposition of taxes on the sale or purchase of goods in interstate trade or commerce, except as provided by Parliament.
 
• This provision ensures uniformity in the taxation system across states, preventing double taxation or undue burden on interstate commerce.
 
• Parliament has the power to legislate and provide exceptions or conditions under which such taxes can be imposed, as per this article.
 
• The purpose of Article 286 is to facilitate free trade and commerce within the country while maintaining the authority of the central government over interstate trade taxation.
 
• This article is supported by the framework of the Goods and Services Tax (GST), which aims to create a unified tax system across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 269**

 
 
• Article 269 deals with taxes on the sale or purchase of goods and consignment of goods in the course of inter-state trade or commerce.
 
• It specifies that certain taxes shall be levied and collected by the Government of India but distributed among the states.
 
• It includes taxes on inter-state trade and transactions, such as consignment of goods.
 
 
 
• **Article 276**
 
 
• Article 276 allows the states to impose taxes on professions, trades, callings, and employment, subject to a maximum limit as determined by Parliament.
 
• This article ensures that states have the power to generate revenue through professional taxes, but it imposes an upper ceiling to prevent excessive taxation.
 
 
 
• **Article 294**
 
 
• Article 294 deals with the succession of property, assets, rights, and liabilities of the Union and the states after independence.
 
• It is not directly related to taxation but focuses on the distribution of assets and liabilities between the Union and state governments post-independence.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Interstate Trade Taxation**
 
 
• Interstate trade taxation is governed under the framework of the Constitution to ensure a seamless flow of goods and services across state boundaries.
 
• Articles like 286, 269, and related provisions ensure a balanced taxation system and prevent trade barriers in the country.
 
• The introduction of GST further streamlined interstate trade taxation by subsuming various state and central taxes into a unified system.

__ 

• **Article 275** of the Constitution of India provides for **Grants-in-Aid to States** from the Consolidated Fund of India to meet the costs of schemes of welfare and development. 

• The grants are primarily provided to assist the **states with special needs** or to ensure that **certain regions or areas within the states receive adequate funding** for their development needs. 

• This provision is used to provide financial assistance particularly to **economically weaker states**, ensuring balanced regional development. 

• These Grants-in-Aid are **recommended by the Finance Commission**, which is constituted under **Article 280** of the Indian Constitution. 

• The funds can be used for specific purposes or to address **structural imbalances in finances** at the state level. 

• **Hence, Article 275 plays a crucial role in ensuring federal equity** by enabling the central government to support states in need. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 

• **Article 280**: 
 

• **Finance Commission** is constituted under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution by the President of India every five years or earlier as necessary. 

• Its primary role is to make recommendations for the distribution of tax revenues between the **Union and the States**, and to propose Grants-in-Aid to states under **Article 275**. 

• The latest Finance Commission, the **15th Finance Commission**, chaired by **N.K. Singh**, submitted its report for the financial year 2021-26. 
 
 

• **Grants-in-Aid:** 
 

• The concept of Grants-in-Aid is significant in ensuring **cooperative federalism** in India. 

• These grants are classified into **Statutory Grants** (under Article 275) and **Discretionary Grants** (under Article 282). 

• The purpose of these grants is to address fiscal imbalances and ensure that states have sufficient resources to meet their developmental and administrative needs. 
 
 

• **Types of Grants:** 
 

• **Statutory Grants:** Recommended by the Finance Commission under Article 275. 

• **Discretionary Grants:** Provided under Article 282 for any public purpose as deemed fit by the central government. 

• **Special Purpose Grants:** These are given for specific development programs or projects. 
 
 

• **Important Examples of Grants-in-Aid:** 
 

• The **Special Category States** (like the North-Eastern States, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand) often receive such grants to address their unique geographical and economic challenges. 

• Assistance under centrally sponsored schemes like **Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan** and **National Health Mission** are also examples of how Grants-in-Aid are used. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 

• **Article 275 is a statutory provision** ensuring financial support to states, particularly those with disadvantages such as geographical isolation, backwardness, or other challenges. 

• It is distinct from **Article 282**, which allows the Union or State governments to make grants for any public purpose, even if it falls outside their legislative competence. 

• The recommendation of the Finance Commission under Article 275 ensures transparency and fairness in the allocation of funds to states. 

• Grants-in-Aid play a crucial role in the implementation of welfare schemes and programs in states with limited financial resources.

question: The Finance Commission is established under which Article of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 280**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Article 280** of the **Indian Constitution** provides for the establishment of the **Finance Commission of India**. 
• The Finance Commission is constituted by the **President of India** every five years or earlier as deemed necessary. 
• The primary role of the Finance Commission is to make recommendations on the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the **Union and the States**, and the allocation among states themselves. 
• The Finance Commission also advises on matters related to **grants-in-aid** to the states by the Union government from the Consolidated Fund of India. 
• The first Finance Commission was established in **1951** under the chairmanship of **K.C. Neogy**. 
• The recommendations of the Finance Commission are advisory in nature and are not binding on the government. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Constitutional Provisions for Finance Commission:** 
• **Article 280:** This article mandates the President to set up the Finance Commission and outlines its functions and responsibilities. 
• **Article 275:** Provides for grants-in-aid to needy states as determined by the Finance Commission. 
• **Article 282:** Allows both the Union and State governments to make discretionary grants for public purposes. 
• **Key Functions of Finance Commission:** 
• Distribution of net tax proceeds between the **Centre and the States**. 
• Determination of principles governing **grants-in-aid** to the states. 
• Recommendations regarding measures to improve the **financial position of states**. 
• Reviewing the fiscal policies of both the Union and the State governments to ensure financial stability. 
• **Significant Finance Commissions:** 
• **First Finance Commission (1951):** Chaired by **K.C. Neogy**, it laid the foundation for federal fiscal relations in India. 
• **14th Finance Commission (2015-2020):** Chaired by **Dr. Y.V. Reddy**, it recommended increasing the states' share of central taxes to **42%**. 
• **15th Finance Commission (2020-2025):** Chaired by **N.K. Singh**, it addressed fiscal challenges posed by the **COVID-19 pandemic**. 
• **Key Characteristics of Finance Commission:** 
• It is a **quasi-judicial body** established under the Constitution of India. 
• Its recommendations aim to **ensure fiscal equity** and financial stability in the country. 
• The commission is typically composed of a chairperson and four other members, with qualifications specified by Parliament. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Comparison of Articles:** 
• **Article 268:** Deals with duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States. 
• **Article 246:** Specifies the subject matter of laws made by Parliament and by the Legislatures of States. 
• **Article 365:** Deals with the effect of failure to comply with, or to give effect to, directions given by the Union government. 
• **Evolution of Finance Commission:** 
• The Finance Commission has played a pivotal role in balancing the financial relations between the Centre and the States since **India’s Independence**. 
• It ensures that states have adequate financial resources to carry out their responsibilities under the federal structure. 
• **Role in Governance:** The recommendations of the Finance Commission significantly influence budgetary allocations and fiscal policies in India.

question:
**Fill in the blanks:**

The collective responsibility clause for State CoMs appears in Article ___.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 164**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Article 164** of the **Constitution of India** deals with the appointment of the Chief Minister and other Ministers for the states. It also provides for the **principle of collective responsibility** of the Council of Ministers (CoM) to the Legislative Assembly of the state. 
• The clause states that the **Council of Ministers (CoM)** shall be collectively responsible to the **Legislative Assembly** of the state. This means that if any minister loses the confidence of the assembly, the entire CoM must resign. 
• This collective responsibility ensures accountability of the executive to the legislature and strengthens the principles of democracy. 
• The **Governor** of the state appoints the Chief Minister and, based on the Chief Minister's advice, appoints other ministers. 
• The tenure of the CoM is not fixed but is subject to the majority support in the Legislative Assembly. If a vote of no-confidence is passed, the CoM must resign. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Collective Responsibility:** 
• The principle of collective responsibility is a cornerstone of the parliamentary system of governance in India. It ensures that the CoM works as a cohesive unit, and all decisions are taken collectively, with no individual minister acting independently. 
• If any policy or action of the CoM is not approved by the legislature, the entire CoM must take responsibility and resign. 
• **Role of the Governor:** 
• The Governor acts as the constitutional head of the state, appointing the Chief Minister and other ministers based on the majority party or coalition in the Legislative Assembly. 
• The Governor has the power to dismiss the CoM if they lose the confidence of the Legislative Assembly. 
• **Difference Between Individual and Collective Responsibility:** 
• **Individual Responsibility:** Ministers are individually responsible for their respective departments and can be asked to resign for their personal failures. 
• **Collective Responsibility:** The CoM as a whole is responsible for its policies and decisions. If the legislature rejects any policy or action, the entire CoM must resign. 
• **Examples of Collective Responsibility in India:** 
• During the **Emergency (1975-77)**, the principle of collective responsibility was questioned due to the centralization of power with the Prime Minister. 
• In various instances, if a minister is involved in a controversy or scandal, the entire CoM may face the consequences if the Legislative Assembly loses confidence in them. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Article 163 vs. Article 164:** 
• **Article 163:** Deals with the discretionary powers of the Governor in certain situations. 
• **Article 164:** Focuses on the composition, tenure, and collective responsibility of the CoM to the Legislative Assembly. 
• **Comparison with Union Council of Ministers:** 
• The principle of collective responsibility is also applicable to the Union CoM under **Article 75** of the Constitution. 
• The Union CoM is collectively responsible to the **Lok Sabha**, whereas the State CoM is responsible to the **Legislative Assembly**. </ul

question: Which of the following articles from Directive Principles of state policy mentions about organization of Village Panchayats?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 40**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 40 of the Indian Constitution directs the State to organize Village Panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.
 
• This article is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), which are guidelines for the framing of laws by the government.
 
• Village Panchayats are a form of decentralized government where each village is responsible for its own affairs, promoting local self-governance.
 
• The inclusion of Village Panchayats in the Constitution reflects the importance of grassroots democracy and the empowerment of local communities in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are enumerated in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• DPSP serve as guidelines for the central and state governments of India, which are intended to be kept in mind while framing laws and policies.
 
• Though not enforceable by any court, these principles are considered fundamental in the governance of the country and aim to create social and economic conditions under which citizens can lead a good life.
 
• Examples of DPSP include securing a living wage, ensuring equal pay for equal work, promoting the health and strength of workers, and fostering respect for international law and treaty obligations.
 
 
 
• **Village Panchayats:**
 
 
• Village Panchayats are part of the Panchayati Raj system in India, which is a three-tier system of local self-government in rural areas.
 
• The three tiers include the Village Panchayat at the village level, the Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and the Zila Parishad at the district level.
 
• The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 provided a constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions and brought them under the purview of the justiciable part of the Constitution.
 
• This amendment aimed at creating a uniform structure of Panchayati Raj throughout India and ensuring more powers and responsibilities to these bodies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 43** of the Indian Constitution is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP).
 
• It states that **'The State shall endeavour to promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas'**.
 
• The objective of this article is to promote economic growth and self-sufficiency in rural areas.
 
• It aims to provide economic opportunities and employment in rural areas through the promotion of small-scale industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• The DPSP are guidelines or principles given to the federal institutes governing the state of India, to be kept in consideration while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are enshrined in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These principles are aimed at ensuring social and economic democracy through a welfare state.
 
• While they are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation, they are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
 
 
• **Cottage Industries**
 
 
• Cottage industries are small-scale, decentralized manufacturing businesses often operated out of a home rather than a purpose-built facility.
 
• They typically involve the production of handmade goods and are labor-intensive.
 
• These industries play a vital role in the economy by providing employment and promoting traditional crafts.
 
• In rural areas, cottage industries help in reducing unemployment and migration to urban areas by providing local employment opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Rural Development**
 
 
• Rural development involves improving the quality of life and economic well-being of people living in rural areas, often relatively isolated and sparsely populated areas.
 
• It focuses on the development of infrastructure, education, healthcare, and employment opportunities.
 
• Promoting cottage industries is one way to achieve rural development by utilizing local resources and skills.
 
• Government policies and programs often aim to support rural development through various schemes and initiatives.

question: __________ Directive principles of State Policy were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Four__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

**Four Directive** Principles of State Policy were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976.

__
 
• Article 39A – Equal justice and free legal aid.
 
• Article 43A – Participation of workers in the management of industries.
 
• Article 48A – Protection and improvement of the environment and safeguarding of forests and wildlife.
 
• Article 39(f) – Protection of children and youth from exploitation and moral and material abandonment (added to modify Article 39).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**

 
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines or principles given to the federal institutes governing the state of India, to be kept in consideration while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are enumerated in Part IV of the Constitution from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• The principles aim to create social and economic conditions under which the citizens can lead a good life.
 
• They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but the principles laid down are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
 
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**
 
 
• Also known as the "Mini-Constitution", this amendment brought about significant changes to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It attempted to reduce the powers of the Supreme Court and High Courts and gave Parliament unlimited power to amend the Constitution, among other changes.
 
• It also added ten Fundamental Duties to the Constitution.
 
• Many of its provisions were later repealed by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978.

question: What is the primary objective of a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) in India?

options.text: To establish a common criminal law for all citizens.
To unify direct and indirect tax laws.
To provide a common set of personal laws for all citizens, irrespective of religion.
To standardize administrative procedures across all states.

solution:
The correct answer is __**To provide a common set of personal laws for all citizens, irrespective of religion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Uniform Civil Code (UCC) aims to replace personal laws based on the customs and scriptures of various religious communities with a common set of laws governing marriage, divorce, inheritance, and adoption for all citizens of India.
 
• The UCC is enshrined as a directive principle under Article 44 of the Indian Constitution, which calls for the State to endeavor to secure a uniform civil code for all citizens.
 
• It seeks to ensure equality and secularism by eliminating discriminatory practices embedded in personal laws based on religion or gender.
 
• The implementation of UCC is viewed as a significant step toward achieving gender justice and promoting national integration by ensuring uniformity in legal matters across all communities.
 
• The Supreme Court of India has, on several occasions, emphasized the need for a Uniform Civil Code to ensure equality and uniformity in personal laws.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Classification of **DPSPs** (Philosophical Basis):

 
 
• Socialistic Principles: Aim for socio-economic justice, reducing inequality (e.g., equal pay, right to work).
 
• Gandhian Principles: Promote Gandhian ideals (e.g., village panchayats, cow protection, cottage industries).
 
• Liberal-Intellectual Principles: Advocate for individual freedoms and state action (e.g., uniform civil code, separation of judiciary from executive).

question: Article 50 is part of which section of the Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Directive Principles of State Policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 50 of the Indian Constitution falls under the **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP)**, which are outlined in Part IV of the Constitution (Articles 36-51).
 
• It specifically states, "**The State shall take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State**."
 
• The purpose of Article 50 is to maintain the independence of the judiciary, a vital component of a democratic system, and to ensure the impartiality of justice.
 
• DPSPs, including Article 50, are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts, but they act as guiding principles for the State to establish policies and laws.
 
• Article 50 has played a crucial role in the Indian judicial system by emphasizing the doctrine of separation of powers between the judiciary and the executive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• Fundamental Duties are listed under Part IVA of the Indian Constitution (Article 51A).
 
• They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• These duties serve as moral obligations for citizens to promote a spirit of patriotism and uphold the unity of the nation.
 
• Examples include abiding by the Constitution, respecting the national flag and anthem, protecting the environment, and promoting harmony.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution (Articles 12-35).
 
• They guarantee basic rights to all citizens, essential for their development and protection against state actions.
 
• Key Fundamental Rights include the Right to Equality (Article 14-18), Right to Freedom (Article 19-22), and Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32).
 
• These rights are justiciable, meaning individuals can approach the courts if their rights are violated.
 
 
 
• **Preamble:**
 
 
• The Preamble serves as the introductory statement of the Indian Constitution, outlining its objectives and philosophy.
 
• It declares India as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, and Democratic Republic and ensures Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity to all its citizens.
 
• Although not enforceable in a court of law, the Preamble is considered a guiding light for interpreting the Constitution.
