question: The ______ of every state unfurls the flag in its capital on the Republic Day.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of a state in India, appointed by the President of India.
 
• On Republic Day, the Governor unfurls the national flag at the state capital as part of the official celebration.
 
• The Governor's role is to represent the central government in the state and act according to the advice of the state's Council of Ministers.
 
• The Governor has various powers and functions including legislative, executive, and discretionary powers as outlined in the Constitution of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Republic Day**

 
 
• Republic Day in India is celebrated on January 26th every year to honor the date on which the Constitution of India came into effect in 1950.
 
• It marks the transition of India from a British Dominion to a republic.
 
• The day is celebrated with grand parades in the national capital, New Delhi, and state capitals, showcasing India's defense capability, cultural and social heritage.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Governor**
 
 
• The Governor is the nominal executive head of the state, functioning as a representative of the President of India.
 
• The Governor's powers and duties include summoning and proroguing the state legislature, granting pardons, and appointing the Chief Minister.
 
• Governors can also reserve bills passed by the state legislature for the President's consideration.
 
 
 
• **Chief Minister**
 
 
• The Chief Minister is the head of the government in a state and is responsible for running the state administration.
 
• They are appointed by the Governor and are usually the leader of the majority party in the state legislature.
 
• The Chief Minister advises the Governor on various matters related to the state's governance.

question: The Upper House of a State Legislature is known as the _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vidhan Parishad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Vidhan Parishad** is the Upper House of the State Legislature in India.
 
• It is similar to the Rajya Sabha, which is the Upper House of the Parliament of India.
 
• Not all states in India have a Vidhan Parishad; it exists only in a few states like Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.
 
• Members of the Vidhan Parishad are not directly elected by the public; they are elected by members of the Legislative Assembly, graduates, teachers, and local authority members.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajya Sabha**

 
 
• The Rajya Sabha is the Upper House of the Parliament of India.
 
• It represents the states and union territories of India.
 
• Members of the Rajya Sabha are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies, and by the members of the Electoral college for Union Territories, using a single transferable vote system.
 
• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and is not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every two years.
 
 
 
• **Lok Sabha**
 
 
• The Lok Sabha is the Lower House of the Parliament of India.
 
• Members of the Lok Sabha are directly elected by the people of India through general elections held every five years.
 
• The Lok Sabha is also known as the House of the People.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the law-making process in India.
 
 
 
• **Vidhan Sabha**
 
 
• The Vidhan Sabha is the Lower House of the State Legislature in India.
 
• Members of the Vidhan Sabha are directly elected by the people of the respective states through general elections held every five years.
 
• The Vidhan Sabha is also known as the Legislative Assembly.
 
• It is responsible for making laws on matters listed in the State List and Concurrent List in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.

question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the political parties in India?

options.text: A political party symbol is assigned by the President of India.
India has a multi-party system classified as national, state or regional level.
All parties are registered with the Supreme Court of India.
Status of party is accorded by the Parliament.

solution:
The correct answer is __**India has a multi-party system classified as national, state or regional level.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India follows a multi-party system where multiple political parties can exist and participate in elections.
 
• Political parties in India are classified into national, state or regional level based on their performance and influence.
 
• National parties are those that have influence over a larger part of India, while state or regional parties have influence limited to specific states or regions.
 
• This classification helps in managing the democratic process and ensuring representation at both the national and state levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI)**

 
 
• The Election Commission of India is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.
 
• It administers elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies, as well as the offices of the President and Vice President in the country.
 
• The ECI ensures free and fair elections in India.
 
 
 
• **Registration of Political Parties**
 
 
• Political parties in India are registered with the Election Commission of India under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
 
• Registration with the ECI is a precondition for a political party to be recognized as a national or state party.
 
 
 
• **Recognition of Political Parties**
 
 
• The status of a political party, whether national or state, is determined based on its performance in elections.
 
• Criteria for recognition include the number of seats won in elections and the percentage of votes obtained.
 
 
 
• **Symbols of Political Parties**
 
 
• The Election Commission of India assigns symbols to political parties to help voters identify them during elections.
 
• Symbols play a significant role in the election process, especially for illiterate voters who may not recognize party names.

question: Sports Authority of India comes under which ministry?

Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sports Authority of India (SAI) operates under the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, Government of India.
 
• SAI was established in **1984** to promote sports and oversee the development of sports facilities and training programs in India.
 
• It is responsible for the **preparation of athletes for major international events** such as the Olympics, Asian Games, and Commonwealth Games.
 
• SAI also manages various **sports training centers and academies** across the country, providing infrastructure, coaching, and other support to budding sportspersons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Education:**

 
 
• The Ministry of Education is responsible for the development and implementation of educational policies and programs in India.
 
• It oversees various institutions such as the University Grants Commission (UGC), National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT), and others.
 
• The Ministry's focus is on improving the quality of education and ensuring access to education for all.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment:**
 
 
• This ministry focuses on the welfare, social justice, and empowerment of disadvantaged and marginalized sections of society.
 
• It implements schemes and policies for the upliftment of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, Divyangjan (Persons with Disabilities), and other vulnerable groups.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare:**
 
 
• The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare is responsible for the formulation and implementation of health policies and programs in India.
 
• It aims to ensure the accessibility and affordability of quality healthcare for all citizens.
 
• It manages various national health schemes like Ayushman Bharat, National Health Mission, and others.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports:**
 
 
• The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports is dedicated to the development and promotion of sports and youth welfare in India.
 
• It formulates policies and programs to nurture young talent in sports and provides necessary infrastructure and training facilities.
 
• It also organizes national and international sports events and collaborates with various sports bodies and organizations.

question: Articles 52 to 78 in Part V of the Indian Constitution deal with ________.

The correct answer is __**Union Executive**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Articles 52 to 78 in Part V of the Indian Constitution deal with the Union Executive.
 
• The Union Executive consists of the President, the Vice-President, the Prime Minister, the Council of Ministers, and the Attorney General of India.
 
• The President of India is the head of the Union Executive and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• Articles 52 to 62 deal with the President, Articles 63 to 71 deal with the Vice-President, Articles 74 and 75 deal with the Council of Ministers, and Articles 76 and 78 deal with the Attorney General of India and the duties of the Prime Minister.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Finance Commission of India**

 
 
• The Finance Commission is a constitutional body for the purpose of allocation of certain revenue resources between the Union and the State Governments.
 
• It was established under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Finance Commission is appointed every five years and consists of a chairman and four other members.
 
 
 
• **Amendment of the Constitution**
 
 
• The procedure for the amendment of the Constitution is laid down in Article 368 in Part XX of the Constitution.
 
• It provides for a flexible procedure for the amendment to address the changing needs and circumstances of the country.
 
• An amendment can be initiated only by the introduction of a Bill in either House of Parliament and must be passed by a special majority.
 
 
 
• **National Emergency**
 
 
• National emergency provisions are contained in Article 352 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• A National Emergency can be declared on the grounds of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• During a National Emergency, the federal structure of the country changes to a unitary one, and the central government becomes more powerful.

question: Articles 214 to 231 in Part VI of the Indian Constitution deal with the ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**High Courts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Articles 214 to 231 in Part VI of the Indian Constitution deal with the **establishment and constitution of the High Courts.**
 
• A High Court is the principal civil court of original jurisdiction in a state.
 
• Each state of India is provided with a High Court which has its own jurisdiction and powers as defined under the Constitution.
 
• The High Courts have the authority to issue writs for the enforcement of the Fundamental Rights of citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High Courts**

 
 
• High Courts are the highest courts in a state in India, and each state has its own High Court.
 
• High Courts have jurisdiction over all subordinate courts within their territory.
 
• They have the power to hear appeals and to issue writs to enforce Fundamental Rights.
 
• The judges of the High Courts are appointed by the President of India.
 
 
 
• **District Courts**
 
 
• District Courts are established by the state governments of India for every district or for one or more districts together taking into account the number of cases and population distribution.
 
• They administer justice at the district level and are subordinate to the High Court of the respective state.
 
 
 
• **Subordinate Courts**
 
 
• Subordinate Courts are the lower courts under the District Courts, which deal with civil, criminal, and other cases at a more local level.
 
• They operate under the supervision and control of the District Court.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court**
 
 
• The Supreme Court of India is the highest judicial forum and final court of appeal as established by Part V, Chapter IV of the Constitution of India.
 
• It comprises the Chief Justice of India and a number of other judges appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Supreme Court has extensive original, appellate, and advisory jurisdictions.

question: The number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a state shall NOT be less than _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**12**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• The number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a state shall not be less than **12**.

• This provision is part of the 91st Amendment Act of 2003 to the Constitution of India.

• The Amendment was introduced to avoid jumbo ministries and ensure efficient governance.

• The maximum number of ministers in a state, including the Chief Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **91st Amendment Act of 2003**

• The 91st Amendment Act was enacted to curb defections and to limit the size of the Council of Ministers to prevent the formation of oversized cabinets.

• It is one of the key measures to ensure stability in the legislative assembly by preventing political horse-trading and defection.

• The Amendment mandates that a person who is disqualified under the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law) from being a member of the legislature shall also be disqualified from being appointed as a minister or holding any remunerative political post.

• This amendment also ensures that the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister in the Central Government, shall not exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Parliament in the Lok Sabha.

• **Anti-Defection Law (Tenth Schedule)**

• The anti-defection law was introduced by the 52nd Amendment Act of 1985 and later strengthened by the 91st Amendment Act of 2003.

• The main objective of the law is to combat the evil of political defections by elected members.

• According to this law, if a member of a house belonging to a political party voluntarily gives up the membership of his party or votes (or abstains from voting) contrary to the directions issued by his party, he can be disqualified from being a member of the house.

• The decision on disqualification questions on the ground of defection is referred to the Chairman or the Speaker of such House and their decision is final.

question: Which Article deals with the election of the President?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 54**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 54 of the Indian Constitution deals with the election of the President of India.
 
• The President is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories.
 
• The process of election is conducted by the Election Commission of India.
 
• The election is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 72:**

 
 
• Article 72 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment or to suspend, remit or commute the sentence of any person convicted of any offense.
 
• This power can be exercised in all cases where the punishment or sentence is by a court-martial, in cases where the punishment or sentence is for an offense against any law relating to a matter to which the executive power of the Union extends, and in all cases where the sentence is a sentence of death.
 
 
 
• **Article 54:**
 
 
• Article 54 deals with the election of the President.
 
• The President is elected by an electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and Legislative Assemblies of States and Union territories.
 
• The election is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
 
 
 
• **Article 74:**
 
 
• Article 74 of the Indian Constitution states that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President.
 
• The President shall, in the exercise of his functions, act in accordance with such advice.
 
 
 
• **Article 66:**
 
 
• Article 66 deals with the election of the Vice-President of India.
 
• The Vice-President is elected by the members of an electoral college consisting of the members of both Houses of Parliament.
 
• The election is held in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

• These articles cover various aspects such as the composition of Parliament, the powers, and functions of its members, and the procedures for conducting parliamentary business.

• **Article 36 to 51**

question: Which of the following Articles and Parts of the Indian Constitution deal with the State Legislature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 168 to 212 in Part VI**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Articles 168 to 212 in Part VI of the Indian Constitution deal with the State Legislature.
 
• The State Legislature consists of the Governor and one or two Houses, as the case may be.
 
• In some states, the legislature is bicameral, consisting of the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council, while in others, it is unicameral, consisting only of the Legislative Assembly.
 
• These articles lay down the composition, duration, and functions of the State Legislatures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 168:** This article specifies the composition of the State Legislature, which can be either unicameral (with only the Legislative Assembly) or bicameral (with both the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council).
 
• **Article 170:** This article deals with the composition of the Legislative Assemblies, including the number of seats and the delimitation of constituencies.
 
• **Article 171:** This article outlines the composition of the Legislative Councils, including the method of election and nomination of members.
 
• **Article 174:** This article mandates that the Governor shall summon the Legislature at least once every six months.
 
• **Article 176:** This article requires the Governor to address the Legislature at the commencement of the first session after each general election and at the commencement of the first session of each year.
 
• **Article 178:** This article provides for the election of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly.
 
• **Article 194:** This article grants certain privileges and immunities to the members of the State Legislature.
 
• **Article 212:** This article states that the validity of any proceedings in the Legislature of a state shall not be called in question on the ground of any alleged irregularity of procedure.

__
 
• **Part V** of the Indian Constitution is titled **"The Union"**.
 
• It encompasses provisions related to the **President**, the **Vice-President**, the **Council of Ministers**, and the **Parliament**.
 
• Articles **52 to 151** deal with the executive, legislative, and administrative functions of the Union Government.
 
• The election of the **Vice President of India** is specifically covered under **Articles 63 to 71** in Part V of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part IV**

 
 
• Part IV of the Indian Constitution is titled **"Directive Principles of State Policy"**.
 
• It contains **Articles 36 to 51**.
 
• These articles guide the State in making laws and policies to establish a just society in the country.
 
• However, they are **non-justiciable**, meaning they are not enforceable by any court.
 
 
 
• **Part III**
 
 
• Part III of the Indian Constitution is titled **"Fundamental Rights"**.
 
• It contains **Articles 12 to 35**.
 
• These articles guarantee essential rights such as equality, freedom, and protection against exploitation.
 
• These rights are **justiciable**, meaning they can be enforced by the courts.
 
 
 
• **Part VI**
 
 
• Part VI of the Indian Constitution is titled **"The States"**.
 
• It contains **Articles 152 to 237**.

question: Which writ is issued by a high court or supreme court when a lower court has considered a case going beyond its jurisdiction?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Prohibition**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Prohibition** is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to prevent it from exceeding its jurisdiction or usurping a jurisdiction that it does not possess.
 
• This writ is used to control the actions of lower courts and ensure that they do not overstep their boundaries.
 
• The writ of prohibition directs inactivity, ordering the lower court or tribunal to stop the proceedings in a case that falls outside its jurisdiction.
 
• It is a form of judicial control over the lower courts by the higher courts like the High Courts and the Supreme Court in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quo Warranto**

 
 
• This writ is issued to inquire into the legality of a claim of a person to a public office. It restrains a person from acting in a public office to which they are not entitled.
 
• The purpose is to prevent illegal usurpation of public office by an individual.
 
 
 
• **Habeas Corpus**
 
 
• This writ is issued to produce a person who has been detained, whether in prison or private custody, before a court and to release that person if such detention is found illegal.
 
• The primary objective is to ensure the personal liberty of citizens against unlawful detention.
 
 
 
• **Certiorari**
 
 
• This writ is issued by a higher court to a lower court or tribunal to transfer a case pending with the latter to itself or to quash the order of the latter in a case.
 
• It is issued on grounds of excess of jurisdiction or lack of jurisdiction or error of law apparent on the face of the record.

question: Who among the following was the shortest-serving Prime Minister of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gulzarilal Nanda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gulzarilal Nanda served as the acting Prime Minister of India twice, each time for a short period.
 
• His first term was from 27th May 1964 to 9th June 1964, following the death of Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• His second term was from 11th January 1966 to 24th January 1966, following the death of Lal Bahadur Shastri.
 
• Both terms combined make him the shortest-serving Prime Minister of India, with a total of 26 days in office.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prime Minister of India**

 
 
• The Prime Minister of India is the head of government and is appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Prime Minister leads the executive branch of the Government of India and is the chief advisor to the President.
 
• The Prime Minister also heads the Council of Ministers and is responsible for running the government and implementing policies.
 
 
 
• **Acting Prime Minister**
 
 
• An Acting Prime Minister is appointed when the incumbent Prime Minister is temporarily unable to perform duties, often due to death or resignation.
 
• Gulzarilal Nanda served as Acting Prime Minister twice under these circumstances.
 
 
 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru**
 
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India, serving from 1947 until his death in 1964.
 
• His death led to Gulzarilal Nanda's first term as Acting Prime Minister.
 
 
 
• **Lal Bahadur Shastri**
 
 
• Lal Bahadur Shastri was the second Prime Minister of India, serving from 1964 until his death in 1966.
 
• His death led to Gulzarilal Nanda's second term as Acting Prime Minister.

question:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:

a. Eastern Zonal Council meeting 2022

b. States Reorganisation Act passed

c. First Central Zonal Council meeting
solution:
The correct answer is __**b-c-a**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **States Reorganisation Act** was passed in **1956**. It restructured India's states and territories, marking a significant moment in the political and administrative history of the country.
 
• The **First Central Zonal Council meeting** was held after the creation of zonal councils, which were established following the **States Reorganisation Act**. These councils aimed to promote cooperation and coordination between states.
 
• The **Eastern Zonal Council meeting in 2022** occurred significantly later and focused on contemporary issues related to the states in the eastern region of India.
 
• The chronological order of the events is therefore: **States Reorganisation Act passed (b)**, followed by the **First Central Zonal Council meeting (c)**, and finally the **Eastern Zonal Council meeting in 2022 (a)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **States Reorganisation Act**__

 __
 
• The **States Reorganisation Act, 1956** was a major reform that reorganized the boundaries of Indian states and territories based on linguistic lines.
 
• It led to the creation of **14 states** and **6 union territories**.
 
• This Act also provided the basis for the establishment of **Zonal Councils** under the **States Reorganisation Commission**.
 
 
 
• **Zonal Councils**__
 __
 
• The **Zonal Councils** were set up to foster interstate cooperation and coordination, as recommended by the **States Reorganisation Commission**.
 
• They are statutory bodies, established under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**.
 
• There are **five Zonal Councils**: Northern, Southern, Eastern, Western, and Central Zonal Councils.
 
• The **Central Zonal Council** includes states like Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Chhattisgarh.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Zonal Council**__
 
 
• The **Eastern Zonal Council** comprises the states of **West Bengal, Odisha, Bihar, and Jharkhand**.
 
• It focuses on issues like **economic and social development, border disputes, and security concerns** specific to the eastern region of India.
 
• The **2022 meeting of the Eastern Zonal Council** aimed at resolving issues related to connectivity, infrastructure, and law and order in the eastern states.

solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Anglo-Indian representation in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies** was provided under **Article 331 and Article 333** of the Indian Constitution, respectively.
 
• The **104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019**, abolished the **provision for the nomination of Anglo-Indian members** to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies. This amendment came into effect on **January 25, 2020**.
 
• The provision for Anglo-Indian representation was initially introduced to provide political representation to a small minority community in India. However, the government reasoned that the Anglo-Indian population had significantly decreased, and there was no longer a need for this special representation.
 
• **Governors of states** were earlier empowered to nominate **one Anglo-Indian member** to the State Legislative Assemblies under Article 333, but this provision was removed by the **104th Amendment.**
 
• Statements in the question:
 
 
• Statement 1: "The Governor still nominates one Anglo-Indian member to the Assembly." – **Incorrect**, as this provision was abolished by the 104th Constitutional Amendment.
 
• Statement 2: "The provision was abolished by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment." – **Incorrect**, as the 42nd Amendment (1976) did not deal with Anglo-Indian representation.
 
• Statement 3: "The provision was abolished by the 104th Constitutional Amendment." – **Correct**.
 
• Statement 4: "Anglo-Indian members are elected through proportional representation." – **Incorrect**, as they were nominated and not elected.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Anglo-Indian Community:**

 
 
• Anglo-Indians are a small community in India that originated during the British colonial period, with mixed Indian and European ancestry.
 
• The community played an important role in India's administration, railways, and education system during British rule.
 
 
 
• **104th Constitutional Amendment Act:**
 
 
• It abolished the special representation of Anglo-Indians in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
 
• It also extended the reservation for Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies for another 10 years.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Anglo-Indian representation was initially a safeguard for a minority community to voice their concerns in legislative bodies.
 
• Over time, with the decline in the population of Anglo-Indians and their assimilation into mainstream society, this provision was deemed unnecessary.
 
 
 
• **Other Reserved Categories in India:**
 
 
• Seats are reserved for **Scheduled Castes (SC)** and **Scheduled Tribes (ST)** in legislative bodies under **Articles 330 and 332** of the Constitution.
 
• These reservations aim to ensure the political representation of historically disadvantaged communities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act** (1976) is often referred to as the "Mini-Constitution" because it introduced significant changes but did not address Anglo-Indian representation.
 
• The **104th Constitutional Amendment** was passed in December 2019 and came into effect on **January 25, 2020**.
 
• Currently, no seats are reserved for Anglo-Indians in either the Lok Sabha or State Legislative Assemblies.
 
• This amendment highlights the dynamic nature of the Constitution, which adapts to social and demographic changes.

__
 
• The Governor of a state in India is **appointed by the President of India** under Article 155 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Governor acts as the **nominal head of the state**, while the real executive powers lie with the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers.
 
• The Governor serves a term of **5 years**, but they hold office at the pleasure of the President, meaning they can be removed earlier.
 
• The appointment process ensures that the Governor is a representative of the central government in the state and maintains coordination between the center and state.
 
• The role of the Governor includes duties such as granting assent to bills, appointing the Chief Minister, and overseeing the formation of the state government after elections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Election Commission: Chief Election Commissioner and other Commissioners.
 
• Union Public Service Commission (UPSC): Chairman and Members.
 
• Attorney General of India: The government's chief legal advisor.
 
• Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG): Guardian of public finances.
 
• Governors: Appointed for each state.

question:
**Consider the following statements: **

1. The Governor can dissolve the State Legislative Assembly.

2. The President has no such power regarding the Lok Sabha. Which of the above is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Governor of a state has the constitutional authority to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly under Article 174(2)(b) of the Indian Constitution, usually on the advice of the Chief Minister or in certain circumstances like a no-confidence motion.
 
• The President of India, on the other hand, has the power to dissolve the Lok Sabha under Article 85(2)(b) of the Indian Constitution. Therefore, Statement 2 is incorrect.
 
• The dissolution of the State Legislative Assembly is an executive action of the Governor and is generally done to pave the way for fresh elections.
 
• The President's power to dissolve the Lok Sabha is exercised on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• Thus, only Statement 1 is correct, as the Governor has the power to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor's Role and Powers:**

 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of the state and acts on the advice of the state's Chief Minister and Council of Ministers.
 
• The Governor can summon, prorogue, or dissolve the State Legislative Assembly under Article 174 of the Constitution.
 
• In extraordinary circumstances (e.g., no-confidence motion passed), the Governor can dissolve the assembly without the advice of the Chief Minister, but this is subject to judicial review.
 
 
 
• **President's Power to Dissolve Lok Sabha:**
 
 
• The President of India can dissolve the Lok Sabha under Article 85(2)(b) of the Constitution.
 
• This power is exercised on the advice of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers.
 
• The dissolution of the Lok Sabha paves the way for general elections in the country.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Dissolution and Prorogation:**
 
 
• **Dissolution:** Refers to the complete termination of the current House of Parliament or State Legislative Assembly. It necessitates fresh elections.
 
• **Prorogation:** Refers to the termination of a session of the House without dissolving it. It simply ends the proceedings for the session.

question:
Arrange the following steps in the correct legislative process for the passage of a Money Bill in India:

A) Introduction of Money Bill in Lok Sabha

B) Passage in Lok Sabha

C) Transmission to Rajya Sabha

D) Presentation for President's assent
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: A-B-C-D**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In India, a Money Bill is exclusively introduced in the Lok Sabha, as per Article 110 of the Constitution of India.
 
• Once introduced, the Money Bill must be passed by the Lok Sabha, where the majority support is required.
 
• After passage in the Lok Sabha, the bill is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha for its recommendations, but the Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject the bill; it can only suggest changes within 14 days.
 
• Finally, the bill is presented to the President of India for his/her assent, which is mandatory for the bill to become a law.
 
• The process ensures that the Lok Sabha, as the house of elected representatives, has the final say in matters related to financial legislation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Important Facts about Money Bills:**

 
 
• A bill is considered a Money Bill if it deals with taxation, borrowing of money by the government, appropriation of money out of the Consolidated Fund of India, or any matter incidental to these issues.
 
• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha has the final authority to decide whether a bill is a Money Bill or not.
 
• The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a Money Bill but can suggest recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may choose to accept or reject.
 
• If the Rajya Sabha does not return the Money Bill within 14 days, it is deemed to have been passed by both houses in the form originally passed by the Lok Sabha.

question:
**Read the below statement:**

1. Solicitor General of India is appointed by the president of India.

2. A candidate contesting for the post of the President of India is required to make a security deposit of ₹15,000.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only statement 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **security deposit of ₹15,000** is mandatory for candidates contesting the election for the President of India, as per **Article 58 of the Constitution of India** and the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952.
 
• The deposit is forfeited if the candidate fails to secure at least one-sixth of the votes cast in the election.
 
• The security deposit ensures that only serious candidates participate in the election process.
 
• The election of the President of India is conducted by an electoral college consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies of States and Union Territories.
 
• As per the rules, the nomination paper must be supported by at least **50 proposers and 50 seconders** to ensure legitimacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Statement 1: Solicitor General of India is appointed by the president of India**

 
 
• The Solicitor General of India is the **second-highest law officer** in the country after the Attorney General of India.
 
• Unlike the Attorney General, the Solicitor General is not appointed directly by the President of India. Instead, the appointment is made by the **Union Government**, specifically by the Ministry of Law and Justice.
 
• The Solicitor General assists the Attorney General in performing legal duties and advises the government on legal matters.
 
• Therefore, **Statement 1 is incorrect**.
 
 
 
• **Concept of Presidential Elections in India:**
 
 
• The President is elected by an electoral college through a proportional representation system using a single transferable vote.
 
• Every member of the electoral college casts their vote, and the candidate receiving the highest number of votes is elected.
 
• The process is governed by the provisions in **Articles 52 to 62** of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Other Important Facts:**
 
 
• The President of India serves a term of five years and can be re-elected.
 
• The eligibility criteria for candidates contesting the Presidential elections include being a citizen of India, at least 35 years old, and qualified to be a member of the Lok Sabha.
 
• In case of vacancy, the election must be held within six months.

question: How are Money Bills handled in both Houses of Parliament and State Legislatures with bicameralism under the Constitution?

options.text: Rajya Sabha must approve Money Bills within 14 days
In States, the Legislative Council can amend a Money Bill within 14 days
Both Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils have equal powers on Money Bills
Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils can only make recommendations within 14 days

solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils can only make recommendations within 14 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under Article 110 of the Indian Constitution, a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha and not in the Rajya Sabha.
 
• Once the Lok Sabha passes a Money Bill, it is sent to the Rajya Sabha for its recommendations, but the Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject it.
 
• The Rajya Sabha must return the Money Bill to the Lok Sabha with or without recommendations within a period of 14 days. If not returned within this period, the Bill is deemed passed by both Houses of Parliament.
 
• In the case of State Legislatures with bicameralism, the Legislative Council can only make recommendations to the Legislative Assembly on Money Bills and must return the Bill within 14 days.
 
• The powers of the Rajya Sabha and the Legislative Councils on Money Bills are limited to recommendations, and the final decision rests with the Lok Sabha and the Legislative Assembly, respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A Money Bill deals exclusively with matters listed in Article 110(1) of the Constitution, such as taxation, borrowing, expenditure, and matters incidental to these.
 
• The distinction between Money Bills and other financial Bills is significant because it limits the role of the Rajya Sabha and Legislative Councils in the legislative process.
 
• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha or the Legislative Assembly is the final authority to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill.

question:
**Consider the following statements:**

1. Supreme Court can transfer cases from one High Court to another.

2. Article 139A was introduced by the 42nd Amendment.

Which of the above is/are **correct?**
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1: Supreme Court can transfer cases from one High Court to another** – Article 139A of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to transfer cases involving the same or substantially the same question of law from one High Court to another to ensure uniformity in decisions.
 
• This provision is aimed at eliminating conflicting judgments by different High Courts on the same legal matter, thereby ensuring consistency in the interpretation of laws across the country.
 
• **Statement 2: Article 139A was introduced by the 42nd Amendment** – The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added Article 139A to the Indian Constitution. This amendment is often referred to as the "mini-Constitution" due to the extensive changes it introduced.
 
• Article 139A allows the Supreme Court to withdraw cases from one or more High Courts if it feels that these cases involve a substantial question of law of general importance.
 
• Both statements are correct, as Article 139A was indeed introduced by the 42nd Amendment, and it authorizes the Supreme Court to transfer cases between High Courts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment of 1976:**

 
 
• Known as the "mini-Constitution," this amendment brought significant changes to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It added several articles, including Article 139A, and amended many existing provisions to strengthen the central government's powers.
 
• Key changes included the addition of the Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) and the insertion of the words "Socialist," "Secular," and "Integrity" into the Preamble.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court’s Powers under Article 139A:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court has the authority to transfer cases between High Courts or withdraw cases from High Courts to itself if substantial questions of law are involved.
 
• This provision ensures uniformity in the interpretation of laws across different jurisdictions in India.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Transfers under Article 139A:**
 
 
• This article is critical for maintaining judicial discipline and consistency in legal interpretations by higher judiciary bodies.
 
• Such transfers are often considered in cases involving constitutional interpretation or significant questions of national importance.
 
 
 
• **Role of High Courts:**
 
 
• High Courts are the principal civil courts of original jurisdiction in India, but their decisions may differ based on regional contexts.
 
• Article 139A ensures that conflicting decisions on similar issues are avoided by centralizing the matter in the Supreme Court.

question:
**Fill in the blanks:**

Zonal Councils were created by the ______ Act, 1956.
solution:
The correct answer is __**States Reorganisation Act, 1956**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Zonal Councils in India were established under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**, which aimed to reorganize states based on linguistic and administrative considerations.
 
• The primary objective of Zonal Councils was to foster **cooperation and coordination among states and Union Territories** in a particular zone.
 
• There are **five Zonal Councils**—Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, and Southern—each comprising states grouped based on geographical proximity.
 
• The Zonal Councils are chaired by the **Union Home Minister** and include the Chief Ministers of the member states, along with other ministers as representatives.
 
• Zonal Councils serve as a platform to resolve inter-state disputes and promote regional development by addressing common issues such as economic planning, border disputes, and cultural exchanges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Finance Commission**

 
 
• The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is primarily responsible for **dividing tax revenues between the Central and State governments** and addressing financial relations between them.
 
• The Finance Commission is appointed every five years, and its recommendations are advisory in nature.
 
• It does not pertain to the creation of Zonal Councils but plays a crucial role in managing fiscal matters in federal governance.
 
 
 
• **Panchayati Raj**
 
 
• The Panchayati Raj system was introduced as a form of **decentralized governance** under Article 40 of the Directive Principles of State Policy in the Constitution.
 
• The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, provided constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• It focuses on grassroots-level governance and local self-government but does not relate to Zonal Councils.
 
 
 
• **Representation of the People Act**
 
 
• The Representation of the People Act, 1951, governs the conduct of elections in India.
 
• It provides provisions for the qualification and disqualification of Members of Parliament and State Legislatures.
 
• While it is critical in ensuring free and fair elections, it is unrelated to the establishment of Zonal Councils.

question: Which of the following statements regarding the distribution of legislative powers between the Union and State legislatures is **correct**?

options.text: The State legislature can legislate on matters enumerated in the Union List
The Union legislature can legislate on matters in the Concurrent List only with State approval
The Union Government can issue directions to the States under Article 256
The Union and States have equal powers on matters in the Union List

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Union Government can issue directions to the States under Article 256**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 256 of the Indian Constitution states that the executive power of every state is to be exercised in a way that ensures compliance with the laws made by the Parliament.
 
• The Union Government has the authority to issue directions to the states to ensure the implementation of such laws.
 
• This provision ensures the supremacy of parliamentary laws over state laws in case of conflict.
 
• Such directions issued by the Union are binding on the states, and non-compliance may result in consequences under Article 356 (President’s Rule).
 
• This mechanism ensures the cohesive functioning of the federal structure in India and maintains the unity and integrity of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Legislature (Parliament)**

 
 
• Composition: President, Lok Sabha (House of the People), and Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• Powers: Exclusive power over Union List, concurrent power over Concurrent List, with overriding power over states.
 
• Rajya Sabha: Indirectly elected, permanent house (not dissolved), one-third members retire every two years, 12 nominated members for arts/science.
 
• Lok Sabha: Directly elected, represents the people. 
 
 
 
• **State Legislature**
 
 
• Composition: Varies; some bicameral (Assembly & Council), most unicameral (Assembly only).
 
• Powers: Exclusive power over State List, concurrent power over Concurrent List.
 
• Legislative Council (Upper House): Indirectly elected members from local authorities, graduates, teachers, MLAs, and nominated by Governor; permanent house, not dissolved, one-third retire every two years.
 
• Legislative Assembly (Lower House): Directly elected by people, members 40-500.

• All India Services officers are recruited and trained by the central government but serve both the central and state governments, ensuring better coordination between the two levels of administration.

• **About Article 312:**

• The services created under this article are meant to ensure uniform standards of administration across the country.
 
• The central government handles recruitment and training for these services through institutions like the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC).
 
 
 
• **Existing All India Services:**

question:
Which of the following statements is/are **correct**?

1) The Governor's discretionary power to recommend President's Rule is mentioned in Article 356(1).

2) The 41st Constitutional Amendment curtailed the Governor's term from 5 years to 4 years.

3) The Sarkaria Commission advised that Governors should not be removed before completing their term unless in rare and compelling circumstances.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: 1 & 3 correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1**: The Governor's discretionary power to recommend President's Rule is indeed mentioned in Article 356(1) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Article 356(1) allows the Governor to report to the President if the governance in a state cannot be carried out according to the provisions of the Constitution, thereby leading to the imposition of President's Rule.
 
• **Statement 3**: The Sarkaria Commission, which was constituted to examine the relationship between the Union and State governments, recommended that Governors should not be removed arbitrarily and must be allowed to complete their term unless there are rare and compelling reasons for their removal.
 
• The Sarkaria Commission's recommendations are widely recognized as a guiding framework for maintaining the independence and impartiality of the Governor's position.
 
• **Statement 2** is incorrect as the 41st Constitutional Amendment did not curtail the Governor's term. The Governor's term remains five years, as per Article 156 of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 356 of the Indian Constitution**:

 
 
• It is also known as the "President's Rule" provision.
 
• The Governor of a state can report to the President if there is a failure of the constitutional machinery in the state.
 
• Based on this report, the President can assume control over the state's administration.
 
• It is considered a controversial article, as it has been invoked multiple times, often leading to debates about misuse.
 
 
 
• **The Sarkaria Commission**:
 
 
• Constituted in 1983 to review the working of the Centre-State relations in India and suggest improvements.
 
• Among its key recommendations was the advice that Governors should be apolitical and impartial.
 
• It emphasized that the Governor should be allowed to complete their five-year term except in exceptional circumstances.
 
 
 
• **42nd Constitutional Amendment**:
 
 
• This amendment was passed in 1976 during the Emergency period in India.
 
• It extended the term of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from five years to six years.
 
• However, this was reversed by the 44th Constitutional Amendment in 1978, bringing the term back to five years.
 
• It had no impact on the term of Governors, which remains five years as per Article 156.

question:
Consider the following statements:

1. Indian federalism is biased towards the Centre.

2. The Constitution uses the word 'federal' explicitly.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Indian federalism is considered biased towards the Centre because the Constitution of India establishes a **quasi-federal structure**, where the Centre has more power compared to the states.
 
• The Union List in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains more items (97 subjects initially, now 100) compared to the State List (66 subjects initially, now 61), ensuring greater control for the Centre.
 
• The President of India has significant powers, such as the ability to impose President's Rule under Article 356, which allows the Centre to take over the administration of a state.
 
• Financial arrangements also favor the Centre, as it controls the major sources of revenue and allocates funds to the states, as per recommendations of the Finance Commission.
 
• However, the Constitution does not explicitly use the term "federal." Instead, it describes India as a "Union of States" in Article 1, emphasizing the indestructible nature of the Union.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Federal Features of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Division of powers between the Union and the States through three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.
 
• Independent judiciary with the Supreme Court as the final arbiter in disputes between the Centre and the states.
 
• Bicameral legislature at the Centre, consisting of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, representing both the people and the states.
 
 
 
• **Unitary Features of the Indian Constitution:**
 
 
• Emergency provisions allow the Centre to assume greater control over states during crises (Articles 352, 356, and 360).
 
• Centralized financial powers, as the Centre collects and allocates major sources of revenue.
 
• The Governor, appointed by the President, acts as the Centre's representative in states.

question:
Consider the following statements:

1) Both the Prime Minister (PM) and Chief Minister (CM) can advise dissolution of the respective Lower House.

2) Only the PM can recommend President's Rule under Article 356 of the Constitution.

Which of the statements is/are **correct**?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** Both the **Prime Minister (PM)** and the **Chief Minister (CM)** can advise the dissolution of their respective Lower Houses. **Correct.**

 
 
• The **Prime Minister**, along with the **Council of Ministers**, can advise the **President** to dissolve the **Lok Sabha** under **Article 85** of the Constitution.
 
• Similarly, the **Chief Minister**, along with the **Council of Ministers**, can advise the **Governor** to dissolve the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)** of the state.
 
• The President and Governor generally act on the aid and advice of their respective Councils of Ministers.
 
 ***Hence, Statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 2:** Only the PM can recommend President's Rule under **Article 356** of the Constitution. **Incorrect.**
 
 
• **President's Rule** is imposed by the **President of India** under **Article 356** when a state's constitutional machinery fails.
 
• The recommendation is generally made by the **Union Council of Ministers**, headed by the Prime Minister, and is often based on a report from the **Governor** of the concerned state.
 
• The Constitution does not provide that the **Prime Minister alone** can recommend President's Rule.
 
 ***Hence, Statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Therefore, only Statement 1 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 74** provides that the **President** shall act in accordance with the aid and advice of the **Council of Ministers** headed by the **Prime Minister**.
 
• **Article 163** provides that the **Governor** acts on the aid and advice of the **Council of Ministers** headed by the **Chief Minister**, except in matters where the Constitution grants discretionary powers.
 
• **Article 356** deals with the imposition of **President's Rule** in a state if the constitutional machinery fails.
 
• During **President's Rule**, the powers of the state government are assumed by the **President**, and the state legislature may be suspended or dissolved.
 
• The proclamation of President's Rule must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within **two months** from the date of its issuance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The landmark **S.R. Bommai vs Union of India (1994)** judgment placed significant restrictions on the arbitrary use of **Article 356**.
 
• The **Lok Sabha** is the Lower House at the Union level, while the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)** is the Lower House at the state level.
 
• The power to dissolve the Lower House is exercised formally by the **President** or **Governor**, but usually on the advice of the elected executive.

question: Which of the following disputes falls under the Supreme Court's exclusive original jurisdiction as per Article 131 of the Indian Constitution?

options.text: Election disputes of MPs and MLAs
Disputes between Centre and one or more States

solution:
The correct answer is __**Disputes between Centre and one or more States**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 131 of the Indian Constitution provides the **exclusive original jurisdiction** of the Supreme Court of India in certain disputes.
 
• These disputes include those between the Government of India and one or more States or between two or more States.
 
• The Supreme Court's original jurisdiction is called "exclusive" because it cannot be exercised by any other court in India.
 
• The jurisdiction applies only to legal matters and not political disputes or policy matters.
 
• This provision ensures the role of the Supreme Court as the **final arbiter** in resolving disputes concerning the interpretation of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Key Jurisdictions of the Supreme Court of India:
 
 
• **Original Jurisdiction (Article 131):**

 
 
• Hears disputes between the Government of India and States, or between States themselves, involving questions of law or fact.
 
• Writ Jurisdiction (Article 32): Enforces Fundamental Rights by issuing writs like Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Quo Warranto, and Certiorari.
 
 
 
• **Appellate Jurisdiction:**
 
 
• The final court of appeal, hearing appeals from High Courts in constitutional, civil, criminal, and special leave petition (SLP) cases.
 
 
 
• **Advisory Jurisdiction (Article 143):**
 
 
• Advises the President on matters of public importance or law, though these are not binding.
 
 
 
• **Review Jurisdiction:**
 
 
• Power to review its own judgments or orders.
 
 
 
• **Extraordinary & Other Powers:**
 
 
• Transfer of Cases: Can transfer civil/criminal cases between High Courts or subordinate courts.
 
• Suo Moto Powers: Can take up cases on its own motion.
 
• Article 142: Powers to pass orders for "complete justice".

question: Under Article 258A, what power is granted to States?

options.text: States need Presidential assent to assign functions to Union
Governor can entrust Union tasks to State Legislature with President's consent
State Legislature can entrust Union work to State officers with Centre's approval
State Government can, with Union's consent, assign Union functions to its officers

solution:
The correct answer is __**State Government can, with Union's consent, assign Union functions to its officers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 258A** of the Indian Constitution allows the State Government to assign functions that are part of Union duties to its officers, subject to the Union Government's consent.
 
• This provision enables **cooperative federalism** by facilitating smooth coordination between the Union and State Governments for administrative efficiency.
 
• The purpose of this article is to ensure that certain Union responsibilities can be carried out by State officers in cases where it is more practical or efficient to do so.
 
• Such assignments are typically used in areas of administrative overlap or when specific functions require local expertise or resource deployment at the state level.
 
• Through this article, the Constitution ensures that there is no legal ambiguity in delegating Union functions to state authorities with mutual agreement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: States need Presidential assent to assign functions to Union**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect. The Constitution does not require Presidential assent for States to assign functions to the Union. Instead, Article 258 allows the Union Government to delegate its powers to the State, with Presidential consent.
 
• Article 258 pertains to the delegation of Union functions to State authorities and requires Presidential approval for such delegation but does not apply in reverse (States to Union).
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Governor can entrust Union tasks to State Legislature with President's consent**
 
 
• This is incorrect as per constitutional provisions. Governors do not have the authority to directly entrust Union tasks to the State Legislature.
 
• Under Article 258, the delegation of Union functions is usually administrative and does not involve legislative powers, which remain distinct for the Union and States.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: State Legislature can entrust Union work to State officers with Centre's approval**
 
 
• This option is incorrect because the State Legislature does not have the authority to assign Union work. Such powers are vested in the State Government (executive) and not the legislature.
 
• Legislative powers and administrative functions are separate under the Indian Constitution, and this distinction is maintained in the allocation of responsibilities.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Article 258A**
 
 
• Article 258A was inserted in the Constitution by the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956.
 
• Its primary purpose is to establish a framework for the delegation of Union functions to State Governments for better governance and administrative coordination.
 
• This article complements Article 258, which allows the President to entrust Union functions to States.

question:
Consider the following statements:

1. Article 300 allows legal suits against State Governments.

2. The term 'Government of India' is a legal entity under Article 300.

Which of the above is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3 (Both 1 and 2)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 300** of the Indian Constitution establishes the legal liability of the Government of India and State Governments, allowing legal suits to be filed against them in cases of contractual or tortious obligations.
 
• The term **'Government of India'** is recognized as a legal entity under Article 300, enabling it to sue and be sued in its name.
 
• The scope of Article 300 derives from the legal framework of the Government of India Act, 1935, and continues under the Constitution of India.
 
• Legal suits against the State Governments or the Government of India must be initiated in accordance with the rules and procedures prescribed under Article 300.
 
• Both statements in the question are correct because Article 300 explicitly provides for legal accountability and establishes the Government of India and State Governments as juristic entities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 300 - Legal Liability:**

 
 
• Under Article 300, the Government can be held liable for acts done by its officials or representatives in their official capacity.
 
• It covers cases of breach of contract, negligence, or wrongful acts committed by government officials.
 
• The Government of India or State Governments can be sued in the same manner as private individuals, subject to certain legal restrictions.
 
 
 
• **Historical Background:**
 
 
• Article 300 traces its roots to Section 176 of the Government of India Act, 1935, which also dealt with the legal liability of the Crown.
 
• Post-independence, the provisions were adapted and incorporated into the Constitution of India.
 
 
 
• **Legal Entity Concept:**
 
 
• The term 'Government of India' refers to the Union Government as a juristic person capable of legal rights and obligations.
 
• This ensures accountability and transparency in governance, allowing citizens to seek legal remedies against government actions.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Article 300:**
 
 
• While Article 300 allows for legal suits against the Government, certain restrictions apply, such as sovereign immunity in specific cases.
 
• Legal proceedings must adhere to the procedures outlined in the Code of Civil Procedure and other relevant laws.
 
 
 
• **Relevance:** Article 300 plays a critical role in ensuring accountability of the government and upholding the rule of law.

question:
Consider the following statements:

1. Article 131 provides exclusive original jurisdiction to High Courts in federal disputes.

2. The Supreme Court can adjudicate disputes between States under Article 131.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 131 of the Indian Constitution grants the Supreme Court exclusive original jurisdiction** to adjudicate disputes between the Government of India and one or more States, or between two or more States.
 
• This jurisdiction is termed "original" because the Supreme Court can directly hear such disputes instead of them being referred to a lower court first.
 
• The disputes under Article 131 typically involve federal issues such as disagreements over laws, constitutional interpretation, or treaties.
 
• High Courts do not have jurisdiction under Article 131; this article is specifically reserved for the Supreme Court.
 
• Thus, Statement 2 is correct as it accurately reflects the role of the Supreme Court in resolving inter-state disputes under Article 131.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regarding Statement 1:**

 
 
• Statement 1 is incorrect because Article 131 pertains to the Supreme Court, not High Courts.
 
• The High Courts have original jurisdiction in matters such as enforcement of fundamental rights under Article 226, but not in federal disputes between States or the Union Government.
 
 
 
• **Article 131 Detailed Explanation:**
 
 
• This article is foundational in maintaining the federal structure of India.
 
• The disputes it covers include issues like boundary disputes, financial disputes, or questions over the execution of constitutional provisions.
 
• However, the Supreme Court's jurisdiction under Article 131 does not extend to disputes arising out of political agreements or treaties.
 
 
 
• **Role of High Courts in Indian Judiciary:**
 
 
• High Courts function primarily under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution.
 
• They have jurisdiction over the respective States or Union Territories they serve and can issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
 
 
• **Related Provisions in the Constitution:**
 
 
• Article 132: Deals with the appellate jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in constitutional matters.
 
• Article 136: Grants the Supreme Court special leave to appeal against any judgment or order of any court or tribunal in India.

question: What is the role of Article 263 in maintaining Union-State coordination?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Provides Inter-State Council framework**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 263 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council if it appears to him that the public interests would be served by such a council.
 
• The primary role of the Inter-State Council is to facilitate coordination between the Union and State governments, ensuring harmonious decision-making.
 
• The Council can inquire into and discuss disputes or subjects of common interest between states or between the Union and one or more states.
 
• It provides a forum for discussing administrative issues and suggesting better methods for policy and implementation of decisions affecting Union-State relations.
 
• The Inter-State Council is an advisory body and does not have executive powers; its recommendations are not binding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Settles taxation disputes (Option 1)**

 
 
• Taxation disputes between states or between the Union and states are primarily resolved through institutions such as the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council, set up under Article 279A of the Constitution.
 
• The GST Council is responsible for making recommendations to the Union and States on issues related to GST, including tax rates and exemptions.
 
• Article 263 does not directly deal with settling taxation disputes.
 
 
 
• **Creates Zonal Councils (Option 2)**
 
 
• Zonal Councils are established under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, and are not directly linked to Article 263.
 
• These councils aim to promote cooperation and coordination between states in each zone and with the Union government.
 
• There are five Zonal Councils: Northern, Southern, Eastern, Western, and Central, and they address regional issues like economic development, infrastructure, and border disputes.
 
 
 
• **Enforces Emergency Provisions (Option 4)**
 
 
• Emergency provisions are governed by Articles 352, 356, and 360 of the Constitution and are unrelated to Article 263.
 
• These provisions empower the President to declare a National Emergency, President’s Rule in a state, or a Financial Emergency under specific circumstances.
 
• Article 263 is focused on coordination and cooperation between the Union and states and does not deal with emergencies.

question:
**Consider the following statements: **

1. Both President and Governor can grant pardons under Article 72.

2. The Governor cannot pardon in cases of death sentence. Which of the above statements is/are **correct**?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 72** of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment, or to suspend, remit, or commute the sentence of any person convicted of an offense under certain circumstances, including in cases of death sentences.
 
• The **Governor**, under **Article 161**, has similar powers but does not have the authority to pardon a death sentence. The power to pardon a death sentence is exclusively vested in the President under Article 72.
 
• The second statement, "The Governor cannot pardon in cases of death sentence," is correct as the Governor can only commute or remit such sentences but cannot grant a full pardon.
 
• The first statement, "Both President and Governor can grant pardons under Article 72," is incorrect because the Governor does not exercise powers under Article 72. The Governor's pardoning power is provided under Article 161.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Only 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **President's Pardoning Powers (Article 72):**

 
 
• The President has the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, remissions, or commutations of punishments for offenses under:
 
 
• Union law.
 
• Matters concerning the executive power of the Union.
 
• Death sentences (exclusive power).
 
 
 
• This power is exercised on the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
 
 
• **Governor's Pardoning Powers (Article 161):**
 
 
• The Governor can grant pardons, reprieves, respites, remissions, or commutations for offenses under:
 
 
• State law.
 
 
 
• The Governor **cannot pardon a death sentence**, as this power is exclusively reserved for the President.
 
 
 
• **Key Differences Between Article 72 and 161:**
 
 
• While both the President and Governor can grant pardons and similar reliefs, only the President can pardon death sentences.
 
• The jurisdiction of the President's power extends to offenses under Union laws, while the Governor's power is limited to State laws.

question:
Consider the following statements about the Rajya Sabha and choose the **correct **option:

1) Rajya Sabha is a continuing house of the Parliament, immune to dissolution under any circumstance.

2) Rajya Sabha members serve staggered six-year terms, with one-third retiring every two years.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
