__
 
• **The first rocket launched in India:**

 
 
• Sounding rockets are one or two-stage solid propellant rockets used for probing the upper atmospheric regions and for space research.
 
• They also serve as easily affordable platforms to test or prove prototypes of new components or subsystems intended for use in launch vehicles and satellites.
 
• **With the establishment of the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS) in 1963 at Thumba, a location close to the magnetic equator, there was a quantum jump in the scope for aeronomy and atmospheric sciences in India.**
 
• **The launch of the first sounding rocket from Thumba near Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala on 21 November 1963, marked the beginning of the Indian Space Programme. Hence, Option 3 is correct.**
 
• Sounding rockets made it possible to probe the atmosphere in situ using rocket-borne instrumentation.
 
• The first rockets were two-stage rockets imported from Russia (M-100) and France (Centaure).
 
• While the M-100 could carry a payload of 70 kg to an altitude of 85 km, the Centaure was capable of reaching 150 km with a payload of approximately 30 kg.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Its vision is to harness space technology for national development while pursuing space science research and planetary exploration.
 
• Antrix Corporation Limited (ACL) is a Marketing arm of ISRO for promotion and commercial exploitation of space products, technical consultancy services, and transfer of technologies developed by ISRO.
 
• **The space research activities were initiated in India under Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, the founding father of the Indian space programme, during the 1960s.**

question: The Regional Rural Banks were established on the recommendations of the ______ on Rural Credit.

The correct answer is __**Narsimha Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Regional Rural Banks were established on the recommendations of the Narsimha Committee Rural Credit.**
 
• **Regional Rural Bank:**
 
 
• Regional Rural Banks were established on the basis of the recommendations of the **Narasimham Working Group (1975), and after the legislation of the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976.**
 
• They are financial institutions that ensure adequate credit for agriculture and other rural sectors. 
 
• They were set up on the recommendations of the Narasimham Working Group (1975).
 
• RRBs were granted legal provisions under the Regional Rural Banks Act, 1976.
 
• The first Regional Rural Bank **"Prathama Grameen Bank"** was set up on 2nd October 1975. 
 
• The equity of a regional rural bank is held by the Central Government, the concerned State Government, and the Sponsor Bank in the proportion of 50:15:35.
 
• The RRBs have combined characteristics of a cooperative and a commercial bank.
 
• It operates within the local limits as notified by the Government.
 
• The **main objectives of RRBs** are:
 
 
• To provide credit and other facilities to the small and marginal farmers, agricultural labourers, artisans, and small entrepreneurs in rural areas.
 
• To check the outflow of rural deposits to urban areas.
 
• To reduce regional imbalances.
 
• To increase rural employment generation.
 
• They are required to provide 75% of their total credit as priority sector lending.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rekhi Committee on Indirect Tax Reform**:-

 
 
• The Rekhi Committee was constituted in **1992 under the chairmanship of K.L. Rekhi.** The recommendations are a Tribunal should be set up to deal with problems between taxpayers and tax collectors.
 
• A High-Level India classification committee with trade and industry representatives should be set up.
 
• Important consignments should be cleared within 3 days.
 
• The monopoly of one nominated bank in each state should be supplemented by another bank.
 
• Coercive measures must not be used for recovery of disputed duty amount when the assessee files a stay application.
 
 
 
• **Kelkar Committee Report on Tax Reforms:-**
 
 
• A task force on Direct and Indirect Taxes was constituted under the chairmanship of DR. Vijay Kelkar in 2002. The recommendation of the Vijay Kelkar committee are:
 
 
• The income tax exemption limit must be increased to Rs. 1 Lakh from the present 50,000 tax exemption limit for senior citizens and widows should be Rs. 1.5 lakhs.
 
• There should be a two-tier income tax structure with a 20% tax for earnings of Rs. 1 lakh to 4 lakh and 30% tax for over Rs. 4 lakhs. The standard deduction must be abolished but suggested an exemption for conveyance

 allowance.
 
• There should be the abolition of long-term capital gains tax, dividend tax, and wealth tax. There should not be any surcharge on income tax.
 
• There should be an interest subsidy of 2% for housing loans up to Rs. 5 lakh.
 
• There must be a 30% corporate tax for domestic companies and 35% for foreign companies and there should be no Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT).
 
• There Should be a 14% Central Value Added Tax (CENNAT) rate.
 
• There should be nationwide VAT and Comprehensive Service Tax.
 
• Exemptions for life-saving drugs, security items, and farm products.
 
• Exemption of tax for small-scale units with a turnover up to Rs. 50 lakh.

question:
Which of the following is a negative effect of Green Revolution in India?

(i) Depletion of groundwater table

(ii) Deterioration in the quality of soil

(iii) Increased input cost
solution:
The correct answer is __**(i), (ii) and (iii).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Green Revolution:-**

 
 
• It​ was a significant development in **India's agricultural sector **that aimed to increase **agricultural productivity** and **reduce food insecurity.**
 
• **However, it also had some negative effects.**
 
 
 
• **Depletion of groundwater table:-**
 
 
• The Green Revolution promoted the use of** high-yielding crop varieties,** which required **more water for irrigation.**
 
• As a result, farmers started **extracting groundwater **at an** unsustainable rate,** leading to a decline in the groundwater table.
 
• This, in turn, led to **water scarcity **and affected the livelihoods of farmers who depended on groundwater for irrigation.
 
 
 
• **Deterioration in the quality of soil:-**
 
 
• The use of** chemical fertilizers and pesticides** was a key feature of the Green Revolution.
 
• Over time, this led to **soil degradation, loss of soil fertility,** and **reduced crop yields.**
 
• **Soil erosion, salinization, and acidification **were some of the other negative impacts on soil quality.
 
 
 
• **Increased input cost:-**
 
 
• The adoption of **new technologies and practices** under the Green Revolution required farmers to invest in expensive inputs like** seeds, fertilizers, and machinery.**
 
• This increased the** cost of cultivation**, making it difficult for **small and marginal farmers** to afford these inputs.
 
• As a result, they had to** borrow money **from moneylenders at** high-interest rates,** leading to a **cycle of debt and poverty.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution:** It refers to the period of **rapid agricultural development** in the **1960s and 1970s, **which aimed to **increase food production** through the use of **high-yielding crop varieties, chemical fertilizers, and pesticides.**
 
• **Positive Effects:** The Green Revolution led to a significant **increase in food production, reduced food prices, and improved food security** in India.
 
 
• It also created new** job opportunities** and** increased rural income.**
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Agriculture: **It refers to an agricultural system that is** environmentally friendly, socially just, and economically viable.** 
 
 
• It promotes the use of **organic farming practices, crop diversification**, and **conservation of natural resources.**

question: The central bank of India or Reserve Bank of India was created before Independence, in the year 1934. The recommendation to create a central bank was made by a commission called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hilton Young Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was established on the basis of the recommendations of the **Hilton Young Commission**.
 
• The Hilton Young Commission was set up in 1926 to review the working of the Indian currency and to suggest changes for its stabilization and better management.
 
• The Commission's report led to the enactment of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India commenced operations on April 1, 1935, as the central bank of the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**

 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank of the country, responsible for regulating the issue of banknotes, maintaining reserves to ensure monetary stability, and operating the currency and credit system of India.
 
• It was established on April 1, 1935, in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• The RBI plays a crucial role in the development strategy of the Government of India.
 
• The institution is headquartered in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India.
 
 
 
• **Hilton Young Commission**
 
 
• The Hilton Young Commission, also known as the Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, was established in 1926.
 
• The Commission was chaired by Sir Edward Hilton Young.
 
• Its primary purpose was to examine the Indian currency system and to recommend measures for its stabilization and management.
 
• The Commission's recommendations were instrumental in the establishment of the Reserve Bank of India.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**
 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, is the legislative framework that led to the creation of the Reserve Bank of India.
 
• The Act was passed to constitute the Reserve Bank of India to regulate the issue of banknotes and the keeping of reserves to ensure monetary stability in India.
 
• It also aims to operate the currency and credit system of the country to its advantage.
 
• The Act came into force on April 1, 1935, which is when the RBI began its operations.

question: Which of the following commissions/committees identified the existence of legal provisions for implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice Verma Committee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Justice Verma Committee was established to recommend amendments to criminal laws to provide for quicker trial and enhanced punishment for criminals accused of committing sexual assault against women.
 
• One of the significant contributions of the Justice Verma Committee was identifying the existence of legal provisions for the implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties.
 
• The Committee underscored the importance of fundamental duties as a counterpart to fundamental rights, emphasizing their role in ensuring the proper functioning of democracy.
 
• The recommendations of the Justice Verma Committee have been instrumental in shaping reforms in India's legal framework, especially concerning women's safety and legal provisions related to fundamental duties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties:**

 
 
• Fundamental Duties are specified in Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution (Article 51A).
 
• They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• Originally, ten duties were listed; the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, added an eleventh duty.
 
• These duties are moral obligations on all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.
 
 
 
• **Justice Verma Committee:**
 
 
• The Justice Verma Committee was constituted in the wake of the 2012 Delhi gang-rape case.
 
• It was tasked with reviewing existing laws and suggesting changes to ensure the safety and dignity of women.
 
• Its report, submitted in January 2013, made several landmark recommendations for legal reforms.
 
• The Committee's work led to the enactment of the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, which introduced stricter penalties for sexual crimes.
 
 
 
• **Sarkaria Commission:**
 
 
• Formed in 1983, the Sarkaria Commission was set up to review the working of the Indian federal system and the balance of power between the state and central governments.
 
• It submitted its report in 1988 with recommendations to improve center-state relations.
 
 
 
• **Rajamannar Commission:**
 
 
• The Rajamannar Committee, established by the Tamil Nadu government in 1969, was tasked with examining center-state relations.
 
• It recommended greater autonomy for states and the establishment of a permanent inter-state council.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Justice Verma Committee was formed to identify the existence of legal provisions for the implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties enshrined in the Constitution of India.
 
• The Committee was set up in 1999 under the chairmanship of Justice J.S. Verma, former Chief Justice of India.
 
• It reviewed the existing legal framework and suggested measures to make the Fundamental Duties more enforceable.
 
• The Committee's recommendations emphasized the role of education and awareness in promoting a sense of duty among citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• The Fundamental Duties are a set of moral obligations for all citizens of India, enshrined in Part IV-A of the Constitution (Article 51A).
 
• These duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties, which include respect for the Constitution, national symbols, the promotion of harmony, and the protection of public property.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts.
 
 
 
• **Justice Verma Committee**
 
 
• Justice J.S. Verma, a renowned jurist and former Chief Justice of India, chaired the committee.
 
• The Committee's focus was to enhance the implementation of Fundamental Duties through legal and educational reforms.
 
• It highlighted the need for incorporating the Fundamental Duties into the education system to instill a sense of responsibility in citizens from a young age.
 
• The Committee's report has been influential in shaping policies and programs aimed at promoting civic responsibility.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**
 
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its extensive changes to the Constitution of India.
 
• It introduced the Fundamental Duties, provided for the establishment of Administrative Tribunals, and made several changes to the Preamble and other parts of the Constitution.
 
• The Amendment was passed during the Emergency period under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's government.
 
• It aimed to strengthen the central government's powers and bring about socio-economic reforms.

question: Which of the following commissions recommended the establishment of a Permanent Secretariat for the Inter-State Council to institutionalize Centre-State cooperation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarkaria Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Sarkaria Commission was established by the Government of India in June 1983 to review the Centre-State relations.
 
• It recommended the establishment of a Permanent Secretariat for the Inter-State Council to institutionalize Centre-State cooperation.
 
• The Inter-State Council is a constitutional body under Article 263 of the Indian Constitution to investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between the Union and States.
 
• The Sarkaria Commission emphasized the need for better communication and coordination between the Centre and States to strengthen federalism in India.
 
• Its recommendations led to the formation of the Inter-State Council in 1990, which serves as an important platform for resolving disputes and promoting cooperative federalism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajamannar Committee**

 
 
• It was set up by the Tamil Nadu government in 1969 under the chairmanship of P.V. Rajamannar.
 
• The committee recommended more autonomy to states and a redefinition of Centre-State relations.
 
• It suggested the abolition of the Planning Commission, the discontinuation of All India Services, and the transfer of subjects from the Union List to the State List.
 
• However, its recommendations were not implemented at the national level.
 
 
 
• **Punchhi Commission**
 
 
• The Punchhi Commission was set up in April 2007 under the chairmanship of Justice M.M. Punchhi to look into Centre-State relations.
 
• It recommended a fixed term for Governors, a comprehensive framework for disaster management, and changes to the role of the Governor in state politics.
 
• It focused on addressing challenges to federalism in the context of globalization and socio-economic changes.
 
• Its report is considered significant for improving Centre-State relations but is yet to be fully implemented.
 
 
 
• **Venkatachelliah Commission**
 
 
• Also known as the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC), it was established in 2000 under Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah.
 
• The commission aimed to review the Constitution to make it more effective and relevant in contemporary times.
 
• It suggested reforms in electoral processes, judicial accountability, and the functioning of parliamentary institutions.
 
• It did not specifically focus on Centre-State relations or the Inter-State Council.

question: In the 2025 Global Firepower (GFP) review, which of the following statements is correct regarding the ranking methodology?

options.text: It considers only the number of active military personnel
It ranks nations solely based on nuclear capabilities
It uses over 60 factors including logistics and geography to calculate the PowerIndex
It ranks countries alphabetically within continents

solution:
The correct answer is __**It uses over 60 factors including logistics and geography to calculate the PowerIndex**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Global Firepower (GFP) review is an annual military strength ranking that evaluates nations based on their military capabilities.
 
• The PowerIndex (PwrIndx) score is calculated using over 60 individual factors, encompassing categories like manpower, equipment, natural resources, financial stability, and geography.
 
• The ranking methodology emphasizes diversity over quantity; for instance, having a balanced mix of naval assets is more favorable than having a large fleet of a single type.
 
• Geography plays a crucial role, as nations with strategic locations or extensive coastlines may gain an advantage in specific areas.
 
• Nuclear stockpiles are considered but do not dominate the ranking system, ensuring non-nuclear nations can also rank competitively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: It considers only the number of active military personnel**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect because the GFP ranking is not solely based on manpower but evaluates a comprehensive range of factors.
 
• While active military personnel is an important component, other elements like reserve forces, equipment, and logistics are equally significant.
 
• Focusing only on manpower would ignore critical aspects like training, technology, and operational readiness.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: It ranks nations solely based on nuclear capabilities**
 
 
• This is incorrect as nuclear capability is only one of the factors considered in the GFP ranking.
 
• The review includes nuclear stockpiles but ensures that non-nuclear powers are not unfairly disadvantaged.
 
• The methodology focuses on overall military potential rather than singular factors like nuclear weapons.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: It ranks countries alphabetically within continents**
 
 
• This option is incorrect as the GFP ranking is based on calculated PowerIndex scores and not alphabetical or regional order.
 
• Countries are ranked globally, with their position determined by overall military strength rather than their location or name.
 
 
 
• **Global Firepower (GFP) Overview**
 
 
• The GFP review is widely recognized for its thorough and unbiased assessment of military strength.
 
• The ranking includes data from 145 nations, providing a comprehensive analysis of global military power.
 
• The PowerIndex score is inversely proportional, meaning a lower score indicates a stronger and more capable military.
 
• It excludes political or current conflict considerations, focusing purely on measurable military factors.
 
 

``

__
 
• The Sarkaria Commission was established by the Government of India in **1983** to examine and review the working of existing arrangements between the Central and State governments.
 
• The commission was chaired by Justice R.S. Sarkaria, a former judge of the Supreme Court of India.
 
• Its primary objective was to recommend changes to improve the relationship and distribution of powers between the Centre and States.
 
• The Sarkaria Commission submitted its report in **1988**, providing detailed recommendations on various issues concerning federal governance in India.
 
• The commission emphasized cooperative federalism and suggested ways to strengthen the autonomy of states while maintaining the unity of the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: 1990**

 
 
• This year does not align with the establishment of the Sarkaria Commission.
 
• However, during the early 1990s, significant political changes occurred in India, including the rise of coalition governments which further highlighted the importance of Centre-State relations.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: 1992**
 
 
• 1992 marks the introduction of the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments, which provided constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions and urban local bodies.
 
• These amendments focused on decentralization and strengthening grassroots governance but are unrelated to the Sarkaria Commission.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: 2000**
 
 
• In 2000, India witnessed administrative reforms such as the formation of new states like Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Uttarakhand.
 
• While these changes impacted Centre-State relations, they are not connected to the establishment of the Sarkaria Commission.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Centre-State Relations in India**
 
 
• India has a quasi-federal structure, where powers are distributed between the Centre and States as per the Constitution.
 
• The Sarkaria Commission was a landmark initiative to address challenges in this arrangement and recommend measures for effective governance.
 
• Key recommendations included guidelines for the imposition of President’s Rule, principles for the appointment of Governors, and the role of the Inter-State Council.
 
• Many of its recommendations continue to influence debates and policies on federalism in India.

question: According to the Global Firepower (GFP) methodology, what is the purpose of using special modifiers like bonuses and penalties in its ranking formula?

options.text: To exclude non-military nations from the ranking
To prioritize countries with higher nuclear stockpiles
To balance rankings between technologically advanced and lesser-developed nations
To calculate the GDP-to-defense budget ratio

solution:
The correct answer is __**To balance rankings between technologically advanced and lesser-developed nations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Global Firepower (GFP) methodology employs special modifiers, such as bonuses and penalties, to create a balanced and equitable military strength ranking.
 
• These modifiers ensure that rankings are not overly influenced by a single factor, such as the size of a country's military or its financial resources.
 
• The goal is to provide a fair comparison between technologically advanced nations with smaller militaries and nations with larger but less technologically advanced forces.
 
• Modifiers account for variables such as logistical capabilities, geographical factors, and natural resource availability, which play a significant role in a nation's military effectiveness.
 
• This balanced approach enables the GFP ranking to reflect a more comprehensive view of a nation's overall military strength rather than focusing solely on quantitative metrics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: To exclude non-military nations from the ranking**

 
 
• While the GFP methodology focuses on military power, it does not specifically aim to exclude non-military nations.
 
• Instead, it evaluates nations with significant military capabilities and resources, ensuring that all eligible nations are included in the rankings.
 
• Non-military nations are naturally not part of the GFP ranking as they lack the necessary data points for evaluation.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: To prioritize countries with higher nuclear stockpiles**
 
 
• The GFP ranking does consider nuclear stockpiles as a factor; however, it does not prioritize them disproportionately.
 
• Nuclear capability is one of many aspects of military power, but it is balanced with other factors like conventional forces, logistics, and economic strength.
 
• This ensures that nations with smaller nuclear arsenals but strong conventional forces are not unfairly ranked lower.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: To calculate the GDP-to-defense budget ratio**
 
 
• The GDP-to-defense budget ratio is an important economic indicator, but it is not the primary focus of the GFP ranking methodology.
 
• Instead, the GFP uses a more comprehensive formula that accounts for military, economic, and logistical factors to rank nations.
 
• While economic strength is a factor, the ranking does not rely solely on financial metrics like GDP ratios.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Global Firepower (GFP) Ranking**
 
 
• The GFP ranking is an annual assessment of military strength for nations worldwide, based on over 60 individual factors.
 
• These factors include manpower, equipment, financial resources, logistical capabilities, and geography.
 
• The aim is to provide a realistic and balanced comparison of military power across nations, avoiding biases toward specific metrics like sheer size or spending.
 
• The GFP index uses a "Power Index" score, where lower scores indicate stronger military capabilities.

__
 
• The Gaganyaan mission is India's first human spaceflight mission, aimed at advancing the nation’s space technology and research capabilities.
 
• The mission primarily focuses on enhancing India's space exploration capabilities and human spaceflight technology, not on climate-related objectives like reducing Earth's temperature.
 
• Reduction in Earth's temperature is not a realistic or intended outcome of the Gaganyaan mission, as space missions do not directly influence global climate systems.
 
• Gaganyaan aims to develop indigenous technologies for human space travel, such as crew modules, life support systems, and space docking mechanisms, among others.
 
• The benefits of the mission are mainly technological, economic, and strategic, with no direct relation to environmental or climate control measures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The Gaganyaan mission fosters international partnerships and collaborations in space science by working with countries like Russia, France, and the USA for training, technology sharing, and research.
 
• Such collaborations enhance India’s global standing in space exploration and encourage knowledge exchange with leading space agencies like NASA, Roscosmos, and ESA.
 
 
 
• **Advancement in space-related R&D and technology**
 
 
• The mission is expected to drive significant advancements in space technology, including innovations in materials, propulsion systems, life support, and spacecraft design.
 
• It will also boost research in artificial intelligence, robotics, and automation, which are critical for future space missions.
 
• The technologies developed for Gaganyaan have potential applications in defense, healthcare, communication, and disaster management sectors.
 
 
 
• **Boost to India's human spaceflight capability**
 
 
• The Gaganyaan mission is a major milestone in establishing India as a leader in human spaceflight capabilities.
 
• It aims to send a crew of Indian astronauts, also known as "vyomanauts," into a 300-400 km low Earth orbit for 5-7 days.
 
• This will make India the fourth country, after the USA, Russia, and China, to achieve independent human spaceflight capability.

question: In the Olympic flag, the total number of rings are _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**5**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The total number of rings in the Olympic flag is five.
 
• The five rings are interlaced and colored blue, yellow, black, green, and red.
 
• These five rings symbolize the unity of the **five continents: America (North and South considered as a single continent), Africa, Europe, Asia, and Oceania.**
 
• The interlacing of the five rings represents the unity of athletes from all nations.
 
• The flag was adopted in 1914 and **first flown in an Olympic games in 1920**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Olympics**: The Olympic Games originated in ancient Greece about 3,000 years ago. The first modern Olympics took place in 1896 in Athens, Greece, with 14 countries participating.
 
• **Symbol of Olympic Games**: The symbol of the Olympic Games is composed of five interlocking rings, coloured blue, yellow, black, green, and red on a white field. This was designed by Pierre de Coubertin, the co-founder of the Modern Olympics. The rings represent the five continents that participate in the Olympics and the colours were chosen because at least one of them appears on every nation's flag.
 
• **Motto**: The Olympic motto is "Citius, Altius, Fortius." This is Latin for "Faster, Higher, Braver," but is more commonly translated as "Faster, Higher, Stronger."
 
• **Olympic Torch**: The tradition of the Olympic Torch or Olympic Flame originates from ancient Greece. The flame gets lit several months before the start of the Games at the site of the ancient Olympics in Olympia, Greece and carried in a relay by torch bearers to the host city.
 
• **Winter and Summer Games:** The Olympics comprise both Summer and Winter Games. They occur every four years but, since 1994, they've been staggered so they occur every two years in alternation. The Winter Games include sports such as skiing, curling, ice hockey, and snowboarding.
 
• **Paralympics**: Occurring immediately after the Summer or Winter Olympics, the Paralympics are designed for athletes with a range of disabilities. The Paralympics became an official event in 1960 in Rome, Italy.
 
• **Youth Olympics**: For younger athletes, there's the Youth Olympic Games—a global event comprising both a Summer and Winter Games, held every four years, for athletes aged 14 to 18 years old. The first Youth Olympics was celebrated in 2010 in Singapore.

question: What was the official mascot of the Khelo India Winter Games 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Snow leopard 'Sheen-e She' (Shan)**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The **official mascot** of the **Khelo India Winter Games 2024** was the **Snow Leopard named 'Sheen-e She' (Shan).** 
• The name **'Sheen-e She'** translates to **'The Snow Leopard'** in the local Kashmiri language, symbolizing the rich biodiversity and the majestic wildlife of the Himalayan region. 
• The **snow leopard** was chosen to represent the games because it is an **iconic species of the Himalayan region**, known for its resilience and adaptability to the extreme winter conditions, aligning with the spirit of the winter games. 
• The **Khelo India Winter Games 2024** aimed to **promote winter sports** and encourage youth participation in sports activities in the Himalayan region and across India. 
• The event was hosted in **Gulmarg, Jammu & Kashmir**, a well-known destination for winter sports and tourism, further emphasizing the importance of preserving the region's ecology and promoting sustainable tourism. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **About Snow Leopards:** 
• Snow leopards are a **vulnerable species** as per the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Red List, with their population under constant threat due to habitat loss and poaching. 
• They are commonly found in the **mountain ranges** of Central and South Asia, including the **Himalayas**, and are often referred to as "ghosts of the mountains" due to their elusive nature. 
• The snow leopard serves as a **flagship species** for conservation efforts in the Himalayan region and symbolizes the importance of preserving biodiversity. 
• **About Khelo India Initiative:** 
• Launched in **2018**, the **Khelo India Programme** is an initiative by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to **revive the sports culture** in India at the grassroot level. 
• It aims to identify young talent from schools and universities and provide them with the necessary infrastructure and training to excel in sports. 
• The Khelo India Winter Games is a part of this initiative to **promote winter sports** and establish India as a global hub for such activities. 
• **Objectives of Khelo India Winter Games:** 
• To **promote adventure tourism** and winter sports in the Himalayan regions. 
• To encourage **youth participation** in winter sports and develop their competitive spirit. 
• To highlight the rich **cultural heritage** and natural beauty of regions like Jammu and Kashmir. 
• **Key Features of Khelo India Winter Games 2024:** 
• The event included **various disciplines** like skiing, snowboarding, ice skating, and ice hockey. 
• It witnessed the participation of athletes from **across India** and international competitors, promoting the global recognition of India’s winter sports capability. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Other Mascots in Indian Sports:** 
• **Bharati the Leopard** - Mascot for the **36th National Games 2022** held in Gujarat. 
• **Veera the Bull** - Mascot for the **Khelo India Youth Games 2020** held in Guwahati, Assam. 
• **Mauli** - Mascot for the **18th Asian Games 2018** held in Jakarta, Indonesia (not related to Indian events but often referenced in sports discussions). 
• **Significance of Mascots:** 
• Mascots serve as **symbols of identity** and bring cultural, environmental, or regional significance to sports events. 
• They engage the audience emotionally and help in **branding** and promoting the event.

question: The term 'Dolphin Kick' is associated with which sport?
solution:
__
 
• **The Dolphin kick is associated with the Swimming.**__
 
• The Dolphin kick technique is used by professional swimmers, they use that motion that propels them forward underwater after diving in, and at the underwater turns.
 
• This technique is not just about the legs but It requires a swimmer's entire body to crack like a whip, creating a fluid wave that starts at the chest and increases in amplitude as it travels all the way through the toes, and it seems like a dolphin that's why it is called **Dolphin kick**.
 
• The Dolphin Kick is assumed as the fastest way to get from one point to another underwater but it needs a lot of practice as it is a very difficult move.

 
• The international rules for swimming disciplines are laid down by Federation Internationale de Natation (International Swimming Federation) FINA.
 
• There are four standard strokes in swimming a front crawl, backstroke, breaststroke, and butterfly.

question: India and ______ were declared joint winners of the 2020 Online FIDE Chess Olympiad.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Russia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India and Russia have become the joint winners of the FIDE online Chess Olympiad.**

 
 
• World chess governing body FIDE declared both the finalists as joint winners after at least two games in the second match were affected by internet connectivity issues.
 
• India and Russia were declared joint winners of the 2020 Online FIDE Chess Olympiad after the final was marred by internet disconnection.
 
• Russia was initially declared winners after 2 Indian players, Nihal Sarin and Divya Deshmukh, lost out on time in the final after suffering a disconnection with the server.
 
• India had appealed against the controversial decision.
 
• The international chess federation Fide's president Arkady Dvorkovich decided to award the gold medal to both teams.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The FIDE Online Chess Olympiad was held for the first time due to the coronavirus pandemic.
 
• The first round of the final ended in a 3-3 draw with all six games finishing in a stalemate.
 
• Russia won the second round 4.5-1.5 with wins for Andrey Esipenko over Sarin and Polina Shuvalova over Deshmukh, leading to controversy as the Indians claimed the losses were due to connection issues.
 
• In the second round, Anand, coming in for P Harikrishna, had drawn with Ian Nepomniachtchi while captain Vidit Gujrathi drew with Daniil Dubov.

question: In Tennis, what is the score when the receiver wins the next point after deuce?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Advantage out**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tennis is a game played on a rectangular-shaped court, which can be one of many surfaces.
 
• It is either played with two players (singles match), or four players (doubles match).
 
• Players stand on opposite sides of the net and use a stringed racquet to hit the ball back and forth to each other.
 
• Most tennis matches are played in a best-of-three format, which means that players need to win 2 sets to win the match.
 
• The score when the receiver wins the next point after deuce **Advantage out**.
 
• In Grand Slams, men play best-of-five sets while women play best-of-three sets.
 
• Doubles matches are best-of-3 with a 10-point tiebreak in lieu of the third set.
 
• USTA and club matches are usually best-of-3.
 
• There are two main ways of scoring a set.
 
 
• Advantage Set
 
 
• In an advantage set, a player or team needs to win six games, by two, to win the set.
 
• This means that there is no tiebreak game played at 6-6.
 
• The set continues until one player/team wins by two games.
 
 
 
• Tiebreak Set
 
 
• In a tiebreak set, a player or team needs to win six games wins a set.
 
• If the score gets to 5-5 (5-all), one player must win the next two games to win the set.
 
• If the score reaches 6-6 (6-all) in the set, a tiebreak game is played.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Tennis is an Olympic sport and is played at all levels of society and at all ages.

question: Agricultural shot is a term used in which of the following sports?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cricket**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term "Agricultural shot" is used in **Cricket** to describe an unorthodox or poorly executed shot.
 
• In cricket, an agricultural shot typically refers to a wild swing of the bat, which is not played with the standard technique.
 
• This type of shot often results in the ball going in an unintended direction, usually not as per the plan of the batsman.
 
• It is generally considered to be a high-risk shot, often played in desperation or by less technically skilled players.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cricket Terminologies:**

 
 
• **Cover Drive:** A classic cricket shot played by driving the ball through the covers with a vertical bat.
 
• **Yorker:** A delivery bowled right at the batsman's feet, typically aimed at the base of the stumps.
 
• **Duckworth-Lewis Method:** A complex mathematical formula used to calculate the target score for the team batting second in a limited-overs cricket match interrupted by weather or other circumstances.
 
• **Leg Spin:** A type of spin bowling where the ball spins from the leg side to the off side (for a right-handed batsman).
 
• **All-rounder:** A player who excels at both batting and bowling.
 
 
 
• **Types of Shots in Cricket:**
 
 
• **Straight Drive:** A shot played straight down the ground with a vertical bat.
 
• **Sweep:** A shot played to a ball pitched on or outside the leg stump, typically hit towards the leg side.
 
• **Pull Shot:** A cross-batted shot played to a short-pitched ball, usually hit towards the leg side.
 
• **Cut Shot:** A shot played to a ball pitched short and wide of off stump, hit towards the point or gully region.
 
• **Hook Shot:** A shot played to a bouncer, where the batsman hits the ball towards the leg side, typically into the stands.
 
 
 
• **Cricket Fielding Positions:**
 
 
• **Slip:** A fielding position behind the batsman on the off side, typically placed to catch edges from the bat.
 
• **Gully:** Positioned between the slips and point, intended to catch edges that slip through.
 
• **Mid-wicket:** A position on the leg side, in the region square of the wicket.
 
• **Long-on:** Positioned straight down the ground, typically near the boundary.
 
• **Square Leg:** A position on the leg side, square with the wicket.

question: In chess, which of the following may only move forward to the unoccupied square immediately in front of it?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Pawn**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A pawn can only move forward to the unoccupied square immediately in front of it on the same file.
 
• On its first move, a pawn has the option to move forward two squares.
 
• Pawns capture diagonally, one square forward and to the left or right.
 
• If a pawn reaches the opposite end of the board, it can be promoted to any other piece, typically a queen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chess Pieces and Their Movements:**

 
 
• **The Bishop:** The bishop moves diagonally any number of squares. Each bishop starts on one color (light or dark) and must always stay on that color.
 
• **The Queen:** The queen can move any number of squares along a rank, file, or diagonal. It is the most powerful piece in terms of mobility.
 
• **The Rook:** The rook can move any number of squares along a rank or file. Rooks also play a crucial role in the endgame due to their ability to control large portions of the board.
 
• **The Knight:** The knight moves in an "L" shape: two squares in one direction and then one square perpendicular. Knights are unique because they can "jump" over other pieces.
 
• **The King:** The king moves one square in any direction. The objective of the game is to checkmate the opponent's king.
 
 
 
• **Special Pawn Moves:**
 
 
• **En Passant:** This special pawn capture can occur if a pawn moves two squares forward from its starting position and lands beside an opponent's pawn. The opponent's pawn can capture it "en passant" (in passing), as if it had only moved one square.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term "Blue Line" is a significant part of the game **Ice Hockey**.
 
• It refers to the lines that divide the hockey rink into three zones: the defending zone, neutral zone, and attacking zone.
 
• The blue lines play a crucial role in determining offside violations in the game of ice hockey.
 
• They are essential in regulating the flow of the game and ensuring that players adhere to the rules related to positioning on the rink.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Offside Rule in Ice Hockey**

 
 
• The offside rule is one of the fundamental rules in ice hockey, aimed at preventing players from gaining an unfair advantage.
 
• A player is considered offside if they enter the attacking zone before the puck crosses the blue line.
 
• If an offside violation occurs, the referee stops the play, and a faceoff is conducted in the neutral zone to resume the game.
 
• Understanding the offside rule is crucial for players and coaches as it impacts offensive strategies and game planning.
 
 
 
• **Zones on the Rink**
 
 
• The ice hockey rink is divided into three zones by two blue lines: the defending zone, the neutral zone, and the attacking zone.
 
• The defending zone is the area between the blue line closest to a team's goal and the end boards.
 
• The neutral zone lies between the two blue lines, where much of the game's transition play occurs.
 
• The attacking zone is the area between the blue line farthest from a team's goal and the end boards, where a team aims to score goals.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the Blue Line**
 
 
• The blue lines are critical for maintaining the structure and flow of the game, ensuring that players adhere to the rules of positioning.
 
• They are used to judge offside violations and play a role in determining where faceoffs occur on the rink.
 
• Blue lines also contribute to the strategic aspects of the game, influencing how teams execute their offensive and defensive plays.
 
• Properly understanding and leveraging the blue lines can provide a competitive edge to teams in ice hockey.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Castling is a unique move in chess involving the king and one of the rooks.
 
• It is the only move in chess where two pieces, the king and a rook, move simultaneously.
 
• Castling can only be done if neither the king nor the rook involved has previously moved, and there are no pieces between them.
 
• The purpose of castling is often to protect the king and to develop the rook.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Castling Conditions:**

 
 
• Neither the king nor the rook involved in castling may have previously moved.
 
• There must be no pieces between the king and the rook.
 
• The squares the king passes over must not be under attack.
 
• The king may not be in check before or after castling.
 
 
 
• **Types of Castling:**
 
 
• There are two types of castling: kingside (short) and queenside (long).
 
• In kingside castling, the king moves two squares towards the kingside rook and the rook moves to the square next to the king.
 
• In queenside castling, the king moves two squares towards the queenside rook and the rook moves to the square next to the king.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• Castling is a key strategic move that helps in the protection of the king by placing it behind a wall of pawns.
 
• It also helps in bringing the rook into play, connecting the rooks, and developing the pieces for the middle game.

question: In freestyle wrestling, which of the following actions can result in a technical point for the wrestler?

options.text: Running out of the mat deliberately

solution:
The correct answer is __**Performing a successful takedown**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A takedown is a critical technique in freestyle wrestling that allows a wrestler to bring their opponent from a standing position to the mat and gain control.
 
• Performing a successful takedown awards the wrestler technical points, which depend on the skill level and execution of the move (usually 2 to 5 points).
 
• Common types of takedowns include single-leg takedown, double-leg takedown, and throws.
 
• In addition to scoring points, a takedown puts the wrestler in an advantageous position to attempt further scoring or pinning.
 
• Freestyle wrestling emphasizes both offensive and defensive techniques, with takedowns being one of the primary methods of scoring.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Running out of the mat deliberately**

 
 
• Running out of the mat is considered a form of passive wrestling or avoiding engagement, which can lead to penalties.
 
• Instead of gaining points, wrestlers may receive warnings or penalties for deliberately stepping out of the mat to escape an opponent’s hold or avoid engagement.
 
• In some cases, referees may award points to the opponent if this action is deemed intentional.
 
 
 
• **Holding the opponent's singlet**
 
 
• Grabbing the opponent's singlet, headgear, or other parts of their uniform is prohibited in freestyle wrestling.
 
• This action is considered illegal and results in penalties or warnings against the wrestler committing the foul.
 
• The purpose of this rule is to ensure fairness and maintain the integrity of the sport.
 
 
 
• **Using an illegal headlock**
 
 
• An illegal headlock occurs when a wrestler applies a headlock without an arm included in the hold.
 
• This technique is not allowed as it can cause serious injuries and is against the rules of freestyle wrestling.
 
• Wrestlers using illegal holds may face penalties, warnings, or even disqualification in extreme cases.

question: Elite long jumpers typically use how many strides in their approach run?
solution:
The correct answer is __**18-22**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 

• Elite long jumpers typically take around **18 to 22 strides** during their approach run. The number of strides varies depending on the athlete's **height, speed, and technique.** 

• The approach run is a critical phase in the **long jump**, as it provides the necessary speed and momentum required for an optimal jump. 

• Long jumpers aim to achieve their maximum controlled speed during the approach to ensure a powerful take-off at the board. 

• The number of strides is carefully determined and practiced to ensure that the jumper can accurately hit the take-off board without overstepping or fouling. 

• While **18-22 strides** is the typical range, the exact number of strides may vary based on the athlete's training, biomechanics, and personal preferences. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **Phases of Long Jump:** 
 

• The long jump consists of four main phases: **approach run, take-off, flight, and landing**. 

• The approach run generates the momentum needed for a successful jump. 

• The take-off involves converting horizontal speed into vertical lift. 

• The flight phase requires the jumper to maintain balance and maximize the forward motion. 

• The landing phase focuses on extending the body forward to maximize the distance covered. 
 
 

• **Importance of Approach Run:** 
 

• The approach run is the most important phase in the long jump as it determines the jumper's **speed, rhythm, and accuracy**. 

• Successful long jumpers practice their approach runs extensively to ensure consistency in hitting the **take-off board**. 

• The optimum speed during the approach ensures a balance between horizontal distance and vertical height during the jump. 
 
 

• **Factors Affecting Number of Strides:** 
 

• Athlete's **height**: Taller athletes might require fewer strides due to their longer stride length. 

• **Strength and speed**: Faster and stronger athletes can achieve the desired velocity with fewer strides. 

• **Experience and technique**: Experienced jumpers optimize their stride patterns to hit the take-off board consistently. 
 
 

• **Examples of Elite Long Jumpers:** 
 

• Famous long jumpers like **Mike Powell** and **Carl Lewis** utilized efficient approach runs with approximately 20 strides to achieve their record-breaking jumps. 

• Mike Powell's world record jump of **8.95 meters** in 1991 is considered a benchmark in long jump history. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Training for Approach Run:** 
 

• Long jumpers focus on improving their **sprinting ability, stride length, and take-off accuracy** during training. 

• Drills like **bounding, sprint starts, and plyometric exercises** are commonly used to enhance approach run efficiency. 

• Regular video analysis helps athletes refine their stride patterns and maintain consistency. 
 
 

• **Key Metrics:** 
 

• The average approach run speed for elite male long jumpers is approximately **10.5 m/s**, while for female athletes, it is around **9.5 m/s**. 

• The take-off angle is typically between **18-22 degrees** for optimal performance. 
 
 

• **Rules for Long Jump:** 
 

• A valid jump requires the athlete to take off from the **take-off board** without overstepping its edge. 

• The jump distance is measured from the edge of the take-off board nearest to the landing pit to the nearest mark made in the sand by any part of the athlete's body. 

• Wind assistance must not exceed **2 m/s** for a record to be valid. 
 
 
</ul

• It is considered a perfect shot, demonstrating precision and accuracy in shooting. 
• The swish sound occurs due to the ball brushing against the net, creating an audible "swish" sound that players and spectators recognize as a sign of skillful shooting. 
• Swish shots are often celebrated in basketball as they symbolize a high level of shooting proficiency and are aesthetically pleasing.

• Slam dunks are popular in competitive games and highlight reels but are different from a swish as they involve physical contact with the hoop.

• A number of different types of foul may be punished in a game of hockey.

• Third-party obstruction- This is awarded when a hockey player positions themselves between the ball and an opponent, allowing a team-mate an unobstructed play on the ball.
 
• Advancing- This is awarded against a player who shoves, pushes, or advances the ball in any way, using any part of their body.
 
• Hockey stick interference- This is awarded against a player who uses their stick to hit an opponent’s stick, either intentionally or unintentionally.
 
• Undercutting- This is awarded against a player who lifts the ball in a dangerous manner.
 
• Sticks- This is awarded against a player who raises their stick dangerously near another player.

__
 
• If, for any reason, the ball strikes the frame of the goal or the referee and remains within the goal and touch lines,** it is still in play**. A goal is scored when the entire ball has crossed the goal line within the frame of the goal.
 
• A** challenge or tackle** that **threatens **an opponent's **safety **or makes use of **excessive force or brutality **must be penalized as **serious foul play.**

• The ball is** out of play** when it has **wholly passed over the goal line** or touchline on the ground or in the air play has been stopped by the** referee** it** touches a match official**, remains on the field of play and a team starts a **promising attack** or the ball goes **directly into the goal** or the team in** possession** of the ball changes in all these cases, play is restarted with a** dropped ball.**
 
• **Ball in play**
 
 
• The ball is in play at all other times when it touches **a match official** and when it **rebounds off a goalpost, crossbar or corner flagpost** and remains on the field of play.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Backstroke**

 
 
• The** ****stroke in swimming** that does **NOT **start with a dive into the pool from outside is **Backstroke**.
 
• One of the **four swimming strokes** used in competitive events governed by **FINA **is the** backstroke or back crawl, **which is the only one swum on the back.
 
• The benefit of easy breathing comes at the expense of swimmers being unable to see where they are going when swimming in this manner.
 
• In contrast to the other** three competition swimming styles**, it also has a different start. 
 
• **Backstroke **is the **second style swum** in the individual medley, although it is the first style swum in the medley relay.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Butterfly Stroke**

 
 
• The **butterfly** is a **swimming** **stroke** performed on the chest with the hips and both arms moving symmetrically. The **butterfly kick**, also referred to as the "**dolphin kick**," is also used.
 
• While novices can swim competently in other strokes like the **backstroke**, front crawl, or **breaststroke**, the butterfly is a more challenging type that calls for both solid technique and strong muscles.
 
 
 
• **Breaststroke**
 
 
• **​**The swimming stroke known as "**breaststroke**" is one in which the torso does not rotate, and the swimmer is on their chest.
 
• Because it can safely swim at slow rates and the swimmer's head is out of the water for a significant percentage of the swim, it is the most popular leisure technique.
 
 
 
• **Freestyle** 
 
 
• The** International Swimming Federation (FINA) **has established the category of swimming competition known as "**freestyle**," where participants are restricted to a few modest restrictions on their **swimming stroke.**
 
• The majority of **swimming **contests are freestyle races, which range in length from 50 metres (55 yards) to 1,500 metres (1,600 yards), or the mile. Since front crawl is the fastest surface **swimming stroke**, the word "**freestyle stroke**" is occasionally used as a synonym for **"front crawl."** Today, it is the stroke that is most frequently utilised in freestyle contests.

• Volleyball is a team sport.

• Teams are separated by a net.

**Volleyball Pointing System:**

The volleyball point system uses a rally scoring system, meaning a point is awarded on every rally, regardless of which team serves. Here's a breakdown of the key points:

**Sets:**

 
• Most matches are played as best-of-five sets.
 
• The first four sets are played to 25 points, with a two-point lead required to win. So, a set can continue until one team leads by two points, even if the score goes beyond 25-25.
 
• The final set (if necessary) is played to 15 points, again with a two-point lead requirement.

**Scoring:**

A point is awarded to the opposing team whenever your team commits a fault, such as:

 
• Hitting the ball out of bounds.
 
• Touching the net during play.
 
• Four touches by your team before returning the ball over the net.
 
• Foot faults or other technical violations.
 
• Serving errors also result in a point for the opposing team.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Test Matches**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term **Follow On** is used exclusively in the format of **Test cricket**.
 
• It occurs when a team, batting second, fails to avoid the follow on by scoring a certain percentage of the first team's score, usually **200 runs fewer** than the first team in a 5-day test match.
 
• The captain of the first batting team has the option to enforce the follow on, making the second team bat again immediately.
 
• This rule is designed to expedite the outcome of a match and is unique to Test cricket, emphasizing the strategic depth of this format.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Test Cricket**

 
 
• Test cricket is the longest form of the sport of cricket, where a match is played over five days, with each team having two innings.
 
• It is considered the ultimate test of playing ability and endurance, with matches often swinging back and forth in momentum.
 
• Introduced in 1877, Test cricket is the oldest form of the game and is played between international teams that are full members of the International Cricket Council (ICC).
 
• The follow on rule adds a strategic layer, where teams must decide whether to enforce it based on match conditions, player fitness, and weather forecasts.
 
 
 
• **One Day International (ODI) Cricket**
 
 
• ODI cricket is a limited-overs format where each team faces a set number of overs, usually 50.
 
• Matches are completed in a single day, making them more dynamic and fast-paced compared to Test matches.
 
• There is no follow on in ODIs as each team gets only one innings to bat.
 
• ODIs are part of major international tournaments like the ICC Cricket World Cup.
 
 
 
• **T20 Cricket**
 
 
• T20 cricket is the shortest form of the game, with each team playing a maximum of 20 overs.
 
• It is designed to be completed in about three hours, providing a quick and entertaining format for spectators.
 
• There is no follow on in T20 cricket, as each team has only one innings.
 
• It has led to the creation of several domestic leagues, including the Indian Premier League (IPL), which have greatly increased the game's popularity.

• Each player starts the game with two Bishops, placed on either side of the King and Queen.
 
• The Bishop can move any number of squares along the diagonal, but cannot jump over other pieces.
 
• The Bishop's movement allows it to control squares of only one color throughout the game.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chess Pieces and Their Movements:**

 
 
• **The Knight:** Moves in an L-shape: two squares in one direction and then one square perpendicular to that direction. It is the only piece that can jump over other pieces.
 
• **The Queen:** Can move any number of squares along a row, column, or diagonal. It combines the power of the Rook and Bishop.
 
• **The Rook:** Moves any number of squares along a row or column but cannot move diagonally.
 
• **The Pawn:** Moves forward one square, but captures diagonally. On its first move, it can move forward two squares.
 
• **The King:** Moves one square in any direction. The objective of the game is to checkmate the opponent's King.
 
 
 
• **Chessboard Layout:**
 
 
• The chessboard is an 8x8 grid with alternating light and dark squares.
 
• Each player begins with 16 pieces: one King, one Queen, two Rooks, two Knights, two Bishops, and eight Pawns.
 
• The pieces are placed on the two rows closest to each player, with Pawns on the second row and the major pieces on the first row.
 
 
 
• **Objective of the Game:**
 
 
• The primary objective in chess is to checkmate the opponent's King, which means the King is in a position to be captured (in check) and there is no legal move to escape.
 
• Players must use strategy and tactics to outmaneuver their opponent and gain a positional or material advantage.

question: Why is the weight and circumference of a cricket ball strictly regulated in official matches?

options.text: Heavier balls suit bowlers, lighter ones suit batsmen, so balance is needed
Variations affect bounce, swing, and fairness on standard pitches
ICC mandates it to cut costs and simplify logistics
Only red balls follow this; white balls have separate norms

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Regulation by ICC:** The **International Cricket Council (ICC)** strictly regulates the weight and circumference of cricket balls in official matches to maintain uniformity and fairness across all formats of the game.
 
• **Impact on performance:** Variations in weight and size significantly affect the **bounce, swing, and spin** of the ball. These factors are crucial in determining the outcome of matches and ensuring equal opportunities for both bowlers and batsmen.
 
• **Standard pitches:** Standard pitches are designed with specific dimensions and characteristics. Cricket balls must conform to regulated specifications to ensure predictable behavior on these pitches, contributing to a balanced contest.
 
• **Consistency in gameplay:** Uniformity in ball specifications helps ensure consistency in gameplay across different venues and conditions, fostering fair competition.
 
• **Quality assurance:** Strict regulations ensure that cricket balls are produced with high-quality materials and standardized manufacturing processes, preventing any unfair advantages or discrepancies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Specifications for Cricket Balls:**

 
 
• The weight of a cricket ball must be between **156 grams and 163 grams** as per ICC regulations.
 
• The circumference should be between **22.4 cm and 22.9 cm**.
 
• Red balls are used in **Test matches**, while white balls are used in **ODIs and T20s**.
 
• Different ball brands such as **Kookaburra, Dukes, and SG** are used globally, with slight variations in seam and finish.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Ball Variations:**
 
 
• Heavier balls may offer more swing, while lighter balls might favor batsmen due to less movement.
 
• The seam plays a critical role in generating spin and swing, affecting bowler performance.
 
• Changes in ball dimensions can disrupt the balance between batting and bowling, leading to unfair outcomes.
 
 
 
• **Role of ICC in Cricket:**
 
 
• The ICC is the governing body for international cricket, responsible for **standardizing rules, regulations, and equipment specifications**.
 
• Its guidelines ensure uniformity in gameplay across various formats and tournaments.
 
• ICC also monitors ball manufacturing to uphold these standards.
 
 
 
• **Red vs. White Balls:**
 
 
• **Red balls:** Used in longer formats, they have a pronounced seam for better swing and spin.
 
• **White balls:** Used in limited-overs formats, they are treated for durability under floodlights.
 
• White balls tend to deteriorate faster, affecting their performance over time.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advantages of Standardized Cricket Balls:**

 
 
• Ensures fair gameplay and equal opportunities for all players.
 
• Maintains consistency across matches played in different regions and conditions.
 
• Helps bowlers and batsmen strategize effectively based on predictable ball behavior.
 
 
 
• **Examples of ICC Regulations:**
 
 
• In Test cricket, only **red balls** conforming to ICC specifications are permitted.
 
• In ODIs and T20s, **white balls** are used, but they must meet the same weight and circumference standards as red balls.
 
• Special cases like **pink balls** are used for day-night Test matches but are also regulated for consistency.

question: Which of the following statements about cricket dismissals is **correct?**

options.text: Hitting the ball twice deliberately results in dismissal.
Retired Out' requires only umpire approval.
Obstructing the Field' can occur accidentally.
Retired Out' happens automatically without any approval.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Hitting the ball twice deliberately results in dismissal.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Hitting the ball twice deliberately** is considered an illegal action in cricket and results in dismissal under the laws of the game.
 
• This dismissal is covered under **Law 34 of the MCC Laws of Cricket**, which prohibits a batter from intentionally striking the ball twice unless it is done to defend their wicket.
 
• Such an action is judged by the umpire, who determines whether the batter deliberately hit the ball twice.
 
• The first strike is considered legitimate (e.g., hitting the ball with the bat), but the second strike intended to gain runs or mislead the fielding team constitutes a breach.
 
• This rule upholds the integrity of fair play in cricket and ensures that the batter does not use unfair methods to gain an advantage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Retired Out:**

 
 
• A player retiring out does not need umpire approval; it is the batter's voluntary decision.
 
• Unlike "retired hurt," where a player leaves due to injury with an option to return, "retired out" is final and does not allow re-entry into the game.
 
• This form of dismissal is uncommon and usually occurs in practice matches or under special circumstances.
 
 
 
• **Obstructing the Field:**
 
 
• According to **Law 37 of the MCC Laws of Cricket**, "Obstructing the Field" occurs when a batter deliberately interferes with a fielder attempting to field or catch the ball.
 
• This dismissal is not accidental; it requires clear intent by the batter to obstruct the fielding side.
 
• Examples include using the bat or body to stop the ball while a fielder is attempting to effect a run-out or catch.
 
• Accidental interference, such as running in the path of a fielder without intent, does not constitute this dismissal.
 
 
 
• **Cricket Dismissals:**
 
 
• There are several ways a batter can be dismissed in cricket, including bowled, caught, leg before wicket (LBW), stumped, and run-out.
 
• Other less common dismissals include obstructing the field, retired out, hitting the ball twice, and timed out.
 
• Each type of dismissal has specific rules outlined by the **MCC Laws of Cricket** and is subject to umpire judgment.

solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1:** Men and women compete in identical freestyle distances from 50m to 1500m in World Championship swimming events (50m pool). This includes events such as 50m, 100m, 200m, 400m, 800m, and 1500m freestyle.
 
• **Statement 2:** Individual Medley events are held only up to 400m for both men and women. The recognized distances include 200m and 400m Individual Medley events at the World Championships (50m pool).
 
• Both statements are factually correct, as the International Swimming Federation (FINA) defines the standard distances and event formats for World Championship swimming competitions.
 
• These events are held under standardized rules to maintain consistency in competition formats for all genders and categories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Freestyle Events:**

 
 
• Freestyle swimming events are conducted at various distances, including 50m, 100m, 200m, 400m, 800m, and 1500m.
 
• Both male and female swimmers compete in these distances under identical formats in World Championship competitions conducted in a 50m pool.
 
• The 800m freestyle event for men and the 1500m freestyle event for women were added to the Olympic Games program in 2020, ensuring parity in event offerings.
 
 
 
• **Individual Medley Events:**
 
 
• Individual Medley (IM) consists of four strokes—Butterfly, Backstroke, Breaststroke, and Freestyle—performed in succession during a single race.
 
• At the World Championship level, IM events are limited to 200m and 400m distances for both men and women.
 
• No IM events longer than 400m are conducted in 50m pools as per FINA regulations.

question: Which of the following is true about "en passant" in chess?

options.text: Only after a pawn moves two squares and waits a turn.
Can be done within two moves after the pawn's advance.
Must be done immediately after the pawn moves two squares.
Only if the capturing pawn is on a dark square.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Must be done immediately after the pawn moves two squares**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **En passant** is a special pawn capture rule in chess that allows a pawn to capture an opponent's pawn immediately after it moves two squares forward from its starting position.
 
• The capture must be made **on the very next move**; otherwise, the opportunity is lost.
 
• The opponent's pawn must have moved two squares forward from its starting position, landing adjacent to the capturing pawn.
 
• When the en passant capture occurs, the capturing pawn moves diagonally to the square where the opponent's pawn would have landed if it had advanced only one square.
 
• The rule was introduced to prevent pawns from bypassing a potential capture when advancing two squares, maintaining fairness in the game.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Pieces: King, Queen, Rook, Bishop, Knight, Pawn.
 
• Board: Chessboard, Center (e4, d4, e5, d5), Ranks (rows), Files (columns). 
 
 
 
• **Game States & Results**
 
 
• Check: King is attacked.
 
• Checkmate: King is attacked and cannot escape (Game Over).
 
• Stalemate: No legal moves, but not in check (Draw).
 
• Draw: Tie game (e.g., Perpetual Check, Threefold Repetition).

A fresh toss is taken if the match is tied even after 5-5 raids.

• This rule ensures a fair opportunity for both teams and avoids indefinite extensions of the match duration.
 
• The **Golden Raid** is a tiebreaker mechanism where each team gets five raids to score points and secure a win.
 
• In the event of another tie after the Golden Raid phase, the fresh toss decides which team gets to initiate the next set of raids.

question: Which of the following statements about Judo techniques and rules is **correct**?

options.text: Shime-Waza are arm locks targeting the elbows.
A Judo match ends immediately if a player scores an Ippon or receives a Hansoku-make.
Judoka can strike and kick but cannot attack joints other than elbows.
Hansoku-make is a minor penalty in Judo.

solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In Judo, a match ends immediately if a player scores an **Ippon**, which is equivalent to a full point, or receives a **Hansoku-make**, which signifies disqualification.
 
• **Ippon** is awarded when a player executes a perfect technique, such as a throw where the opponent lands on their back with force and control, or achieves a successful pin for 20 seconds.
 
• **Hansoku-make** refers to a serious violation of Judo rules, such as prohibited actions or dangerous techniques, which results in the immediate disqualification of the player.
 
• This rule ensures safety and adherence to the principles of Judo, emphasizing respect, discipline, and fair play during the match.
 
• The immediate termination of the match upon Ippon or Hansoku-make is a fundamental aspect of Judo competitions and aligns with the sport’s emphasis on decisive outcomes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: Shime-Waza are arm locks targeting the elbows**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect. **Shime-Waza** refers to choking techniques in Judo, which involve restricting the opponent’s airflow or blood flow to induce submission.
 
• The arm locks targeting the elbows in Judo are categorized under **Kansetsu-Waza**, not Shime-Waza.
 
• Kansetsu-Waza techniques are designed to apply pressure on joints, particularly the elbows, forcing the opponent to submit.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Judoka can strike and kick but cannot attack joints other than elbows**
 
 
• This statement is incorrect. Strikes and kicks are strictly prohibited in Judo as it is a grappling martial art focused on throws, pins, joint locks, and chokeholds.
 
• Judoka are allowed to attack joints only within the scope of **Kansetsu-Waza**, and even then, only the elbow joint is targeted.
 
• The prohibition of strikes and kicks reflects Judo’s emphasis on technique, control, and safety rather than brute force or aggression.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Hansoku-make is a minor penalty in Judo**

• **Main Theme: Judo Techniques and Rules**
